# Sample databases and templates

Rutba Data Files comes with a working database for each kind of small business we make Office for, and
five simple templates. Each sample has related tables, the questions that business asks as saved queries,
a form for every table, reports, and print templates for what it sends out (invoices, receipts,
agreements, payslips). It comes either with a year or more of invented records to learn from, or empty,
ready for your own: on the Data Files start screen, choose a business and then **With sample records** or
**Empty**. The same files, and this documentation a page each, are on
[office.rutba.io/samples](https://office.rutba.io/samples).

The samples are made by `packages/database/src/samples` (one file each), checked by `check.js` and
`tests/database-samples.test.js`, and written as files by `node tools/make-samples.mjs`. This page is made by
`node tools/make-samples.mjs --docs` from each database's own description and its design, so it says what the
files hold. It was made on 2026-10-22.

With each release, the downloads on office.rutba.io are made again so their dates are current: in the
management repository, `npm run import:samples` in `portal/apps/office` builds every sample from this
repository, zips it with a read-me into `public/samples/` and writes the pages' catalogue,
`src/site/samples.json`. A sample that fails `checkSample` stops the import.

## Larkspur Corner Store

**Shop.** Products, the till and its receipts, VAT, stock, supplier orders, deliveries, loyalty customers and running costs for a neighbourhood shop.

Larkspur Corner Store is an invented neighbourhood shop open from seven in the morning to nine at night, every day of the week. It sells bread, milk, fruit and vegetables, drinks, snacks, groceries, household goods and newspapers, from about forty lines bought from six suppliers.

The sample holds a year of trading made up a day at a time. The till rings up a sale every few minutes, more at lunchtime and after school and more on Saturdays, and every sale has a numbered receipt. The evening before each supplier's delivery day the owner sends it an order for what has run low, so stock goes down between deliveries and back up again; now and then a supplier is short of a line. At each month end the rent, wages, power and card fees are paid, so the takings can be set against what the shop costs to run.

Prices on the shelf include VAT, as a shop's do. Most food is zero-rated, while soft drinks, alcohol, sweets, crisps, household goods and greeting cards carry the standard rate of twenty percent, and stamps and phone top-ups carry none. Each product has its VAT code, each receipt shows the VAT within its total, and a query adds up the VAT on the month's sales for the VAT return.

Use it to see how a till, stock and suppliers fit together in one database, or start from it empty for a shop of your own.

It suits, with small changes: A convenience store or minimarket; A farm shop; A newsagent; A gift shop; A pharmacy counter for the goods it sells off the shelf; A market stall.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Prices in Products and Sale Lines include VAT, as the shelf labels do. Cost Price and Unit Cost on orders and deliveries are before VAT, as suppliers invoice them. Profit by category takes the VAT off the takings before it takes off the cost.
- A sale's Total, VAT, Standard Rated and Saved are what the till worked out and printed when the sale was made, each line's VAT rounded to the penny and then added up. They are stored, not worked out again, so the receipt reprints exactly as it was; the query Receipt totals works them out from the lines when you enter a sale by hand.
- Only one VAT rate other than nought is used: twenty percent. The receipt's VAT summary and the VAT queries count everything with a rate above nought as standard rated. If you sell goods at a reduced rate, see the ways to adapt it.
- In Stock goes down as the till sells and up as deliveries come in, in the sample's records. Entering a sale or a delivery by hand does not change it by itself: change In Stock in the Products form, or count it at a stock take.
- The print template Sale receipt prints the sales that were not refunded, and Supplier order prints every order. Print one from its form for the record on screen: a refunded sale chosen there still prints its receipt, marked as refunded.
- Refunded sales stay in the Sales table with their receipt numbers, so no number is missing; they are left out of the takings, the VAT and the best sellers.

### Tutorial

#### Ring up a sale and print its receipt

1. Open the Sales form and press New. Type the next receipt number in Number (look at the last one in the Sales table: RCP-2026-01234 is followed by RCP-2026-01235), and the date and time in When.
2. Choose who is on the till in Staff and, if the customer shows a loyalty card, choose them in Customer. Choose Card, Cash or Mobile in Payment.
3. In the Sale Lines below, choose each Product, type the Quantity and the Unit Price from the shelf label, and copy the product's Tax Rate (0.2 or 0).
4. Run the query Receipt totals and find the sale. Type its Total, VAT, Standard Rated and Saved into the sale. For cash, type what was handed over in Tendered and the difference in Change.
5. Open the print template Sale receipt from Print templates, choose the sale, and press Print, or press Print on the Sales form to print the sale on screen.

#### Cash up at closing time

1. Run the query Today's takings. It shows the takings by Card, Cash and Mobile, with refunds left out.
2. Count the cash drawer and set it against the Cash line, less the float you started with. Set the Card and Mobile lines against the card terminal's end-of-day slip.
3. If a sale was refunded, open it in the Sales form and tick Refunded, then run Today's takings again.

#### Order from the shopping list

1. The evening before a supplier comes, open the report Shopping list. It lists, on a page for each supplier, what is at or below its reorder level.
2. Open the Supplier Orders form and press New. Type the next number in Number (ORD-2026-0042 is followed by ORD-2026-0043), choose the Supplier, and type today in Ordered On and the delivery day in Delivery Due. Status stays Sent.
3. In the Supplier Order Lines below, choose each product from the shopping list and type how many to order and the Unit Cost.
4. Open the print template Supplier order, choose the order, and press Save as PDF to e-mail it, or Print to hand it to the driver.

#### Take in a delivery

1. When the goods come, open the Deliveries form and press New. Choose the Supplier and the Order it answers, type the day in Received and the number on the supplier's invoice in Invoice Number.
2. In the Delivery Lines below, enter each product that came, how many, and the Unit Cost on the invoice.
3. Add what came to each product's In Stock in the Products form, and set the order's Status in Supplier Orders to Delivered, or Part delivered if something was short.
4. When you pay the invoice, tick Paid on the delivery. The report Deliveries to pay lists what is still owed.

#### Do the month end

1. On the last day of the month, open the Expenses form and enter the rent, wages, power, card fees and anything else paid, one record each.
2. Open the report Takings by month and the report Running costs to set the month's takings against its costs.
3. Open the report Profit by category to see which sections earned most after VAT and the cost of the goods.
4. For the VAT return, open the report VAT on sales and take the VAT for the months of the quarter. The VAT you paid on what you bought is on your suppliers' invoices.

#### Count the stock

1. Print the report Stock take sheet. It lists every product by section with its barcode and what the database thinks is in stock.
2. Count the shelves and the back room and write the real number beside each line.
3. Open the Products form and type the counted numbers into In Stock where they differ.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 27 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The name printed at the top of every document. |
| Address | Short text | The street address. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country. |
| Phone | Short text | The phone number customers call. |
| E-mail | Short text | The address customers write to. |
| Website | Short text | The website, if there is one. |
| Tax Number | Short text | The VAT or sales tax registration number, printed on invoices. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Company Number | Short text | The registered company number, where the business is a company. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Bank Details | Short text | Where customers pay by transfer: the bank, account name and number. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Payment Terms | Short text | The words printed under an invoice's total, such as "Payment within 30 days". |
| Tax Rate | Number | The usual rate of VAT or sales tax as a fraction: 0.2 is twenty percent. Lines may carry a rate of their own. |
| Currency | Short text | The currency the business trades in, as its three-letter code. |
| Document Footer | Long text | A line or two at the foot of every document: thanks, opening hours, returns policy. |

### Relationships

- Products.Category points at a record in Categories
- Products.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Sales.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Sales.Customer points at a record in Customers
- Sale Lines.Sale points at a record in Sales
- Sale Lines.Product points at a record in Products
- Supplier Orders.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Supplier Orders.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Supplier Order Lines.Order points at a record in Supplier Orders
- Supplier Order Lines.Product points at a record in Products
- Deliveries.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Deliveries.Order points at a record in Supplier Orders
- Delivery Lines.Delivery points at a record in Deliveries
- Delivery Lines.Product points at a record in Products

### Queries

#### Today's takings

What the till has taken today so far, by how people paid, and how many items went out. Run it at closing time to check against the cash drawer and the card terminal.

From Sales, Sale Lines. Shows Payment, Takings, Items.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago = 0` and `Refunded = No`.

#### Daily takings

Takings and items sold on each of the last 30 days, the newest first, to spot a slow day.

From Sales, Sale Lines. Shows Day, Takings, Items.
Calculated: Day is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30` and `Refunded = No`.

#### Monthly takings

Takings for each month of the year, refunds left out.

From Sales, Sale Lines. Shows Month, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm")`; Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Refunded = No`.

#### Busy hours

How many sales the till rang up in each hour of the day over the last 90 days, to plan who works when.

From Sales. Shows Hour, Sales.
Calculated: Hour is `Mid([When], 12, 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Best sellers

The products that sold most in the last 30 days, with what they took.

From Sale Lines, Products, Sales. Shows Product, Sold, Takings.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Refunded = No` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Profit by category

For each section of the shop, what it took, the VAT within that, and what it earned after the VAT and the cost of the goods, the best earner first.

From Sale Lines, Products, Categories, Sales. Shows Category, Takings, VAT, Profit.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`; VAT is `Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) / (1 + [Sale Lines].[Tax Rate]), 2)`; Profit is `Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) / (1 + [Sale Lines].[Tax Rate]), 2) - [Quantity] * [Cost Price], 2)`.
Only where `Refunded = No`.

#### Takings by staff

What each person rang up over the last 30 days.

From Sales, Staff, Sale Lines. Shows Staff Member, Role, Takings.
Calculated: Staff Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30` and `Refunded = No`.

#### Low stock

Products at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with the days each supplier delivers. This is the shopping list each supplier order is made from.

From Products, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Delivers On, Product, In Stock, Reorder Level.
Only where `Spare <= 0` and `Active = Yes`.

#### Stock value

What the stock on the shelves is worth by section, at cost and at sale price.

From Products, Categories. Shows Category, Items, At Cost, At Sale Price.
Calculated: At Cost is `Round([In Stock] * [Cost Price], 2)`; At Sale Price is `Round([In Stock] * [Sale Price], 2)`.

#### Costs by month

What the shop paid out each month, by kind of cost.

From Expenses. Shows Month, Kind, Amount.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Best customers

Loyalty customers by what they have spent, with their points.

From Customers, Sales, Sale Lines. Shows Customer, Spent, Points.
Calculated: Customer is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Spent is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Refunded = No`.

#### Unpaid deliveries

Supplier invoices not yet paid, oldest first, with what each one comes to.

From Deliveries, Suppliers, Delivery Lines. Shows Delivery, Supplier, Received, Invoice Number, Owed.
Calculated: Owed is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Paid = No`.

#### VAT on sales by month

For each month, the takings, the part at the standard rate, the VAT within it and the part at zero or exempt: the output VAT for the VAT return, refunds left out.

From Sales. Shows Month, Takings, At 20%, VAT, At 0% or Exempt.
Calculated: Month is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm")`; At 0% or Exempt is `Round([Total] - [Standard Rated], 2)`.
Only where `Refunded = No`.

#### Receipt totals

Today's and yesterday's receipts with their total, VAT, standard-rated part and saving worked out from their lines. When you enter a sale by hand, read its figures here and type them into the sale.

From Sales, Sale Lines. Shows Receipt, When, Total, VAT, Standard Rated, Saved.
Calculated: Total is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`; VAT is `Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) / (1 + [Sale Lines].[Tax Rate]), 2)`; Standard Rated is `IIf([Sale Lines].[Tax Rate] > 0, Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2), 0)`; Saved is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * Nz([Discount]), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 1`.

#### Supplier orders, last 7 days

The orders sent to suppliers in the last week, the newest first, with when each is due and whether it came.

From Supplier Orders, Suppliers. Shows Number, Supplier, Ordered On, Delivery Due, Status.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 6`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Categories, Suppliers, Products, Staff, Customers, Sales, Sale Lines, Supplier Orders, Supplier Order Lines, Deliveries, Delivery Lines, Expenses. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Takings by month

One line a month with the takings and a total for the year.

From the query Monthly takings: Month, Takings, with the total of Takings.

#### Takings, the last 30 days

Takings and items for each of the last 30 days, with the total and the average day.

From the query Daily takings: Day, Items, Takings, with the total of Takings, average of Takings.

#### Profit by category

Takings, VAT and profit by section, with totals: the page to look at when deciding what to stock more of.

From the query Profit by category: Category, Takings, VAT, Profit, with the total of Takings, total of VAT, total of Profit.

#### To order

What to order, on a page for each supplier, with what is left and the reorder level.

From the query Low stock, a group for each Supplier: Product, In Stock, Reorder Level.

#### Stock take sheet

Every product by section with its barcode and what the database says is in stock, to count against.

From the table Products, a group for each Category: Name, Barcode, In stock, with the total of In Stock.

#### Running costs

Each month's costs by kind, with a total for the month.

From the query Costs by month, a group for each Month: Kind, Amount, with the total of Amount.

#### Deliveries to pay

Supplier invoices still to pay, by supplier, with a total for each.

From the query Unpaid deliveries, a group for each Supplier: Delivery, Received, Invoice Number, Owed, with the total of Owed.

#### VAT on sales, by month

The VAT on sales month by month, for the accountant or the VAT return.

From the query VAT on sales by month: Month, Takings, At 20%, VAT, At 0% or Exempt, with the total of Takings, total of VAT.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Sale receipt

The till receipt on an 80 mm roll: the shop's name, address and VAT number, the receipt number, date, time and who served, each item with its price and VAT code, the total, the VAT included by rate, and the returns policy from the Business record. The saving shows only when there was one, the cash tendered and change only for a cash sale, and the loyalty card and its points only when a card was shown. It is for the sales that were not refunded; a refunded sale chosen on the Sales form still prints, marked as refunded. Print it from the Sales form for the sale on screen. One for each record of Sales, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Date and time, Served by, Paid by, Loyalty card
- Lines from Sale Lines: Item, Qty, Price, Amount, VAT
- Totals: Total, You saved, Cash tendered, Change, S: sales at 20% VAT, VAT at 20% included, Z, E, O: sales at 0% or exempt, Loyalty points earned
- Words: This sale was refunded in full.
- Words: VAT codes: S standard rate 20%, Z zero rate, E exempt, O outside the scope of VAT. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Supplier order

The order sent to a supplier: its number, the shop's account with them, the delivery day, each product with its barcode, quantity and cost, how many lines and items, and the total before VAT. Every order prints, delivered ones too, so a delivery can be checked against what was asked for. Print it from the Supplier Orders form for the order on screen, or e-mail it as a PDF. One for each record of Supplier Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Order {Number}
- Fields: To, Order number, For the attention of, Date, Address, Deliver on, City, Our account, Postcode, Ordered by
- Lines from Supplier Order Lines: Barcode, Product, Quantity, Unit Cost, Total
- Totals: Lines, Items, Total before VAT
- Words: Please deliver on the day above to {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}, and quote {Number} on your invoice. If a line is out of stock, please tell us on the day rather than send a substitute.
- Words: Chilled and fresh lines are checked on arrival and will be refused with less than three days left on their date.

### Starting empty

Start with Business, the shop's own name, address and VAT number and the returns policy in Document Footer, which every receipt prints. Then Categories and Suppliers, then your Products with their VAT code, tax rate, prices and reorder levels, then your Staff. Sales, supplier orders and deliveries come in as you trade. Put your running costs in Expenses as you pay them.

### Making it yours

- Sell by weight: add a Unit field to Products (each, kg, 100 g) and make Quantity in Sale Lines a Number rather than a whole number.
- Track sell-by dates: add a Best Before field to Delivery Lines and a query for lines within three days of it.
- Sell at a reduced VAT rate as well: add a Reduced Rated field to Sales beside Standard Rated, and lines to the receipt's totals and the VAT query for it.
- Keep more than one till or shop: add a Tills table, point Sales at it, and group the takings queries by till.
- Reward points differently: change Points to count one for every two spent, or add a Points Redeemed field to Sales.
- Record the VAT you pay: add a VAT field to Deliveries for the VAT on each supplier invoice, and a query that sets it against VAT on sales by month.

### Questions people ask

**How do I reprint a customer's receipt?**

Find the sale in the Sales form, by its receipt number or by the date and time, and press Print with the print template Sale receipt. It prints from the stored totals, so it reads as the first one did.

**Where do I see how much VAT I owe?**

Open the report VAT on sales: the VAT column is the VAT within your takings each month. Add up the months of your VAT quarter and take off the VAT on your suppliers' invoices, which this database does not keep.

**Why is there no VAT on bread or milk?**

Most food is zero-rated, so its Tax Rate is 0 and its VAT Code is Z. Soft drinks, alcohol, sweets, crisps and household goods carry the standard rate. Check the rules for your own country and set each product's VAT Code and Tax Rate to match.

**How does the shop know what to order?**

Each product has a Reorder Level. The query Low stock and the report Shopping list show everything at or below it, by supplier, and the supplier order is made from that list.

**How are loyalty points worked out?**

One point for each whole pound spent on a sale, stored in the sale's Points Earned and added to the customer's Points. A refunded sale earns none.

**A supplier did not bring everything. How do I show that?**

Enter only what came in the delivery's lines, and set the order's Status to Part delivered. The lines left out are still on the order, so you can see what to chase.

**Can I start with my own products and none of the sample's sales?**

Yes. Open the sample empty, fill in Business first, then Categories, Suppliers and Products, then Staff. Sales, orders and deliveries come in as you trade.

## Bramblegate Wine and Deli

**Food and beverages.** Batches with their dates, markdowns, write-offs, the till, age checks and refusals, suppliers and purchase orders for a food and drink shop.

Bramblegate Wine and Deli is an invented independent food and drink shop. It sells wines, beers, ciders, spirits and soft drinks, has a deli counter of cheese, cured and cooked meats, olives and salads, takes fresh bread from a bakery every morning, and keeps a shelf of fine foods: oils, pasta, preserves, crackers, coffee and chocolate. It is open from nine to eight, Monday to Saturday, and from ten to four on Sunday, and holds a premises licence to sell alcohol.

Much of what it sells has a date on it. Every delivery comes in as batches, each with its batch code and its use-by or best-before date, and the till takes each sale from the batch with the earliest date. Each morning a date check marks down what is close to its date, printing a reduced label for each pack, and takes off sale what has passed it, writing it off at what it cost. So the records show the waste that selling fresh food brings, by month and by product, and what each category earns once the markdowns are paid for.

Anyone who looks under 25 is asked for ID before an alcohol sale; the till records the check on each sale, and each refusal goes into a register kept month by month and signed by the personal licence holder. Six or more bottles of wine, or twelve or more beers and ciders, earn ten percent off as a mixed case.

The sample holds a year of trading, made up a day at a time: busier on Friday and Saturday evenings and in December, rose, beer and cider in summer, whisky, sparkling wine and chocolates at Christmas. Prices on the shelf include VAT; deli, bakery and fine foods are zero-rated, while drinks, crisps and sweets carry the standard rate.

It suits, with small changes: An off-licence or liquor store; A delicatessen; A farm shop; A health food shop; A cheese shop or butcher with a counter; A village shop selling fresh food.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Stock lives in Batches. A product's In Stock is all its batches' Remaining added up; in the sample's records the till takes each sale from the batch with the earliest date, and the date check takes what has passed its date off sale. When you enter sales or deliveries by hand, change Remaining on the batch and In Stock on the product yourself.
- Use by and best before are not the same. A use-by line (chilled meats, cheese, salads, fresh juice) must not be sold after its date, so it is written off the next morning. A best-before line may be sold after its date, but this shop marks it down within two weeks of it and writes it off once the date has passed. Wine and spirits carry no date, only a batch code.
- The markdown rules in the sample: a use-by line is reduced by a quarter the day before its date and by half on the day; bread is reduced by half on its date; food that keeps is reduced by 30 percent within two weeks of its date and by half in its last three days. Change them to your own.
- A sale's Total, VAT, Standard Rated and Saved are what the till worked out and printed: each line's VAT rounded to the penny, then added up. They are stored so a receipt reprints exactly as it was. The query Receipt totals works them out from the lines.
- Prices include VAT. Cost Price, Unit Cost and purchase orders are before VAT, as suppliers invoice them. The margin queries take the VAT off the takings before they take off the cost.
- The refusals register keeps no names, only what is needed to recognise someone: an age, what they looked like, what happened. Keep it on the premises and show it when the licensing authority or the police ask.
- The print template Purchase order prints the orders still to come (Status Submitted); the others print every record of their table. Print one from its form for the record on screen: a receipt from the Sales form, a received order from the Purchase Orders form, a day's sheet from the Date Checks form, a month's register from the Refusal Registers form.
- The refusals register counts its own refusals as it prints, and says when a month has none or is not reviewed yet; nobody types the count.

### Tutorial

#### Do the morning date check

1. Before opening, run the report Date check list. It lists by category every batch on the shelf with a date in the next seven days.
2. Open the Date Checks form and press New. Type the next number in Number (DC-2026-0042 is followed by DC-2026-0043), today in Date, choose yourself in Staff, and type the two fridge readings in Fridge Temperatures.
3. For each batch to reduce, open the Markdowns form and press New: choose the date check in Check and the batch in Batch, type today in Date, the shelf price in Was, the reduced price in Now, how many packs are left in Labels, and the reason. Type the reduced price into the batch's Marked Down To in the Batches form.
4. For each batch past its date, open the Write-offs form and press New: choose the check and the batch, type the units, Out of date in Reason and the units at the batch's Unit Cost in Cost. Take the same number off the batch's Remaining.
5. Open the print template Markdown label sheet, choose today's check and press Print. Print a Reduced label from the Markdowns form for each pack, and stick them over the shelf price.

#### Sell from the till, with an age check

1. Open the Sales form and press New. Type the next receipt number in Number, the date and time in When, and choose who is on the till in Staff and how the customer paid in Payment.
2. In the Sale Lines below, choose each Product and the Batch it came from (the one with the earliest date: the query Stock by batch shows them in order), and type the Quantity, the shelf price in Full Price and the price charged in Unit Price. Copy the category's Tax Rate and the batch's Unit Cost.
3. If the sale has six or more bottles of wine, or twelve or more beers and ciders, type 0.1 in Discount on those lines, except any already reduced.
4. If there is alcohol, type Looked over 25 or ID checked in Age Check, and what was shown in ID Seen.
5. Run the query Receipt totals and type the sale's Total, VAT, Standard Rated and Saved from it. For cash, type the money handed over in Tendered and the difference in Change.
6. Open the print template Till receipt, choose the sale and press Print. Take each line's units off its batch's Remaining.

#### Refuse a sale and keep the register

1. When you refuse to sell alcohol, open the Refusals form straight away and press New. Type the next number in Number and the date and time in When.
2. Choose this month's register in Register (if the month has none yet, add it in the Refusal Registers form first, with the month as 2026-10), yourself in Staff and what was asked for in Product.
3. Type the Reason, how old the customer looked in Approx Age, the ID shown, and a few words in Description. No names.
4. At the month end the licence holder runs the query Refusals, last 30 days to read the month through, types their name and the day in Reviewed By and Reviewed On, then prints the print template Refusals register for the month and signs it.

#### Order from your suppliers

1. Run the report Stock to reorder. It shows, on a page for each supplier, what is at or below its reorder level and the pack size it comes in.
2. Open the Purchase Orders form and press New. Type the next number in Number (PO-2026-0042 is followed by PO-2026-0043), choose the Supplier and yourself in Staff, and type today in Ordered On and the delivery day in Expected. Status stays Submitted.
3. In the Purchase Lines below, choose each product and type how many to order, in whole packs, and the Unit Cost.
4. Open the print template Purchase order, choose the order and press Save as PDF to e-mail it to the supplier.

#### Take in a delivery as batches

1. When the goods come, check each case's date and batch code. Open the order in the Purchase Orders form, type the day in Received On, Received in Status and the number on the supplier's invoice in Supplier Invoice.
2. For each line, open the Batches form and press New: choose the Product and the Purchase Order, type the Batch Code and the date from the pack in Expiry Date (leave it empty for wine and spirits), the day in Received, how many came in Quantity and again in Remaining, and the Unit Cost.
3. Add the units to the product's In Stock in the Products form.
4. When you pay the supplier, tick Paid on the order. The query Deliveries to pay lists what is still owed.

#### Look at the month

1. Open the report Takings by month and the report Margin by category to see what each category took and earned after VAT and the cost of the goods.
2. Open the report Write-offs by month for what was thrown away, and run the query Write-offs by product for the lines to order less of.
3. Run the query Age checks by month to see how often the till asked for ID.
4. For the VAT return, open the report VAT on sales and take the VAT for the months of the quarter.

| Quantity | Whole number | How many units. |
| Reason | Short text | Out of date, Broken or Damaged. |
| Cost | Currency | What the units cost: the quantity at the batch's unit cost. |
| Staff | Points at Staff | Who wrote it off. |

#### Refusal Registers

The refusals register, one record a month, reviewed and signed by the personal licence holder when the month ends. The sample has 12 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Month | Short text, required, unique | The month the register covers, as 2026-10. Each month is used once. |
| Reviewed By | Points at Staff | Who reviewed it: a personal licence holder. |
| Reviewed On | Date | The day it was reviewed; empty for the month still running. |

#### Refusals

Each sale of alcohol refused, written down at the time, as a licensed shop keeps them. The sample has 99 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The refusal's number: REF-2026-0042, a new run each year. |
| Register | Points at Refusal Registers | The month's register it is written in. |
| When | Date and time | The date and time. |
| Staff | Points at Staff | Who refused the sale. |
| Product | Points at Products | What the customer tried to buy. |
| Reason | Short text | No ID shown, ID not acceptable, Under 18 on ID, Suspected proxy sale (buying for someone under age) or Customer drunk. |
| Approx Age | Whole number | How old the customer looked, in years. |
| ID Shown | Short text | What ID was offered, if any. |
| Description | Short text | What happened, in a few words, so the person could be recognised if they come back. No names. |

### Relationships

- Products.Category points at a record in Categories
- Products.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Purchase Orders.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Purchase Orders.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Purchase Lines.Purchase Order points at a record in Purchase Orders
- Purchase Lines.Product points at a record in Products
- Batches.Product points at a record in Products
- Batches.Purchase Order points at a record in Purchase Orders
- Sales.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Sale Lines.Sale points at a record in Sales
- Sale Lines.Product points at a record in Products
- Sale Lines.Batch points at a record in Batches
- Date Checks.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Markdowns.Check points at a record in Date Checks
- Markdowns.Batch points at a record in Batches
- Write-offs.Check points at a record in Date Checks
- Write-offs.Batch points at a record in Batches
- Write-offs.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Refusal Registers.Reviewed By points at a record in Staff
- Refusals.Register points at a record in Refusal Registers
- Refusals.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Refusals.Product points at a record in Products

### Queries

#### Expiring in the next 7 days

Batches still on the shelf whose date is in the next week, by category and date, with how many days are left, what is left and any reduced price. This is the list for the morning date check.

From Batches, Products, Categories. Shows Category, Expiry Date, Product, Batch Code, Date Kind, Days Left, Remaining, Sale Price, Marked Down To.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Expiry Date])`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 7` and `Remaining > 0`.

#### Marked down, last 30 days

Every markdown of the last month, the newest first, with the price before and after and how many labels were printed.

From Markdowns, Batches, Products. Shows Date, Number, Product, Batch Code, Expiry Date, Was, Now, Labels, Reason.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Written off by month

Units and cost written off each month, by reason: out of date, broken or damaged.

From Write-offs. Shows Month, Reason, Units, Cost.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Write-offs by product

Which lines were written off most over the last 90 days, by cost: the ones to order less of.

From Write-offs, Batches, Products, Categories. Shows Category, Product, Units, Cost.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Refusals, last 30 days

The refusals of the last month, the newest first, with what was asked for, why and who refused.

From Refusals, Products, Staff. Shows When, Number, Asked For, Reason, Approx Age, ID Shown, Refused By.
Calculated: Refused By is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Age checks by month

How many alcohol sales each month were to customers who looked over 25 and how many had their ID checked.

From Sales. Shows Month, Age Check, Sales.
Calculated: Month is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Age Check <> "Not needed"`.

#### Best sellers

What sold most in the last 30 days, with what it took.

From Sale Lines, Products, Sales. Shows Product, Sold, Takings.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Margin by category

For each category, the takings, the VAT within them, what the goods cost by batch and the margin left, the best earner first. Markdowns lower the margin; write-offs are counted in their own queries.

From Sale Lines, Products, Categories. Shows Category, Takings, VAT, Cost, Margin.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`; VAT is `Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) / (1 + [Sale Lines].[Tax Rate]), 2)`; Cost is `Round([Quantity] * [Sale Lines].[Unit Cost], 2)`; Margin is `Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) / (1 + [Sale Lines].[Tax Rate]), 2) - [Quantity] * [Sale Lines].[Unit Cost], 2)`.

#### Stock to reorder

Lines at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with the pack size they are ordered in.

From Products, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Code, Product, In Stock, Reorder Level, Pack Size.
Only where `Spare <= 0` and `Active = Yes`.

#### Stock by batch

Every batch with stock left, by category and product, earliest date first, with its value at cost.

From Batches, Products, Categories. Shows Category, Product, Batch Code, Received, Expiry Date, Remaining, Value at Cost.
Calculated: Value at Cost is `Round([Remaining] * [Batches].[Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Remaining > 0`.

#### Daily takings

Sales and takings on each of the last 30 days, the newest first.

From Sales. Shows Day, Sales, Takings.
Calculated: Day is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm-dd")`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Monthly takings

Sales and takings each month.

From Sales. Shows Month, Sales, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### VAT on sales by month

For each month, the takings, the part at 20%, the VAT within it and the part at 0%: the output VAT for the VAT return.

From Sales. Shows Month, Takings, At 20%, VAT, At 0%.
Calculated: Month is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm")`; At 0% is `Round([Total] - [Standard Rated], 2)`.

#### Deliveries to pay

Deliveries in whose supplier invoice is not yet paid, by supplier, with what each comes to before VAT.

From Purchase Orders, Suppliers, Purchase Lines. Shows Number, Supplier, Received On, Supplier Invoice, Owed.
Calculated: Owed is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Status = Received` and `Paid = No`.

#### Purchase orders open

Orders sent and not yet delivered, by the day they are expected.

From Purchase Orders, Suppliers. Shows Number, Supplier, Ordered On, Expected.
Only where `Status = Submitted`.

#### Receipt totals

Today's and yesterday's receipts with their total, VAT, standard-rated part and saving worked out from their lines. When you enter a sale by hand, read its figures here and type them into the sale.

From Sales, Sale Lines. Shows Receipt, When, Total, VAT, Standard Rated, Saved.
Calculated: Total is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`; VAT is `Round(Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) - Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2) / (1 + [Sale Lines].[Tax Rate]), 2)`; Standard Rated is `IIf([Sale Lines].[Tax Rate] > 0, Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2), 0)`; Saved is `Round(Round([Quantity] * [Full Price], 2) - Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 1`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Suppliers, Staff, Categories, Products, Purchase Orders, Purchase Lines, Batches, Sales, Sale Lines, Date Checks, Markdowns, Write-offs, Refusal Registers, Refusals. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Use first: dates in the next 7 days

The batches with a date in the next seven days, on a page for each category, to walk the shelves with each morning.

From the query Expiring in the next 7 days, a group for each Category: Product, Batch Code, Date Kind, Expiry Date, Days Left, Remaining, Marked Down To, with the total of Remaining.

#### Write-offs by month

Each month's write-offs by reason, with the units and their cost, and the totals.

From the query Written off by month, a group for each Month: Reason, Units, Cost, with the total of Units, total of Cost.

#### Margin by category

Takings, VAT, cost and margin by category, with totals.

From the query Margin by category: Category, Takings, VAT, Cost, Margin, with the total of Takings, total of VAT, total of Cost, total of Margin.

#### Stock to reorder

What is low, on a page for each supplier.

From the query Stock to reorder, a group for each Supplier: Code, Product, In Stock, Reorder Level, Pack Size.

#### Takings by month

Sales and takings month by month, with the totals.

From the query Monthly takings: Month, Sales, Takings, with the total of Sales, total of Takings.

#### Stock by batch

Every batch in stock by category, with its date and value at cost: the stock take sheet for a shop that sells by date.

From the query Stock by batch, a group for each Category: Product, Batch Code, Expiry Date, Remaining, Value at Cost, with the total of Value at Cost.

#### VAT on sales, by month

The VAT on sales month by month, for the accountant or the VAT return.

From the query VAT on sales by month: Month, Takings, At 20%, VAT, At 0%, with the total of Takings, total of VAT.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Till receipt

The receipt on an 80 mm till roll: the shop's name, address and VAT number, the receipt number, time and who served, each item with its price and VAT code, the total, the VAT included by rate, and the returns policy. What was saved shows only when something was, the cash tendered and change only for cash, and the age check and the ID seen only for a sale with alcohol. Print it from the Sales form for the sale on screen. One for each record of Sales, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Date and time, Served by, Paid by, Age check, ID seen
- Lines from Sale Lines: Item, Qty, Price, Amount, VAT
- Totals: Total, You saved, Cash tendered, Change, S: sales at 20% VAT, VAT at 20% included, Z: sales at 0% VAT
- Words: Mixed cases: 10% off six or more bottles of wine, and 10% off twelve or more beers and ciders. Reduced items are sold as seen. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Purchase order

The order sent to a supplier: the shop's account with them, the delivery day, each product with its code, unit, quantity and cost, the number of lines, the total before VAT, and the shop's rules for dates and batch codes on what arrives. It is for the orders still to come, Status Submitted; a received order prints when you choose it on the Purchase Orders form. One for each record of Purchase Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Purchase order {Number}
- Fields: To, Order number, For the attention of, Date, Address, Deliver on, City, Our account, Postcode, Ordered by
- Lines from Purchase Lines: Code, Product, Unit, Quantity, Unit Cost, Total
- Totals: Lines, Units, Total before VAT
- Words: Please deliver on the day above to {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}, and quote {Number} on your delivery note and invoice.
- Words: Every case and pack must carry its batch code and its use-by or best-before date. Chilled and deli lines must arrive with at least two thirds of their life left, or they will be refused at the door. All alcohol must be duty paid.

#### Markdown label sheet

The sheet from each morning's date check: what to reduce, with the label number, batch, date, the old and new price and how many labels to print, then what was taken off sale and what it cost, signed by whoever did the check. A day with nothing to reduce or nothing taken off says so, and leaves out the totals that do not apply. Print it from the Date Checks form for the day on screen. One for each record of Date Checks, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Date check {Number}
- Fields: Date, Checked by, Fridges
- Words: Reduce to clear: print a label for each, stick it over the shelf price on the pack, and put the packs at the front.
- Lines from Markdowns: Label, Product, Batch, Date kind, Date, Was, Now, Labels
- Words: Nothing to reduce today.
- Words: Taken off sale: past their date, broken or damaged. Put them in the waste bin, not back on the shelf.
- Lines from Write-offs: Product, Batch, Date, Reason, Units, Cost
- Words: Nothing taken off sale today.
- Totals: Labels to print, Units taken off sale, Cost written off
- Signed by: Checked by, Manager

#### Reduced label

The yellow-sticker label for one markdown, on a 58 mm label roll: the product, its date and batch, the old price and the reduced price, and the label number and the day it was reduced. Print it from the Markdowns form, once for each pack. One for each record of Markdowns, on receipt-58 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: REDUCED
- Fields: Product, Date kind, Date, Batch
- Totals: Was, Now
- Fields: Label, Reduced on

#### Refusals register

The month's refusals register, kept for the licensing authority: every refusal with its time, what was asked for, why, the ID shown and who refused, the number of refusals counted from them, and the review signature of the personal licence holder. A month not reviewed yet says so. Print it from the Refusal Registers form for the month on screen. One for each record of Refusal Registers, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Refusals register {Month}
- Fields: Month, Reviewed by, Reviewed on
- Words: The shop asks anyone who looks under 25 to show photo ID with a date of birth: a photo driving licence, a passport or a proof-of-age card. When none is shown, when the ID does not fit the person, when the drink seems to be bought for someone under 18, or when the customer is drunk, the sale is refused and written down here at the time.
- Lines from Refusals: No, Date and time, Asked for, Reason, Age (about), ID shown, What happened, Refused by
- Words: No sales were refused this month.
- Totals: Refusals this month
- Words: Not reviewed yet: the personal licence holder reviews and signs the register once the month is over.
- Words: Kept on the premises for the licensing authority, trading standards and the police to see on request.
- Signed by: Reviewed by the personal licence holder, Date

### Starting empty

Start with Business, the shop's name, address and VAT number and the returns policy in Document Footer, which the receipts print. Then Categories (with their VAT, age rule and case discount), Suppliers, Staff and Products with their date kind, prices, reorder levels and pack sizes. Enter what you hold now as one batch per product with its date, and set In Stock to match. Purchase orders, batches, sales, date checks and refusals come in as you trade; add a Refusal Registers record at the start of each month.

### Making it yours

- Sell cheese and meat by weight: add a Weight field to Sale Lines in kilograms, make the price per kilogram, and change the line amount to Round([Weight] * [Unit Price], 2).
- Keep a wine list for the trade: add a Customers table for restaurants and offices, an Invoices table pointing at it, and a print template that invoices them monthly.
- Record temperatures properly: add a Temperature Readings table (date, time, fridge, reading, staff) in place of the text on Date Checks, and a query for readings above 5 degrees.
- Run a loyalty or wine club: add a Members table, point Sales at it, and give members their own case discount in a calculated column.
- Track supplier credits for what arrives short-dated: add a Credits table pointing at Batches, with the units refused and the credit note number.
- Sell tobacco or other age-restricted goods: add a category with Age Restricted ticked; the age check and the refusals register work for it as they do for alcohol.
- Order to a plan: add a Par Level field to Products for each weekday and make Stock to reorder compare In Stock with it.

### Questions people ask

**How do I see what is going out of date?**

Run the query Expiring in the next 7 days, or print the report Date check list, which puts it on a page for each category. Days Left 0 means the date is today.

**Why does the till sell a reduced pack before a full-price one?**

It sells the batch with the earliest date first, which is the one most likely to have been reduced. On the shelf, reduced packs go at the front for the same reason.

**How much do we throw away?**

Open the report Write-offs by month for units and cost each month by reason. Set it against the takings in Takings by month: a few percent of the takings of a deli counter is usual. The query Write-offs by product shows which lines to order less of.

**What do I need to show the licensing officer?**

Print the print template Refusals register for each month asked about, signed by the personal licence holder, and the Staff table with each person's Age Check Training date.

**How does the mixed-case discount work?**

Each category has a Case Quantity and a Case Discount. When a sale has that many units of the category, its lines at the shelf price get the discount: ten percent off six bottles of wine, or twelve beers and ciders. It is not given on top of a reduced price.

**Why does a batch of wine have no expiry date?**

Wine and spirits do not go off on a shelf, so their Date Kind is None and their batches carry only a batch code, for tracing a bad case back to its delivery.

**A supplier has recalled a batch. How do I find it?**

Open the Batches form and find the Batch Code. Its Sale Lines show every sale it went into, and the query Stock by batch shows how many are still on the shelf to take off sale.

## Little Fig Cafe

**Cafe or restaurant.** Menu, recipes and food costs, till orders, rota, deliveries, waste and the nightly cash-up for a small cafe.

For the owner or manager of a small cafe who wants to see what each dish costs to make, what sells and when, whether the wages are in hand against the takings, what to order from each supplier and what is being thrown away.

Little Fig Cafe is an invented all-day cafe with about thirty seats and a takeaway counter. It opens every day but Christmas Day, from half past seven (half past eight at weekends) until half past four. Breakfast is served until half past eleven and lunch until half past three; coffee, cold drinks and cakes all day. Its head baker makes the cakes on site each morning. Eight people work there, and six invented suppliers deliver coffee, dairy, produce, meat and fish, bread and dry goods, each on its own days.

The records cover the last fourteen months: a cash-up sheet for every day the cafe opened, the rota as it was worked, every delivery and its bill, and what was thrown away. The till's orders are here line by line for the last eight weeks, about six thousand of them; older days are in their cash-up sheets. Trade is busier at weekends, in July and August and on sunny days, and quieter in January. The rota runs two weeks ahead. The records stop at the start of today: this morning's deliveries are not booked in yet and this morning's orders to suppliers are not placed, so the order list shows what to ask for.

Every dish has a recipe in its ingredients' own units, so its food cost comes from the ingredients' current prices. Prices are pounds, as a cafe in the UK would charge them, but nothing in the design depends on the currency.

The menu prices include VAT, as a cafe's prices to the public do. The sample keeps the VAT simple and says so: everything eaten in, every drink and any hot food taken away carries the standard rate of 20%, and cold food taken away (the cakes and bakes, the cold bagel and rolls) carries none. The real rules have more cases than that, such as hot food kept warm, cold drinks and snacks, so set each dish's Takeaway VAT Rate to what applies to you. Each line of a bill keeps the rate it was sold at, each bill keeps its VAT, and each day's cash-up keeps the day's VAT for the return.

It prints three documents: a till receipt for every bill that was not voided, numbered RCP-2026-00042, with its items under each VAT rate; a purchase order for each order to a supplier not yet delivered, numbered PO-2026-0042, made each morning from the order list; and a weekly payslip for each person, numbered PAY-2026-0042, from the shifts on the rota. The payslip shows hours, rate and gross pay only: tax, National Insurance, pension and other deductions are left for the payroll to work out.

It suits, with small changes: A coffee shop or kiosk; A small restaurant or bistro; A bakery with a few tables; A food truck or market stall; A sandwich bar or takeaway; A tea room or farm shop cafe.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- The till's bills, Orders and Order Lines, go back eight weeks; the Cash Ups go back the whole fourteen months and are where the weekly and monthly figures come from. If your till keeps its own records you can skip Orders and keep only the cash-ups.
- Nothing here takes sales off the stock by itself. In Stock is what the last count, the deliveries and the waste sheet say, so count the stock now and then and correct it.
- A bill's Total, Net and Tax, and a payslip's Hours and Gross Pay, are stored figures, typed when the record is made, not added up from the lines by the form. The sample's own are exactly the sums of their lines, rounded line by line as a till rounds them.
- The VAT is kept simple: 20% on everything eaten in, on drinks and on hot food taken away; nought on cold food taken away. Set each dish's Takeaway VAT Rate to what the rules say for you, and have your VAT checked by an accountant.
- Each print template prints the records it is for: Receipt the bills not voided, Purchase order the purchases not delivered yet, Payslip every payslip. Choose some to print fewer; a voided bill or a delivered purchase prints when you choose it.
- The records stop at the start of today: this morning's deliveries are not booked in and this morning's orders not yet placed, so the order list shows what to ask for today. The rota runs two weeks ahead, and the week now running has no payslips yet.
- The VAT number, company number and bank details on the Business record are placeholders of noughts and Xs. Put in your own before printing anything for real.

### Tutorial

#### Ring up a bill and print the receipt

1. Open the Orders form and press New. Type the next receipt number in Number, one on from the last (RCP-2026-00042 after RCP-2026-00041), and the date and time in When.
2. Set Service to Dine in or Takeaway. For a table, type the Table No and the Covers; for a takeaway leave Table No empty and Covers at nought. Choose who took it in Staff and how it was paid in Payment.
3. In the Order Lines below, choose each dish in Menu Item, type the Quantity and its menu price in Unit Price. Set Tax Rate to 0.2 eaten in, or the dish's Takeaway VAT Rate (on the Menu Items form) when it is taken away.
4. Type the bill's Total, the VAT within it in Tax and the rest in Net. A form does not add the lines up by itself, so check the Total against the lines.
5. Open the print template Receipt from Print templates, choose the bill, and press Print. The receipt prints the stored Total, Net and VAT under the lines.

#### Order from the suppliers in the morning

1. Run the query Ingredients to order, or print the report Order list for suppliers: what is at or below its reorder level with nothing on order, a section for each supplier with its delivery days and the usual amount.
2. For each supplier on the list, open the Purchases form and press New. Type the next number in Number (PO-2026-0042), choose the Supplier, type today in Ordered On and the next delivery day in Due On.
3. In the Purchase Lines below, choose each Ingredient and type the Quantity in its unit and the Unit Cost from the last bill.
4. Open the Ingredients form and type the same amount in On Order for each ingredient ordered, so it leaves the order list.
5. Open the print template Purchase order from Print templates: it shows the purchases not yet delivered, which are this morning's. Print them or press Save as PDF and e-mail each to the address on its Suppliers record.

#### Book in a delivery and pay the bill

1. When the delivery comes, open the Purchases form, find it by its Number (the query Deliveries due lists the ones expected), and type today in Received On and the supplier's bill number in Invoice Number.
2. Check the goods against the printed purchase order and sign it. Open the Ingredients form and add what came to In Stock for each line, and set its On Order back to nought.
3. Each week, run the query Bills to pay or print the report Bills to pay: the bills not yet paid, with the days left to pay; below nought is overdue.
4. When you pay one, type the day in Paid On on the Purchases form, and it leaves the list.

#### Plan the rota and pay the week

1. Open the Shifts form and press New for each shift in the coming weeks: choose the Staff, type Start and End, the Break Minutes, the Paid Hours (end less start less the break) and the Station, and leave Status at Rota. Print the report Rota to pin up.
2. After each day, change each shift's Status to Worked, Holiday or Sick, and its End if someone stayed on. A sick day has Paid Hours of nought.
3. When the week is over (Monday to Sunday), run the query Hours and wages by staff, last 28 days to see the hours. Open the Payslips form and press New for each person: the next Number (PAY-2026-0042), the Staff, the Week Beginning and Week Ending, the Pay Date, their Hourly Rate, and the week's Hours and Gross Pay.
4. Open the Shifts form as a datasheet and set Payslip to the new payslip on each of that person's shifts in the week: they are the payslip's lines.
5. Open the print template Payslip from Print templates, choose the week's payslips, and print them. Give them out with the payroll's statement of net pay, which has the tax and deductions.

#### Cash up at close

1. Take the till's end of day reading. Open the Cash Ups form and press New: the Date, who closed in Closed By, the Weather, the Orders and Covers, Card Takings, Cash Takings and the VAT from the reading.
2. Count the cash in the drawer less the float and type it in Cash Counted. Type the day's Wage Cost from the rota, and anything worth remembering in Notes.
3. Run the query Cash over or short now and then: the days the cash counted did not match the reading.
4. On Monday, print the report Weekly takings and wages to see last week's takings against the wages.

#### Cost the menu when a price goes up

1. When a supplier's bill shows a new price, open the Ingredients form and change Cost per Unit. Every dish that uses it costs more at once.
2. Print the report Menu costing sheet: each dish's price, food cost and margin by section. Most cafes aim to keep the food cost under about 30% of the price.
3. To change a price, open the Menu Items form and change Price. Old bills keep the price they were sold at, so past takings do not change.
4. For a new dish, press New on the Menu Items form, then add its Recipe Lines from Line 1, one ingredient each. Print the report Recipe cards for the kitchen.

#### Close the month

1. Print the report Monthly takings: each month's takings, the VAT within them, the takings less VAT and the wages. Add the VAT of the three months of your VAT quarter for the return.
2. Count the stock in each store, put the counts in In Stock on the Ingredients form, and run the query Stock value by storage for the accounts.
3. Print the report Waste report for the kitchen meeting, and run Waste by ingredient, last 90 days to see what to order less of.
4. Run Spend by supplier by month to see what each supplier was paid.
