### Queries

#### Menu costing

Each dish on the menu with its price, food cost, food cost as a share of the price, and the gross profit and margin left over. Use it when setting prices or when a supplier puts a price up: most cafes aim for a food cost under about 30% of the price.

From Menu Items, Menu Categories, Recipe Lines, Ingredients. Shows Category, Menu Item, Price, Food Cost, Food Cost %, Gross Profit, Gross Margin %.
Calculated: Food Cost is `Round([Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`; Food Cost % is `Round(100 * [Quantity] * [Cost per Unit] / [Price], 2)`; Gross Profit is `Round(IIf([Line] = 1, [Price], 0) - Round([Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2), 2)`; Gross Margin % is `Round(IIf([Line] = 1, 100, 0) - 100 * [Quantity] * [Cost per Unit] / [Price], 2)`.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

#### Recipe card

Every line of every recipe with what it costs, for checking a recipe or showing a new cook how a dish is made up.

From Recipe Lines, Menu Items, Ingredients. Shows Menu Item, Line, Ingredient, Quantity, Unit, Cost per Unit, Line Cost.
Calculated: Line Cost is `Round([Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

#### Menu

The dishes on the menu now, by section, with their diet marks and prices.

From Menu Items, Menu Categories. Shows Category, Served, Menu Item, Diet, Takeaway, Price.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

#### Best sellers, last 30 days

How many of each dish sold in the last 30 days and what they took, most sold first. Use it to plan the bake and the prep, and to spot dishes worth dropping.

From Order Lines, Orders, Menu Items, Menu Categories. Shows Menu Item, Category, Sold, Takings.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30` and `Voided = No`.

#### Sales by hour

Bills, takings and the average bill for each hour of the day over the last eight weeks: when the rush comes and when the cafe is quiet, for setting shift times.

From Orders. Shows Hour, Orders, Takings, Average Spend.
Calculated: Hour is `Mid([When], 12, 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 1 And 56` and `Voided = No`.

#### Sales by day of the week

Bills, covers, takings and the average bill for each day of the week over the last eight weeks, for planning who works when.

From Orders. Shows Day, Orders, Covers, Takings, Average Spend.
Calculated: Day is `IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [When]) Mod 7 = 0, "Monday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [When]) Mod 7 = 1, "Tuesday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [When]) Mod 7 = 2, "Wednesday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [When]) Mod 7 = 3, "Thursday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [When]) Mod 7 = 4, "Friday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [When]) Mod 7 = 5, "Saturday", "Sunday"))))))`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 1 And 56` and `Voided = No`.

#### Average spend by service

For the last 30 days, how many bills were eaten in and how many taken away, what each brought in and the average bill for each.

From Orders. Shows Service, Orders, Covers, Takings, Average Spend.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30` and `Voided = No`.

#### Takings and wages by week

Each week's takings from the cash-up sheets against the wages on the rota, what was left after wages, and the average day's wages as a share of its takings. The week starts on Monday; the newest week comes first.

From Cash Ups. Shows Week Beginning, Days Open, Orders, Covers, Takings, Wages, Left After Wages, Average Day Wage %.
Calculated: Takings is `[Card Takings] + [Cash Takings]`; Left After Wages is `Round([Card Takings] + [Cash Takings] - [Wage Cost], 2)`; Average Day Wage % is `Round(100 * [Wage Cost] / ([Card Takings] + [Cash Takings]), 1)`.

#### Takings by month

Takings, the VAT within them and the takings less VAT, and wages, for each month, oldest first: to see the seasons, compare with the same month last year, and fill in the VAT return.

From Cash Ups. Shows Month, Days Open, Orders, Takings, VAT, Takings less VAT, Wages, Left After Wages.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Takings is `[Card Takings] + [Cash Takings]`; Takings less VAT is `Round([Card Takings] + [Cash Takings] - [VAT], 2)`; Left After Wages is `Round([Card Takings] + [Cash Takings] - [Wage Cost], 2)`.

#### Takings by weather

The average day's takings and covers in the warmer months (May to September) by the weather noted on the cash-up sheet.

From Cash Ups. Shows Weather, Days, Average Takings, Average Covers.
Calculated: Average Takings is `[Card Takings] + [Cash Takings]`.
Only where `Month In ("05", "06", "07", "08", "09")`.

#### Cash over or short

The days the cash counted at close did not match the till's cash reading, and by how much, with who closed up.

From Cash Ups, Staff. Shows Date, Closed By, Cash Takings, Cash Counted, Over or Short, Notes.
Calculated: Closed By is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Over or Short is `Round([Cash Counted] - [Cash Takings], 2)`.
Only where `Over or Short <> 0`.

#### Hours and wages by staff, last 28 days

Each person's shifts, hours and wages over the last four weeks, with holiday paid in and sick days left out. Use it for the payroll and to keep hours fair.

From Shifts, Staff. Shows Name, Role, Hourly Rate, Shifts, Hours, Wages.
Calculated: Name is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Wages is `Round([Paid Hours] * [Hourly Rate], 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 1 And 28` and `Status In ("Worked", "Holiday")`.

#### Rota for the next 7 days

Who is on, when and where, today and for the next six days, earliest first.

From Shifts, Staff. Shows Day, From, To, Name, Station, Paid Hours, Status.
Calculated: Day is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; From is `Mid([Start], 12, 5)`; To is `Mid([End], 12, 5)`; Name is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 6`.

#### Ingredients to order

Ingredients at or below their reorder level with nothing on order, by supplier, with the usual amount to order and what it will cost. Work through it each morning before phoning the orders in.

From Ingredients, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Delivers On, Ingredient, Unit, In Stock, On Order, Reorder Level, Order, Bought As, Estimated Cost.
Calculated: Estimated Cost is `Round([Reorder Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`.
Only where `Above Reorder Level <= 0`.

#### Deliveries due

Orders placed with suppliers and not yet delivered, the earliest due first, with how many lines and their value.

From Purchases, Suppliers, Purchase Lines. Shows Purchase, Supplier, Ordered On, Due On, Lines, Value.
Calculated: Value is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Received On Is Null`.

#### Bills to pay

Delivered orders whose bills are not yet paid, with the days left until each is due; below nought means it is overdue.

From Purchases, Suppliers, Purchase Lines. Shows Purchase, Supplier, Invoice Number, Received On, Days to Pay, Amount.
Calculated: Days to Pay is `[Payment Days] - DateDiff("d", [Received On], Date())`; Amount is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Received On Is Not Null` and `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Spend by supplier by month

What was spent with each supplier each month, from the delivered orders.

From Purchases, Suppliers, Purchase Lines. Shows Month, Supplier, Deliveries, Spent.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Received On], "yyyy-mm")`; Spent is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Received On Is Not Null`.

#### Waste by ingredient, last 90 days

For each ingredient thrown away in the last 90 days, how often, how much and what it cost, the dearest first. Use it to order less of what goes off.

From Waste, Ingredients. Shows Ingredient, Unit, Times, Wasted, Cost.
Calculated: Cost is `Round([Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Waste in the last 30 days

Each entry on the waste sheet in the last 30 days with its cost and who recorded it.

From Waste, Ingredients, Staff. Shows Date, Reason, Ingredient, Quantity, Unit, Cost, Recorded By.
Calculated: Cost is `Round([Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`; Recorded By is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Stock value by storage

What the stock in each store is worth at today's cost, for the month end stock count and the accounts.

From Ingredients. Shows Storage, Ingredients, Value at Cost.
Calculated: Value at Cost is `Round([In Stock] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Menu Categories, Menu Items, Suppliers, Ingredients, Recipe Lines, Staff, Payslips, Shifts, Orders, Order Lines, Purchases, Purchase Lines, Waste, Cash Ups. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Menu costing sheet

Every dish on the menu by section with its price, food cost, food cost percentage, gross profit and margin, and the average for each section. For the owner when pricing the menu.

From the query Menu costing, a group for each Category: Menu Item, Price, Food Cost, Food Cost %, Gross Profit, Gross Margin %, with the average of Food Cost %, average of Gross Profit.

#### Recipe cards

A card for each dish listing its ingredients, the quantity of each and its cost, with the dish's total food cost. For the kitchen wall and for training.

From the query Recipe card, a group for each Menu Item: Line, Ingredient, Quantity, Unit, Line Cost, with the total of Line Cost.

#### Menu

The menu by section with prices and diet marks, ready to check against the printed menu.

From the query Menu, a group for each Category: Menu Item, Diet, Price.

#### Weekly takings and wages

One line a week: days open, bills, covers, takings, wages, what was left after wages and the wage share, with the totals. For the owner's weekly look at the business.

From the query Takings and wages by week: Week Beginning, Days Open, Orders, Covers, Takings, Wages, Left After Wages, Average Day Wage %, with the total of Takings, total of Wages, total of Left After Wages.

#### Monthly takings

Takings, VAT, takings less VAT and wages month by month with the totals, for the accountant, the VAT return or the bank.

From the query Takings by month: Month, Days Open, Orders, Takings, VAT, Takings less VAT, Wages, Left After Wages, with the total of Takings, total of VAT, total of Takings less VAT, total of Wages, total of Left After Wages.

#### Rota for the next 7 days

The coming week's shifts, a section for each day with its total hours, to pin up in the back.

From the query Rota for the next 7 days, a group for each Day: From, To, Name, Station, Paid Hours, Status, with the total of Paid Hours.

#### Order list for suppliers

What to order today, a section for each supplier with its delivery days, the quantities and the estimated cost. For whoever phones the orders in.

From the query Ingredients to order, a group for each Supplier: Ingredient, Unit, In Stock, On Order, Reorder Level, Order, Bought As, Estimated Cost, with the total of Estimated Cost.

#### Waste report

The last 30 days of waste grouped by reason, with the cost of each and in all. For the weekly kitchen meeting.

From the query Waste in the last 30 days, a group for each Reason: Date, Ingredient, Quantity, Unit, Cost, Recorded By, with the total of Cost.

#### Bills to pay

Unpaid supplier bills grouped by supplier, with their invoice numbers, the days left to pay and the total owed to each.

From the query Bills to pay, a group for each Supplier: Purchase, Invoice Number, Received On, Days to Pay, Amount, with the total of Amount.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Receipt

The till receipt for a bill, on an 80 mm roll: the cafe's name, address and VAT number, the receipt number, time, eat in or take away and the table, the items under each VAT rate with what that rate comes to and the VAT within it, then the total, the net and the VAT within it, and how it was paid. The table and covers show only for a table's bill. Numbered RCP-2026-00042. It is for the bills that were not voided; a voided bill chosen on the Orders form still prints, marked void. One for each record of Orders, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Date and time, Service, Table, Covers, Paid by
- Lines from Order Lines: Qty, Item, Each, Price, Rate, VAT
- Totals: Total, Net of VAT, VAT included
- Words: Void: this bill was cancelled before it was paid and is not a receipt.
- Words: You were served by {Staff.First Name}. Please keep this receipt as your proof of purchase.
- Words: VAT number {Business.Tax Number}. {Business.Document Footer}

#### Purchase order

The order sent to a supplier each morning from the order list: what to send, how much, at the last price paid, and the day to deliver, with the cafe's address to deliver to. Numbered PO-2026-0042, which the supplier quotes on the delivery note and the bill. It is for the purchases not delivered yet (no Received On), which are the ones placed this morning; a delivered one prints when you choose it on the Purchases form. One for each record of Purchases, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Purchase order {Number}
- Fields: To, Order number, Address, Order date, City, Deliver on, Postcode, For the attention of
- Lines from Purchase Lines: Ingredient, Comes as, Quantity, Unit, Price per unit, Amount
- Totals: Lines, Order total
- Words: Please deliver to {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} on the day above, before 7 in the morning if you can. Quote {Number} on your delivery note and your invoice. Prices are those we last paid; tell us before delivery if any has changed.
- Words: Questions about this order: {Business.Phone} or {Business.E-mail}.
- Signed by: Ordered by, Received by

#### Payslip

The weekly payslip for one person: the week, the hourly rate, each shift worked or on holiday with its day, times, hours and pay at that rate, the number of shifts, and the gross pay. Numbered PAY-2026-0042. It shows gross pay only; tax, National Insurance, pension and other deductions are for the payroll to work out, and its statement of net pay goes with this one. One for each record of Payslips, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Payslip {Number}
- Fields: Employee, Week beginning, Role, Week ending, Hourly rate, Paid on
- Lines from Shifts: Date, Day, From, To, Break (min), Station, Status, Hours, Pay
- Totals: Shifts, Hours paid, Gross pay
- Words: Gross pay for the hours on the rota, holiday included at the usual rate and sick days unpaid here. Tax, National Insurance, pension and any other deductions are worked out by the payroll and shown on the payroll's own statement of net pay.

### Starting empty

Start with Business: your own name, address, VAT number and the footer your receipts carry. Then Suppliers, then Ingredients with each one's unit, cost per unit, supplier and reorder level. Then Menu Categories, then Menu Items, then the Recipe Lines for each dish, numbering each recipe's lines from 1; Menu costing works as soon as a dish has its recipe. Add your Staff and plan the Shifts for the coming week. From then on, day to day: a Purchase and its lines when you order from a supplier, its Received On when it arrives and its Paid On when the bill is paid; the Waste sheet as things are thrown away; and a Cash Up at each close. If your till keeps its own records, the Cash Ups alone give the weekly and monthly figures; enter Orders and Order Lines only if you want best sellers and the busy hours here too. Keep In Stock up to date from a stock count, as Data Files does not take sales off it by itself.

### Making it yours

- Measure the food cost against what the cafe keeps rather than what the customer pays: in a copy of Menu costing, divide by [Price] / 1.2 in place of [Price], so the VAT within the price is left out.
- Add a Packaging Cost field to Menu Items for the cup, lid or box a takeaway goes out in, and add it to the food cost in a copy of Menu costing to see what a takeaway really costs.
- Add yes/no allergen fields to Ingredients (gluten, milk, eggs, nuts and the rest) and a query that lists the dishes using any ingredient marked Yes, for the allergen folder.
- A bakery can add a Bakes table (date, dish, made, left over at close) to see how much of each cake to make on each day of the week.
- A food truck can drop Table No and Covers and add a Pitch field to Cash Ups, then group the takings by pitch to see which places pay.
- A restaurant can add a Bookings table (date, time, covers, name, phone, table) and a query for the bookings in the next 7 days.
- Add a Running Costs table (date, kind, amount) for rent, power and card fees, and a query by month beside Takings by month to see the profit.
- Add a Tips field to Cash Ups and a column summing it in Takings and wages by week, so tips are kept apart from the takings.

### Questions people ask

**How do I reprint a customer's receipt from last week?**

Find the bill on the Orders form by its time in When or its Number, then open the print template Receipt, choose that bill and press Print. Bills older than eight weeks are not in the sample; in your own file every bill you keep can be reprinted.

**Why does a carrot cake have VAT eaten in but none taken away?**

In the UK, food eaten on the premises carries the standard rate, while cold food taken away is zero-rated. Each line of a bill keeps the rate it was sold at in Tax Rate, from the dish's Takeaway VAT Rate when it went out the door. The real rules have more cases; the sample keeps to these two.

**Where are tax and National Insurance on the payslip?**

They are not worked out here. The payslip shows the hours from the rota, the rate and the gross pay; the payroll works out tax, National Insurance and pension from the gross pay and gives its own statement of net pay. You can add a Payslip Deductions table pointing at Payslips if you want them here.

**I placed an order but the ingredient is still on Ingredients to order. Why?**

The list leaves out what has something On Order. Type the amount ordered in On Order on the Ingredients form, and set it back to nought when the delivery is booked in.

**If I put a price up, do last month's takings change?**

No. Each bill line keeps its own Unit Price, so old bills and their totals stay as they were. Menu costing uses today's price and today's ingredient costs.

**How do I find the VAT for my quarter's return?**

Print the report Monthly takings and add up the VAT column for the three months of the quarter. It comes from the VAT on each day's cash-up, which is the till's reading.

**Can I start with my own menu and keep the design?**

Yes. Make the sample empty, fill in Business with your own details, then follow the order under starting empty: suppliers and ingredients first, then the menu and its recipes, then your staff.

## Saffron Lane Pizza and Curry

**Takeaway.** Phone, walk-in and online orders, delivery zones and drivers, the menu with sizes, extras and meal deals, and the night's takings for a takeaway.

For the owner of a takeaway who wants to see tonight's orders as they come in, how long deliveries take in each zone, which channel brings the money, what sells, what each driver is owed, which regulars have gone quiet, and how much of each ingredient the kitchen gets through.

Saffron Lane Pizza and Curry is an invented takeaway in south London. It cooks pizzas in three sizes, burgers and curries, with rice, breads, sides, desserts and drinks, and four meal deals. Customers order by phone, at the counter or on its own website, and either collect or have it delivered by one of its five drivers, who use their own cars and are paid a fee for each drop. Three delivery zones each have a delivery charge, a minimum order, a target time and the driver's fee for a drop there. It opens every evening from five until eleven, and from twelve until half past two on Saturday and Sunday.

The records cover the last fourteen months: a night sheet for every night with the takings by channel, the VAT, the kitchen's wages and the drivers' pay. The orders themselves are kept line by line for the last twelve weeks, about four thousand of them, with a pay sheet for each driver for each finished week in that time. Friday and Saturday nights are about twice as busy as the rest; wet and cold nights and the winter months are busier, the summer quieter. Some customers have stopped ordering, and a few orders are booked ahead for tonight and the next two nights.

Prices include VAT, as a takeaway's prices to the public do. Hot food, drinks, ice cream and the delivery charge carry the standard rate of 20%; the cold desserts and the coleslaw, sold cold, carry none. The real rules have more cases than that, so set each dish's VAT Rate to what applies to you. The documents are a customer receipt, a kitchen ticket and a delivery slip for every order, numbered ORD-2026-00042, and a weekly pay sheet for each driver, numbered DRV-2026-0042.

It suits, with small changes: A pizza shop or kebab house; A fish and chip shop that delivers; A Chinese or Indian takeaway; A burger or chicken shop; A cafe or restaurant with its own delivery; A bakery or caterer taking orders for collection.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- The orders are kept line by line for the last twelve weeks; the night sheets go back fourteen months and are where the monthly figures come from. The driver pay sheets cover the finished weeks of those twenty.
- Goods, Total, Tax and Net on an order, and Drops and Drop Pay on a pay sheet, are stored figures typed when the record is made, not added up by the form. The sample's own are exactly the sums of their lines.
- A meal deal is a line at the deal's price followed by each thing chosen at nought, so best sellers count the pizzas and curries in deals as sold, and the money stays with the deal.
- Recipes are written for one item, and for the smallest pizza; the Portion on each order line scales them for the size. Extras have recipes of their own. Ingredient use is worked out from these, not counted, so check it against a stock count now and then.
- The three order templates leave cancelled orders out, and the Delivery slip prints for deliveries only. Choose the orders you mean before pressing Print; an order chosen on the Orders form always prints, a cancelled one marked as cancelled.
- Time is kept to the minute in Placed, Due, Ready, Out and Handed Over, and the delivery times are worked out from them. Leave Handed Over empty until the customer has the food.
- The VAT is kept simple: 20% on hot food, drinks, ice cream and delivery, nought on the cold desserts and coleslaw. Have yours checked by an accountant for your own country.
- A few orders are booked ahead for tonight and the next two nights, so Tonight's orders and Orders still to go out have something on them whenever the sample is made. Orders taken today before the time it was made are there too, with their status at that time.

### Tutorial

#### Take a phone order and send it to the kitchen

1. Open the Customers form and find the caller by Phone or name. For someone new, press New and type their name, Phone, Address, Postcode and any Delivery Notes, and choose their Zone from the postcode district (the Delivery Zones form lists the districts in Areas).
2. Open the Orders form and press New. Type the next order number in Number, one on from the last (ORD-2026-00042 after ORD-2026-00041), the time now in Placed, Phone in Channel, and Collection or Delivery in Method. Choose the Customer.
3. For a delivery, choose the Zone, copy the Address, Postcode and Delivery Notes, and type the Due time: now plus the zone's Target Minutes. For a collection, Due is about 20 minutes away.
4. In the Order Lines below, add each item in order with its Line number: the Menu Item, the Size for a pizza (and its Portion from the Sizes form), the Quantity, the Unit Price with the size added, and any Notes. Put an extra on its own line under the dish it goes on. For a meal deal, add the deal at its price, then each thing chosen at nought with the deal's name in Notes.
5. Type Goods (the lines added up), the Delivery Charge from the zone (nought if Goods is over its Free Over), Total, and the VAT in Tax and the rest in Net. Set Payment, tick Paid for a card payment taken now, and set Status to Cooking.
6. Open the print template Kitchen ticket from Print templates, choose the order, and press Print for the kitchen. For a delivery, print the Delivery slip too; print the Customer receipt to go in the bag.

#### Take a walk-in order at the counter

1. Open the Orders form and press New: the next Number, the time in Placed, Walk-in in Channel and Collection in Method. Leave Customer empty unless they are a regular who gives their name.
2. Add the Order Lines as for a phone order, type Goods and Total (no delivery charge), Tax and Net, and set Payment to Card or Cash with Paid ticked.
3. Print the Kitchen ticket for the kitchen and the Customer receipt for the customer.
4. When it comes off the pass, type the time in Ready and Handed Over and set Status to Done.

#### Run the evening: what is due and who takes it

1. Keep the query Tonight's orders open, or print the report Tonight: every order due tonight, earliest first.
2. Run Orders still to go out every so often: the minutes left on each order, below nought when it is late. The query Tonight by the hour shows what is due in the next hour.
3. When an order comes off the pass, type Ready. When a driver takes it, choose the Driver, type Out, set Status to Out, and type the zone's Drop Fee.
4. When the driver is back, type Handed Over, set Status to Done, and tick Paid for a cash order once the cash is handed in.

#### Cash up at close

1. Open the Nights form and press New. Type the Date, the Weather, and from the till and the website the Orders, Deliveries, Collections, Phone Takings, Walk-in Takings, Online Takings, Delivery Charges and VAT.
2. Count the cash from the till and the drivers and type Card, Cash and Online Payments. They should add up to the three takings.
3. Type the Kitchen Wages from the rota and the Driver Pay: the night's drop fees, from the Drop Fee of the night's delivered orders. Note anything that went wrong in Notes.
4. On Monday, run Busy nights, last 12 weeks and Takings by channel, last 28 days to see how the week went.

#### Pay the drivers for the week

1. When the week is over (Monday to Sunday), run the query Drops by driver, last 28 days, or print the report Driver drops, to check each driver's drops and cash.
2. Open the Driver Pay form and press New for each driver: the next Number (DRV-2026-0042), the Driver, the Week Beginning and Week Ending, the Pay Date, and their Drops and Drop Pay for the week.
3. Open the Orders form as a datasheet and set Driver Pay to the new sheet on each order the driver delivered that week: they are the sheet's lines.
4. Open the print template Driver pay sheet from Print templates, choose the week's sheets, and print them for the drivers to sign. The query Driver pay by week lists the last eight weeks.

#### Win back customers who have gone quiet

1. Run the query Customers not ordered for 60 days, or print the report Come-back list: customers who agreed to offers and have not ordered for two months, the biggest spenders first.
2. Send each a come-back offer by text or e-mail from their Phone or E-mail on the Customers form.
3. If someone asks not to be sent offers again, untick Offers on their Customers record and they leave the list.

#### Check the menu, the costs and the ingredients each week

1. Print the report Ingredient use: what the last seven nights used of each ingredient, by supplier, to check the week's orders to suppliers against it.
2. When a supplier puts a price up, change Cost per Unit on the Ingredients form, then print the Menu costing sheet to see each item's food cost against its price less VAT.
3. To change a price, open the Menu Items form and change Price; old orders keep the price they were charged. Print the Price list to check the website and the printed menu.
4. Run Best sellers, last 28 days and Pizza sizes sold, last 28 days to see what to make more of and what to drop.

#### Close the month

1. Print the report Monthly takings: the takings by channel, the VAT within them, the kitchen's wages and the drivers' pay, month by month.
2. Add up the VAT of the three months of your VAT quarter for the return.
3. Print the report Delivery times to see whether the zones are keeping to their targets, and change a zone's Target Minutes or its Charge on the Delivery Zones form if they are not.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 36 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The name printed at the top of every document. |
| Address | Short text | The street address. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country. |
| Phone | Short text | The phone number customers call. |
| E-mail | Short text | The address customers write to. |
| Website | Short text | The website, if there is one. |
| Tax Number | Short text | The VAT or sales tax registration number, printed on invoices. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Company Number | Short text | The registered company number, where the business is a company. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Bank Details | Short text | Where customers pay by transfer: the bank, account name and number. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Payment Terms | Short text | The words printed under an invoice's total, such as "Payment within 30 days". |
| Tax Rate | Number | The usual rate of VAT or sales tax as a fraction: 0.2 is twenty percent. Lines may carry a rate of their own. |
| Currency | Short text | The currency the business trades in, as its three-letter code. |
| Document Footer | Long text | A line or two at the foot of every document: thanks, opening hours, returns policy. |

The areas the takeaway delivers to, each with its charges and the driver's fee for a drop there. Enter these first. The sample has 3 records.

| Menu Item | Points at Menu Items, required | What it is. |
| Size | Points at Sizes | The size of a pizza; empty for anything else. |
| Portion | Number | How much of the recipe it takes, from its size: 1 for anything not sized. |
| Quantity | Whole number | How many. |
| Unit Price | Currency | The price of one, size included and VAT included, as it was charged. Nought for what is part of a deal. |
| Tax Rate | Number | The VAT rate within the price, from the item when it was sold. |
| Notes | Short text | What the kitchen needs to know: extra hot, no onions, well done, or which deal it is part of. |

#### Nights

The sheet filled in at close each night: the takings by channel and by how they were paid, the VAT, and the night's wages and drivers' pay. The sample has 425 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Date | Date, required, unique | The night. One sheet per night. |
| Weather | Short text | Dry, Rain or Cold: wet and cold nights are busier. |
| Orders | Whole number | How many orders went out, cancelled ones left out. |
| Deliveries | Whole number | How many of them were delivered. |
| Collections | Whole number | How many were collected. |
| Phone Takings | Currency | Taken on phone orders, delivery charges included. |
| Walk-in Takings | Currency | Taken at the counter from people who walked in. |
| Online Takings | Currency | Taken on the website. |
| Delivery Charges | Currency | The delivery charges within those takings. |
| VAT | Currency | The VAT within the night's takings, for the VAT return. |
| Card | Currency | Paid by card, at the counter or over the phone. |
| Cash | Currency | Paid in cash, at the counter or to the drivers. |
| Online Payments | Currency | Paid on the website. |
| Kitchen Wages | Currency | What the night's kitchen and counter shifts cost, from the rota. |
| Driver Pay | Currency | The drop fees earned that night. |
| Notes | Long text | Anything worth remembering: a driver short, the oven down, a big party order. |

### Relationships

- Customers.Zone points at a record in Delivery Zones
- Menu Items.Category points at a record in Menu Categories
- Recipe Lines.Menu Item points at a record in Menu Items
- Recipe Lines.Ingredient points at a record in Ingredients
- Driver Pay.Driver points at a record in Staff
- Orders.Customer points at a record in Customers
- Orders.Zone points at a record in Delivery Zones
- Orders.Driver points at a record in Staff
- Orders.Driver Pay points at a record in Driver Pay
- Order Lines.Order points at a record in Orders
- Order Lines.Menu Item points at a record in Menu Items
- Order Lines.Size points at a record in Sizes

### Queries

#### Tonight's orders

Every order due tonight, earliest first, with how it came in, where it goes, its status and its total. Keep it open through the evening.

From Orders. Shows Number, Due Time, Channel, Method, Postcode, Status, Payment, Total.
Calculated: Due Time is `Mid([Due], 12, 5)`.
Only where `Nights Ago = 0`.

#### Orders still to go out

Orders booked, cooking, ready or out, by the time they are due, with the minutes left; below nought means it is late. The orders booked ahead for later nights are on it too.

From Orders. Shows Due, Number, Method, Channel, Postcode, Status, Minutes Left, Total.
Calculated: Minutes Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), Format([Due], "yyyy-mm-dd")) * 1440 + (Mid([Due], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Due], 15, 2)) - (Mid(Now(), 12, 2) * 60 + Mid(Now(), 15, 2))`.
Only where `Status In ("Booked", "Cooking", "Ready", "Out")`.

#### Tonight by the hour

Tonight's orders by the hour they are due: how many, deliveries and collections, and their takings. Look at the next hour's row to see what is coming, and call in another driver when it is heavy.

From Orders. Shows Hour, Orders, Deliveries, Collections, Takings.
Calculated: Hour is `Mid([Due], 12, 2)`; Deliveries is `IIf([Method] = "Delivery", 1, 0)`; Collections is `IIf([Method] = "Collection", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Nights Ago = 0` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Delivery times by zone, last 28 days

For each zone, the deliveries in the last 28 nights, the average and the longest time from the order going in to the door, and how many took longer than the zone's target.

From Orders, Delivery Zones. Shows Zone, Target Minutes, Deliveries, Average Minutes, Longest, Over Target.
Calculated: Average Minutes is `(DateDiff("d", Format([Placed], "yyyy-mm-dd"), Format([Handed Over], "yyyy-mm-dd")) * 1440 + (Mid([Handed Over], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Handed Over], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Placed], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Placed], 15, 2)))`; Longest is `(DateDiff("d", Format([Placed], "yyyy-mm-dd"), Format([Handed Over], "yyyy-mm-dd")) * 1440 + (Mid([Handed Over], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Handed Over], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Placed], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Placed], 15, 2)))`; Over Target is `IIf((DateDiff("d", Format([Placed], "yyyy-mm-dd"), Format([Handed Over], "yyyy-mm-dd")) * 1440 + (Mid([Handed Over], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Handed Over], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Placed], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Placed], 15, 2))) > [Target Minutes], 1, 0)`.
Only where `Nights Ago Between 1 And 28` and `Status = Done`.

#### Takings by channel, last 28 days

Orders, deliveries, takings, the average order and the delivery charges for phone, walk-in and online orders over the last 28 nights.

From Orders. Shows Channel, Orders, Deliveries, Takings, Average Order, Delivery Charges.
Calculated: Deliveries is `IIf([Method] = "Delivery", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Nights Ago Between 1 And 28` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Takings by month

Each month's takings by channel from the night sheets, the VAT within them, the kitchen's wages and the drivers' pay, and what was left.

From Nights. Shows Month, Nights Open, Orders, Phone, Walk-in, Online, Takings, VAT, Kitchen Wages, Driver Pay, Left After VAT and Wages.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Takings is `[Phone Takings] + [Walk-in Takings] + [Online Takings]`; Left After VAT and Wages is `Round([Phone Takings] + [Walk-in Takings] + [Online Takings] - [VAT] - [Kitchen Wages] - [Driver Pay], 2)`.

#### Busy nights, last 12 weeks

The average night for each day of the week over the last twelve weeks: orders, deliveries and takings. For planning the rota and the drivers.

From Nights. Shows Day, Nights, Average Orders, Average Deliveries, Average Takings.
Calculated: Day is `IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [Date]) Mod 7 = 0, "Monday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [Date]) Mod 7 = 1, "Tuesday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [Date]) Mod 7 = 2, "Wednesday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [Date]) Mod 7 = 3, "Thursday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [Date]) Mod 7 = 4, "Friday", IIf(DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, [Date]) Mod 7 = 5, "Saturday", "Sunday"))))))`; Average Takings is `[Phone Takings] + [Walk-in Takings] + [Online Takings]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 1 And 84`.

#### Best sellers, last 28 days

How many of each item went out in the last 28 nights and what they took, the most first. Items in a meal deal are counted as sold at nought; the deal carries the money.

From Order Lines, Orders, Menu Items, Menu Categories. Shows Menu Item, Category, Sold, Takings.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.
Only where `Nights Ago Between 0 And 28` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Pizza sizes sold, last 28 days

How many pizzas of each size went out in the last 28 nights, for the dough and the boxes.

From Order Lines, Orders, Sizes. Shows Size, Pizzas.
Only where `Nights Ago Between 0 And 28` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Drops by driver, last 28 days

Each driver's deliveries over the last 28 nights, their drop fees, their average delivery time and the cash they collected.

From Orders, Staff. Shows Driver, Drops, Drop Fees, Average Minutes, Cash Collected.
Calculated: Driver is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Average Minutes is `(DateDiff("d", Format([Placed], "yyyy-mm-dd"), Format([Handed Over], "yyyy-mm-dd")) * 1440 + (Mid([Handed Over], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Handed Over], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Placed], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Placed], 15, 2)))`; Cash Collected is `IIf([Payment] = "Cash", [Total], 0)`.
Only where `Nights Ago Between 1 And 28` and `Status = Done`.

#### Driver pay by week

The pay sheets of the last eight weeks: each driver, their drops and their pay, the newest week first.

From Driver Pay, Staff. Shows Week Beginning, Number, Driver, Drops, Drop Pay, Pay Date.
Calculated: Driver is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 7 And 62`.

#### Customers not ordered for 60 days

Customers who have agreed to offers and have not ordered for more than 60 days, the biggest spenders first, with how many orders they made and when the last was. The list for a come-back offer.

From Customers, Orders. Shows Customer, Phone, Postcode, Orders, Spent, Last Order, Days Since.
Calculated: Customer is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Last Order is `Format([Placed], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Days Since is `DateDiff("d", Format([Placed], "yyyy-mm-dd"), Date())`.
Only where `Days Since > 60` and `Offers = Yes` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Ingredient use, last 7 nights

How much of each ingredient the last seven nights' orders used, from the recipes and the pizza sizes, and what it cost, by supplier. Use it when ordering and to check against what was delivered.

From Order Lines, Orders, Menu Items, Recipe Lines, Ingredients. Shows Supplier, Ingredient, Unit, Bought As, Used, Cost.
Calculated: Used is `Round([Order Lines].[Quantity] * [Portion] * [Recipe Lines].[Quantity], 3)`; Cost is `Round([Order Lines].[Quantity] * [Portion] * [Recipe Lines].[Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`.
Only where `Nights Ago Between 1 And 7` and `Status = Done`.

#### Menu

The items on the menu now, by section, with their descriptions, diet and spice marks, when a deal is available, and prices.

From Menu Items, Menu Categories. Shows Category, Menu Item, Description, Diet, Spice, Available, Price.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

#### Menu costing

Each item with a recipe, its price, its price less VAT, its food cost and the share of the price that is, and the gross profit left. Pizzas are costed at the smallest size.

From Menu Items, Menu Categories, Recipe Lines, Ingredients. Shows Category, Menu Item, Price, Price less VAT, Food Cost, Food Cost %, Gross Profit.
Calculated: Price less VAT is `Round([Price] / (1 + [VAT Rate]), 2)`; Food Cost is `Round([Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2)`; Food Cost % is `Round(100 * [Quantity] * [Cost per Unit] / ([Price] / (1 + [VAT Rate])), 2)`; Gross Profit is `Round(IIf([Line] = 1, [Price] / (1 + [VAT Rate]), 0) - Round([Quantity] * [Cost per Unit], 2), 2)`.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Delivery Zones, Customers, Staff, Sizes, Menu Categories, Menu Items, Ingredients, Recipe Lines, Driver Pay, Orders, Order Lines, Nights. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

#### Ingredient use

The last seven nights' ingredient use, a section for each supplier, with its cost.

Each item by section with its price, price less VAT, food cost, food cost percentage and gross profit, and the averages. For setting prices.

### Print templates

#### Customer receipt

Goes in the bag or to the customer at the counter, on an 80 mm roll: the order number, when it was ordered and is due, each item with its size, notes and price, the food and drink, the delivery charge when there is one, the total and the VAT within it, how it is paid, and the cash to pay when it is not paid yet. It is for every order not cancelled; a cancelled one chosen on the Orders form still prints, marked cancelled. One for each record of Orders, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Order {Number}
- Fields: Ordered, Ordered by, Collection or delivery, Due, Name, Payment
- Lines from Order Lines: Qty, Item, Size, Notes, Price
- Totals: Food and drink, Delivery, Total, VAT included, Cash to pay
- Words: Free delivery: your order is over the zone's amount for free delivery.
- Words: Cancelled: this order was cancelled and nothing is owed for it.
- Words: Payment: {Payment}. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Kitchen ticket

Printed on the kitchen printer as the order is taken: the order number, the time due, collection or delivery, and each item with its size and notes in the order taken, an extra under the dish it goes on, with no prices. Meal deals show what was chosen. It is for every order not cancelled; choose the new ones to print. One for each record of Orders, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Kitchen {Number}
- Fields: Due, Collection or delivery, Taken, Came by
- Lines from Order Lines: Qty, Item, Size, Notes
- Totals: Items
- Words: CANCELLED: do not cook.

#### Delivery slip

Taped to the bag for the driver: the customer's name, address, postcode, phone and delivery notes, the zone, the time due, what is in the bag, and either the cash to collect or a line saying it is paid already. It is only for deliveries that are not cancelled: a collection has no slip. One for each record of Orders, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Delivery {Number}
- Fields: Deliver to, Address, Postcode, Phone, Notes, Zone, Due by, Driver
- Lines from Order Lines: Qty, Item, Size
- Totals: Order total, Cash to collect
- Words: Cash: collect the amount above and hand it in at the end of the night.
- Words: Paid already ({Payment}): nothing to collect.

#### Driver pay sheet

Given to each driver with their pay each week: every drop they made, night by night, with its time, zone and fee and each night's fees and cash handed in, the number of drops, the cash they collected, and the pay for the drops. Numbered DRV-2026-0042. Tax and deductions are left for the payroll. One for each record of Driver Pay, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Driver pay sheet {Number}
- Fields: Driver, Week beginning, Phone, Week ending, Paid on
- Lines from Orders: Night, Order, Delivered, Zone, Postcode, Drop Fee, Cash Taken
- Totals: Drops, Pay for the drops, Cash collected, handed in each night
- Words: Paid per drop at the zone's fee, which covers the driver's own fuel and car. Tax, National Insurance and any other deduction are worked out by the payroll, not on this sheet.
- Signed by: Driver, Manager

### Starting empty

Start with Business: your name, address, phone, VAT number and the words at the foot of a receipt. Then Delivery Zones, with each zone's districts, charges and the drivers' fee; Sizes; Menu Categories; Menu Items; Ingredients; and the Recipe Lines for each item, numbered from 1. Then Staff, the drivers among them. Customers are added as they first order. From then on, each order is an Orders record with its Order Lines, each night a Nights sheet, and each week a Driver Pay sheet for each driver with their drops pointing at it.

### Making it yours

- Charge by distance rather than zone: add a Miles field to Customers and a calculated delivery charge in a query, such as 1.50 plus 0.50 a mile.
- Take orders through a delivery app as well: add App as a Channel, and an App Fee field on Orders for the commission, so Takings by channel shows what each channel leaves you.
- Run a loyalty card: add a Stamps field to Customers and a query counting each customer's orders since their last free one.
- Pay drivers by the hour as well as per drop: give them an Hourly Rate and add Hours and Hourly Pay to Driver Pay, with a gross pay that adds both.
- Keep allergens: add yes/no fields to Ingredients (gluten, milk, egg, nuts, sesame and the rest) and a query listing the menu items using any marked Yes, for the counter and the website.
- Add a Table No and Covers to Orders and Eat in as a Method if you have a few tables.
- Track stock: add In Stock and Reorder Level to Ingredients and a Deliveries table, and compare the ingredient use with what came in.

### Questions people ask

**How do I reprint a customer's receipt?**

Find the order on the Orders form by its Number or the customer, then open the print template Customer receipt, choose that order and press Print.

**Why is a pizza at nought on the receipt?**

It is part of a meal deal. The deal is the line above it at the deal's price, and each thing chosen for it follows at nought, with the deal's name in its notes, so the kitchen sees what to make.

**Where does the delivery time come from?**

From Placed and Handed Over on each order: the minutes between the order going in and the food reaching the door. Delivery times by zone, last 28 days averages them and counts those over the zone's Target Minutes.

**How are the drivers paid?**

Per drop, at the Drop Fee of the zone each delivery went to, which covers their own fuel and car. Each week's drops are added up on a Driver Pay sheet; tax and National Insurance are worked out by the payroll.

**A customer wants their usual delivered somewhere else tonight. What do I change?**

Type the other Address, Postcode and Delivery Notes on that order only, and choose the Zone that address is in. Their Customers record stays as it is.

**Why is someone missing from the come-back list?**

The list shows only customers who have ticked Offers, have not ordered for more than 60 days and have an order within the twelve weeks kept here. Someone who said no to offers is never on it.

**How do I change the delivery charge for one zone?**

Open the Delivery Zones form and change Charge, Free Over or Minimum Order. Orders already taken keep the charge they were given.

**Can I start with my own menu and keep the design?**

Yes. Make the sample empty and follow the order under starting empty: your Business details, the zones, the menu with its sizes and recipes, then your staff.

## Hazel Row Flowers

**Florist.** Stems and their waste, bouquets and recipes, orders and deliveries, weddings and the till for a florist.

Hazel Row Flowers is an invented florist's shop in Stoke Newington, north London, run by its owner with two florists, a Saturday junior and a delivery driver. It sells hand-tied bouquets, arrangements, plants and wrapped bunches over the counter, takes orders by phone and online for delivery across north and east London or for collection, makes funeral tributes, and does the flowers for a dozen or more weddings a year.

The sample holds twelve months of the shop, made up a day at a time, and the orders already booked for the coming week. Three mornings a week the owner buys at an invented wholesale market and from a grower, buying for the days until the next market from what is booked and what the till usually sells. Each stem lasts a set number of days; what passes its best before it is used is thrown away and logged. Each product has a recipe of the stems it takes, so the orders booked turn into the stems to buy, and the price and the recipe give its margin.

Valentine's Day, Mother's Day and the weeks before Christmas are the busy days, with red roses at more than twice their usual market price in early February. Weddings are quoted months ahead, mostly for summer Saturdays; a quarter is paid to book and the rest four weeks before. Prices include VAT, as a shop's do, so receipts and invoices show the VAT within them.

It suits, with small changes: A florist with a shop or a studio; A flower stall or market trader; A wedding and events florist; A plant shop or garden centre counter; A gift and hamper shop that makes up orders; A cake maker who takes orders for set days.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- In Stock on an item is kept by hand: add the stems when you buy, take them off as they are used or thrown away. The sample's figures were made that way, so they never go below nought.
- A product's recipe is what the margin and the stems to buy are worked out from. Keep it close to what the florists really use; when a bouquet changes, change its recipe lines.
- The margin query counts each product's price once, on its recipe's line 1, and takes the cost of every line from it. Every recipe needs a line 1.
- Prices include VAT. The VAT within a price is the price less the price divided by 1.2; each line's is worked out to the penny and added up, as the receipt and invoice print it.
- Each print template prints only the orders it is for: no confirmation for a standing order, no card where none is wanted, no delivery note for a collection, and nothing for a cancelled order. The Wedding invoice prints for booked weddings only. Choose the orders to print, or print the one on screen, which always prints.
- Weddings are separate from orders, with their own lines, because they are quoted and paid differently. A quote not yet booked prints a Wedding invoice with no number; print the invoice only once the wedding is booked.
- Walk-in sales are in Till Sales and are not given an occasion, so the query Takings by occasion counts orders only.

### Tutorial

#### Take an order for delivery

1. Find the customer in the Customers form, or press New and type their name, address, phone and e-mail.
2. Open the Orders form and press New. Type the next Number, choose the customer in Customer and yourself in Taken By, and type when it was taken in Taken.
3. Choose Delivery in Kind and the Occasion, type the Due Date and Slot, the Recipient, their phone and the address, and choose the Area. Type its charge in Delivery Charge.
4. Type what to make in Description, and the card's words in Card Message and Card From; tick Card Included.
5. In the order lines below, choose each product and type the quantity and price. Type the Total, the Tax within it and the Net, how it was paid and Paid On.
6. Open the print template Order confirmation, choose the order, and press Save as PDF to e-mail it.

#### Get the day's deliveries out

1. First thing, open the Delivery Runs form and add the morning run (and the afternoon one on a busy day) with its driver. On each order going out, choose the run in Run.
2. Print the report Delivery sheet: the deliveries for today and tomorrow, by area.
3. Open the print template Gift card message and print the cards for today's orders; open Delivery note and print a note for each.
4. As each order is made set its Status to Made, then Out for delivery, then Delivered when the driver is back.

#### Buy at the market

1. The evening before, run the query Stems to buy for the next 3 days, or print the report Market list, and add what the till usually sells.
2. After buying, open the Purchases form and press New: type the next Number, choose the supplier and type Bought On.
3. In the lines below, add each item with the Units, the Unit Cost, the Stems and the Use By day (the day bought and the item's Life Days).
4. Add the stems to In Stock in the Items form, and type the new Cost per Stem when the price has changed.

#### Log the morning waste check

1. Go through the buckets. For each item past its best, open the Waste form and press New: choose the Item and the batch, type the day, the Stems and what they cost, and choose the Reason.
2. Take the stems off In Stock in the Items form.
3. On Mondays print the report Weekly waste, and run Waste by item to see what to buy less of.

#### Sell at the till

1. Open the Till Sales form and press New. Type the next Number, the time in Sold At, and choose yourself in Served By.
2. In the lines below, choose each product and type the quantity and its price. Type the Total, the Tax within it and Net, and choose Card or Cash in Payment.
3. Open the print template Till receipt, choose the sale, and press Print.
4. At closing, print the report Till takings to cash up.

#### Quote for a wedding and book it

1. Add the couple in the Customers form. Open the Weddings form and press New: type the next Quote No, choose the customer, and type the Couple, the Wedding Date, the venues and the Colours.
2. Type Quoted On and Valid Until (a month on). In the lines below, add each piece: the product, the description with the colours, the quantity and the price. Type the Total, Tax and Net.
3. Open the print template Wedding quote, choose the wedding and press Save as PDF to send it.
4. When they book, set Status to Booked, type the Deposit and Deposit Paid On, the next Invoice No, the Invoice Date and Balance Due On (four weeks before). Print the print template Wedding invoice.
5. Each week run the query Weddings in the next 60 days, or print Wedding balances, to see which balances are due. Type Balance Paid On when one comes in.

#### Look back over the month

1. Print the report Monthly orders for the orders delivered, and Till takings for the counter.
2. Print the report Occasion takings to see what people buy flowers for, and Product margins to see which products earn most.
3. Run the query Market spend by month to set what was bought against what was sold, and Deliveries by area to check the delivery charges.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 33 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

### Queries

#### Deliveries today and tomorrow

Every delivery for today and tomorrow, by area and then by time, with the address and the recipient's phone: the driver's list and the workroom's.

From Orders, Delivery Areas. Shows Area, Due Date, Slot, Order, Kind, Recipient, Address, Postcode, Recipient Phone, Status.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 1` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Stems to buy for the next 3 days

The flowers and foliage that the orders booked for the next three days need, item by item, beside what is in the workroom: buy the difference, and more for the till.

From Orders, Order Lines, Products, Recipe Lines, Items. Shows Item, Kind, Unit, Stems per Unit, In Stock, Stems Needed.
Calculated: Stems Needed is `[Order Lines].[Quantity] * [Stems]`.
Only where `Status = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 3` and `Kind In ("Flower", "Foliage")`.

#### Waste by week

Stems thrown away and what they cost, a line for each of the last twelve weeks: week 0 is the last seven days.

From Waste. Shows Weeks Ago, From, To, Stems, Cost.
Calculated: Weeks Ago is `Round((DateDiff("d", [When], Date()) - 3) / 7, 0)`.
Only where `Weeks Ago Between 0 And 11`.

#### Waste by item

What has been thrown away in the last four weeks, item by item, the costliest first: the items to buy less of.

From Waste, Items. Shows Item, Kind, Stems, Cost.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 27`.

#### Weddings in the next 60 days

Booked weddings in the next sixty days whose balance has not been paid, with the balance and how many days until it is due (below nought when it is late).

From Weddings, Customers. Shows Wedding Date, Days to Go, Couple, Phone, Ceremony Venue, Total, Deposit, Balance, Balance Due On, Days Until Due.
Calculated: Days to Go is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Wedding Date])`; Balance is `Round([Total] - Nz([Deposit]), 2)`; Days Until Due is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Balance Due On])`.
Only where `Days to Go Between 0 And 60` and `Status = Booked` and `Balance Paid On Is Null`.

#### Margin per product

Each product on sale with its price, what its stems cost at the last market price, and the margin left after VAT and stems, the best first.

From Recipe Lines, Products, Items. Shows Kind, Product, Price, Cost of Stems, Margin.
Calculated: Cost of Stems is `Round([Stems] * [Cost per Stem], 2)`; Margin is `IIf([Line] = 1, Round([Price] / (1 + [Tax Rate]), 2), 0) - Round([Stems] * [Cost per Stem], 2)`.
Only where `On Sale = Yes`.

#### Takings by occasion

Orders paid in the last twelve months by occasion, with what they brought in.

From Orders. Shows Occasion, Orders, Takings, VAT.
Only where `Status <> "Cancelled"` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Till takings by day

Receipts, takings and VAT at the till for each of the last fourteen days.

From Till Sales. Shows Day, Receipts, Takings, VAT.
Calculated: Day is `Format([Sold At], "yyyy-mm-dd")`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 13`.

#### Orders by month

Orders by the month they were delivered, with their takings and the delivery charges.

From Orders. Shows Month, Orders, Takings, Delivery Charges.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Due Date], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Deliveries by area

Deliveries in the last ninety days by area, with the charges collected: whether each area's charge is right.

From Orders, Delivery Areas. Shows Area, Charge, Deliveries, Charges.
Only where `Status = Delivered` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Market spend by month

What was spent with each supplier each month.

From Purchases, Suppliers. Shows Month, Supplier, Purchases, Spent.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Bought On], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Customers who order most

Customers who have spent 150 or more on orders, the biggest first.

From Customers, Orders. Shows Customer, Phone, Kind, Orders, Spent.
Calculated: Customer is `IIf(Nz([Company], "") = "", [Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name], [Company])`.
Only where `Total >= 150` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Staff, Suppliers, Items, Products, Recipe Lines, Purchases, Purchase Lines, Waste, Delivery Areas, Delivery Runs, Customers, Orders, Order Lines, Till Sales, Till Lines, Weddings, Wedding Lines. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Delivery sheet

Today's and tomorrow's deliveries on a page for each area, for the driver to take.

From the query Deliveries today and tomorrow, a group for each Area: Due Date, Slot, Order, Recipient, Address, Postcode, Recipient Phone, Status, with the count of Order.

#### Market list

What the booked orders need from the market for the next three days, beside what is in stock.

From the query Stems to buy for the next 3 days, a group for each Kind: Item, Unit, Stems per Unit, In Stock, Stems Needed, with the total of Stems Needed.

#### Weekly waste

Stems and money thrown away each week for twelve weeks, with the totals.

From the query Waste by week: Weeks Ago, From, To, Stems, Cost, with the total of Stems, total of Cost.

#### Wedding balances

Balances due on the weddings of the next sixty days, and the total to come.

From the query Weddings in the next 60 days: Wedding Date, Couple, Ceremony Venue, Total, Deposit, Balance, Balance Due On, with the total of Balance.

#### Product margins

The price list with the cost of stems and the margin of each product, by kind.

From the query Margin per product, a group for each Kind: Product, Price, Cost of Stems, Margin.

#### Occasion takings

A year's order takings by occasion.

From the query Takings by occasion: Occasion, Orders, Takings, VAT, with the total of Orders, total of Takings.

#### Till takings

The till for the last fourteen days, with the totals for cashing up and the VAT return.

From the query Till takings by day: Day, Receipts, Takings, VAT, with the total of Receipts, total of Takings, total of VAT.

#### Monthly orders

Orders and their takings, month by month.

From the query Orders by month: Month, Orders, Takings, Delivery Charges, with the total of Orders, total of Takings.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Order confirmation

The letter or e-mail sent when an order is taken: what will be made, for whom, where and when, the card's words, what was paid and when, and how to change or cancel. The delivery charge shows only when there is one. It is for the orders customers place, not the weekly standing orders, and not cancelled ones; any order chosen on the Orders form still prints. One for each record of Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Fields: To, Order, Address, Taken, Town, Postcode
- Heading: Your order {Number}
- Words: Dear {Customer.First Name},
- Words: Thank you for your order. This is what we have written down. If anything is not right, call us on {Business.Phone} and we will put it right.
- Lines from Order Lines: Flowers, Quantity, Price, Amount
- Totals: Flowers, Delivery, Total, VAT included
- Fields: Delivery or collection, On, For, Time, Address, Town, Postcode, What we will make, Paid by, Paid on
- Words: The card will read: {Card Message} {Card From}
- Words: No card goes with the flowers. If you would like one, call us and tell us what to write.
- Words: Payment: {Payment}. We take it before the flowers are made.
- Words: Flowers are made fresh on the day from what is best at the market, so a stem may differ a little from the picture; the colours and the size will not. If you need to change or cancel the order, tell us by 5pm the day before and we refund you in full. Once the flowers are made we can change the delivery but cannot refund them.
- Words: This order was cancelled. If you have paid for it, the money is refunded to the card you paid with.
- Words: With best wishes,
- Words: {Taken By}, {Business.Name}
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Gift card message

The small card that goes with the flowers: the message and who it is from, nothing else. It is only for the orders with Card Included ticked, so a standing order with no card has none. One for each record of Orders, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Words: {Card Message}
- Words: {Card From}

#### Delivery note

Goes with the driver: the recipient, the address, the time, that a card is enclosed when there is one, and what is being delivered, with no prices, a line of care for the flowers (or for a funeral tribute, or the weekly arrangement), and a line for whoever takes them in to sign. It is for the orders that go out in the van, not collections or cancelled orders. One for each record of Orders, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Delivery note {Number}
- Fields: For, Delivery date, Address, Time, Town, Area, Postcode, Driver, Phone, Card enclosed
- Lines from Order Lines: Flowers, Quantity
- Totals: Items
- Words: Someone has sent you flowers from {Business.Name}. To keep them fresh, cut the stems at an angle, put them in clean water and keep them out of direct sun. Change the water every two days.
- Words: A funeral tribute from {Business.Name}, made to order. Please keep it flat and out of the sun until the service.
- Words: Your weekly flowers from {Business.Name}. We take away last week's arrangement when we bring the new one.
- Signed by: Received by, Time

#### Wedding quote

Sent after the consultation: the couple, the date and venues, each piece with its price, the total with its VAT, and the deposit to book. Once the wedding is booked the quote shows the deposit paid instead, and a declined quote says it was not taken up. One for each record of Weddings, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Wedding flowers: quote {Quote No}
- Fields: For, Quote, Address, Date, Postcode, Prices hold until, The couple, Wedding date, Ceremony, Reception, Colours
- Lines from Wedding Lines: Description, Quantity, Each, Amount, VAT within
- Totals: Total for the flowers, VAT included, Deposit to book (a quarter), Deposit paid
- Words: To book, pay the deposit above: we then hold the date for you and send an invoice. The balance is due four weeks before the wedding. Flowers are seasonal: if a flower is not at its best that week we use the closest we can find, and we tell you first.
- Words: Booked: thank you for your deposit. We hold the date for you, and the balance is on your invoice, due four weeks before the wedding. Flowers are seasonal: if a flower is not at its best that week we use the closest we can find, and we tell you first.
- Words: The flowers for this wedding have been made and delivered. Thank you for choosing us.
- Words: This quote was not taken up. If your plans change, call us and we will quote again at the prices of the day.
- Words: The price includes making everything, delivery on the morning of the wedding, and setting up at the ceremony and the reception. Vases and stands we bring are collected the next working day.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Wedding invoice

Sent when a wedding is booked: the same lines, the deposit paid and the balance due four weeks before the day, or the balance paid and a thank you once it has come in. It is for the weddings with an invoice number, the booked ones. One for each record of Weddings, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Invoice {Invoice No}
- Fields: Invoice to, Invoice, Address, Date, Town, Your quote, Postcode, Wedding date, The couple, Deposit paid on, Balance due by, Balance paid on
- Lines from Wedding Lines: Description, Quantity, Each, Amount, VAT within

- Words: Please pay the balance by the date above to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Invoice No}. If you have paid it since this invoice was sent, thank you.
- Words: Paid in full. Thank you, and we hope the day was everything you wished for.
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms}

The receipt from the till, on an 80 mm roll: what was bought, the total and the VAT within it. One for each record of Till Sales, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.
