- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name, address, VAT number and bank details, which every document prints. Then Staff, Suppliers, Items (every stem, foliage and sundry you buy, with its life) and Products, then each product's Recipe Lines, and Delivery Areas. Count what is in the workroom into In Stock. Customers, orders, runs, till sales, purchases, waste and weddings come in as you trade.

### Making it yours

- Sell online: add a Source field to Orders (Phone, Website, Shop) and a query of orders by source.
- Remember the dates customers send flowers for: add a Reminders table (customer, occasion, date, recipient) and a query of reminders in the next fourteen days, to call or e-mail them.
- Price by size: add Small, Medium and Large as separate products, each with its own recipe, as the sample does with hand-tied bouquets.
- Take accounts for businesses and funeral directors: add Payment Days to Customers and an Invoices table, so standing orders are invoiced monthly.
- Record substitutions: add a Substitutions table (order, item asked for, item used) for the days the market runs short.
- Hire out vases and stands for weddings: add a Hire Items table and a Wedding Hire table with the return date, and a query of what is still out.
- Count the van's miles: add Miles and Fuel to Delivery Runs and a monthly query of the cost of delivering.

### Questions people ask

**How do I know what to buy at the market?**

Run the query Stems to buy for the next 3 days (or print the report Market list). It adds up the recipes of every order booked for the next three days, beside what is in stock. Add what the till sells on a usual day, and more before a busy day.

**Why do my margins change from week to week?**

The margin uses each item's Cost per Stem, the price at the last buy. When roses go up at the market before Valentine's Day, the margin on a dozen roses comes down until the price falls again.

**How do I print tomorrow's cards?**

Open the print template Gift card message from Print templates and choose tomorrow's orders (the query Deliveries today and tomorrow lists them). Each card has only the message and who it is from.

**How do I change the delivery charges?**

Edit the Charge in the Delivery Areas form. New orders take the new charge; orders already taken keep theirs.

**A customer has cancelled. What do I do?**

Set the order's Status to Cancelled and clear Paid On when the money has gone back. Cancelled orders are left out of the takings and the deliveries.

**How do I see what is being thrown away?**

Print the report Weekly waste for twelve weeks of waste, and run Waste by item for the last four weeks by item, the costliest first.

**Where is a wedding's balance?**

The Total less the Deposit. The query Weddings in the next 60 days shows it for each booked wedding not yet paid, with the days until it is due.

## Tansy Row Pharmacy

**Pharmacy counter.** Counter sales, stock by batch and expiry, pharmacist checks, prescription collections and home deliveries for an independent pharmacy.

For the shop side of an independent pharmacy: the medicines and toiletries sold over the counter, the stock behind them kept batch by batch with expiry dates, the orders to the wholesalers, and the deliveries made to customers who cannot get out. Tansy Row Pharmacy is invented: two pharmacists, a pharmacy technician, two counter assistants and two delivery drivers, open every day but Christmas Day.

The records cover the year up to the day the file is made, and the next two days of deliveries. Cough and cold remedies sell in winter, hay fever tablets and sun cream in summer. A sale takes the batch nearest its expiry date first. Each Monday the technician takes off the shelf anything that runs out of date within the week, and on the first Monday of the month it goes back to the wholesaler on an expiry return note for credit; what the toiletries supplier will not take back is written off for disposal. Whatever has fallen to its reorder level is ordered: from the main wholesaler every weekday, from the second on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and from the toiletries supplier on Mondays.

Some lines are sold only after a word with the pharmacist. Each of those sales has a record of the check: who it was for, which pharmacist, and whether it was sold. A few are not. The prescription log is kept deliberately small: initials, a reference, how many items, and whether they were collected, so the counter can see what is waiting on the shelf. It holds no medicines, doses or anything clinical, and the dispensary's own records belong in its own system.

Every name is generic and every person is made up. Nothing here is advice about any medicine, and the pharmacy-only lines and pack limits are only examples: check the rules where you work.

It suits, with small changes: A pharmacy's counter and shop; A health food or vitamin shop that tracks expiry dates; A chemist and toiletries shop; An optician's or audiologist's shop that sells products as well; A veterinary practice's counter, with pet medicines and food; A farm or garden shop that keeps batches with dates.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Units in Stock is the sum of Quantity Left over a product's batches. Data Files does not work it out by itself: when you sell, receive or write off stock, change the batch and the product together.
- A sale takes from the batch that runs out first. Keep the shelf in that order too, so the oldest packs go first.
- Prices in Products and Sale Lines include VAT, as shelf prices do. The VAT on a receipt is worked out within each line, rounded to the penny, and added up. Period products carry no VAT and stop smoking products 5 percent in the UK; check the rates where you are.
- The Prescriptions table is a collection log, not a dispensary record. Keep it to initials, a reference and a count of items, and keep anything clinical out of this file.
- Which lines need a pharmacist's check, and any limit on packs in one sale, are set on each product. The sample's choices are examples only; follow the rules where you work.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: every sale has a receipt, but purchase orders print while they are Submitted and round sheets while the round is Planned. Any record prints from its own form, whatever it is.
- The dispensary's own income, from prescriptions, is not in this file: the takings are the counter's.

### Tutorial

#### Serve a customer and print the receipt

1. Open the Sales form and press New. Type the next receipt Number, the date and time in When, choose who served in Served By, and set Payment to Card or Cash.
2. In Sale Lines, add a line for each product: choose the Product, type the Quantity, and copy its Retail Price into Unit Price, its group's Tax Rate, and its Cost Price into Unit Cost. Tick Pharmacist Check for a pharmacy-only line.
3. Type the Total (the sum of the lines), the VAT within it, what was handed over in Paid, and the Change.
4. Take the packs off the batch that runs out first: open the Batches form, find the product's batch with the earliest Expiry Date, and lower its Quantity Left. Lower the product's Units in Stock to match.
5. Open the print template Till receipt from Print templates, choose the sale, and press Print.

#### Record a pharmacist check

1. When a customer asks for a line with Pharmacist Check ticked in Products, the pharmacist speaks to them before anything is sold.
2. Open the Pharmacist Checks form and press New. Type When, choose the Product and the Pharmacist, type the Quantity asked for, and set For Whom.
3. Set Outcome to Sold and choose the Sale it went on, or to Not sold, with a short Note such as Chose a different product.
4. Print the Pharmacist check log report each month for the pharmacist to look over, and the Restricted sales by week report to see the pattern.

#### Order stock and book it in

1. Print the Stock to reorder report on the supplier's order day.
2. Open the Supplier Orders form and press New. Give it the next PO number, choose the Supplier and who ordered it, type Ordered On and Expected, and leave Status as Submitted. Add each product and quantity in Supplier Order Lines.
3. Print the Purchase order template for it from Print templates, or send it to the supplier as a PDF.
4. When the goods arrive, open the Batches form and add a batch for each product with the Batch No and Expiry Date printed on the packs and the Quantity Received; set Quantity Left to the same. Raise the product's Units in Stock. Then set the order's Received On and Status to Received.

#### Do the weekly date check and the monthly return

1. Each Monday, print the Expiry check report and take off the shelf anything running out within the week.
2. For each batch taken off, open the Waste form and press New: choose the Batch, type the date, the Quantity and the Unit Cost, and the Reason. Set the batch's Quantity Left to nought and lower Units in Stock.
3. On the first Monday of the month, open the Supplier Returns form and add a return for each wholesaler that takes returns, with the next RTN number. Choose that return in Return on each of its Waste records.
4. Type the total value in Credit Claimed, print the Expiry return note template, and put it in the box. When the credit note arrives, type its reference, Credited On, and set Status to Credited. The Returns awaiting credit query shows what is still owed.

#### Look after prescription collections

1. When a prescription bag is made up, open the Prescriptions form and press New: the next RX reference, the customer's initials, Received On, the number of Items, Ready On and the Shelf. Status is Ready.
2. When it is collected, type Collected On and set Status to Collected.
3. Each morning open the Prescriptions waiting over 7 days query, or print the Prescriptions to chase report, and contact those customers.
4. A bag not collected after 28 days goes back to the dispensary: set Status to Not collected.

#### Plan and run the delivery rounds

1. Open the Delivery Customers form to see who is due: each customer's Round Day, Area and how often (Every Weeks).
2. Open the Delivery Rounds form and press New for each driver's round: the next RND number, the Delivery Date, the Driver and the Area. Add each stop in Deliveries with the Stop number, the Customer, the Prescription Ref and the Bags. Mark those prescriptions For Delivery.
3. Print the Delivery round sheet template: it prints a sheet for each round still Planned. Or print the Delivery list report for both days at once.
4. When the driver is back, set each stop's Status to Delivered with Delivered At and Received By, or to Not in, card left and add it to the next day's round. Set the round's Status to Done, and the delivered prescriptions to Delivered.

#### Cash up and look at the month

1. At the end of each day, print the Daily takings report and check the cash and card against the till.
2. At the month's end, print Takings by category and Margin by category, and open Margin by product when reviewing prices.
3. Print Waste by month to see what is being lost to dates and damage, and the Stock value query for the stock take.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 32 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |

| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

### Queries

#### Expiring in the next 30 days

Batches still on the shelf that run out of date in the next 30 days, by supplier, with how many packs and their value at cost, and whether the supplier takes them back. Use it to put short-dated stock at the front, and to plan the next return.

From Batches, Products, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Expiry Date, Days Left, Code, Product, Batch No, Quantity Left, Value at Cost, Takes Returns.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Expiry Date])`; Value at Cost is `Round([Quantity Left] * [Cost Price], 2)`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 30` and `Quantity Left > 0`.

#### Prescriptions waiting over 7 days

Bags that have been ready for collection for more than a week, oldest first, with the shelf they are on. The counter rings or texts the customer about them.

From Prescriptions. Shows Ready On, Reference, Initials, Items, Days Waiting, Shelf.
Calculated: Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Ready On], Date())`.
Only where `Days Waiting > 7` and `Status = Ready` and `For Delivery = No`.

#### Deliveries today and tomorrow

Every stop on today's and tomorrow's rounds, by driver and stop, with the address, phone and bag reference.

From Deliveries, Delivery Rounds, Staff, Delivery Customers. Shows Delivery Date, Driver, Area, Stop, Customer, Address, Postcode, Phone, Prescription, Bags, Status.
Calculated: Driver is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Customer is `[Delivery Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Delivery Customers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 1`.

#### Restricted sales by week

Pharmacist checks on pharmacy-only lines over the last 13 weeks, a line a week: how many checks, how many sold and not sold, and the packs sold. Week Of is the first day in the week a check was made.

From Pharmacist Checks, Products. Shows Week Of, Checks, Sold, Not Sold, Packs Sold.
Calculated: Week Of is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Sold is `IIf([Outcome] = "Sold", 1, 0)`; Not Sold is `IIf([Outcome] = "Sold", 0, 1)`; Packs Sold is `IIf([Outcome] = "Sold", [Pharmacist Checks].[Quantity], 0)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Pharmacist check log

Every pharmacist check in the last 30 days, newest first: the product, who it was for, which pharmacist, and the outcome.

From Pharmacist Checks, Products, Staff. Shows When, Product, Quantity, For Whom, Outcome, Note, Pharmacist.
Calculated: Pharmacist is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Stock to reorder

Lines at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with how many to order. Discontinued lines are left out.

From Products, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Code, Product, Pack, Units in Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity.
Only where `Above Reorder Level <= 0` and `Discontinued = No`.

#### Takings by category

What each group of products took over the last 12 months, with the VAT within it and the takings before VAT.

From Sale Lines, Sales, Products, Categories. Shows Category, Items, Takings, VAT, Net.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`; VAT is `Round(Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) - Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) / (1 + Nz([Sale Lines].[Tax Rate])), 2)`; Net is `Round(Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) - Round(Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) - Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) / (1 + Nz([Sale Lines].[Tax Rate])), 2), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 364`.

#### Margin by category

Sales before VAT, their cost and the margin left for each group over the last 12 months, the largest margin first.

From Sale Lines, Sales, Products, Categories. Shows Category, Net Sales, Cost, Margin.
Calculated: Net Sales is `Round(Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) - Round(Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) - Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) / (1 + Nz([Sale Lines].[Tax Rate])), 2), 2)`; Cost is `Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Sale Lines].[Unit Cost], 2)`; Margin is `Round(Round(Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) - Round(Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) - Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2) / (1 + Nz([Sale Lines].[Tax Rate])), 2), 2) - Round([Sale Lines].[Quantity] * [Sale Lines].[Unit Cost], 2), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 364`.

#### Margin by product

Every line's shelf price, its price before VAT, its cost, and the margin on one pack in money and as a percentage. Use it when setting prices.

From Products, Categories. Shows Category, Code, Product, Retail Price, Price before VAT, Cost Price, Margin, Margin %.
Calculated: Price before VAT is `Round([Retail Price] / (1 + [Tax Rate]), 2)`; Margin is `Round([Retail Price] / (1 + [Tax Rate]) - [Cost Price], 2)`; Margin % is `Round(100 * ([Retail Price] / (1 + [Tax Rate]) - [Cost Price]) / ([Retail Price] / (1 + [Tax Rate])), 1)`.
Only where `Discontinued = No`.

#### Takings by day

The till each day for the last fortnight: the number of sales, cash and card, the total, and the VAT within it.

From Sales. Shows Day, Sales, Cash, Card, Takings, VAT Included.
Calculated: Day is `Format([When], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Cash is `Round(IIf([Payment] = "Cash", [Total], 0), 2)`; Card is `Round(IIf([Payment] = "Cash", 0, [Total]), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 13`.

#### Waste by month

Stock written off each month, by reason, in packs and at cost.

From Waste, Batches, Products. Shows Month, Reason, Units, Cost.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Written Off On], "yyyy-mm")`; Cost is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.

#### Supplier orders to come

Orders sent and not yet arrived, by the day they are expected.

From Supplier Orders, Suppliers. Shows Number, Supplier, Ordered On, Expected, Status.
Only where `Status = Submitted`.

#### Returns awaiting credit

Return notes not yet credited, with the credit claimed. The wholesalers take six weeks or more; chase any over ten weeks old.

From Supplier Returns, Suppliers. Shows Number, Supplier, Raised On, Collected On, Status, Credit Claimed.
Only where `Status <> "Credited"`.

#### Prescriptions by month

How many prescriptions came in each month over the last year, with their items, how many went out for delivery, and how many were never collected.

From Prescriptions. Shows Month, Prescriptions, Items, Delivered, Not Collected.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Received On], "yyyy-mm")`; Delivered is `IIf([For Delivery], 1, 0)`; Not Collected is `IIf([Status] = "Not collected", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Stock value

Lines, packs on the shelf, and their value at cost and at shelf price, by group.

From Products, Categories. Shows Category, Lines, Units, Value at Cost, Value at Retail.
Calculated: Value at Cost is `Round([Units in Stock] * [Cost Price], 2)`; Value at Retail is `Round([Units in Stock] * [Retail Price], 2)`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Suppliers, Categories, Staff, Supplier Orders, Supplier Returns, Products, Supplier Order Lines, Batches, Waste, Sales, Sale Lines, Pharmacist Checks, Prescriptions, Delivery Customers, Delivery Rounds, Deliveries. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

Takings, VAT and net sales by group for the last 12 months, with totals. For the owner and the accountant.

#### Pharmacy medicines by week, last 13 weeks

Pharmacy-only lines asked for, sold and not sold, week by week, for the last 13 weeks.

From the query Restricted sales by week: Week Of, Checks, Sold, Not Sold, Packs Sold, with the total of Checks, total of Sold, total of Not Sold, total of Packs Sold.

#### Pharmacist checks, last 30 days

The last 30 days of pharmacist checks, for the pharmacist to look over and sign off.

Stock written off, month by month and by reason, at cost.

#### Takings by day, last 14 days

The last fortnight's till, a line a day, with cash and card, for cashing up and banking.

From the query Takings by day: Day, Sales, Cash, Card, Takings, VAT Included, with the total of Sales, total of Takings, total of VAT Included.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Till receipt

The receipt the till prints for each sale, on an 80 mm roll: the date and time, each item with its price, the total, the cash handed over and the change for a cash sale, and the VAT included. Pharmacy-only lines are marked P. Numbered RCP-2026-00042. One for each record of Sales, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Date, Till, Served by, Paid by
- Lines from Sale Lines: Item, Qty, Price, Amount,  
- Totals: Total, Cash, Change, VAT included
- Words: P: a pharmacy medicine, sold after a word with the pharmacist.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Purchase order

Sent to a supplier: the lines to send, the pack, quantity and cost, and the day they are wanted, with the pharmacy's account number. Numbered PO-2026-0042. It prints for orders still Submitted; one already received prints from the Supplier Orders form, with the day it came in. One for each record of Supplier Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Purchase order {Number}
- Fields: To, Order number, Address, Date, Town, Deliver by, Postcode, Our account, Ordered by, Received
- Lines from Supplier Order Lines: Code, Product, Pack, Quantity, Unit Cost, Total
- Totals: Units, Order total before VAT
- Words: Please quote {Number} and our account number on your delivery note and invoice. Medicines with less than six months before their expiry date by agreement only.
- Words: Deliver to {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}.

#### Delivery round sheet

The sheet a driver takes out: one for each driver on each day still to come, with each stop in order, the address, the phone, what to know at the door, the bag reference, and a column for the customer to sign. It prints for Planned rounds only; a round already done prints from the Delivery Rounds form. One for each record of Delivery Rounds, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Delivery round {Number}
- Fields: Date, Driver, Area, Stops, Status
- Lines from Deliveries: Stop, Customer, Address, Postcode, Phone, At the door, Prescription, Bags, Signed
- Totals: Bags to deliver
- Words: Hand each bag only to the customer, their carer, or someone they have named to us. If no one is in, bring the bag back to the pharmacy and leave a card: never leave medicines on a doorstep or with a neighbour who has not been named.
- Signed by: Driver, Bags checked back in by

#### Expiry return note

Goes in the box of out-of-date stock sent back to a wholesaler: each product, batch, expiry date and quantity, the number of lines, and the credit claimed at cost. It is the statement the supplier's credit note is checked against. Numbered RTN-2026-0007. One for each record of Supplier Returns, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Expiry return {Number}
- Fields: To, Return number, Address, Date, Town, Our account, Postcode, Collected
- Words: The goods below have reached, or are about to reach, their expiry date, or arrived damaged. They are unopened and are returned for credit under your returns terms.
- Lines from Waste: Code, Product, Batch, Expiry, Quantity, Unit Cost, Value
- Totals: Lines, Units, Credit claimed
- Words: Please send a credit note quoting {Number} and our account number.
- Signed by: Packed by, Collected by

### Starting empty

Start with Business: the pharmacy's name, address, VAT number and the words at the foot of a receipt. Then Suppliers, Categories with their VAT rates, and Staff. Add Products with their supplier, prices and reorder levels, ticking Pharmacist Check where it applies. Enter the stock you hold as one Batch per product with its expiry date, and set Units in Stock to match. Add Delivery Customers if you deliver. Sales, Pharmacist Checks, Prescriptions, Supplier Orders, Waste and rounds come in as you trade.

### Making it yours

- Take a deposit or keep an account for a care home: add an Accounts table and an Account field on Sales, and a statement template on Accounts with its sales as lines.
- Add a second till: type Till 2 on its sales, and group the Takings by day query by Till as well.
- Run promotions: add a Promotions table (product, price, from, to) and use its price on the sale line while it runs.
- Track stock in a back room: add a Location field to Batches, Shelf or Store room, and show it on the Expiry check report.
- Count stock: add a Stock Counts table (product, date, counted) and a query comparing it with Units in Stock.
- Keep a fridge temperature log: add a Fridge Log table with the date, the reading and who took it, and a query for readings outside your range.

### Questions people ask

**How do I see what is going out of date?**

Open the Expiring in the next 30 days query, or print the Expiry check report. It lists batches with packs left and fewer than 31 days to their expiry date, by supplier.

**Why does a product have more than one batch?**

Each delivery is a batch of its own, with its own expiry date. Units in Stock is what is left over all of them.

**How do I reprint a customer's receipt?**

Open the Sales form, find the sale by its Number or its time, and print the Till receipt template for it.

**Where is the VAT on a receipt?**

Shelf prices include VAT, so the receipt shows the total paid and, below it, the VAT included in that total. The Takings by category query shows the same split for the year.

**What happens to stock the toiletries supplier will not take back?**

It is written off in Waste with the reason Out of date, for disposal, and no return note. Waste by month shows the cost.

**Can I add a customer who collects for someone else?**

The collection log only keeps initials. If you need more, keep it in the dispensary's own system rather than here.

**How do I change a driver's round?**

Change the customer's Area or Round Day in Delivery Customers. Rounds already made stay as they were; the next ones follow the new day.

## Northbank Trading

**Wholesale and trading.** Customers, suppliers, products, orders, purchase orders, stock and invoices for a wholesaler.

Northbank Trading is an invented wholesaler of specialty foods and supplies for the trade: teas and coffee, spices, rice and grains, dried fruit and nuts, oils, sauces, baking goods and kitchen supplies. It sells to shops, delis, cafes, restaurants and hotels in ten countries, and buys from a dozen suppliers.

The sample holds eighteen months of trading, made up a day at a time. Customers order more as the year ends. Each order is cut to what is on the shelf, so stock never goes below nought, and it goes down as orders ship. Twice a week the buyer raises purchase orders for whatever has fallen to its reorder level, and those arrive some days later. Every shipped order is invoiced; most invoices are paid on time, some late, and the newest are not yet due.

Customers, suppliers and carriers share one Companies table, told apart by their Kind, so a company that both buys from you and sells to you is entered once.

It suits, with small changes: A distributor or importer; A cash and carry; A builders' merchant or parts supplier; A wine merchant selling to the trade; An online shop that sells to businesses; A manufacturer's sales office.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Units in Stock on a product is the sum of its Stock Movements: received above nought, sold and corrected below. When you change one, change the other, or count the stock and add an Adjusted movement to put it right.
- An order line keeps its own Unit Price, Discount and Tax Rate, so a later price change never alters an order already taken or invoiced. An invoice prints the lines of its order, so there is nothing to mark on the lines when you invoice.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: delivery notes for shipped orders, statements for customers. One you print from its form always prints.
- Invoice and purchase order numbers are typed by you, a new run each year. Number them in date order and never use one twice; Data Files refuses a number already used.
- Customers, suppliers and carriers share the Companies table. Kind says which a company is, and most queries choose by it.
- VAT is a rate on each order line, taken from the product's group in Categories: food at 0, kitchen and cleaning supplies at 0.2. Delivery is charged at the standard rate. Check the rates for your own country and goods.

### Tutorial

#### Take an order

1. Open the Orders form and press New. Choose the customer in Customer and yourself in Employee; type today in Order Date and the day they need it in Required Date.
2. Choose the carrier in Shipper and type any delivery charge in Shipping Fee. Leave Status as New.
3. Open the Order Lines form and add a line for each product: choose the Order you just made, the Product, and type the Quantity. Type the Unit Price from the product's List Price, any Discount (0.05 is five percent), and the Tax Rate from the product's group in Categories.
4. Run the query Orders to ship to see it waiting, with the days left before the customer needs it.

#### Ship the order and send its delivery note

1. Pick the goods, then open the Orders form, find the order and type the Shipped Date. Change Status to Shipped.
2. For each product sent, open the Stock Movements form and add a Sold movement with the quantity below nought (-12 for twelve sent) and Order and its number in Reference; then lower Units in Stock on the Products form by the same.
3. Open Print templates, choose Delivery note, choose the order and press Print. It goes in the box for the customer to check and sign. Only orders with a Shipped Date are listed there.

#### Invoice it

1. Open the Invoices form and press New. Type the next number in Number (INV-2026-0301 after INV-2026-0300), choose the Order and the Customer, and type today in Invoice Date.
2. Type the Due Date: the invoice date plus the customer's Payment Days from the Companies form.
3. Type Net (the goods after discounts, with the delivery charge), Tax (the VAT on them) and Amount (the two together). The query Order totals shows the goods for the order.
4. Open Print templates, choose Invoice, choose the new invoice and press Save as PDF to e-mail it, or Print. It lists the lines of the order you chose in Order.

#### Record a payment and see who owes what

1. When a customer pays, open the Invoices form, find the invoice and type the day in Paid On. Then open the Orders form and change the order's Status to Closed.
2. Run the query Unpaid invoices for every invoice not yet paid, by due date, with how many days each is overdue.
3. Open the report Invoices due for the same list a page a customer, with what each owes in total.
4. At the month's end, open Print templates and choose Statement: it prints for each customer, listing their unpaid invoices and the balance owing. Send it to those who owe money.

#### Reorder stock

1. Run the query Products to reorder: products at or below their Reorder Level, by supplier, with how many to order.
2. Open the Purchase Orders form and press New: type the next number (PO-2026-0120), choose the Supplier and yourself, today in Ordered On and the day it should come in Expected. Status is Submitted.
3. Open the Purchase Lines form and add a line for each product to order, with the Quantity and the Unit Cost.
4. Open Print templates, choose Purchase order and send it to the supplier as a PDF. Only purchase orders still Submitted are listed there.
5. When the goods come, type the day in Received On and change Status to Received; add a Received movement in Stock Movements for each line and raise Units in Stock by the same.

#### See how the business is doing

1. Open the report Monthly sales for sales and units each month, and run Sales by category, Sales by employee and Top customers for who and what sells.
2. Run Stock value for what the stock in the warehouse is worth at cost.
3. Run Purchases on order for what is coming in and when.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 27 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Number | Short text, unique | The purchase order's number, printed on it and quoted by the supplier: PO-2026-0042. |
| Supplier | Points at Companies, required | Who you ordered from. |
| Employee | Points at Employees | Who placed the order. |
| Ordered On | Date | The day it was sent. |
| Expected | Date | When the goods should arrive. |
| Received On | Date | The day they arrived; empty until then. |
| Status | Short text | Submitted or Received. |

#### Purchase Lines

The products on each purchase order. The sample has 271 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Purchase Order | Points at Purchase Orders, required | The purchase order the line belongs to. |
| Product | Points at Products, required | What was ordered. |
| Quantity | Whole number | How many units. |
| Unit Cost | Currency | What one unit costs on this order. |

#### Stock Movements

Every change to stock: goods received, goods sold and corrections from a stock count. Added up, they give what is on the shelf. The sample has 2,083 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Product | Points at Products, required | The product that moved. |
| When | Date | The day it moved. |
| Kind | Short text | Received, Sold or Adjusted. |
| Quantity | Whole number | How many: above nought coming in, below nought going out. |
| Reference | Short text | The order or purchase order it came from, or Stock count. |

#### Invoices

An invoice for each shipped order. The sample has 610 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The invoice's number, given in date order and once only: INV-2026-0042, a new run each year. |
| Order | Points at Orders, required | The order invoiced. |
| Customer | Points at Companies | Who the invoice is to: the order's customer, kept here so a statement can list a customer's invoices. |
| Invoice Date | Date | The day it was raised, the day the order shipped. |
| Due Date | Date | When payment is due, from the customer's payment days. |
| Net | Currency | The goods after discounts, and delivery, before VAT. |
| Tax | Currency | The VAT on the goods and the delivery. |
| Amount | Currency | What the invoice comes to: net and VAT together. |

### Relationships

- Contacts.Company points at a record in Companies
- Orders.Customer points at a record in Companies
- Orders.Employee points at a record in Employees
- Orders.Shipper points at a record in Companies
- Order Lines.Order points at a record in Orders
- Order Lines.Product points at a record in Products
- Products.Category points at a record in Categories
- Products.Supplier points at a record in Companies
- Purchase Orders.Supplier points at a record in Companies
- Purchase Orders.Employee points at a record in Employees
- Purchase Lines.Purchase Order points at a record in Purchase Orders
- Purchase Lines.Product points at a record in Products
- Stock Movements.Product points at a record in Products
- Invoices.Order points at a record in Orders
- Invoices.Customer points at a record in Companies

### Queries

#### Order totals

Every order with its customer, status and the value of its goods after discounts, the newest first.

From Orders, Companies, Order Lines. Shows Order, Order Date, Customer, Status, Goods.
Calculated: Goods is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.

#### Sales by month

Sales and units for each month, cancelled orders left out.

From Orders, Order Lines. Shows Month, Sales, Units.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Order Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Sales by category

What each product group has sold, the biggest first.

From Order Lines, Orders, Products, Categories. Shows Category, Sales, Units.
Calculated: Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Sales by employee

What each sales person has sold.

From Orders, Employees, Order Lines. Shows Employee, Sales.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Top customers

Customers by what they have bought, with their country.

From Companies, Orders, Order Lines. Shows Customer, Country, Sales.
Calculated: Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Products to reorder

Products at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with how many to order. Discontinued lines are left out.

From Products, Companies. Shows Supplier, Code, Product, Units in Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity.
Only where `Above Reorder Level <= 0` and `Discontinued = No`.

#### Orders to ship

Orders not shipped yet, oldest first, with the days left before the customer needs them.

From Orders, Companies. Shows Order, Order Date, Customer, Required Date, Days Left.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Required Date])`.
Only where `Shipped Date Is Null` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Unpaid invoices

Invoices not yet paid, by due date, with how many days each is overdue (nought when it is not due yet).

From Invoices, Orders, Companies. Shows Invoice, Customer, Invoice Date, Due Date, Amount, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Days Overdue is `IIf(DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date()) > 0, DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date()), 0)`.
Only where `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Stock value

Units in stock and their value at cost, by product group.

From Products, Categories. Shows Category, Units, Value at Cost.
Calculated: Value at Cost is `Round([Units in Stock] * [Cost Price], 2)`.

#### Product list

The products you still sell, by group and code, with their list prices.

From Products, Categories. Shows Category, Code, Product, Unit, List Price.
Only where `Discontinued = No`.

#### Purchases on order

Purchase orders sent and not yet received, by the day they are expected.

From Purchase Orders, Companies. Shows Purchase Order, Supplier, Ordered On, Expected, Status.
Only where `Status = Submitted`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Companies, Contacts, Employees, Orders, Order Lines, Categories, Products, Purchase Orders, Purchase Lines, Stock Movements, Invoices. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Product catalogue

The price list: every product you still sell by group, with its unit and list price.

From the query Product list, a group for each Category: Code, Product, Unit, List Price.

#### Monthly sales

One line a month with units and sales, and the totals.

From the query Sales by month: Month, Units, Sales, with the total of Sales, total of Units.

#### Orders by customer

Each customer's orders, the newest first, with a total for each customer.

From the query Order totals, a group for each Customer: Order, Order Date, Status, Goods, with the total of Goods.

#### Invoices due

Unpaid invoices by customer with their due dates, days overdue and a total owed: the list for chasing payment.

From the query Unpaid invoices, a group for each Customer: Invoice, Invoice Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, Amount, with the total of Amount.

#### Stock to reorder

What to order, on a page for each supplier.

From the query Products to reorder, a group for each Supplier: Code, Product, Units in Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Invoice

The tax invoice sent when an order ships: the business's details at the head, the customer's address, the order's lines with their VAT rates, and the goods, delivery (when charged), VAT and total due. While it is owed it says how to pay; once paid, the day it was paid. Numbered INV-2026-0042. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Invoice {Number}
- Fields: Invoice to, Invoice number, Address, Date, City, Payment due, Postcode, Your order, Country, Shipped
- Lines from Order Lines: Code, Product, Unit, Quantity, Unit Price, Discount %, Net, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Goods, Delivery, VAT, Total due
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Please pay to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}.
- Words: Paid in full on {Paid On}. Thank you.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Delivery note

Goes in the box with a shipped order: what was sent and how many, without prices, for the customer to check and sign. It prints for orders with a Shipped Date only. One for each record of Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Delivery note DN-{ID}
- Fields: Deliver to, Order, Address, Ordered, City, Shipped, Postcode, Carrier, Country, Instructions
- Lines from Order Lines: Code, Product, Unit, Quantity
- Totals: Lines, Units
- Words: Please check the goods against this note. Shortages or damage to be reported within 48 hours of delivery.
- Signed by: Received in good order by, Date

#### Purchase order

Sent to a supplier: what to send, at what cost, and when it is expected. Numbered PO-2026-0042. It prints for purchase orders still Submitted; one already received prints from the Purchase Orders form, with the day it came in. One for each record of Purchase Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Purchase order {Number}
- Fields: To, Order number, Address, Date, City, Deliver by, Country, Ordered by, Received
- Lines from Purchase Lines: Code, Product, Unit, Quantity, Unit Cost, Total
- Totals: Order total
- Words: Please quote {Number} on your delivery note and invoice. Deliver to {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}.

#### Statement

Sent to a customer each month: the invoices they have not paid yet, oldest first, with the days each is overdue and the balance as it builds up to what they owe. It prints for customers only, not suppliers or carriers. One for each record of Companies, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Statement of account
- Fields: Account, Terms (days), Address, City, Postcode, Country
- Lines from Invoices: Invoice, Date, Due, Days overdue, Amount, Balance
- Totals: Statement date, Invoices unpaid, Balance owing
- Words: Please pay the balance owing to {Business.Bank Details}. If you have paid since this statement was made, thank you.
- Words: Nothing is owed on your account today. Thank you for your custom.

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name, address and payment details, which every document prints. Then Categories and Companies (your suppliers and carriers first, then your customers), then Employees and Products. Orders, purchase orders, stock movements and invoices come in as you trade. If you already hold stock, enter it as one Received movement per product and set Units in Stock to match.

### Making it yours

- Sell in more than one currency: add a Currency field to Companies and a rate to Orders, and a calculated column for the amount in your own currency.
- Keep several warehouses: add a Warehouses table, point Stock Movements at it, and group the stock queries by warehouse.
- Record part payments: add a Payments table pointing at Invoices, and an Unpaid invoices query that sums what has been paid against each one.
- Give customers their own prices: add a Price Lists table (customer, product, price) and use it when taking an order.
- Track batches and best-before dates: add a Batch and a Best Before field to Purchase Lines and Stock Movements.
- Add sales tax: add a Tax Rate field to Products and a calculated column for the tax on each line.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print one invoice?**

Open Print templates, choose Invoice and choose the invoice. Press Print, or Save as PDF to send it by e-mail. From the Invoices form, the invoice on screen prints with the Print button.

**Why does a product show below its reorder level when a delivery is due?**

Products to reorder looks at Units in Stock only. Run Purchases on order to see what is already coming before ordering again.

**How do I give one customer a discount on everything?**

Type the discount on each of their order lines. To make it automatic, add a Discount field to Companies and copy it onto each line as you take the order.

**Where do I change the name and bank details on invoices?**

In the Business table: its one record is printed at the head and foot of every document.

**Can a customer also be a supplier?**

Yes. Enter the company once with the Kind it is most, and choose it as either; queries that choose by Kind will show it under that one.

**How do I start again with my own records?**

Make the sample again from the Data Files start screen and choose Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them.

## Granite and Grain Woodworks

**Workshop or maker.** Materials, bills of materials, work orders, makers' hours, quotes, orders, deliveries and VAT invoices for a small furniture workshop.

Granite and Grain Woodworks is an invented workshop of five makers in a unit on an industrial estate. They build dining tables, chairs, stools, benches, shelves, bookcases and chopping boards from oak, ash, walnut and beech, and make kitchen doors, drawer fronts and worktops to measure. About ten gift and homeware shops buy boards, coasters and shelves at a trade discount, interior designers order kitchens and furniture for their clients, and members of the public buy from the workshop's showroom and website.

Every product has a bill of materials: the timber, sheet, fittings, finish and packing that one of it takes. Small goods, chairs and shelves are made in batches to keep a stock on the shelf. Tables, bookcases, worktops and kitchen doors are made to order, so each order line of them gets a work order of its own. Planning a work order sets its materials aside, starting it takes them from stock, and the makers book their hours to it each day until it is finished.

The records cover fifteen months up to the morning the file is made, with orders already taken for the weeks ahead. Shops order more boards before Christmas, kitchens slow in August, the workshop closes between Christmas and New Year, and timber prices went up part way through. Some deliveries are late, most of them in January after the break or when a maker was off sick, and a few trade customers pay late. The buyer orders twice a week for the work starting in the next fortnight, so a job further off can show as a shortage until it comes closer.

Made-to-order work is quoted first: a quote for a kitchen or a table is sent, and when the customer says yes it becomes a sales order, linked back to its quote. About half of the quotes for one-off pieces come to nothing, and a few are always waiting for an answer. Every delivery is invoiced the same day with VAT at twenty percent on the goods and the delivery, and prices in the records are before VAT.

The workshop prints six documents from the file: the quote, the VAT invoice, the delivery note that goes in the van, the purchase order sent to a merchant, a statement for each account, and the works order sheet that goes on the bench with the list of materials the job takes.

Use it to see how a bill of materials, stock and production fit together, or start from it empty for a workshop of your own.

It suits, with small changes: A cabinet maker or joiner; A bakery's production side; A print shop; A sign maker; A soap or candle maker; A garment or textile maker; An electronics assembler; A metal fabricator.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Prices in Products, quotes and orders are before VAT. Everything the workshop sells is at the standard rate, 0.2, and delivery carries VAT too. A shop that shows prices with VAT in its showroom adds a fifth to these.
- An invoice is the sales order itself once it is delivered: its Invoice No, Invoice Date, Net, VAT and Invoice Amount are filled in on the day. So the Invoice print template prints from Sales Orders, for the orders that have an Invoice No.
- Net and VAT are worked out the way the invoice shows them: each line rounded to the penny, its VAT rounded to the penny, then added up, and the VAT on delivery added. Work them out the same way when you type them, or the invoice and the record will differ by a penny.
- Stock and materials are not counted by the database on its own. In Stock, On Order and Allocated are typed figures, kept right by the Material Movements and Stock Movements records you add. Count once a month and correct them with a Counted or Adjusted movement.
- A work order's materials are copied into Work Order Materials when it is planned. Changing a product's bill of materials afterwards changes new work orders, not ones already planned.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: quotes waiting for an answer, invoices for delivered orders, delivery notes for open orders, purchase orders not yet received, statements for trade accounts and works orders for the bench. Any record prints from its own form, whatever it is.
- Document numbers run in date order with a new run each year. When you type a new one, look at the last number used in that table and add one.

### Tutorial

#### Quote for a made-to-order piece

1. Open the Customers form. If the customer is new, press New and type their Name, Kind (Public or Designer), address, phone and e-mail.
2. Open the Quotes form and press New. Choose the customer in Customer, type the Quote Date and a Valid Until thirty days on, set Status to Sent and write what they asked for in Notes.
3. In Quote Lines, add each product with its Quantity, Unit Price from the product, any trade Discount, and the Tax Rate 0.2.
4. Work out Net, VAT and Total on the quote as the lines add up (the Quote print template shows the figures), and type them in.
5. Open Print templates, choose Quote, pick the quote and press Print or Save as PDF. Send it to the customer.

#### Turn an accepted quote into an order and plan the work

1. Open the Sales Orders form and press New. Choose the customer, type the Order Date and the Delivery Due you agreed, and copy the quote's Notes.
2. In Sales Lines, add the same products, quantities, prices, discount and tax rate as the quote.
3. Open the quote in the Quotes form, set Status to Accepted and choose the new order in Sales Order.
4. Open the Work Orders form and press New for each made-to-order line: the Product, the Quantity, the Maker, the Sales Order, the Planned Start and Due Date, Standard Hours and the Instructions. Set Status to Planned.
5. Add the job's materials in Work Order Materials, one record per line of the product's bill of materials (the Costed bill of materials query lists them), with Needed set to the quantity times the bill. Add the same amounts to Allocated on each material.
6. Open Print templates, choose Works order, pick the work order and press Print. Give the sheet to the maker.

#### Run the workshop week

1. On Monday open the Production plan report: each maker's open work orders in the order they start.
2. When a maker starts a job, open it in the Work Orders form, type Started and set Status to In progress. Take its materials from stock: lower In Stock and Allocated on each material, and add a Used record in Material Movements with the work order's number as Reference.
3. Each evening the makers add their hours in the Time Sheets form: Maker, Work Order, Worked On and Hours.
4. When a job is done, type Finished, set Status to Done, add one Made record per job in Stock Movements, and raise In Stock on the product.
5. On Friday open Maker hours, last 4 weeks to see who has time, and Work order costs to compare hours booked with standard hours.

#### Order timber and fittings

1. On Monday and Thursday open the Reorder list report and the Shortages for buying report.
2. Open the Material Purchases form and press New. Type the next Number (PO-2026-0043 after PO-2026-0042), choose the Supplier, type Ordered On and Expected, and set Status to Ordered.
3. In Purchase Lines, add each material with its Quantity and Unit Cost. Raise On Order on each material by the quantity.
4. Open Print templates, choose Purchase order, pick it and press Print or Save as PDF to send to the supplier.
5. When the delivery comes, type Received On, set Status to Received, add a Received record in Material Movements for each line, and move the quantities from On Order to In Stock.

#### Deliver an order and invoice it

1. Open the Delivery schedule report to see what goes out in the next two weeks.
2. The day before, open Print templates, choose Delivery note, pick the order and press Print. It goes in the van; the customer signs one copy.
3. On the day, open the order in the Sales Orders form. Type Delivered On, set Status to Delivered, type the next Invoice No, the Invoice Date, Net, VAT, Invoice Amount and Invoice Due (the delivery day plus the customer's Payment Days).
4. Add a Delivered record in Stock Movements for each line and lower In Stock on each product.
5. Open Print templates, choose Invoice, pick the order and press Print or Save as PDF. E-mail it to the customer.

#### Take a payment and send statements

1. When money comes in, open the order in the Sales Orders form and type Paid On.
2. At the start of each month open the Invoices due report: every unpaid invoice by customer, with days overdue.
3. Open Print templates and choose Statement: it prints for each shop and designer, listing what they have not paid. Press Print or Save as PDF and send each its statement.
4. Ring anyone more than a fortnight overdue. The Unpaid invoices query shows the oldest first.

#### Chase quotes and see how many are won

1. On Friday open the Quotes to chase report: quotes still waiting, with the days left on each.
2. Ring the customer. If they say yes, take the order as above; if no, open the quote in the Quotes form and set Status to Declined.
3. A quote past its Valid Until with no answer is set to Expired.
4. At the end of the month open the Quote results by month query to see how many quotes became work.

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 38 records.

| Material Cost | Currency | The cost of one product's materials from its bill of materials, worked out at today's unit costs. The Costed bill of materials query shows how it is made up. |
| Labour Minutes | Whole number | How long one takes to make, in minutes, by a maker working at a normal pace. |
| Made to Order | Yes/No | Ticked for products made for each order (tables, bookcases, worktops, kitchen doors); left clear for products kept on the shelf. |
| In Stock | Whole number | Finished pieces on the shelf, including made-to-order pieces finished and waiting for delivery. |
| Stock Level | Whole number | How many to keep on the shelf beyond what is already ordered. A batch is planned when stock and work in hand fall short of it. |
| Batch Size | Whole number | How many are made at once. |
| Tax Rate | Number | The VAT rate it is sold at, as a fraction: 0.2 is twenty percent. Copied to each quote and order line when it is sold. |
| Active | Yes/No | Untick a product you no longer make; it stays in the old orders. |
