### Queries

#### Costed bill of materials

Every material in every product, with how much it takes, the unit cost and the line cost. Use it to check a price or to see what a price rise in one timber does to each product.

From Products, Bill of Materials, Materials. Shows Product Code, Product, Material, Quantity, Unit, Unit Cost, Line Cost.
Calculated: Line Cost is `Round([Bill of Materials].[Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

#### Product margins

Each product's price less its material cost and its labour, with the margin as a percentage of the price, the best first. Labour is costed at 21 an hour; change the number in the query to your own rate.

From Products. Shows Code, Product, Category, Price, Material Cost, Labour Cost, Margin, Margin %.
Calculated: Labour Cost is `Round([Labour Minutes] / 60 * 21, 2)`; Margin is `Round([Price] - [Material Cost] - [Labour Minutes] / 60 * 21, 2)`; Margin % is `Round(100 * ([Price] - [Material Cost] - [Labour Minutes] / 60 * 21) / [Price], 1)`.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

#### Materials for planned work

What the planned work orders need of each material, from their bills of materials, beside what is allocated and in stock. The Needed column is how the Allocated figure is made up.

From Materials, Bill of Materials, Products, Work Orders. Shows Code, Material, Unit, Needed, Allocated, In Stock.
Calculated: Needed is `Round([Work Orders].[Quantity] * [Bill of Materials].[Quantity], 2)`.
Only where `Status = Planned`.

#### Material shortages

Materials where the planned work needs more than is in stock and on order, with how much is short. Buy these before the work that needs them is due to start, or it will wait.

From Materials, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Code, Material, Unit, Allocated, In Stock, On Order, Short By.
Calculated: Short By is `Round([Allocated] - [In Stock] - [On Order], 2)`.
Only where `Short By > 0`.

#### Materials to reorder

Materials whose free stock (in stock, plus on order, less allocated to planned work) is at or below the reorder level, by supplier, with the minimum order for that supplier and how much you usually order. Free stock below nought is a shortage.

From Materials, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Minimum Order, Code, Material, Unit, Free Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity.
Calculated: Free Stock is `Round([In Stock] + [On Order] - [Allocated], 2)`.
Only where `Above Reorder Level <= 0`.

#### Purchases on order

Orders placed with suppliers that have not arrived, with when each is expected and what it is worth.

From Material Purchases, Suppliers, Purchase Lines. Shows Purchase, Supplier, Ordered On, Expected, Value.
Calculated: Value is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Status = Ordered`.

#### Open work orders

Work planned or in progress, the soonest due first, with the maker, the order it is for and the days left. Days left below nought means it is late.

From Work Orders, Products, Makers. Shows Work Order, Product, Quantity, Maker, For Order, Planned Start, Due Date, Started, Status, Days Left.
Calculated: Maker is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Due Date])`.
Only where `Status In ("Planned", "In progress")`.

#### Work order costs

Work orders finished in the last 90 days, with the hours booked against the standard hours, the labour cost at each maker's rate and the material cost.

From Time Sheets, Makers, Work Orders, Products. Shows Work Order, Product, Quantity, Finished, Standard Hours, Hours Booked, Labour Cost, Material Cost.
Calculated: Standard Hours is `Round([Work Orders].[Quantity] * [Labour Minutes] / 60, 2)`; Labour Cost is `Round([Hours] * [Hourly Cost], 2)`; Material Cost is `Round([Work Orders].[Quantity] * [Material Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Status = Done` and `Days Since Between 0 And 90`.

#### Maker hours by month

The hours each maker booked to work orders in each month, and what they cost.

From Time Sheets, Makers. Shows Maker, Month, Hours, Cost.
Calculated: Maker is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Month is `Format([Worked On], "yyyy-mm")`; Cost is `Round([Hours] * [Hourly Cost], 2)`.

#### Maker hours, last 4 weeks

The hours each maker booked over the last four weeks, to see who is busy and who has time.

From Time Sheets, Makers. Shows Maker, Role, Hours, Cost.
Calculated: Maker is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Cost is `Round([Hours] * [Hourly Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 27`.

#### Orders to deliver

Open orders due in the next 14 days, and any already late, the soonest first, with what the goods come to.

From Sales Orders, Customers, Sales Lines. Shows Order, Customer, Kind, Order Date, Delivery Due, Days Left, Goods.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Delivery Due])`; Goods is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Days Left <= 14` and `Status = Open`.

#### Late deliveries

Orders delivered after the promised day in the last year, with how many days late.

From Sales Orders, Customers. Shows Order, Customer, Kind, Delivery Due, Delivered On, Days Late.
Calculated: Days Late is `DateDiff("d", [Delivery Due], [Delivered On])`.
Only where `Days Late > 0` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Unpaid invoices

Invoices for orders delivered and not yet paid, the oldest due date first, with the days overdue. Below nought means it is not due yet.

From Sales Orders, Customers. Shows Invoice No, Order, Customer, Kind, Delivered On, Invoice Due, Invoice Amount, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Invoice Due], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Delivered` and `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Finished goods in stock

Products on the shelf, with what they are worth at cost and at price.

From Products. Shows Category, Code, Product, In Stock, Stock Level, Value at Cost, Value at Price.
Calculated: Value at Cost is `Round([In Stock] * ([Material Cost] + [Labour Minutes] / 60 * 21), 2)`; Value at Price is `Round([In Stock] * [Price], 2)`.
Only where `In Stock > 0`.

#### Sales by month

Goods delivered in each month, after discounts and without delivery fees.

From Sales Orders, Sales Lines. Shows Month, Items, Sales.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Delivered On], "yyyy-mm")`; Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Delivered`.

#### Sales by product

What each product has sold, the biggest seller first.

From Sales Lines, Products, Sales Orders. Shows Category, Product, Items, Sales.
Calculated: Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Delivered`.

#### Sales by customer

What each customer has bought, the biggest first, with how many order lines.

From Customers, Sales Orders, Sales Lines. Shows Customer, Kind, Order Lines, Sales.
Calculated: Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Delivered`.

#### Quotes awaiting an answer

Quotes sent and not yet accepted or declined, the oldest first, with the days left before their prices run out. Ring these customers.

From Quotes, Customers. Shows Quote No, Customer, Kind, Quote Date, Valid Until, Days Left, Total.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Valid Until])`.
Only where `Status = Sent`.

#### Quote results by month

How many quotes were sent each month and what became of them, with their value before VAT: how many turn into work.

From Quotes. Shows Month, Status, Quotes, Value.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Quote Date], "yyyy-mm")`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Suppliers, Material Purchases, Materials, Purchase Lines, Material Movements, Products, Bill of Materials, Makers, Customers, Sales Orders, Sales Lines, Quotes, Quote Lines, Time Sheets, Work Orders, Work Order Materials, Stock Movements. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Costed bill of materials

A page for each product listing its materials and their cost, with the total material cost.

From the query Costed bill of materials, a group for each Product: Material, Quantity, Unit, Unit Cost, Line Cost, with the total of Line Cost.

#### Product margins

Every product with its price, costs and margin, for setting prices and deciding what to push.

From the query Product margins: Code, Product, Price, Material Cost, Labour Cost, Margin, Margin %.

#### Production plan

The open work orders for each maker in the order they are planned to start, for the Monday meeting and the workshop wall.

From the query Open work orders, a group for each Maker: Work Order, Product, Quantity, Status, Planned Start, Due Date, Days Left, with the count of Work Order.

#### Shortages for buying

The materials short for planned work, by supplier, for the buyer to order first.

From the query Material shortages, a group for each Supplier: Code, Material, Unit, Allocated, In Stock, On Order, Short By.

#### Reorder list

Materials at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with how much to order.

From the query Materials to reorder, a group for each Supplier: Code, Material, Unit, Free Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity.

#### Delivery schedule

Orders to deliver in the next two weeks and those late, for planning the van.

From the query Orders to deliver: Order, Customer, Kind, Order Date, Delivery Due, Days Left, Goods, with the total of Goods.

#### Monthly sales

Sales for each month, with a total.

From the query Sales by month: Month, Items, Sales, with the total of Items, total of Sales.

#### Quotes to chase

The quotes waiting for an answer, with what they are worth, for a phone round on Friday afternoon.

From the query Quotes awaiting an answer: Quote No, Customer, Kind, Quote Date, Valid Until, Days Left, Total, with the total of Total.

#### Invoices due

What each customer owes, invoice by invoice, with the due dates and days overdue, for chasing payment.

From the query Unpaid invoices, a group for each Customer: Invoice No, Order, Delivered On, Invoice Due, Days Overdue, Invoice Amount, with the total of Invoice Amount.

#### Hours by maker

Each maker's booked hours and their cost month by month, with totals.

From the query Maker hours by month, a group for each Maker: Month, Hours, Cost, with the total of Hours, total of Cost.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Quote

The quotation sent for made-to-order work: the customer's name and address, each piece with its price, trade discount and VAT, the delivery, the total, how long the prices hold, and a place to sign to accept. It prints for quotes still Sent, waiting for an answer; any other prints from the Quotes form. One for each record of Quotes, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Quotation {Number}
- Fields: Prepared for, Quote number, For the attention of, Date, Address, Prices held until, Town, Postcode
- Words: Thank you for asking us to quote.
- Words: Thank you for asking us to quote. What you asked for: {Notes}
- Lines from Quote Lines: Code, Description, Qty, Each, Discount %, Net, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Goods, Delivery, Net total, VAT, Total
- Words: Each piece is made to order in our workshop from solid timber, so no two are quite alike. The price includes finishing and, where shown, delivery and carrying in; it holds until {Valid Until}. To go ahead, sign below and send this back, or reply to us by e-mail quoting {Number}, and we will confirm a delivery date. Made-to-order pieces are made for you and are not returnable unless faulty.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}
- Signed by: Accepted for the customer, For the workshop

#### Invoice

The VAT invoice that goes with a delivery: the invoice number and tax point, each line with its discount and VAT rate, the goods, delivery, VAT and total due, and how to pay while it is owed, or the day it was paid. It prints from Sales Orders, for the orders delivered and given an invoice number only. One for each record of Sales Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: VAT invoice {Invoice No}
- Fields: Invoice to, Invoice number, For the attention of, Invoice date (tax point), Address, Our order, Town, Delivered, Postcode, Payment due
- Lines from Sales Lines: Code, Description, Qty, Each, Trade discount %, Net, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Goods, Delivery, Net total, VAT, Total due
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Please quote {Invoice No} with your payment. By bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: Paid in full on {Paid On}. Thank you. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Delivery note

Goes in the van with an order: what is being delivered, without prices, where to, a phone number for the driver, and two places to sign. It prints for open orders, those still to go out: print it the day before the delivery. One for each record of Sales Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Delivery note DN-{ID}
- Fields: Deliver to, Our order, Contact, Ordered, Address, Due, Town, Delivered, Postcode, Phone
- Words: Notes: {Notes}
- Lines from Sales Lines: Code, Description, Pieces
- Totals: Pieces in all
- Words: Please check every piece before you sign. Solid timber marks easily in transit: tell us within 48 hours of any damage, with a photograph, and we will put it right. Wax and oil finishes need a few days to harden fully, so keep hot dishes and wet glasses off them for the first week.
- Signed by: Received in good order by, Delivered by

#### Purchase order

Sent to a timber merchant or a fittings supplier: what to send, at what price, and when it is wanted, with the workshop's delivery address. It prints for orders still Ordered; one received prints from the Material Purchases form. One for each record of Material Purchases, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Purchase order {Number}
- Fields: To, Order number, For the attention of, Date, Address, Deliver by, Town, Postcode, Received
- Lines from Purchase Lines: Our code, Description, Unit, Quantity, Price, Amount
- Totals: Total before VAT
- Words: Please deliver to {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}, on a weekday between 8 and 4. Timber to be dry, straight and free of shakes; we may refuse boards that are not. Quote {Number} on your delivery note and your invoice.
- Signed by: Ordered by

#### Statement

Sent to each trade account at the start of the month: the invoices not yet paid, oldest first, with the days each is overdue and the balance as it builds up to what is owed. It prints for shops and designers only, not the public, who pay on delivery. One for each record of Customers, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Statement of account
- Fields: Account, Account type, For the attention of, Days to pay, Address, Town, Postcode
- Lines from Sales Orders: Invoice, Date, Due, Days overdue, Amount, Balance
- Totals: Statement date, Invoices unpaid, Balance owing
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} If you have paid in the last few days, thank you, and please ignore this. Bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}.
- Words: Nothing is owed on your account today. Thank you.

#### Works order

The sheet for the bench: what to make and how many, for whom, when to start and finish, the standard hours, the customer's wishes, and the list of materials to take from stock, with places to sign when it is made and checked. It prints for work orders Planned or In progress; the order and customer show only for made-to-order work. One for each record of Work Orders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Works order {Number}
- Fields: Code, Make, How many, Given to, Start, Finish by, For order, Customer, Standard hours, Status, Started, Finished
- Words: Instructions: {Instructions}
- Lines from Work Order Materials: Code, Material, Unit, Take from stock
- Words: Take the materials listed from the racks before you start, and tell the workshop lead of anything short or not up to grade. Book your hours to {Number} on the time sheet each day. When the last piece is finished and checked, sign below and put it on the finished goods shelf with this sheet.
- Signed by: Made by, Checked by

### Starting empty

Start with Business: your own name, address, VAT number and bank details, which every document prints. Then Suppliers, then Materials with their units, costs and reorder levels, then Products, and then the Bill of Materials for each product. Fill in each product's Material Cost from the Costed bill of materials query. Add your Makers and Customers. After that, Sales Orders and their lines come in as you trade, Work Orders are raised for them, and the makers book Time Sheets as they work. Keep In Stock, On Order and Allocated up to date as deliveries arrive and work starts, or count once a month and correct them.

### Making it yours

- For a bakery or candle maker, change the units to kilogram and gram, make Quantity in Bill of Materials hold small amounts, and add a Batch Yield field to Products for how many one batch makes.
- Record finishes and options: add Finish and Size fields to Sales Lines for made-to-order pieces, and copy them to the work order.
- Track offcuts and waste: add a Waste Percent field to Bill of Materials and use it in the Costed bill of materials query.
- Sell abroad without VAT: give the customer a Tax Rate of their own, and copy it to the order lines instead of the product's for exports.
- Take deposits on commissions: add Deposit and Deposit Paid On fields to Sales Orders, and a query for orders waiting for one.
- Plan by machine as well as maker: add a Machines table and a Machine field to Work Orders, then group the production plan by it.
- Keep batch or lot numbers for traceability: add a Batch field to Material Movements and Stock Movements.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print an invoice I sent last month?**

Open Print templates, choose Invoice, and pick the order by its number or customer. Every invoiced order prints, whatever its date. To find the order, look the invoice number up in the Unpaid invoices query or the Sales Orders table.

**Why is there no Invoices table?**

The workshop invoices each order once, on delivery, so the invoice's fields sit on the sales order and its lines are the order's lines. If you invoice in parts, add an Invoices table pointing at Sales Orders, with lines of its own.

**How do I give a designer their trade discount?**

Set Trade Discount on the customer (0.1 for ten percent), and copy it to Discount on each quote and order line. The invoice shows the discount on each line.

**Where do I see how long a job really took?**

The Work order costs query lists work orders finished in the last 90 days with the standard hours beside the hours booked on time sheets, and what the labour cost.

**What does Allocated mean on a material?**

It is what is set aside for work orders that are planned but not started. Free stock is In Stock plus On Order less Allocated; when that falls to the Reorder Level the material shows on the Reorder list.

**Can I take a deposit on a commission?**

Not as the sample stands. Add Deposit and Deposit Paid On fields to Sales Orders, and take the deposit off the balance on the invoice with a total row in the Invoice print template.

**How do I start my own workshop from this?**

Make the sample empty, fill in the Business record with your own name, address and VAT number, then add your suppliers, materials, products and bills of materials, as Starting empty describes.

## Kilnside Builders

**Builder.** Enquiries, site visits, quotes, contracts, stage payments, variations, retentions, job costs and the site diary for a small building firm.

Kilnside Builders is an invented building firm in Bristol with eleven people on its own books: a contracts manager who visits and prices the work, an office manager, two crews of three who build extensions and loft conversions, a joiner and an apprentice who refit kitchens and bathrooms, and a maintenance builder on repairs. Scaffolders, roofers, a steel fabricator, an electrician, a plumber, a plasterer, a tiler, a drainage firm and a damp specialist come in as subcontractors.

Every piece of work starts as an enquiry. The contracts manager visits, measures up and sends a quote set out in sections (preliminaries, groundworks, roof, finishes and so on), each line marked as labour, materials or subcontract, with a contingency for what cannot be seen. About a third of the bigger quotes are accepted. An accepted quote becomes a job with a contract, a start date given by when a crew is free, and stages: a deposit on signing, a payment as each stage is reached, and the last on completion. Changes agreed on site are variations, priced and signed before the work is done, and charged on the next stage invoice. Five percent of each stage payment is held back as retention and released when the defects period, three or six months, is over.

Every cost is charged to its job in the Job Ledger: each week's labour of the crew, every merchant's and subcontractor's invoice, and the skips. The contract sum and each agreed variation go in the same ledger as the job's value, so the profit on a job is the ledger added up. The crew keeps a site diary every working day: the weather, who was on site, what was done, anything that held the work up.

The records cover about eighteen months up to the morning the file is made, with more enquiries in the spring and fewer over Christmas, when the firm shuts. Visits, starts and stage payments are booked for the weeks ahead, some quotes are waiting for an answer, a variation is waiting for a signature, and a few clients and subcontractors are behind with what they owe or are owed.

It suits, with small changes: An extension and loft conversion builder; A kitchen and bathroom fitter; A roofing contractor; A landscaper or groundworks firm; A shopfitter or joinery contractor; An electrical or plumbing contractor working to contract; A property maintenance firm.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Prices and amounts are before VAT throughout, and VAT is charged at the standard rate, 0.2, as it is on work to an existing home in the UK. New-build homes and some other work are charged at a different rate: change Tax Rate on those lines.
- The contract sum includes a contingency, but the firm does not keep it: work found on site is charged as variations, and the whole contingency is credited back on the completion invoice. So a job's value is the contract sum, plus variations, less the contingency.
- Retention is taken off every invoice except the deposit, and released with one invoice of Kind Retention once the defects period is over. Repairs have none.
- The Job Ledger holds a job's value as well as its costs, so that the Job profit query can add them up in one go. Contract, Variation and Contingency entries are value; Labour, Materials, Plant and Subcontract are costs.
- Labour is costed once a week, on Friday, from who was on site; this week's labour is not in the ledger until then. Office staff are not costed to jobs.
- Stage amounts are worked out when the contract is signed and must add up to the contract sum. Variations do not change them: they are charged on their own lines.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: quotes still Sent, contracts for jobs not yet Closed, variations still Proposed. Invoices and statements print for all. Any record prints from its own form, whatever it is.
- Document numbers run in date order with a new run each year. When you type a new one, look at the last number in that table and add one.

### Tutorial

#### Take an enquiry and book a visit

1. Open the Clients form. If the caller is new, press New and type their Name, Phone, E-mail and the address of the work.
2. Open the Enquiries form and press New. Choose the client, type Received On, choose the Work, write what they want in Description and how they heard of you in Source.
3. Agree a day to visit. Type it in Visit Date, choose who is going in Visited By and set Status to Visit booked.
4. Each morning open the Site visits, next 14 days query for the visits coming up, with addresses and phone numbers.
5. After the visit, write what you found in Visit Notes and set Status to Visited.

#### Price the work and send the quotation

1. Open the Quotes form and press New. Type the next Number (QUO-2026-0043 after QUO-2026-0042), choose the Enquiry and the Client, type a Title, the Quote Date and Valid Until, and set Status to Sent.
2. In Quote Lines add each line: Line (1, 2, 3 in order), Section, Kind (Labour, Materials or Subcontract), Description, Quantity, Unit, Rate and Tax Rate 0.2. End with a Contingency line of about five percent.
3. Add the lines up into Net, the VAT of each line into VAT, and type Total and Weeks on Site. Write what the price leaves out in Notes.
4. Open Print templates, choose Quotation, pick the quote and press Print or Save as PDF. Send it, and set the enquiry's Status to Quoted.
5. On Friday open the Quotes to chase report and ring round.

#### Turn an accepted quote into a contract

1. Open the quote in the Quotes form and set Status to Accepted; set the enquiry to Won.
2. Open the Jobs form and press New. Type the next Number, choose the Quote, Client and Site Manager, copy the Title and Work, and type Signed On, Contract Sum (the quote's Net), Contingency, Start Date and Finish Date. Set Status to Booked, Retention Percent and Defects Months.
3. In Job Stages add the deposit as Stage 0, then each stage with its Name, Payment Percent, Amount and Planned Finish. The amounts must add up to the contract sum.
4. Open Job Ledger and add a Contract entry for the job with the contract sum as Net.
5. Open Print templates, choose Contract, pick the job and press Print. Both sign two copies.
6. Raise the deposit invoice as the next task describes, with Kind Deposit.

#### Invoice a stage payment

1. Each Monday open the Stage payments coming up report to see which stages fall due.
2. When a stage is reached, open the job in the Jobs form, type Done On on the stage and change Current Stage.
3. Open the Invoices form and press New. Type the next Number, choose the Job, Client and Stage, set Kind to Stage, and type Invoice Date and Due Date (the date plus the client's Payment Days).
4. In Invoice Lines add the stage payment, then each variation agreed since the last invoice, then a line taking off the retention (a minus amount). On the completion invoice, add a minus line crediting back the contingency.
5. Type Gross, Retention, Net, VAT and Total on the invoice, and choose this invoice in Invoice on each variation charged.
6. Open Print templates, choose Stage invoice, pick the invoice and press Print or Save as PDF.

#### Agree a variation on site

1. Open the Variations form and press New. Type the next Number, choose the Job, type Raised On, the Description, Reason, Amount (a minus amount for work taken out) and Extra Days, and leave Status as Proposed.
2. Open Print templates, choose Variation order, pick it and press Print. The client signs before the work is done.
3. When it is signed, set Status to Agreed and type Agreed On. Add a Variation entry in Job Ledger with the amount as Net.
4. The Variations awaiting agreement query shows any still waiting for a signature.

#### Book costs and keep the diary

1. When a merchant's or subcontractor's invoice comes in, open the Job Ledger form, press New, choose the Job, the Supplier and the Kind (Materials, Plant or Subcontract), and type Entry Date, Description, Their Ref, Net, VAT and Due Date.
2. On Friday add a Labour entry for each person on each job: the Staff, Hours, and Net at their Hourly Cost.
3. At the end of each day the crew lead opens the Site Diary form, presses New, chooses the Job and types the Weather, On Site, Work Done, Problems and Visitors.
4. When you pay a bill, type Paid On. Before each payment run open the Subcontractors to pay report.
5. Open the Job costs to date query to see how a job on site is doing against its price.

#### Finish a job and release the retention

1. On the last day type Completed On on the job, set Status to Defects period and Current Stage to Finished, and type Retention Due (the completion date plus the defects months).
2. Raise the completion invoice with the contingency credit, and add a Contingency entry in Job Ledger with the contingency as a minus Net.
3. Each month open the Retentions held report. Before a retention is due, visit, put right anything on the snagging list, then raise an invoice with Kind Retention for the total held.
4. Type Retention Released On on the job and set Status to Closed. The Job profit report then shows the job's final margin.

#### See who owes what and send statements

1. Open the Invoices due report: every unpaid invoice by client, with days overdue.
2. When money comes in, open the invoice in the Invoices form and type Paid On.
3. At the month end open Print templates and choose Statement: each lists the client's unpaid invoices and what they owe. Choose the clients who owe something and press Print or Save as PDF.
4. The Contract account report shows each job's contract sum, invoiced, retention held, paid and owing.

### Queries

#### Enquiries to follow up

Enquiries not yet rung back, waiting for a visit, or visited and waiting for a quote, the oldest first, with how many days each has waited.

From Enquiries, Clients. Shows Received On, Client, Phone, Work, Description, Status, Visit Date, Days Waiting.
Calculated: Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Received On], Date())`.
Only where `Status In ("New", "Visit booked", "Visited")`.

#### Site visits, next 14 days

Visits booked for the next fortnight, with the address, phone number and who is going.

From Enquiries, Clients, Staff. Shows Visit Date, Visiting, Client, Address, City, Postcode, Phone, Work, Description, Days Ahead.
Calculated: Visiting is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Ahead is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Visit Date])`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 14` and `Status = Visit booked`.

#### Quotes awaiting an answer

Quotes sent and not yet accepted or declined, the oldest first, with the days since they went.

From Quotes, Clients. Shows Quote No, Client, Phone, Title, Quote Date, Valid Until, Days Since, Total.
Calculated: Days Since is `DateDiff("d", [Quote Date], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Sent`.

#### Quote success by work

For each kind of work, how many quotes were accepted, declined, expired or are still out, and their value: where the firm wins work.

From Quotes, Enquiries. Shows Work, Status, Quotes, Value.

#### Jobs by stage

Jobs booked and on site, with the stage each has reached, its site manager and the days left to the planned finish (below nought means late).

From Jobs, Clients, Staff. Shows Job, Client, Title, Status, Current Stage, Site Manager, Start Date, Finish Date, Days to Finish.
Calculated: Site Manager is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days to Finish is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Finish Date])`.
Only where `Status In ("Booked", "On site")`.

#### Stage payments due

Stages not yet reached that should be in the next 30 days, or are late, with the payment each brings: the money coming in.

From Job Stages, Jobs, Clients. Shows Job, Client, Stage, Planned Finish, Days Left, Amount.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Planned Finish])`.
Only where `Days Left <= 30` and `Done On Is Null`.

#### Invoiced against contract

For each job, the contract sum beside the work invoiced so far before VAT (variations included, retention not taken off), the retention still held, and what has been billed with VAT, paid and is owed.

From Jobs, Invoices. Shows Job, Title, Status, Contract Sum, Work Invoiced, Retention Held, Billed with VAT, Paid, Owing.
Calculated: Work Invoiced is `IIf([Kind] = "Retention", 0, [Gross])`; Retention Held is `IIf(Nz([Retention Released On], "") = "", [Retention], 0)`; Paid is `IIf(Nz([Paid On], "") = "", 0, [Total])`; Owing is `IIf(Nz([Paid On], "") = "", [Total], 0)`.

#### Unpaid invoices

Invoices not yet paid, by due date, with the days overdue (below nought means not due yet).

From Invoices, Jobs, Clients. Shows Invoice No, Client, Job, Kind, Invoice Date, Due Date, Total, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Variations by job

Every variation, job by job, with its reason, amount, extra days and whether it was agreed.

From Variations, Jobs, Clients. Shows Job, Client, Variation, Raised On, Description, Reason, Amount, Extra Days, Status, Agreed On.

#### Variations awaiting agreement

Variations written up and not yet signed by the client. Get these signed before the work is done.

From Variations, Jobs, Clients. Shows Variation, Job, Client, Phone, Raised On, Description, Amount, Extra Days, Days Waiting.
Calculated: Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Raised On], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Proposed`.

#### Job profit

Each finished job's value (contract, variations, contingency credited back) beside its labour, materials and subcontract costs, and the margin.

From Jobs, Job Ledger. Shows Job, Title, Work, Completed On, Value, Labour, Materials, Subcontract, Costs, Margin.
Calculated: Value is `IIf(([Kind] = "Contract" Or [Kind] = "Variation" Or [Kind] = "Contingency"), [Net], 0)`; Labour is `IIf([Kind] = "Labour", [Net], 0)`; Materials is `IIf([Kind] = "Materials" Or [Kind] = "Plant", [Net], 0)`; Subcontract is `IIf([Kind] = "Subcontract", [Net], 0)`; Costs is `IIf(([Kind] = "Contract" Or [Kind] = "Variation" Or [Kind] = "Contingency"), 0, [Net])`; Margin is `IIf(([Kind] = "Contract" Or [Kind] = "Variation" Or [Kind] = "Contingency"), [Net], 0 - [Net])`.
Only where `Status In ("Defects period", "Closed")`.

#### Job costs to date

The same for jobs on site: the value so far against the costs so far. The margin is only fair once the job is near its end.

From Jobs, Job Ledger. Shows Job, Title, Current Stage, Value, Labour, Materials, Subcontract, Margin So Far.
Calculated: Value is `IIf(([Kind] = "Contract" Or [Kind] = "Variation" Or [Kind] = "Contingency"), [Net], 0)`; Labour is `IIf([Kind] = "Labour", [Net], 0)`; Materials is `IIf([Kind] = "Materials" Or [Kind] = "Plant", [Net], 0)`; Subcontract is `IIf([Kind] = "Subcontract", [Net], 0)`; Margin So Far is `IIf(([Kind] = "Contract" Or [Kind] = "Variation" Or [Kind] = "Contingency"), [Net], 0 - [Net])`.
Only where `Status = On site`.

#### Retentions due for release

Finished jobs still in their defects period, with when the retention can be released and how much is held. Book the snagging visit before the date.

From Jobs, Clients, Invoices. Shows Job, Client, Title, Completed On, Retention Due, Days to Release, Retention Held.
Calculated: Days to Release is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Retention Due])`.
Only where `Status = Defects period`.

#### Subcontractors unpaid bills

Subcontractors' invoices not yet paid, by subcontractor and due date, with what to pay and the days overdue.

From Job Ledger, Suppliers, Jobs. Shows Subcontractor, Trade, Job, Their Ref, Bill Date, Due Date, Net, VAT, To Pay, Days Overdue.
Calculated: To Pay is `Round([Net] + Nz([VAT]), 2)`; Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Kind = Subcontract` and `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Labour by person, last 4 weeks

The hours each person was costed to jobs over the last four weeks, and what that cost.

From Job Ledger, Staff. Shows Name, Trade, Crew, Hours, Cost.
Calculated: Name is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Kind = Labour` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 27`.

#### Site diary, last 3 weeks

The diary for every job over the last three weeks, newest first.

From Site Diary, Jobs. Shows Job, Title, Diary Date, Weather, On Site, Work Done, Problems, Visitors.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 20`.

#### Invoiced by month

Work invoiced each month, with the retention held and the VAT, retention releases left out.

From Invoices. Shows Month, Invoices, Work Invoiced, Retention Held, VAT.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Invoice Date], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Kind <> "Retention"`.

#### Costs by month

Costs charged to jobs each month by kind: labour, materials, plant and subcontract.

From Job Ledger. Shows Month, Kind, Cost.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Entry Date], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Kind In ("Labour", "Materials", "Plant", "Subcontract")`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Clients, Staff, Suppliers, Enquiries, Quotes, Quote Lines, Jobs, Job Stages, Variations, Invoices, Invoice Lines, Job Ledger, Site Diary. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Jobs on the go

The jobs booked and on site with their stage and finish date, for the Monday meeting.

From the query Jobs by stage: Job, Client, Title, Status, Current Stage, Site Manager, Start Date, Finish Date, Days to Finish, with the count of Job.

#### Quotes to chase

Quotes waiting for an answer, with phone numbers, for a round of calls.

From the query Quotes awaiting an answer: Quote No, Client, Phone, Title, Quote Date, Valid Until, Days Since, Total, with the total of Total.

#### Stage payments coming up

Stage payments due in the next month, with a total: the cash coming in.

From the query Stage payments due: Job, Client, Stage, Planned Finish, Days Left, Amount, with the total of Amount.

#### Invoices due

Unpaid invoices by client, with days overdue and a total for each.

From the query Unpaid invoices, a group for each Client: Invoice No, Job, Kind, Invoice Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, Total, with the total of Total.

#### Contract account

Each job's contract sum, what has been invoiced, the retention held, paid and owing.

From the query Invoiced against contract: Job, Title, Status, Contract Sum, Work Invoiced, Retention Held, Billed with VAT, Paid, Owing, with the total of Work Invoiced, total of Retention Held, total of Owing.

#### Job profit

Finished jobs with their value, costs and margin, and the totals.

From the query Job profit: Job, Title, Completed On, Value, Labour, Materials, Subcontract, Margin, with the total of Value, total of Costs, total of Margin.

#### Variations register

Every variation by job, with the total each job has moved by.

From the query Variations by job, a group for each Job: Variation, Raised On, Description, Reason, Status, Extra Days, Amount, with the total of Amount.

#### Retentions held

The retention held on each job in its defects period, and when it is due.

From the query Retentions due for release: Job, Client, Title, Completed On, Retention Due, Days to Release, Retention Held, with the total of Retention Held.

#### Subcontractors to pay

Subcontractors' unpaid bills, a section for each, for the payment run.

From the query Subcontractors unpaid bills, a group for each Subcontractor: Job, Their Ref, Bill Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, To Pay, with the total of To Pay.

#### Site diary

The last three weeks' diary, a section for each job.

From the query Site diary, last 3 weeks, a group for each Job: Diary Date, Weather, On Site, Work Done, Problems, Visitors, with the count of Diary Date.

#### Monthly invoicing

Work invoiced each month with retention and VAT, and the totals.

From the query Invoiced by month: Month, Invoices, Work Invoiced, Retention Held, VAT, with the total of Work Invoiced, total of VAT.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Quotation

The quote sent after a site visit: the work in sections with each line's quantity, rate and amount, the price before and with VAT, how long it holds, what it leaves out, and a place for the client to sign. The lines come in their sections, each with its subtotal. It prints for quotes still Sent; any other prints from the Quotes form. One for each record of Quotes, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Quotation {Number}
- Fields: Prepared for, Quote number, Address of the work, Date, Town, Price holds until, Postcode, Weeks on site, about, The work
- Words: Thank you for having us round. This is our price for the work below, as we discussed on site.
- Words: Thank you for having us round. This is our price for the work below, as we discussed on site. {Notes}
- Lines from Quote Lines: Section, Description, Qty, Unit, Rate, Amount, VAT
- Totals: Price before VAT, VAT, Price with VAT
- Words: The price is fixed for the work described. Where there is a contingency line, it is a sum held for work nobody can see before we start, such as rotten timber or a drain in the way; any such work is priced and agreed with you first as a variation, and the contingency is credited back on the final invoice. Larger work is paid by stages as it goes, a deposit when the contract is signed and then a payment as each stage is reached, as the contract sets out. Repairs are invoiced when they are finished.
- Words: Not included unless listed: planning and building control fees, the party wall surveyor, floor coverings, decorating, and moving gas or electricity meters. To go ahead, sign below and send it back, and we will draw up the contract with a start date.
- Signed by: Accepted by the client, For the builder

#### Contract

The building contract for a job, in plain words: the parties, the works, the price and the contingency, the stage payments as a table, start and finish, variations, retention, defects, the site, insurance, ending the contract and the right to cancel, with signatures. The contingency and retention clauses are worded for what the contract holds. It prints for live contracts (every job not yet Closed), repairs included. It is a starting point: have it checked by someone who knows the law where you work. One for each record of Jobs, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Building contract {Number}
- Fields: The client, Contract number, Address of the works, Date of this contract, Town, Our quotation, Postcode, Contract sum, before VAT, Start, Finish, about
- Words: THIS CONTRACT is made on {Signed On} between {Business.Name} of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} ("the Builder") and {Client.Name} of {Client.Address}, {Client.City} {Client.Postcode} ("the Client").
- Words: 1. The works. The Builder will carry out the works described in quotation {Quote.Number}, {Title}, at the Client's property above. The work will be done with care and skill, with materials of the kind described in the quotation, and to meet the building regulations and any planning permission for it.
- Words: 2. The price. The contract sum is {Contract Sum} plus VAT at the rate in force when each invoice is raised. It includes a contingency of {Contingency} for work that cannot be seen before the works start. The contingency is not spent by the Builder on its own account: work it was meant for is agreed as a variation under clause 5, and the whole contingency is credited to the Client on the final invoice.
- Words: 2. The price. The contract sum is {Contract Sum} plus VAT at the rate in force when each invoice is raised. It holds no contingency: any work found once the works start is agreed as a variation under clause 5.
- Words: 3. Stage payments. The Builder will invoice the payments below as each stage is reached. Each invoice after the deposit carries any variations agreed since the last one, less the retention in clause 6. The Client will pay each invoice within {Client.Payment Days} days of its date. If a payment is late the Builder may stop work, after giving seven days' notice in writing, until it is paid.
- Lines from Job Stages: Stage, Payment due when, Percent, Amount before VAT, Expected
- Totals: Contract sum, before VAT
- Words: 4. Start and finish. The Builder will start on {Start Date} and expects to finish by {Finish Date}. The Builder will tell the Client as soon as anything will hold the work up, such as bad weather, a change asked for by the Client, a problem found once work has started, or materials that cannot be had. The finish date moves by the time lost.
- Words: 5. Variations. Any change to the works, whether the Client asks for it or it is found to be needed once work has started, is written on a variation order with its price and any change to the finish date, and signed by both before the work is done. Only work needed at once to keep the building safe or dry may be done first, and it is then written up within two working days.
- Words: 6. Retention. The Client may hold back {Retention Percent} percent of each invoice after the deposit. The amount held is released {Defects Months} months after the works are finished, once any defects reported in that time have been put right.
- Words: 6. Retention. Nothing is held back from the invoices under this contract.
- Words: 7. Defects. For {Defects Months} months after the works are finished the Builder will come back and put right, free of charge, any fault in the work or in materials the Builder supplied, when the Client reports it in writing. This does not cover fair wear and tear, damage done by others, or the hairline cracks of new plaster and timber drying out, which are filled at the end of the period.
- Words: 8. The site. The Client will give access during working hours, 8 until 5 on weekdays, and the use of water and electricity. The Builder will protect the parts of the house not being worked on, keep the site tidy and safe, and take away the waste.
- Words: 9. Insurance and permissions. The Builder holds public liability insurance and insures the works until they are handed over. The Client will tell their home insurer about the works before they start, and is responsible for planning permission and any party wall notices unless the quotation says otherwise.
- Words: 10. Ending the contract. If either side seriously breaks this contract and does not put it right within fourteen days of being asked in writing, the other may end it. The Builder is then paid for the work properly done and the materials bought for the works up to that day.
- Words: 11. Changing your mind. Where this contract is signed at the Client's home, the Client may cancel it within fourteen days of signing, without giving a reason, and any deposit is repaid in full, unless the Client asked for work to start within those fourteen days.
- Signed by: Signed for the Client, Signed for the Builder

#### Stage invoice

The VAT invoice for a deposit, a stage, completion or the retention release: the stage payment, the variations agreed since the last invoice, the contingency credited at the end, the retention taken off, the VAT and the total due, with how to pay while it is owed or the day it was paid. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: VAT invoice {Number}
- Fields: Invoice to, Invoice number, Address, Invoice date (tax point), Town, Payment due, Postcode, Invoice for, Contract, Contract sum, The works
- Lines from Invoice Lines: No, Description, Amount, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Amount before VAT, VAT, Total due
- Words: Retention held on this invoice: {Retention}, released after the defects period.
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Please quote {Number} with your payment, by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: Paid in full on {Paid On}. Thank you. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Variation order

A change to a contract for the client to sign before the work is done: what changes, why, what it adds to or takes off the price, and the extra working days when there are any. It prints for variations still Proposed; one agreed prints from the Variations form. One for each record of Variations, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Variation order {Number}
- Fields: Client, Variation number, Address of the works, Date raised, Contract, Reason, The works, Status, Agreed
- Words: Under clause 5 of contract {Job.Number}, the works are changed as follows:
- Words: {Description}
- Totals: Change to the contract sum, before VAT, VAT, Change with VAT, Extra working days
- Words: Once both sides have signed, the work goes ahead and the amount is added to the next stage invoice.
- Words: This takes work out of the contract: once both sides have signed, the amount comes off the next stage invoice.
- Words: The finish date moves by the extra working days shown. Everything else in the contract stays as it was.
- Words: The finish date does not change. Everything else in the contract stays as it was.
- Signed by: Agreed by the Client, For the Builder

#### Statement

Each client's unpaid invoices, oldest first, with the balance as it builds up to what is owed. A client who owes nothing gets a statement that says so. One for each record of Clients, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Statement of account
- Fields: Client, Days to pay, Address, Town, Postcode
- Lines from Invoices: Invoice, Date, Due, Contract, For, Amount, Balance
- Totals: Statement date, Invoices unpaid, Balance owing
- Words: Retention held under your contract is not shown as owing until it is invoiced at the end of the defects period. If you have paid in the last few days, thank you, and please ignore this.
- Words: Bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}.
- Words: Nothing is owed on your account today. Retention held under a contract is invoiced at the end of its defects period. Thank you.

### Starting empty

Start with Business: your firm's name, address, VAT number, bank details and payment terms, which every document prints. Then Staff with their crews and hourly costs, and Suppliers: your merchants, hire firms and subcontractors. Clients and Enquiries come in as people ring; Quotes and their lines follow the site visits; Jobs, their stages, invoices, variations, ledger entries and the site diary follow when a quote is accepted.

### Making it yours

- Hold retention on the deposit too, or release half of it at completion: add a second Retention invoice and change the contract's clause 6 to match.
- Keep the subcontractors' own retention: add a Retention field to Job Ledger for what you hold back from them, and a query of what you owe them later.
- Value work by applications for payment instead of fixed stages: add a Valuations table (job, date, value of work done) and invoice the difference from the last one.
- Track plant and tools: add a Plant table and a Plant field to Job Ledger for hired or owned machines, with a day rate.
- Record snags: add a Snags table pointing at Jobs, with what, when reported and when put right, and print it for the defects visit.
- Work on new builds: give those lines a Tax Rate of nought, and add a Plot field to Jobs.
- Plan the crews: add a Crew field to Jobs and a query of start and finish dates by crew to see who is free when.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print the contract for a new job?**

Open Print templates, choose Contract, pick the job and press Print or Save as PDF. Its stage payments come from Job Stages, so add those first.

**How much is a job really making?**

Open the Job profit query for finished jobs, or Job costs to date for jobs on site. Both add up the Job Ledger: the value (contract, variations, contingency credited back) less labour, materials, plant and subcontract.

**Why is the completion invoice smaller than the stage payment?**

It credits back the contingency held in the contract sum, and takes off the retention. The variations agreed during the job are charged above those lines.

**What is the difference between Finish Date and Completed On?**

Finish Date is the date planned when the contract was signed. Completed On is the day the work was actually finished. The Site Diary usually says why they differ.

**How do I see what we owe subcontractors?**

Open the Subcontractors unpaid bills query, or print the Subcontractors to pay report before the payment run. Type Paid On in the Job Ledger as you pay.

**Can I keep several sites for one client?**

As it stands the address of the work is the client's address. Add Site Address, Site City and Site Postcode fields to Jobs for clients with more than one property, and print those in the Contract.

**How do I start with my own firm?**

Make the sample empty and fill in the Business record with your name, address, VAT number and bank details. Then add your Staff, your Suppliers and subcontractors, and take enquiries as they come.

## Copperbeech Motors

**Used car dealer.** Stock, preparation costs, test drives, sales, finance, warranties and part-exchanges for a used car dealer.

Copperbeech Motors is an invented independent used car dealer in south-east London, with about forty cars on the forecourt, a sales manager who owns the business, three sales executives, a workshop technician, a valeter and an administrator. It buys most of its cars at two auctions twice a week, some from the trade, and takes about a third of its customers' old cars in part-exchange.

The sample holds fifteen months of trading, made up a day at a time. Each car is prepared before it goes on sale: always a valet, often a service, repairs where the inspection finds them, and an MOT when the old one is close to running out. Its asking price is set from what it cost, and comes down when it has stood for a month. Customers test drive; some buy, pay a deposit, and pay the rest at handover a few days later, about two in five with finance from one of two lenders, who pay the dealer a commission. Every car leaves with a warranty: three months included, or a longer plan bought. The part-exchange comes into stock the day the new car leaves.

Every car and make in it is invented. The makes and models are made-up names, and every registration begins ZZ, which is never issued, so none is a real car's.

It suits, with small changes: A used car or van dealer; A motorcycle dealer; A car supermarket or a dealer's used car site; A specialist or classic car dealer; A caravan or motorhome dealer; A plant or machinery dealer selling used stock.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- The margin in the queries is the car's own: what it sold for, less what it cost, the buying fee, its preparation and the VAT on the margin. Warranty profit and finance commission are counted in their own queries, and overheads (wages, rent, advertising) are not in this database.
- VAT on used cars: most are sold under the margin scheme, where VAT is a sixth of the margin, paid by the dealer and not shown on the invoice. A VAT-qualifying car shows its VAT on the invoice, but because the dealer reclaims the VAT it paid when buying, what it owes comes to the same sixth of the margin, so the margin query treats both alike. Check the rules for your own country with your accountant.
- Prep Cost on a car is kept by hand: add each job's cost when you enter it in Preparation. The query Preparation by vehicle puts the two side by side.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: invoices for sales handed over, agreements for sales not cancelled, valuation letters for offers still open, certificates for warranties still running, and window cards for cars For sale. Any record prints from its own form, whatever its Status.
- A part-exchange comes into stock as a new record in Vehicles, with its allowance as the purchase price and no supplier. Its valuation points at the sale it was taken against and at the new stock record.
- Numbers (orders, invoices, certificates, valuations, stock numbers) are typed in date order, a new run each year: look at the last one in the form and add one.

### Tutorial

#### Buy a car and put it on sale

1. Open the Vehicles form and press New. Type the Registration, the next Stock No, the Make, Model, Year, Mileage and the other details from the registration document.
2. Choose Auction or Trade in Source and the seller in Supplier. Type the Bought On date, the Purchase Price and, from an auction, the Buying Fee. Leave Status as In preparation.
3. Add each preparation job in the Preparation form as it is done (choose the car in Vehicle, then the Kind, Description, Done By and Cost), and add its cost to the car's Prep Cost.
4. Add the car's features in the Vehicle Features form, one record each.
5. When it is ready, type its First Asking Price and Asking Price and set Status to For sale. Open the print template Window card, choose the car and press Print.

#### Book a test drive and follow it up

1. Find the customer in the Customers form, or press New and type their name, phone and e-mail.
2. Open the Test Drives form and press New. Choose the car in Vehicle, the customer in Customer and yourself in Staff, and type the day and time in When. Outcome starts as Booked.
3. After the drive, set Outcome to Bought, Thinking it over, Not for them or Bought elsewhere, and type what they said in Notes.
4. Each morning, run the query Test drives that did not buy, or print the report Test drive follow-ups, and call the people on it.

#### Value a part-exchange

1. Open the Part Exchanges form and press New. Type the next Number, choose the customer and yourself in Valued By, and type the car's details, its Condition and what you noted.
2. Type the Guide Value from your price guide, the allowance you offer in Offered, and Valid Until (usually a week). Outcome starts as Open.
3. Open the print template Part-exchange valuation, choose the valuation and press Print or Save as PDF to send the letter.

#### Take a deposit and agree a sale

1. Open the Sales form and press New. Type the next Order No, choose the car in Vehicle, the customer and the Salesperson, and type Agreed On and the Handover date.
2. In the sale's lines below, add the car (Kind Vehicle, the description and the Amount), the warranty and any extras, with each line's Tax Rate. Type the Price, the Total of the lines and the VAT they hold.
3. Type the Part-Ex Allowance, the Deposit taken and any Finance Amount, and the Balance left to pay. Leave Status as Reserved and set the car's Status to Reserved.
4. Where finance is used, open the Finance Agreements form and press New: choose the sale and the lender and type the terms and the commission. Set its Status to Approved.
5. Open the print template Sales agreement, choose the sale, print two copies and sign them with the customer.

#### Hand a car over

1. Run the query Deposits on unsold vehicles to see which cars go out today and what each customer still owes.
2. On the sale in the Sales form, type the next Invoice No, check the Handover date and set Status to Completed. Set the car's Status to Sold.
3. Open the Warranties form and press New. Type the next Certificate No, choose the sale and the plan, and type Starts, Ends and the Mileage at Start.
4. Open the print templates Vehicle sales invoice and Warranty certificate in turn, choose the sale or the warranty, and press Print.
5. If a car came in part-exchange, add it to the Vehicles form with Source Part-exchange and the allowance as its Purchase Price, then set the valuation's Outcome to Accepted and choose the new car in Taken In.
6. When the lender pays, set the finance agreement's Status to Paid out and type Paid Out On.

#### Review the stock each week

1. Print the report Aged stock. For each car, decide whether to reduce it, advertise it or send it back to auction.
2. To reduce a car, type its new Asking Price in the Vehicles form (keep First Asking Price as it was) and print its Window card again.
3. Run the query Preparation by vehicle to check that each car's Prep Cost agrees with its jobs.

#### See how the month went

1. Print the report Monthly sales for cars sold, takings and gross margin by month.
2. Print the report Salesperson league for the team, and Finance commission for what the lenders paid.
3. Run the query Warranty sales by plan for the warranty profit, and print Warranty renewals to start the renewal calls.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 33 records.

### Queries

#### Stock by days in stock

Every car not yet sold, the longest in stock first, with its asking price and status. The forecourt list.

From Vehicles. Shows Stock No, Registration, Vehicle, Mileage, Fuel, Asking Price, Status, Days in Stock.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`; Days in Stock is `DateDiff("d", [Bought On], Date())`.
Only where `Status Not In ("Sold")`.

#### Stock over 60 days

Cars on sale or in preparation for more than sixty days, with what each has cost so far and the margin left at its asking price: the cars to reduce, advertise harder or send back to auction.

From Vehicles. Shows Stock No, Registration, Vehicle, Bought On, Days in Stock, Cost to Date, First Asking Price, Asking Price, Margin at Asking, Status.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`; Days in Stock is `DateDiff("d", [Bought On], Date())`; Cost to Date is `Round([Purchase Price] + Nz([Buying Fee]) + Nz([Prep Cost]), 2)`; Margin at Asking is `Round([Asking Price] - [Purchase Price] - Nz([Buying Fee]) - Nz([Prep Cost]), 2)`.
Only where `Days in Stock > 60` and `Status In ("For sale", "In preparation")`.

#### Margin per vehicle

Each car sold, the newest first: what it sold for, what it cost, the buying fee and preparation, the VAT on the margin and what is left, and how long it took to sell.

From Sales, Vehicles, Staff. Shows Handover, Stock No, Registration, Vehicle, Salesperson, Sold For, Bought For, Buying Fee, Prep Cost, VAT on Margin, Margin, Days in Stock.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`; Salesperson is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; VAT on Margin is `IIf([Sales].[Price] > [Purchase Price], Round(([Sales].[Price] - [Purchase Price]) / 6, 2), 0)`; Margin is `Round([Sales].[Price] - [Purchase Price] - Nz([Buying Fee]) - Nz([Prep Cost]) - IIf([Sales].[Price] > [Purchase Price], Round(([Sales].[Price] - [Purchase Price]) / 6, 2), 0), 2)`; Days in Stock is `DateDiff("d", [Bought On], [Handover])`.
Only where `Status = Completed`.

#### Sales by month

Cars handed over each month, with the takings and the gross margin on the cars.

From Sales, Vehicles. Shows Month, Cars Sold, Vehicle Sales, Takings, Gross Margin.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Handover], "yyyy-mm")`; Gross Margin is `Round([Sales].[Price] - [Purchase Price] - Nz([Buying Fee]) - Nz([Prep Cost]) - IIf([Sales].[Price] > [Purchase Price], Round(([Sales].[Price] - [Purchase Price]) / 6, 2), 0), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Completed`.

#### Sales by salesperson

Cars sold, takings and gross margin for each salesperson over the last twelve months, the best first.

From Sales, Staff, Vehicles. Shows Salesperson, Cars Sold, Takings, Gross Margin.
Calculated: Salesperson is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Gross Margin is `Round([Sales].[Price] - [Purchase Price] - Nz([Buying Fee]) - Nz([Prep Cost]) - IIf([Sales].[Price] > [Purchase Price], Round(([Sales].[Price] - [Purchase Price]) / 6, 2), 0), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Completed` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Deposits on unsold vehicles

Reserved cars: the deposit held, the finance and the balance still to come, by handover date. Use it each morning to get the cars ready.

From Sales, Vehicles, Customers, Staff. Shows Order No, Agreed On, Customer, Phone, Registration, Vehicle, Deposit, Finance Amount, Balance at Handover, Handover, Salesperson.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`; Salesperson is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Reserved`.

#### Test drives that did not buy

Test drives in the last thirty days that did not end in a sale, the newest first, with the customer's phone and what they said: the follow-up calls.

From Test Drives, Customers, Vehicles, Staff. Shows When, Customer, Phone, E-mail, Registration, Vehicle, Salesperson, Outcome, Notes, Days Ago.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`; Salesperson is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Days Ago is `DateDiff("d", [When], Date())`.
Only where `Outcome In ("Thinking it over", "Not for them", "Bought elsewhere")` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Test drives booked

Test drives booked for today and the next seven days, in time order.

From Test Drives, Customers, Vehicles, Staff. Shows When, Customer, Phone, Registration, Vehicle, Vehicle Status, With.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`; With is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Outcome = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 7`.

#### Warranties expiring

Warranties that run out in the next sixty days, the soonest first, with the customer's phone: who to offer a renewal or a service.

From Warranties, Warranty Plans, Sales, Customers, Vehicles. Shows Ends, Days Left, Certificate No, Plan, Customer, Phone, Registration, Vehicle, Mileage at Start.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Ends])`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 60`.

#### Finance commission by month

Finance agreements paid out each month by lender, with the amount financed and the commission earned.

From Finance Agreements, Lenders, Sales. Shows Month, Lender, Agreements, Amount Financed, Commission.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Paid Out On], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Status = Paid out`.

#### Warranty sales by plan

Warranties sold in the last twelve months by plan, with what they brought in, what they cost and the profit.

From Warranties, Warranty Plans. Shows Plan, Sold, Takings, Cost, Profit.
Calculated: Profit is `Round([Warranties].[Price] - [Warranties].[Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Recent part-exchange valuations

Valuations in the last thirty days, the newest first, with what was offered and how each ended.

From Part Exchanges, Customers, Staff. Shows Number, Valued On, Customer, Registration, Vehicle, Mileage, Guide Value, Offered, Valid Until, Outcome, Valued By.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Vehicle is `[Part Exchanges].[Year] & " " & [Part Exchanges].[Make] & " " & [Part Exchanges].[Model]`; Valued By is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Purchases by source

Cars bought in the last twelve months from auctions, the trade and part-exchange: how many, what they cost, the fees and the preparation.

From Vehicles. Shows Source, Bought, Spent, Fees, Preparation.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Preparation by vehicle

For each car still in stock, the preparation jobs and their cost beside the Prep Cost on its record, to check the two agree.

From Preparation, Vehicles. Shows Stock No, Registration, Vehicle, Status, Jobs, Cost, Prep Cost on Vehicle.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Year] & " " & [Make] & " " & [Model]`.
Only where `Status Not In ("Sold")`.

#### Preparation spend by kind

What was spent on valets, services, MOTs, repairs, tyres and bodywork in the last twelve months.

From Preparation. Shows Kind, Jobs, Cost.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Staff, Suppliers, Customers, Vehicles, Vehicle Features, Preparation, Test Drives, Sales, Sale Lines, Lenders, Finance Agreements, Warranty Plans, Warranties, Part Exchanges. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.
