### Print templates

#### Vehicle sales invoice

The invoice given at handover: the car with its registration, mileage and first registration date, the warranty and extras, the total, the part-exchange allowance, the deposit and finance taken off, and the balance paid. It says whether the car is sold under the margin scheme or is VAT qualifying, in words for that scheme, and leaves out a part-exchange, deposit or finance the sale did not have. It prints for sales with an invoice number, those handed over. One for each record of Sales, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Sales invoice {Invoice No}
- Fields: Sold to, Invoice number, Address, Date of sale, Town, Order, Postcode, Sold by
- Fields: Registration, Make, Model, First registered, Recorded mileage, Colour, Fuel, Stock number, VAT
- Lines from Sale Lines: Description, VAT %, VAT included, Amount
- Totals: Total price, Of which VAT, Less part-exchange allowance, Less deposit paid, Paid by finance, Balance paid at handover
- Words: VAT: Margin scheme. This car is sold under the margin scheme: the VAT is within the price, paid by us on our margin, and is not shown or reclaimable. Warranties are exempt from VAT; VAT on any extras is shown above.
- Words: VAT: VAT qualifying. The VAT within the price of this car is shown above, and a VAT-registered buyer may reclaim it. Warranties are exempt from VAT.
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Bank: {Business.Bank Details}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Sales agreement

The order the customer signs when the deal is agreed and the deposit paid: the parties, the car, what is bought, the deposit, finance and balance, and plainly worded terms on payment, part-exchange, finance, cancelling, handover and warranty, the deposit, part-exchange and finance clauses worded for what the sale has. It prints for every sale not cancelled. Have it checked against the law of your own country before you use it. One for each record of Sales, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Vehicle order and sales agreement {Order No}
- Fields: Buyer, Order number, Address, Date of order, Town, Handover on or about, Postcode, Phone
- Fields: Registration, Make, Model, Year, Recorded mileage, Colour, MOT until, Keys, Service history
- Lines from Sale Lines: What is bought, Amount
- Totals: Total price, Part-exchange allowance, Deposit paid today, To be paid by finance, Balance due at handover
- Words: This agreement is made on {Agreed On} between {Business.Name} of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} ("the Seller") and {Customer} of {Customer.Address}, {Customer.City} {Customer.Postcode} ("the Buyer").
- Words: 1. The vehicle. The Seller agrees to sell and the Buyer agrees to buy the vehicle described above, registration {Vehicle.Registration}, with the extras listed, for the total price above. The mileage shown is the reading on the day of this order; the Seller is not aware of anything suggesting it is wrong.
- Words: 2. Deposit. The Buyer has paid a deposit of {Deposit} today, and the Seller holds the vehicle for the Buyer until the handover date. The deposit is part of the price.
- Words: 2. Deposit. No deposit has been paid. The Seller holds the vehicle for the Buyer until the handover date.
- Words: 3. Payment. The balance due at handover is paid by bank transfer or debit card before the vehicle is driven away. The vehicle remains the Seller's property until the whole price has been paid.
- Words: 4. Part-exchange. No vehicle is taken in part-exchange on this sale.
- Words: 4. Part-exchange. Where a vehicle is taken in part-exchange, the allowance above is given on the understanding that it is the Buyer's to sell, that it is handed over in the condition and with no more than 500 miles more than when it was valued, with its keys and registration document, and that any finance owing on it has been declared. The Seller settles declared finance with the lender and takes the amount settled from the allowance.
- Words: 5. Finance. Part of the price is paid by finance. The finance agreement is between the Buyer and the lender, not the Seller. This sale depends on the lender accepting the Buyer; if it does not, either party may cancel this agreement and the deposit is returned in full.
- Words: 5. Finance. No part of the price is paid by finance.
- Words: 6. Cancelling. If the Buyer cancels for any other reason before handover, the Seller may keep from the deposit the reasonable costs it has already met for this sale, such as work done to the vehicle at the Buyer's request, and returns the rest within 14 days.
- Words: 7. Handover. The vehicle will be ready on or about {Handover}, valeted, with its keys, service records and registration document, and an MOT certificate running until {Vehicle.MOT Expiry}.
- Words: 8. Warranty. The warranty shown above starts on the day of handover. What it covers is set out on its certificate, given at handover.
- Words: 9. The Buyer's rights. Nothing in this agreement takes away any right the Buyer has in law when buying goods as a consumer, including the right to reject a vehicle that is faulty.
- Words: 10. The whole agreement. This is the whole of what has been agreed. Any change must be written down and signed by both parties.
- Signed by: For the Seller, The Buyer

#### Part-exchange valuation

The letter sent after valuing a customer's car: the car, what was noted, the allowance offered, and how long the offer stands. It prints for valuations still Open. One for each record of Part Exchanges, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Fields: To, Our reference, Address, Date, Town, Postcode
- Heading: Your part-exchange valuation
- Words: Dear {Customer.First Name},
- Words: Thank you for letting us look at your {Year} {Make} {Model}, registration {Registration}, when you visited us on {Valued On}. We have checked it over and driven it, and taken account of its {Mileage} recorded miles and its {Condition} condition.
- Words: Thank you for letting us look at your {Year} {Make} {Model}, registration {Registration}, when you visited us on {Valued On}. We have checked it over and driven it, and taken account of its {Mileage} recorded miles and its {Condition} condition. What we noted: {Notes}
- Words: We can offer you {Offered} for it as a part-exchange against any car from our stock.
- Words: This offer stands until {Valid Until}, as long as the car is in the same condition when you bring it in, with no more than 500 miles more on it, both keys if it came with two, its registration document and its service records. If there is finance owing on the car, please tell us how much: we settle it with your lender and take what we pay from the allowance.
- Words: If you have any questions, or would like to talk about a car from our stock, call us on {Business.Phone} or reply to {Business.E-mail}.
- Words: Yours sincerely,
- Words: {Valued By}, {Business.Name}

#### Warranty certificate

Given at handover with every car: the holder, the car, the plan, when it starts and ends, the claim limit, what is covered and how to claim. It prints for warranties still running. One for each record of Warranties, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Warranty certificate {Certificate No}
- Fields: Warranty holder, Certificate, Address, Plan, Postcode, Cover starts, Registration, Cover ends, Make, Mileage at start, Model, Most paid on one claim
- Words: What is covered. {Plan.Cover}
- Words: How to claim. Before any repair is started, call {Business.Name} on {Business.Phone} with this certificate's number. We will tell you where to take the car and agree the work with the garage. Repairs started without our agreement cannot be paid for.
- Words: Conditions. The car must be serviced as its maker recommends, at any garage, and the receipts kept. Wear and tear, damage from accidents, misuse or neglect, and parts that wear in normal use (tyres, brake pads and discs, clutches, wiper blades, bulbs) are not covered. The warranty stays with the car if it is sold, if you tell us. This warranty is in addition to your rights in law.
- Words: Administered by {Plan.Administered By}.
- Signed by: For the Seller

#### Window card

The card in the car's window on the forecourt: the year, make and model, its mileage and details, its key features and the price. It prints for cars For sale only. Print it again after a price change. One for each record of Vehicles, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: {Year} {Make} {Model}
- Fields: Miles, Fuel, Gearbox, Colour, Body, Doors, Owners, Service history, MOT until
- Lines from Vehicle Features: Key features
- Totals: Our price
- Words: Part-exchange welcome. Finance arranged. At least three months' warranty on every car. {Registration}, stock number {Stock No}.

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name, address and bank details, which every document prints. Then Staff (tick Sells for the sales team), Suppliers, Lenders and Warranty Plans. Then add the cars you hold in Vehicles, with their features and preparation. Customers, test drives, valuations, sales, finance agreements and warranties come in as you trade.

### Making it yours

- Sell vans or motorcycles too: add their bodies to Body, and a Payload or Engine Size field to Vehicles.
- Keep a price history: add a Price Changes table (vehicle, date, old price, new price) and a query of the cars reduced this month.
- Track where enquiries come from: add a Leads table (customer, source, vehicle asked about, date) and a query of leads by source and how many bought.
- Send cars back to auction: add a Disposals table (vehicle, date, auction, price) and a Status of Sent to auction, so slow stock leaves with its loss recorded.
- Record warranty claims: add a Claims table pointing at Warranties, with the fault, the garage and what was paid, and a query of claims against each plan.
- Hold overheads: add an Expenses table (date, kind, amount) and a monthly query beside Sales by month to see the profit after costs.
- Pay commission to the sales team: add a Commission Rate to Staff and a calculated column in Sales by salesperson.

### Questions people ask

**Why is there no VAT on most of my invoices?**

Most used cars are sold under the margin scheme: VAT is paid on your margin, not on the price, and the invoice must not show it. The invoice says so under the lines. A VAT-qualifying car, ticked in Vehicles, shows the VAT within its price.

**How do I see which cars have been in stock too long?**

Run the query Stock over 60 days, or print the report Aged stock. Change the criteria under Days in Stock (> 60) in the query designer for another number of days.

**How do I record a sale that falls through?**

Set the sale's Status to Cancelled, write in Notes when and how the deposit was returned, set the car back to For sale, and set any finance agreement and part-exchange valuation to Cancelled and Withdrawn.

**Where does the finance commission go?**

Each finance agreement holds its commission. The query Finance commission by month and the report Finance commission add it up by month and lender, counting agreements that have been paid out.

**How do I print one invoice?**

Open the Sales form on the sale and press Print, choosing Vehicle sales invoice; or open the print template from Print templates and choose the sale.

**Can I change the warranty plans?**

Yes. Edit the Warranty Plans records: the name, months, claim limit, price, cost and the Cover words that print on the certificate. Old warranties keep the price they were sold at.

**How do I find who to call about a warranty running out?**

Run the query Warranties expiring, or print the report Warranty renewals. Only call customers who have ticked Marketing Consent about offers.

## Marigold Hair and Beauty

**Salon.** Clients, the appointment book, services, commission, retail stock and gift vouchers for a salon.

For a salon, barber or beauty room that takes bookings, pays its team commission and sells a little retail over the desk. Marigold Hair and Beauty is an invented high-street salon with four stylists, a beauty therapist and a junior. It opens Tuesday to Saturday, with a late night until eight on Thursday.

The records cover the last thirteen months of the appointment book and the next six weeks. Clients come back on their own rhythm, a gents cut every few weeks and a root tint every six or so, and some stop coming. One stylist left about five months ago and most of her clients moved to the stylist who replaced her. December is the busiest month and January the quietest. A few clients cancel late or do not turn up, and the salon keeps their deposit.

Every service done is kept with the price charged, which depends on whether a junior, a stylist or a senior stylist did it, and new clients have 20 per cent off their first visit. Colour work and lash lifts need a patch test in the six months before. Retail and back-bar products are counted in and out as they are sold or used, and a weekly order goes in on Tuesday for whatever has run low. Two lines have been on back order with the supplier for the last few weeks. Gift vouchers are sold, mostly in December and before Mothering Sunday, and redeemed against bookings.

The salon is registered for VAT, and its prices, like any salon's menu, have VAT in them. Each visit paid for at the desk has a numbered receipt that lists the services and any products bought at the same time, with the VAT within each line, the deposit already paid and any gift voucher used. It prints the gift voucher itself, a commission statement for each stylist each month, and a letter confirming an appointment.

It suits, with small changes: A barber shop; A nail bar; A beauty or brow and lash studio; A massage or spa room; A dog groomer; A mobile hairdresser.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Prices are VAT inclusive. A receipt shows the VAT within each line, worked out as the price less the price divided by one plus the rate, rounded to the penny; the receipt's VAT is those added up. Change the 0.2 in Services and Products if your rate is different, or make it 0 if you are not registered for VAT.
- The services of a visit are kept twice on purpose: in Booking Services, as booked, and in Receipt Lines, as charged and printed. A receipt should not change after it is handed over, so the till keeps its own copy.
- The Appointment confirmation template prints only bookings still to come that are not cancelled, a few hundred at most, and the Gift voucher template only vouchers not yet used and still in date. Print one from the Bookings or Gift Vouchers form to get it whatever its state.
- Commission is worked out on takings with VAT in them, as many salons pay it. To pay it on takings before VAT, divide the price by 1.2 in the commission queries.
- The owner takes no commission, so she has no statements. Staff who have left keep their records with Active set to No.
- Stock is not counted by Data Files on its own: In Stock goes down as products are sold or used at the basin and up as deliveries arrive. In the sample this was worked out while the records were made; in your own salon, change In Stock when you add a sale or a delivery, or count the shelf each week.

### Tutorial

#### Book an appointment and confirm it

1. Open the Clients form. Look the client up; for someone new, press New and fill in their name, mobile, e-mail and Heard Of Us, and tick Marketing Consent only if they agree.
2. Open the Bookings form and press New. Choose the client in Client and the stylist in Staff, type the day and time in Start, and set Booked On to today and Booked Via to Phone, Online or In salon.
3. In Booking Services at the foot of the form, add each service. Type the Price from the stylist's column of the menu (the Price list report has it), taking 20 per cent off for a first visit. Add the minutes of the services together in Minutes.
4. If you take a deposit, type it in Deposit. Then open the print template Appointment confirmation from Print templates, choose the booking, and press Print or Save as PDF to send it.

#### Check tomorrow's column and the skin tests

1. Run the query Bookings next 7 days, or print the report The column, which puts each stylist's week on its own page.
2. Run Patch tests due. Call each client on it to come in for a skin test at least 48 hours before their colour or lash appointment, and when they have had it, type the day in Patch Test Date on the Clients form.

#### Take payment at the end of a visit

1. On the Bookings form, set Status to Completed and Paid By to Card, Cash or Gift voucher.
2. Open the Receipts form and press New. Type the next number in Number (the Receipts last 7 days query shows the latest), choose the booking, and type the time in Taken.
3. In Receipt Lines below, add a line for each service and each product sold, with Kind, Item, Quantity, Unit Price and Tax Rate 0.2. For each product, also add a record to Product Sales with the same receipt, so the stock and the retail commission are counted.
4. Type the Total, the VAT (each line's price less the price divided by 1.2), Net, any Deposit Paid and Voucher, and Paid Today. Open the print template Receipt, choose the receipt and press Print.

#### Sell a gift voucher and take it as payment

1. Open the Gift Vouchers form and press New. Type the next Code, today in Sold On, who is paying in Bought By, who it is for in For, the Value, and a date a year ahead in Expires.
2. Open the print template Gift voucher, choose the voucher, and print it on card.
3. When it is used, type the day in Redeemed On and choose the booking in Booking. On that visit's receipt, type the voucher's value in Voucher and its code in Voucher Code.
4. Run Vouchers outstanding to see what the salon still owes in services, soonest to expire first.

#### Order stock on Tuesday

1. Print the report Products to order. It lists every product at or below its reorder level, a page for each supplier, with the cost of the order.
2. Send each supplier its page. When the goods arrive, add a record to Stock Deliveries for each product, with the supplier's invoice number, and add the quantity to In Stock on the Products form.

#### Pay the month's commission

1. On the first of the month, print the reports Commission statement and Retail commission to see last month's services and retail by person.
2. Open the Commission Statements form and press New for each person on commission. Type the Number, choose them in Staff, and type the month (2026-09) in Month and today in Prepared On.
3. In Commission Lines below, add a line for each kind of work with what was done, the takings, the rate and the commission, and put the total in Commission Due.
4. Open the print template Commission statement, choose the statement, and print it to go with their pay. Type the pay day in Paid On.

#### Do the VAT return

1. Print the report VAT by month. Add up the three months of the VAT quarter: the VAT column is the output tax on takings, and the Net column the sales before VAT.
2. Gift vouchers sold are not in it: VAT is due when a voucher is spent, and that is in the receipt it was spent on.

| Paid Today | Currency | What the client paid at the desk: the total less the deposit and any voucher. |
| Paid By | Short text | How it was paid: Card, Cash, Gift voucher, or a voucher and card or cash for the rest. |

#### Receipt Lines

What is on each receipt: a line for each service done and each product bought at the visit. The sample has 9,193 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Receipt | Points at Receipts, required | The receipt the line is on. |
| Kind | Short text | Service or Retail. |
| Item | Short text | The service or product as printed, with the size of a product and a note of the first-visit offer. |
| Quantity | Whole number | How many: one for a service. |
| Unit Price | Currency | The price of one, VAT included, as charged. |
| Tax Rate | Number | The VAT within the price, as a fraction, from the service or product. |

#### Commission Statements

A statement for each person on commission for each month, made on the first of the next month and paid with the wages on the 7th. The sample has 60 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The statement number, a new run each year: COM-2026-0042. |
| Staff | Points at Staff, required | Who it is for. |
| Month | Short text | The month it covers, as 2026-09. |
| Prepared On | Date | The day it was made. |
| Commission Due | Currency | The commission on all its lines added up. |
| Paid On | Date | The day it was paid with the wages; empty until then. |

#### Commission Lines

The lines of each commission statement: the services done by kind, and the retail sold. The sample has 216 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Statement | Points at Commission Statements, required | The statement the line is on. |
| Line | Whole number | Its place on the statement. |
| Work | Short text | Which kind of work: a heading of the service menu, such as Colour, or Retail products sold. |
| Done | Whole number | How many services were done, or products sold. |
| Takings | Currency | What clients paid for them, VAT included. |
| Rate | Number | The commission rate for that kind of work, as a fraction. |
| Commission | Currency | The commission earned: each service's or sale's rounded to the penny, then added up. |

### Relationships

- Bookings.Client points at a record in Clients
- Bookings.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Booking Services.Booking points at a record in Bookings
- Booking Services.Service points at a record in Services
- Products.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Product Sales.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Product Sales.Client points at a record in Clients
- Product Sales.Product points at a record in Products
- Product Sales.Receipt points at a record in Receipts
- Stock Deliveries.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Stock Deliveries.Product points at a record in Products
- Gift Vouchers.Booking points at a record in Bookings
- Receipts.Booking points at a record in Bookings
- Receipt Lines.Receipt points at a record in Receipts
- Commission Statements.Staff points at a record in Staff
- Commission Lines.Statement points at a record in Commission Statements

### Queries

#### Bookings next 7 days

Every booked appointment from today to a week ahead, by time, with the client's phone number. Use it to send reminders and plan the week.

From Bookings, Clients, Staff. Shows When, Stylist, Client, Phone, Minutes, Deposit, Booked Via.
Calculated: When is `Left([Start], 10) & " " & Mid([Start], 12, 5)`; Stylist is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Away Between 0 And 7` and `Status = Booked`.

#### Takings by stylist last month

What each member of the team took in services last calendar month, and how many services they did.

From Bookings, Staff, Booking Services. Shows Stylist, Role, Services Done, Takings.
Calculated: Stylist is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Completed` and `Months Ago = 1`.

#### Service commission last month

Each service done last month by someone on commission, with the price and the commission it earns. The commission statement prints it.

From Booking Services, Bookings, Staff, Clients, Services. Shows Stylist, Day, Client, Service, Price, Rate, Commission.
Calculated: Stylist is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Day is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Commission is `Round([Price] * [Service Commission], 2)`.
Only where `Service Commission > 0` and `Status = Completed` and `Months Ago = 1`.

#### Retail commission last month

Retail each person sold last month and the commission due on it.

From Product Sales, Staff, Products. Shows Stylist, Items Sold, Retail Sales, Rate, Commission.
Calculated: Stylist is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Retail Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`; Commission is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price] * [Retail Commission], 2)`.
Only where `Retail Commission > 0` and `Months Ago = 1`.

#### Service takings by month

Service takings for each month, completed appointments only. Shows the busy and quiet months.

From Bookings, Booking Services. Shows Month, Services Done, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Status = Completed`.

#### Retail sales by month

Retail sold each month and the profit on it after cost.

From Product Sales, Products. Shows Month, Items Sold, Sales, Profit.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`; Profit is `Round([Quantity] * ([Unit Price] - [Cost Price]), 2)`.

#### Clients to win back

Clients who agreed to hear from the salon, last seen between three months and a year ago, with nothing booked. The ones to send an offer to.

From Clients, Bookings. Shows Client, Phone, E-mail, Last Visit, Visits, Days Since.
Calculated: Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Last Visit is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Days Since is `DateDiff("d", [Start], Date())`.
Only where `Days Since Between 91 And 365` and `Status In ("Completed", "Booked")` and `Marketing Consent = Yes`.

#### Most booked services

Which services were done most over the last year, and what each took.

From Booking Services, Services, Bookings. Shows Service, Category, Times Done, Takings.
Only where `Status = Completed` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Products to order

Retail and back-bar products at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with what the order will cost.

From Products, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Product, Kind, Size, In Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity, Order Cost.
Calculated: Order Cost is `Round([Reorder Quantity] * [Cost Price], 2)`.
Only where `Above Reorder Level <= 0` and `Active = Yes`.

#### No-shows by client

Clients who have missed an appointment, with their late cancellations and the deposits kept. Use it before taking another booking without a deposit.

From Bookings, Clients. Shows Client, Phone, No-shows, Late Cancellations, Deposits Kept.
Calculated: Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; No-shows is `IIf([Status] = "No-show", 1, 0)`; Late Cancellations is `IIf([Status] = "Cancelled" And DateDiff("d", [Cancelled On], [Start]) < 2, 1, 0)`; Deposits Kept is `IIf([Deposit Refunded], 0, Nz([Deposit]))`.
Only where `No-shows >= 1` and `Status In ("No-show", "Cancelled")`.

#### Patch tests due

Colour and lash appointments in the next two weeks where the client has had no patch test in the six months before. Call them in for one at least two days ahead.

From Bookings, Clients, Booking Services, Services. Shows When, Client, Phone, Last Patch Test, Service.
Calculated: When is `Left([Start], 10) & " " & Mid([Start], 12, 5)`; Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Patch Test = Yes` and `Status = Booked` and `Days Away Between 0 And 14` and `Days Since Test > 180`.

#### Vouchers outstanding

Gift vouchers sold and not yet used, soonest to expire first. What the salon still owes in services.

From Gift Vouchers. Shows Code, Sold On, Bought By, For, Value, Expires, Days Left.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Expires])`.
Only where `Days Left >= 0` and `Redeemed On Is Null`.

#### New clients by source

New clients over the last year by how they heard of the salon.

From Clients. Shows Heard Of Us, New Clients.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Retail best sellers

Retail products over the last year, by the profit they made.

From Product Sales, Products. Shows Product, Category, Sold, Sales, Profit.
Calculated: Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`; Profit is `Round([Quantity] * ([Unit Price] - [Cost Price]), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Service menu

The services on offer, by category, with the price at each level.

From Services. Shows Category, Service, Minutes, Junior Price, Stylist Price, Senior Price.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

#### VAT by month

For each month, how many receipts were given, the takings, and the net and VAT within them: the figures for the VAT return, three months at a time.

From Receipts. Shows Month, Receipts, Takings, Net, VAT.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Taken], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Receipts last 7 days

Every receipt of the last week, with the client, the stylist, the total and what was paid at the desk and how. Use it to find a receipt to print again.

From Receipts, Bookings, Clients, Staff. Shows Number, Taken At, Client, Stylist, Total, Paid Today, Paid By.
Calculated: Taken At is `Left([Taken], 10) & " " & Mid([Taken], 12, 5)`; Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Stylist is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 7`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Suppliers, Staff, Services, Clients, Bookings, Booking Services, Products, Product Sales, Stock Deliveries, Gift Vouchers, Receipts, Receipt Lines, Commission Statements, Commission Lines. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### The column: the next 7 days by stylist

The appointment book for the next seven days, a section for each stylist, with times and phone numbers. Print it for the desk.

From the query Bookings next 7 days, a group for each Stylist: When, Client, Phone, Minutes, Deposit, with the total of Minutes.

#### Commission statement: last month

Last month's services for each person on commission, with a total of takings and commission each. For the owner and for payroll.

From the query Service commission last month, a group for each Stylist: Day, Client, Service, Price, Commission, with the total of Price, total of Commission.

Retail commission due for last month, one line a person.

From the query Retail commission last month: Stylist, Items Sold, Retail Sales, Rate, Commission, with the total of Retail Sales, total of Commission.

Service takings month by month with a grand total.

From the query Service takings by month: Month, Services Done, Takings, with the total of Services Done, total of Takings.

The order list for the week, a section for each supplier, with the cost of each line.

A call or mailing list of lapsed clients who agreed to marketing.

From the query Clients to win back: Client, Phone, E-mail, Last Visit, Visits, Days Since, with the count of Client.

The service menu, printed by category, with the junior, stylist and senior prices.

From the query Service menu, a group for each Category: Service, Minutes, Junior Price, Stylist Price, Senior Price.

#### VAT on takings by month

Takings, net and VAT month by month, with the totals, for the bookkeeper.

From the query VAT by month: Month, Receipts, Takings, Net, VAT, with the total of Takings, total of Net, total of VAT.

#### Receipts: the last 7 days

The last seven days of receipts, with the total taken and the total paid at the desk, to check against the card machine and the cash.

From the query Receipts last 7 days: Number, Taken At, Client, Stylist, Total, Paid Today, Paid By, with the total of Total, total of Paid Today.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Receipt

The till receipt for a visit, on an 80 mm roll: the salon's name, address and VAT number, the client and stylist, each service and product with the VAT within it, the total, and what was paid today after the deposit and any gift voucher came off. The deposit and voucher lines print only when there was one. Numbered RCP-2026-00042. One for each record of Receipts, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Date, Client, Stylist
- Lines from Receipt Lines: Item, Qty, Price, Amount, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Total, Of which VAT, Less deposit paid, Less gift voucher, Paid today
- Words: Gift voucher {Voucher Code} taken in full.
- Words: Paid by {Paid By}. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Gift voucher

The voucher a buyer takes away, on A5 card: who it is for and from, what it is worth, its number and use-by date, and the terms. It prints for vouchers not yet used and still in date; to print one already used or expired, print it from the Gift Vouchers form. One for each record of Gift Vouchers, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Gift voucher
- Words: For {For}, from {Bought By}.
- Words: For {For}.
- Fields: Worth, Voucher number, Issued, Use by
- Words: To spend on any service or product at {Business.Name}. Call {Business.Phone} or book at {Business.Website}, and give the voucher number when you book.
- Words: Terms. Valid until the use-by date shown, twelve months from the day it was bought. To be used in full at one visit; it cannot be exchanged for cash and no change is given. Please bring the voucher with you. A lost voucher can be replaced only if we can find its number in our records.

#### Commission statement

Given to each stylist and therapist on commission with their pay: the month's services by kind and the retail they sold, the takings, the rate and the commission due. Numbered COM-2026-0042. One for each record of Commission Statements, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Commission statement {Number}
- Fields: For, Month, Role, Prepared, Level, Paid with wages on
- Lines from Commission Lines: Work, Done, Takings, Rate %, Commission
- Totals: Takings, Commission due
- Words: To be paid with your wages on the 7th.
- Words: Commission is worked out on what clients paid, VAT included, for completed appointments and retail you sold in the month. It is paid with your wages and taxed with them. If anything here looks wrong, please speak to the owner within 14 days.

#### Appointment confirmation

A letter or e-mail confirming an appointment: the day and time, who with, the services and their prices, the deposit, and the skin test and cancellation policy. It prints for bookings still to come that are not cancelled, and a past one prints from the Bookings form. The paragraph about skin tests prints only when a service in the booking needs one, and the deposit only when one was taken. Have the cancellation words checked against the consumer rules of your own country. One for each record of Bookings, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Your appointment
- Words: Dear {Client.First Name},
- Words: Thank you for booking with us. This is to confirm your appointment, booked on {Booked On}.
- Fields: Day, Time, With, Time set aside (minutes), Deposit paid
- Lines from Booking Services: Service, Skin test first, Price
- Totals: Price for the visit, Less deposit paid, To pay on the day
- Words: Prices include VAT. If you would like a different service on the day, the price may change; your stylist will tell you before starting.
- Words: Your appointment includes colour, a tint or a lash lift, which needs a skin test in the six months before. If you have not had one with us in that time, please call in for a quick test at least 48 hours before your appointment. It takes five minutes.
- Words: Our cancellation policy. If you need to move or cancel, please tell us at least 48 hours before, by phone on {Business.Phone} or by e-mail to {Business.E-mail}, and any deposit is refunded or moved to your new booking. With less notice, or if you do not come, we keep the deposit and may ask for one when you next book. If you are running late, please call: we will do what we can in the time left, or offer you another appointment.
- Words: We look forward to seeing you.
- Words: With best wishes, the team at {Business.Name}

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name, address, VAT number and the words at the foot of a receipt. Then Suppliers, then Staff with their level and commission rates, then the Services menu with a price for each level. Add your Products next, with their supplier and reorder level. Clients can be added as they book. Then make Bookings and add the services for each in Booking Services, changing the price where you charge something different. Record Product Sales and Stock Deliveries as they happen, and Gift Vouchers when you sell them. Each visit paid for gets a record in Receipts with its Receipt Lines, and at the end of each month a record in Commission Statements, with its lines, for each person on commission.

### Making it yours

- A barber can drop the beauty services, keep Junior and Senior prices and add a Walk-in choice to Booked Via.
- A dog groomer can rename Clients to Owners and add a Pets table pointing at it (name, breed, size, temperament), then make each booking point at a pet.
- To pay commission only above a target, add a Target field to Staff and a calculated column in Takings by stylist last month that takes it off the takings.
- Add a Reminder Sent yes/no to Bookings and tick it when the reminder goes, so nobody sends two.
- For a nail bar or brow studio, add a Station or Room field to Bookings to show which chair or room each appointment uses.
- Change the patch test rule from six months to another period by editing 180 in the Patch tests due query.
- Add a Tips field to Bookings and a query that totals tips by stylist each month.
- To sell products over the counter without a booking, add a Client field to Receipts and leave Booking empty; the Receipt template can then print {Client} instead of {Booking.Client}.
- Give receipts for gift vouchers too: add a Receipts record with one line, Kind Voucher and Tax Rate 0, since VAT on a voucher is paid when it is spent.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print a receipt again for a client?**

Run Receipts last 7 days, or open the Receipts form and find the number. Then open the print template Receipt, choose that receipt and print it. It prints exactly as it did on the day.

**Where does the VAT number on the receipt come from?**

From the Business table, with the salon's name, address and phone. Change it there once and every receipt, voucher, statement and letter takes the new details.

**A client cancelled with less than 48 hours' notice. What do I do?**

Set the booking's Status to Cancelled and type the day in Cancelled On. Leave Deposit Refunded unticked, so the deposit is kept. No-shows by client counts late cancellations and no-shows together.

**How do I pay part of a bill with a gift voucher?**

In the sample a voucher is used in full on one visit. Type its value in Voucher on the receipt and the rest in Paid Today, with Paid By as Gift voucher and card. To let a balance stay on a voucher, add a Balance field to Gift Vouchers.

**Why does the commission statement for a stylist not match the takings report?**

Takings by stylist last month counts services only; the statement adds the retail they sold, at the retail rate. Both use completed appointments only.

**How do I start with my own salon instead of Marigold?**

Open the sample empty and fill in Business first. Then add your suppliers, staff, service menu and products, in that order, before any client or booking.

## Copper Pole Barbers

**Barber shop.** The queue board, walk-ins and bookings, takings by barber, loyalty cards, chair rent and stock for a barber shop.

For a barber shop that takes walk-ins as well as bookings, with some barbers on the payroll and some renting a chair. Copper Pole Barbers is an invented shop with five chairs, open seven days: Monday to Friday 9am to 7pm, Thursday until 8pm, Saturday 8am to 6pm and Sunday 10am to 4pm. The owner and two employed barbers work the shop's three chairs, with a part-time barber on Sundays and Mondays. Chairs 4 and 5 are rented by the week to self-employed barbers, who keep their own takings and pay chair rent plus VAT each Monday.

The records cover the last year of the queue board and the bookings for the next two weeks. Every visit is kept: when the client arrived, when they sat down and when they left, so the waits of walk-ins can be measured. Saturdays are the busiest day, weekdays peak at lunchtime and after work, December is the busiest month and January the quietest. Most visits are regulars who come back every two to six weeks, some booked and some walking in; a walk-in who would wait longer than they will stand leaves, and is counted. A few bookings are cancelled or not kept.

Prices have VAT in them. The shop is registered for VAT; the chair renters are not, so their cuts carry none, and their receipts say whose takings they are. The loyalty card gives a stamp for each paid cut on any chair, and the tenth cut is free; a free cut given on a rented chair is credited against that barber's next week of rent. The shop sells styling and beard products at the desk and orders them each Monday. One chair renter left part way through the year and another took the chair after two weeks.

It suits, with small changes: A barber shop with or without rented chairs; A hair salon that rents chairs to self-employed stylists; A nail bar that takes walk-ins; A tattoo or piercing studio with resident artists; A walk-in clinic or repair counter that measures waiting times; A beauty room that rents rooms to therapists.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- A visit is also its receipt: the Receipt No, Total and VAT are filled in when it is paid for. A booking still to come, a no-show or a walk-out has no receipt number, so the Receipt template leaves it out.
- Chair renters keep their own takings. Their visits are on the queue board so the queue, the waits and the loyalty cards are right, and their totals show in Takings by barber, but they are left out of the shop's VAT. Their lines carry a Tax Rate of 0.
- Waiting times are worked out from Arrived and Started, which must be on the same day. A walk-in who leaves before their turn is kept, as Walked out, with no Started time, so the queries can count them.
- Stock is not counted by Data Files on its own: take a product off In Stock when you sell it, and add a delivery when it comes. In the sample this was done while the records were made.
- A free cut on a rented chair costs the renter their price, so the shop credits it against the next week's rent: that is the line below nought on a Chair rent invoice.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: receipts for paid visits, agreements in force, loyalty cards still in use, and every rent invoice. Printed from a form, the record on screen prints whatever its state.

### Tutorial

#### Put a walk-in on the queue board and take payment

1. Open the Visits form and press New. Type the client's first name in Name; if they have a record, choose them in Client. Kind is Walk-in, Arrived is now, and Status is Waiting.
2. Run the query Queue board to see who is next. When they sit down, type the time in Started, choose the barber in Barber and set Status to In chair.
3. When the cut is done, add the services in Visit Lines below, with Item, Unit Price and Tax Rate (0.2 on the shop's chairs, 0 on a renter's). Add any product sold as a line with Product chosen, and take one off its In Stock on the Products form.
4. Type Finished, the Total, the VAT (the price less the price divided by 1.2, line by line) and Net, Paid By, and the next Receipt No. Set Status to Done.
5. Open the print template Receipt from Print templates, choose the visit and press Print.

#### Book a cut

1. Open the Visits form and press New. Choose the client, set Kind to Booked, type the day and time in Booked For and today in Booked On, choose the barber, and set Status to Booked.
2. Add the service booked in Visit Lines so the barber knows how long to allow.
3. Print the report Week ahead each evening to see every barber's bookings, or run Bookings next 7 days.

#### Stamp a loyalty card and give the free cut

1. After a paid cut, open the Loyalty Cards form and find the client's open card, or press New to start one with the next Number, the client and today in Started.
2. Add one to Stamps, and choose that card in Card on the visit. At nine stamps, set Status to Due a free cut and type the day in Full On.
3. Run Due a free cut to see who has one waiting. On the free visit, tick Free Cut, put the cut in Visit Lines at a price of nought, set the card's Status to Used and type Free Cut On.
4. To give a client a printed card, open the print template Loyalty card and choose their card.

#### Rent a chair to a self-employed barber

1. Add the barber to the Barbers form with Basis set to Chair renter, their Chair, Trading Name, address, insurance policy and the Receipt Note for their receipts.
2. Open the Chair Rentals form and press New. Type the next Number, choose the barber and the chair, and fill in Signed On, Start Date, Weekly Rent, Rent Day, Deposit, Notice Weeks, Hours, Included and Insurance Cover.
3. Open the print template Chair rental agreement, choose the agreement and print two copies to sign, one for each side.

#### Raise the week's chair rent and record payment

1. Each Friday, open the Rent Charges form and press New for each active rental: the next Number, the rental, today in Invoice Date, the coming Monday in Week Starting and Due On.
2. In Rent Lines below, add the week's rent (quantity 1, the weekly rent, Tax Rate 0.2). If the renter gave free loyalty cuts last week, add a line for them at the menu price below nought. Type the Net, VAT and Total.
3. Open the print template Chair rent invoice, choose the invoice and print or save it as a PDF to send.
4. When the money comes in, type the day in Paid On and how in Paid By. The query Chair rent due, or the report Rent owed, shows what is still unpaid.

#### Close the week

1. Print the report Daily takings and check each day against the card machine and the cash in the till.
2. Print Barber takings for the week's figures by barber, and Walk-in waits to see when the queue was longest.
3. On Monday, print Products to order, send it to the supplier, and when the delivery comes add it to Stock Deliveries and to In Stock.

#### Do the VAT return

1. Print the report VAT by month and add up the three months of the quarter. It counts the shop's own visits and products only; the chair renters' takings are not the shop's.
2. Add the VAT on chair rent from the Rent Charges of the same months: open the query Chair rent by month and take the VAT as the Invoiced less the Rent.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 28 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

- Barbers.Chair points at a record in Chairs
- Loyalty Cards.Client points at a record in Clients
- Visits.Client points at a record in Clients
- Visits.Barber points at a record in Barbers
- Visits.Card points at a record in Loyalty Cards
- Visit Lines.Visit points at a record in Visits
- Visit Lines.Service points at a record in Services
- Visit Lines.Product points at a record in Products
- Stock Deliveries.Product points at a record in Products

### Queries

#### Queue board

Who is waiting, who is in the chair and who is booked, today and the next two days, in time order. The board by the door.

From Visits, Barbers. Shows Day, Time, Name, Kind, Barber, Status.
Calculated: Day is `Format(Nz([Booked For], [Arrived]), "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Time is `Mid(Nz([Booked For], [Arrived]), 12, 5)`; Barber is `[Barbers].[First Name] & " " & [Barbers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Away Between 0 And 2` and `Status In ("Waiting", "In chair", "Booked")`.

#### Bookings next 7 days

Every booking from today to a week ahead, by time, with the barber.

From Visits, Barbers. Shows When, Barber, Name, Booked On.
Calculated: When is `Left([Booked For], 10) & " " & Mid([Booked For], 12, 5)`; Barber is `[Barbers].[First Name] & " " & [Barbers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Away Between 0 And 7` and `Status = Booked`.

#### Takings by barber, last 7 days

For each barber over the last seven days: visits, how many were walk-ins, free cuts given and the takings. A chair renter's takings are their own.

From Visits, Barbers. Shows Barber, Basis, Visits, Walk-ins, Free Cuts, Takings.
Calculated: Barber is `[Barbers].[First Name] & " " & [Barbers].[Last Name]`; Walk-ins is `IIf([Kind] = "Walk-in", 1, 0)`; Free Cuts is `IIf([Free Cut], 1, 0)`.
Only where `Status = Done` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 6`.

#### Takings by barber by day

Each day of the last week, each barber's visits and takings, the newest day first.

From Visits, Barbers. Shows Day, Barber, Visits, Takings.
Calculated: Day is `Format([Arrived], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Barber is `[Barbers].[First Name] & " " & [Barbers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Done` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 6`.

#### Takings by barber by month

Visits and takings for each barber each month, with whether they are employed or renting.

From Visits, Barbers. Shows Month, Barber, Basis, Visits, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Arrived], "yyyy-mm")`; Barber is `[Barbers].[First Name] & " " & [Barbers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Done`.

#### Shop takings and VAT by month

The shop's own takings each month (the employed barbers' visits and the products), with the net and VAT within them, for the VAT return.

From Visits, Barbers. Shows Month, Visits, Takings, Net, VAT.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Arrived], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Status = Done` and `Basis = Employed`.

#### Chair rent due

Rent invoices not yet paid, by due date, with how many days each is overdue (nought when not yet due).

From Rent Charges, Chair Rentals, Barbers. Shows Invoice, Renter, Week Starting, Due On, Total, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Renter is `[Barbers].[First Name] & " " & [Barbers].[Last Name]`; Days Overdue is `IIf(DateDiff("d", [Due On], Date()) > 0, DateDiff("d", [Due On], Date()), 0)`.
Only where `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Chair rent by month

For each renter each month: the weeks invoiced, the rent, the total with VAT, what has been paid and what is owed.

From Rent Charges, Chair Rentals, Barbers. Shows Month, Renter, Weeks, Rent, Invoiced, Paid, Owing.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Week Starting], "yyyy-mm")`; Renter is `[Barbers].[First Name] & " " & [Barbers].[Last Name]`; Paid is `IIf(Nz([Paid On], "") = "", 0, [Total])`; Owing is `IIf(Nz([Paid On], "") = "", [Total], 0)`.

#### Walk-in waits by hour

For walk-ins over the last four weeks, by the hour they arrived: how many came, the average and longest wait in minutes, and how many walked out. Use it to plan who works when.

From Visits. Shows Hour, Walk-ins, Average Wait, Longest Wait, Walked Out.
Calculated: Hour is `Mid([Arrived], 12, 2)`; Average Wait is `(Mid([Started], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Started], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Arrived], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Arrived], 15, 2))`; Longest Wait is `(Mid([Started], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Started], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Arrived], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Arrived], 15, 2))`; Walked Out is `IIf([Status] = "Walked out", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Kind = Walk-in` and `Status In ("Done", "Walked out")` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 28`.

#### Walk-in waits by day

The same for each of the last fourteen days, to see which days the queue got long.

From Visits. Shows Day, Walk-ins, Average Wait, Longest Wait, Walked Out.
Calculated: Day is `Format([Arrived], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Average Wait is `(Mid([Started], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Started], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Arrived], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Arrived], 15, 2))`; Longest Wait is `(Mid([Started], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Started], 15, 2)) - (Mid([Arrived], 12, 2) * 60 + Mid([Arrived], 15, 2))`; Walked Out is `IIf([Status] = "Walked out", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Kind = Walk-in` and `Status In ("Done", "Walked out")` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 14`.

#### Busiest hours

Visits by the hour they arrived over the last thirteen weeks, walk-ins and bookings apart.

From Visits. Shows Hour, Visits, Walk-ins, Booked.
Calculated: Hour is `Mid([Arrived], 12, 2)`; Walk-ins is `IIf([Kind] = "Walk-in", 1, 0)`; Booked is `IIf([Kind] = "Booked", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Status In ("Done", "Walked out")` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 91`.

#### Due a free cut

Loyalty cards with nine stamps whose free cut has not been given yet, the longest waiting first. Text them, or have it ready when they come in.

From Loyalty Cards, Clients. Shows Card, Client, Phone, Started, Full On, Days Waiting.
Calculated: Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Full On], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Due a free cut`.

#### Loyalty cards nearly full

Open cards with seven or eight stamps.

From Loyalty Cards, Clients. Shows Card, Client, Phone, Stamps, Started.
Calculated: Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Stamps Between 7 And 8` and `Status = Open`.

#### Products low

Products at or below their reorder level, with what the order will cost. The Monday order list.

From Products. Shows Supplier, Product, Size, In Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity, Order Cost.
Calculated: Order Cost is `Round([Reorder Quantity] * [Cost Price], 2)`.
Only where `Above Reorder Level <= 0` and `Active = Yes`.

#### Product sales by month

Products sold each month, the sales with VAT in, and the profit after VAT and cost.

From Visit Lines, Visits, Products. Shows Month, Items, Sales, Profit.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Arrived], "yyyy-mm")`; Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`; Profit is `Round([Quantity] * ([Unit Price] / (1 + [Visit Lines].[Tax Rate]) - [Cost Price]), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Done`.

#### Popular services

The services done over the last thirteen weeks, the most done first, with what each took.

From Visit Lines, Services, Visits. Shows Service, Times, Takings.
Calculated: Takings is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.
Only where `Status = Done` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 91`.

#### Regulars not seen lately

Clients who agreed to hear from the shop, last in between eight weeks and a year ago, with nothing booked.

From Clients, Visits. Shows Client, Phone, Usual Cut, Last Visit, Visits, Days Since.
Calculated: Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Last Visit is `Format(Nz([Booked For], [Arrived]), "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Days Since is `DateDiff("d", Nz([Booked For], [Arrived]), Date())`.
Only where `Days Since Between 56 And 365` and `Status In ("Done", "Booked")` and `Marketing Consent = Yes`.

#### Service menu

The price list, the dearest first, with the minutes each takes and whether it earns a stamp.

From Services. Shows Service, Minutes, Price, Earns a Stamp.
Only where `Active = Yes`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Chairs, Barbers, Clients, Services, Products, Loyalty Cards, Visits, Visit Lines, Stock Deliveries, Chair Rentals, Rent Charges, Rent Lines. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Print templates

#### Receipt

The receipt from the till for a visit, on an 80 mm roll: the barber and chair, each service and product with the VAT within it, the total, how it was paid and the loyalty stamps so far. On a rented chair it says the takings are the renter's and carry no VAT, and leaves out the VAT line. It prints for visits paid for, those with a receipt number; the loyalty card lines print only when the visit was on a card. One for each record of Visits, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Receipt No}
- Fields: Date, Barber, Chair, Client, Loyalty card, Stamps on the card
- Lines from Visit Lines: Item, Qty, Price, Amount, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Total paid, Of which VAT
- Words: Your tenth cut, free on your loyalty card.
- Words: Paid by {Paid By}.
- Words: {Barber.Receipt Note}
- Words: Loyalty card: a stamp for every paid cut, on any chair, and the tenth cut is free. Ask at the desk for a card.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Chair rental agreement

The agreement a self-employed barber signs to rent a chair: the parties, the chair, the weekly rent and the day it is due, the deposit, what the rent covers, the hours, clients and payment, insurance, tax, notice and signatures. It prints for agreements in force; an ended one prints from the Chair Rentals form and says when it ended. Plain words of our own: have it checked for your own country before you use it. One for each record of Chair Rentals, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Chair rental agreement {Number}
- Words: This agreement ended on {End Date}.
- Fields: Chair renter, Chair, Trading as, Starts, Address, Weekly rent (plus VAT), City, Rent due each, Postcode, Deposit
- Words: This agreement is made on {Signed On} between {Business.Name} of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} ("the Shop") and {Barber.First Name} {Barber.Last Name}, trading as {Barber.Trading Name}, of {Barber.Address}, {Barber.City} {Barber.Postcode} ("the Barber").
- Words: 1. The chair. The Shop lets the Barber use {Chair.Name} ({Chair.Position}) in the shop, with its mirror, station, drawer and the shared basin, from {Start Date} until either side ends this agreement. The Barber runs their own business from the chair as a self-employed person. The Barber is not an employee or a partner of the Shop.
- Words: 2. Rent. The Barber pays {Weekly Rent} a week plus VAT, in advance, on each {Rent Day}. The Shop sends a numbered invoice for each week on the Friday before. Rent is due for every week of the agreement, including weeks the Barber is on holiday or chooses not to work. Rent more than 14 days late may end the agreement under clause 10.
- Words: 3. Deposit. The Barber has paid a deposit of {Deposit}. The Shop returns it within 14 days of the agreement ending, less any rent still owed and the cost of putting right any damage beyond fair wear.
- Words: 4. What the rent includes. {Included}
- Words: 5. Hours. The Barber may work at the chair during the shop's opening hours: {Hours}. The Barber chooses their own days and hours within these and tells the Shop by Friday which days they will work the next week, so the queue board is right.
- Words: 6. Clients, prices and payment. The Barber keeps their own clients and their own takings, and takes payment for their own work. Walk-ins are offered the first free chair, the Barber's included. The Barber may set their own prices but shows them on the shop's price board. The Barber honours the shop's loyalty card: a stamp for each cut, and the tenth cut free; each free cut the Barber gives is credited at the shop's menu price against the next week's rent.
- Words: 7. Products. The Barber buys their own tools and the products used in their work. Retail products are sold by the Shop; the Barber does not sell products from the chair without the Shop's agreement.
- Words: 8. Insurance and standards. The Barber holds public liability insurance cover of at least {Insurance Cover} and shows the Shop the certificate each year (policy {Barber.Insurance Policy}, renewed by {Barber.Insurance Expires}). The Barber cleans and disinfects tools between clients, keeps the station tidy, and follows the shop's health and safety rules and its rules on behaviour towards clients and colleagues.
- Words: 9. Tax. The Barber is responsible for their own income tax and National Insurance, and for VAT if they become registered for it. The Shop makes no deductions from the Barber's takings and pays the Barber no wages, holiday pay or sick pay.
- Words: 10. Ending the agreement. Either side may end this agreement by giving {Notice Weeks} weeks' notice in writing. The Shop may end it at once if rent is more than 14 days late after a written reminder, or for serious misconduct. On the last day the Barber clears the station, returns the keys, and pays any rent owed up to the end of the notice.
- Words: 11. Changes. Any change to this agreement is made in writing and signed by both sides.
- Signed by: Signed for the Shop, Signed by the Barber, Date

#### Chair rent invoice

The weekly invoice for a rented chair, numbered RENT-2026-0042, with the week's rent, any credit for free loyalty cuts, the VAT and the total due on the rent day. An unpaid invoice says how to pay; a paid one says when and how it was paid. One for each record of Rent Charges, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Invoice {Number}
- Fields: Invoice to, Invoice number, Trading as, Date, Address, Week starting, City, Payment due, Postcode, Agreement
- Lines from Rent Lines: Description, Qty, Unit Price, Net, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Net, VAT, Total due
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Please pay to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}, or in cash at the desk.
- Words: Paid with thanks on {Paid On} by {Paid By}.

#### Loyalty card

A client's loyalty card on the narrow roll: the days of each stamped cut and who did it, the stamps so far and how many to the free cut, or that the free cut is waiting. It prints for cards still in use, not ones whose free cut has been given. One for each record of Loyalty Cards, on receipt-58 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Loyalty card {Number}
- Fields: For, Started, Card
- Lines from Visits: Day, Barber, Stamp, Free
- Totals: Stamps, Cuts to your free one
- Words: Your free cut is waiting: tell us when you come in.
- Words: One stamp for every paid cut, on any chair. Nine stamps and your tenth cut is free. Show your card or give your name at the desk.

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your shop's name, address, VAT number and bank details, which every receipt and invoice prints. Then Chairs, then Barbers on each chair (with Basis, and a renter's trading name, address and insurance), then the Services price list and the Products you sell. If you rent chairs, add a Chair Rentals record for each renter and print the agreement. Clients can be added as they give their details. Visits, their lines, loyalty cards, stock deliveries and rent charges come in as you trade.

### Making it yours

- Pay employed barbers commission: add a Commission Rate to Barbers and a query that takes it off each barber's takings by month.
- Take a deposit for long bookings, such as a cut, beard and hot towel shave: add a Deposit field to Visits and take it off the receipt's total.
- If a chair renter uses the shop's card machine, add a Paid Over field to Visits and a weekly query of what is owed to each renter, less their rent.
- Send a text when a free cut is due: the query Due a free cut has the phone numbers to copy into a message.
- Rent a chair by the day instead of the week: add a Days field to Rent Lines and a daily rate to Chair Rentals.
- For a salon or studio that rents rooms, rename Chairs to Rooms; the agreement and invoices work the same.
- Show the wait on the board: add a calculated column to Queue board with the minutes from Arrived to now, using Now().

### Questions people ask

**How do I see who is next?**

Run the query Queue board. It lists everyone waiting, in the chair and booked, today and for the next two days, in time order.

**How long are walk-ins waiting?**

Run Walk-in waits by hour for the last four weeks by hour of the day, or Walk-in waits by day for each of the last fourteen days. The waits are in minutes; Walked Out counts those who left.

**Why is there no VAT on some receipts?**

Those visits were on a rented chair. The renter is a separate business, not registered for VAT, so their cuts carry none. The note at the foot of the receipt, from the barber's Receipt Note, says so.

**How do I print last week's rent invoices?**

Open the print template Chair rent invoice and choose the invoices for that week; the query Chair rent by month and the Rent Charges form show their numbers.

**A renter is behind with the rent. Where do I see it?**

Run Chair rent due or print Rent owed. Each unpaid invoice is listed with the days overdue. The agreement says rent more than 14 days late after a reminder can end it.

**Can I change the loyalty card to a stamp every visit, beard trims too?**

Yes: tick Stamp on those services in the Services form. To make the eighth cut free instead of the tenth, change the 9 on the Loyalty card template and in your own counting.

**How do I start with my own shop?**

Open the sample empty. Fill in Business, then Chairs, then Barbers, Services and Products. Add Chair Rentals for any renters, and clients as they come in.

## Ironbridge Repairs

**Repair shop.** Jobs, devices, quotes, parts, invoices, warranties and payments for a shop that mends phones, tablets, laptops and small appliances.

Ironbridge Repairs is an invented repair shop on a high street in Bristol. Three technicians work at the bench and one assistant runs the counter, where customers book in a phone with a cracked screen or a coffee machine that has stopped pumping, and come back later to collect it. A handful of local businesses have an account: their staff bring work in, and the shop invoices the business and sends it a statement.

Every job is one record with its own number, JOB-2026-0042. It starts as Booked in, is diagnosed, gets a quote, waits for the customer to approve it, waits for a part if the shelf has none, is repaired and is marked Ready, then Collected. A job can also end as Unrepairable, or Ready with the quote turned down and a small diagnosis charge. The parts and labour each job used are its Job Lines, so the charge can be explained line by line; every payment, deposits included, is recorded against its job.

Prices are shown to customers with VAT included, as a high-street shop shows them. Each line keeps its VAT rate, and the quote, the invoice and the receipt work out the VAT inside each line and add it up, so the VAT on the invoice and in the VAT by month query agree to the penny.

The records cover about fifteen months up to the day the file is made. Phones come in more in the summer holidays and laptops when the school year starts; kitchen appliances pick up before the year ends. Some jobs are waiting on parts today, some customers have not picked up their devices after weeks, a few repairs have come back under warranty, an account or two is behind with its invoices, and the parts shelf has items at or below their reorder level, one of them held up because the supplier has it on back order.

It suits, with small changes: A phone and tablet repair kiosk; A computer support firm that takes machines in; A bike shop workshop, with bikes as the devices; A watch and jewellery repairer; An appliance engineer who also visits homes; A musical instrument or audio repair bench.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Prices are typed with VAT included, as the customer sees them: a phone screen at 79.00 is 65.83 and 13.17 VAT. The VAT is worked out inside each line and rounded to the penny, then added up, so an invoice's Tax is the sum of its lines and not 20 percent of its total worked out once.
- The numbers on jobs, quotes, invoices, warranties and receipts (JOB-, QUO-, INV-, WTY-, RCP-) are typed, not made by Data Files. Keep each run in date order and start again at 0001 each January. The record number (ID) is separate and is what Part Orders shows in For Job.
- An invoice's lines are the job's own lines, Job Lines, found through the job the invoice is for. Raise one invoice for a job, once every part and hour is on it; extra work found later goes on a new job.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: the Booking-in receipt for jobs still in the shop, the Collection receipt for jobs collected, the Quote for quotes not yet answered and the Warranty certificate for warranties still running. Every invoice and every account prints. Printed from a form, the record on screen prints whatever its state.
- The Account statement lists only the invoices still unpaid, oldest first, with the days each is overdue and a running total of what is owed. An account that owes nothing prints a line saying so.
- A job that is beyond economic repair, a warranty return and a declined quote still have lines, at nought or at the diagnosis charge, so the bench time is recorded even when nothing is charged.
- Customers who bring work for a business point at its Accounts record. The invoice is made out to the account and its balance is paid by transfer, not at the counter, so Accounts to chase is the list to watch.

### Tutorial

#### Book a device in and print the receipt

1. Open the Customers form and look the person up by name or phone. If they are new, press New and type their name, phone and how they want to be told (Contact By). If they bring work for a business with an account, choose it in Account.
2. Open the Devices form, press New, choose the customer in Customer, then fill in Kind, Make, Model, Serial and Colour. A device that has been in before already has a record: use that one.
3. Open the Jobs form and press New. Type the next job number in Number (JOB-2026- and the next number in the run), choose the device in Device and the technician in Technician, and fill in Booked In, Fault, Left With It and Promised. For a fixed-price repair such as a screen, type the price in Quote and tick Quote Approved.
4. With the job on screen, open the print template Booking-in receipt from Print templates, and press Print. The customer signs one copy and keeps it.

#### Quote after diagnosis, and hear back

1. When the bench has found the fault, open the Quotes form and press New. Type the next number (QUO-2026-...), choose the job in Job, and set Quoted On to today and Valid Until to thirty days on.
2. In Quote Lines, add a Part line with the part's name and price and a Labour line with the hours and the bench rate, VAT included in both. Put the total in Total and in the job's Quote, and set the job's Status to Awaiting approval.
3. Open the print template Quote, choose the quote, and press Save as PDF to e-mail it, or Print.
4. Each morning open the query Quotes awaiting approval and ring anyone who has not answered. When they answer, fill in Answer and Answered On on the quote, and on the job tick Quote Approved or set the outcome to Quote declined.

#### Order a part for a job and take a deposit

1. If the part is not on the shelf (In Stock on the Parts form), open the Part Orders form, press New, choose the supplier, the part and the job, and fill in Quantity, Unit Cost, Ordered On and Expected. Set the job's Status to Awaiting parts.
2. For a part ordered in specially, take its price as a deposit: type it in the job's Deposit, then open the Payments form, press New, choose the job, and record the amount with Kind Deposit and the next receipt number.
3. When the part arrives, type Received On on the part order and set its Status to Received. The query Awaiting parts shows what is still on its way.

#### Finish a repair, invoice it and give the warranty

1. On the Jobs form, add the job's lines in Job Lines: the part fitted (Kind Part, the part, its name in Description, Quantity 1 and its price) and the labour (Kind Labour, what was done, the hours in Quantity and the rate in Unit Price). Fill in Done On on each.
2. Set the job's Status to Ready and Outcome to Repaired, type today in Finished, the total of the lines in Charge, and in Warranty Until the day 90 days on.
3. Open the Invoices form and press New. Type the next number (INV-2026-...), choose the job, choose the account if it is business work, and fill in Invoice Date, Due Date, Net, Tax, Total, Deposit and Balance. The invoice lists the job's lines on its own, found through the job.
4. Open the Warranties form, press New, type the next number (WTY-2026-...), choose the job and say in Covers what was fitted and done.
5. Open the print templates Invoice and Warranty certificate, choose the new records, and press Save as PDF to e-mail them, or Print to put them in the bag with the device.
6. Ring or text the customer: the query Ready for collection is the list, with how each wants to be told.

#### Hand a device back and take payment

1. Find the job on the Job board query or the Jobs form by its number from the customer's receipt, and check the serial on the device against Devices.
2. Open the Payments form, press New, choose the job, type the amount left to pay, the Method and Kind On collection, with the next receipt number. On the invoice fill in Paid On; on the job type Collected, tick Paid and set Status to Collected.
3. With the job on screen, open the print template Collection receipt and press Print. The customer signs that the device came back in working order.

#### Send the business accounts their statements

1. At the month end, open the report Account invoices due to see what each business owes, and how late.
2. Open the print template Account statement from Print templates. It makes one statement for each record in Accounts, listing only the invoices still unpaid; choose the accounts that owe something, and press Save as PDF to e-mail each one to the address on its Accounts record.
3. When a business pays, open the Payments form, record each invoice paid with Kind On account and Method Bank transfer, fill in Paid On on the invoice, and tick Paid on the job.

#### Reorder parts and do the VAT

1. Every Monday, open the report Parts to order: a page for each supplier with what has fallen to its reorder level and what a full order costs. Place the orders and record them in Part Orders.
2. At the end of each VAT quarter, open the report VAT by month and add up the three months' Net Sales and VAT for the return.
3. The query Parts margin shows what each part has earned over its cost, with the VAT taken out of the price.
