| Quantity | Number | How many parts, or for labour the hours. |
| Unit Price | Currency | The price of one part or one hour, VAT included. |
| Tax Rate | Number | The VAT rate inside the price, as a fraction. |

#### Invoices

An invoice for every job that costs something, raised the day the work is finished. It lists the job's lines, the VAT inside them, any deposit already paid and the balance. Members of the public pay it on collection; businesses on account pay it within their payment days. The sample has 2,272 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The invoice's number, given in date order and once only, a new run each year: INV-2026-0042. |
| Job | Points at Jobs, required | The job invoiced. |
| Account | Points at Accounts | The business account billed, for work brought in on account. Empty for members of the public. |
| Invoice Date | Date | The day it was raised, the day the work was finished. It is the tax point for VAT. |
| Due Date | Date | When payment is due: the invoice date for the public (pay on collection), or that date and the account's payment days. |
| Net | Currency | The total without VAT. |
| Tax | Currency | The VAT inside the total: each line's VAT rounded to the penny, then added up, as the invoice prints it. |
| Total | Currency | What the invoice comes to, VAT included. The same as the job's Charge. |
| Deposit | Currency | The deposit already paid against the job, taken off the total. |
| Balance | Currency | What was left to pay when the invoice was raised: the total less the deposit. |
| Paid On | Date | The day the balance was paid; empty while it is owed. |

#### Warranties

A 90-day warranty certificate for every job repaired (not for a warranty return, which is covered by the first one). The Warranty certificate print template prints from it. The sample has 2,160 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The certificate's number, in date order, a new run each year: WTY-2026-0042. |
| Job | Points at Jobs, required | The job whose repair it covers. The last day of cover is the job's Warranty Until. |
| Issued | Date | The day the repair was finished and the certificate given. |
| Covers | Short text | What it covers, in words: the part fitted and the work done. |

#### Payments

Every payment taken, each against its job, each with its own receipt number. The sample has 2,511 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The receipt number, in date order, a new run each year: RCP-2026-0042. |
| Job | Points at Jobs, required | The job paid for. |
| Paid On | Date | The day the money came in. |
| Amount | Currency | How much. |
| Method | Short text | Card, Cash or Bank transfer. |
| Kind | Short text | Deposit, On collection, or On account for a business paying its invoice. |

### Relationships

- Customers.Account points at a record in Accounts
- Parts.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Devices.Customer points at a record in Customers
- Jobs.Device points at a record in Devices
- Jobs.Technician points at a record in Staff
- Jobs.Warranty Of points at a record in Jobs
- Part Orders.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Part Orders.Part points at a record in Parts
- Part Orders.Job points at a record in Jobs
- Job Lines.Job points at a record in Jobs
- Job Lines.Part points at a record in Parts
- Quotes.Job points at a record in Jobs
- Quote Lines.Quote points at a record in Quotes
- Invoices.Job points at a record in Jobs
- Invoices.Account points at a record in Accounts
- Warranties.Job points at a record in Jobs
- Payments.Job points at a record in Jobs

### Queries

#### Job board

Every job not yet collected, in the order the shop works through them, with who it belongs to, the technician, the promised date and how many days are left (below nought means it is late). Open it first thing in the morning.

From Jobs, Devices, Customers, Staff. Shows Stage, Job, Booked In, Customer, Phone, Device, Fault, Technician, Promised, Days Left.
Calculated: Stage is `IIf([Status] = "Booked in", "1 Booked in", IIf([Status] = "Diagnosing", "2 Diagnosing", IIf([Status] = "Awaiting approval", "3 Awaiting approval", IIf([Status] = "Awaiting parts", "4 Awaiting parts", IIf([Status] = "Repairing", "5 Repairing", IIf([Status] = "Ready", "6 Ready", "7 " & [Status]))))))`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Days Left is `IIf(Nz([Finished], "") = "", DateDiff("d", Date(), [Promised]), Null)`.
Only where `Collected Is Null`.

#### Jobs by status

How many jobs sit at each stage now, and the oldest booking at each. A quick count for the morning meeting.

From Jobs. Shows Stage, Jobs, Oldest Booked In.
Calculated: Stage is `IIf([Status] = "Booked in", "1 Booked in", IIf([Status] = "Diagnosing", "2 Diagnosing", IIf([Status] = "Awaiting approval", "3 Awaiting approval", IIf([Status] = "Awaiting parts", "4 Awaiting parts", IIf([Status] = "Repairing", "5 Repairing", IIf([Status] = "Ready", "6 Ready", "7 " & [Status]))))))`.
Only where `Collected Is Null`.

#### Awaiting parts

Jobs held up for a part, with the part, the supplier and when it is expected. Use it when a customer rings to ask, or to chase a supplier.

From Part Orders, Parts, Suppliers, Jobs, Devices, Customers. Shows Job, Customer, Phone, Device, Part, Supplier, Ordered On, Expected, Promised.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`.
Only where `Received On Is Null` and `Status = Awaiting parts`.

#### Past promised date

Unfinished jobs whose promised date has gone by, latest first, with the customer's number so the counter can ring them with news.

From Jobs, Devices, Customers, Staff. Shows Job, Status, Customer, Phone, Device, Technician, Promised, Days Late.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Days Late is `DateDiff("d", [Promised], Date())`.
Only where `Days Late > 0` and `Finished Is Null`.

#### Ready for collection

Every finished device still on the shelf, longest waiting first, with what is left to pay and how the customer wants to be told. The calling list.

From Jobs, Devices, Customers. Shows Job, Customer, Phone, Contact By, Device, Outcome, Finished, Days Waiting, To Pay.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Finished], Date())`; To Pay is `Round(Nz([Charge]) - Nz([Deposit]), 2)`.
Only where `Finished Is Not Null` and `Collected Is Null`.

#### Uncollected 14 days or more

Devices ready for two weeks or longer and not picked up, with any reminders already sent. Use it to send a final reminder before the shop's storage terms apply.

From Jobs, Devices, Customers. Shows Job, Customer, Phone, E-mail, Device, Finished, Days Waiting, To Pay, Notes.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Finished], Date())`; To Pay is `Round(Nz([Charge]) - Nz([Deposit]), 2)`.
Only where `Days Waiting >= 14` and `Collected Is Null`.

#### Quotes awaiting approval

Quotes given and not yet answered, oldest first, with the price and the phone number to follow up.

From Jobs, Devices, Customers. Shows Job, Quoted On, Days Waiting, Customer, Phone, Device, Fault, Quote.
Calculated: Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Quoted On], Date())`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`.
Only where `Status = Awaiting approval`.

#### Parts to reorder

Shelf parts at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with what a full reorder would cost.

From Parts, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Code, Part, In Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity, Cost, Order Value.
Calculated: Order Value is `Round([Reorder Quantity] * [Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Spare <= 0` and `Stocked = Yes`.

#### Parts on order

Everything ordered and not yet arrived, with the expected date and the record number of the job it is for when there is one.

From Part Orders, Parts, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Part, Quantity, Unit Cost, Ordered On, Expected, For Job.
Only where `Received On Is Null`.

#### Takings by month

Money taken each month, deposits and account payments included, and how many payments made it up.

From Payments. Shows Month, Payments, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Paid On], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Takings last 30 days

The last thirty days of takings split by payment method, for checking against the card machine and the bank statement.

From Payments. Shows Method, Payments, Takings.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Technician workload

How many unfinished jobs each technician has, how many are stuck on parts or quotes, and their oldest job.

From Jobs, Staff. Shows Technician, Open Jobs, Awaiting Parts, Awaiting Approval, Oldest Booked In.
Calculated: Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Awaiting Parts is `IIf([Status] = "Awaiting parts", 1, 0)`; Awaiting Approval is `IIf([Status] = "Awaiting approval", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Finished Is Null`.

#### Technician turnaround

For repairs finished in the last year: how many each technician did, the average days from booking in to finished, and what they were charged at.

From Jobs, Staff. Shows Technician, Jobs Repaired, Average Days, Charged.
Calculated: Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Average Days is `DateDiff("d", [Booked In], [Finished])`.
Only where `Outcome = Repaired` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Work by device kind

Jobs and money by kind of device over the whole period, with the average days each kind takes.

From Jobs, Devices. Shows Kind, Jobs, Charged, Average Days.
Calculated: Average Days is `DateDiff("d", [Booked In], [Finished])`.

#### Warranty returns

Jobs that came back under warranty, newest first; the fault names the first job, so repeat faults on a part or a technician's work show up.

From Jobs, Devices, Customers, Staff. Shows Job, Booked In, Customer, Device, Fault, Technician, Status.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Warranty Of Is Not Null`.

#### Job sheets

Every job booked in over the last fourteen days with its full detail: serial, fault, what was left with it, quote and promised date.

From Jobs, Devices, Customers, Staff. Shows Technician, Job, Booked In, Customer, Phone, Device, Serial, Fault, Left With It, Status, Quote, Promised.
Calculated: Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 14`.

#### Parts margin

Each part fitted over the period: how many, what they were charged at with VAT, and the margin over cost on the price without VAT. Warranty fittings count against the margin.

From Job Lines, Parts. Shows Fits, Part, Fitted, Charged, Margin.
Calculated: Charged is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`; Margin is `Round([Quantity] * ([Unit Price] / (1 + [Tax Rate]) - [Cost]), 2)`.
Only where `Done On Is Not Null`.

#### Accounts to chase

Every invoice a business account has not paid yet, by account and due date, with how many days overdue it is (nought when it is not due yet).

From Invoices, Accounts, Jobs. Shows Account, Contact, E-mail, Invoice, Job, Invoice Date, Due Date, Balance, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Days Overdue is `IIf(DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date()) > 0, DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date()), 0)`.
Only where `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Under warranty

Repairs still inside their 90 days, with the certificate number and what it covers, those ending soonest first. Look a customer up here when a device comes back.

From Warranties, Jobs, Devices, Customers. Shows Certificate, Job, Customer, Phone, Device, Serial, Covers, Warranty Until, Days Left.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Device is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Warranty Until])`.
Only where `Days Left >= 0`.

#### VAT by month

For each month, the invoices raised, their net value, the VAT inside them and the total: the figures for the VAT return.

From Invoices. Shows Month, Invoices, Net Sales, VAT, Invoiced.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Invoice Date], "yyyy-mm")`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Accounts, Customers, Staff, Suppliers, Parts, Devices, Jobs, Part Orders, Job Lines, Quotes, Quote Lines, Invoices, Warranties, Payments. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Job board

The job board printed for the bench, one section per stage, each job with its customer, device, fault, technician and promised date.

From the query Job board, a group for each Stage: Job, Booked In, Customer, Device, Fault, Technician, Promised, Days Left, with the count of Job.

#### Ready for collection: to phone

A calling list for the counter: each device waiting to be collected, the customer's number, how they like to be contacted and what they owe, longest waiting first.

From the query Ready for collection: Job, Customer, Phone, Contact By, Device, Outcome, Finished, Days Waiting, To Pay, with the count of Job, total of To Pay.

#### Parts to order

The parts to reorder, one section per supplier, with the cost of each order. Take it to the phone or the supplier's website.

From the query Parts to reorder, a group for each Supplier: Code, Part, In Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity, Cost, Order Value, with the total of Order Value.

#### Takings by month

Monthly takings with a grand total, for the accountant or the owner's month-end look.

From the query Takings by month: Month, Payments, Takings, with the total of Payments, total of Takings.

#### Job sheets: the last two weeks

The last two weeks of jobs, one section per technician, with every detail taken at the counter. Print it to check work in progress against the shelf.

From the query Job sheets, a group for each Technician: Job, Booked In, Customer, Phone, Device, Serial, Fault, Left With It, Status, Quote, Promised, with the count of Job.

#### Technician turnaround

Each technician's finished repairs over the last year, their average turnaround and the value of their work.

From the query Technician turnaround: Technician, Jobs Repaired, Average Days, Charged, with the total of Jobs Repaired, total of Charged.

#### Account invoices due

Unpaid account invoices, a section for each business, with days overdue and the total owed: the list for chasing payment.

From the query Accounts to chase, a group for each Account: Invoice, Job, Invoice Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, Balance, with the total of Balance.

#### VAT by month, from the invoices

Net sales, VAT and invoiced totals for each month with the grand totals, to fill in the VAT return or hand to the accountant.

From the query VAT by month: Month, Invoices, Net Sales, VAT, Invoiced, with the total of Net Sales, total of VAT, total of Invoiced.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Booking-in receipt

Printed at the counter when a device is booked in, on A5, one copy for the customer: the job number, the device and its serial, the fault as described, what was left with it, the price if one was quoted, the ready-by date, the shop's terms in short and two lines to sign. It prints for jobs not yet collected; the price and deposit print only when there is one, and a warranty return says so. One for each record of Jobs, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Booking-in receipt {Number}
- Fields: Job number, Booked in, Customer, Phone, Ready by, Technician
- Fields: Device, Make, Model, Serial number, Colour, Left with it
- Fields: Fault as described, Quoted price, VAT included, Deposit paid
- Words: This is a return under the warranty of job {Warranty Of}: there is nothing to pay for putting right the same fault.
- Words: Our terms, in short:
- Words: 1. We will check the device and tell you the price before we do any work. If we cannot repair it, there is nothing to pay.
- Words: 1. The price quoted above is for the repair described. If we find another fault once the work starts, we will ask you before doing anything more.
- Words: 2. Please keep a copy of your photos and files. We take care with your data, but a repair can lose it, and we cannot be held to blame for that.
- Words: 3. When a part has to be ordered in for you, we take its price as a deposit. It comes off your bill, and is kept only if you cancel after the part has arrived.
- Words: 4. The ready-by date is our best estimate. We will tell you if it moves, and tell you by your chosen way when the device is ready.
- Words: 5. A device not collected within 90 days of our final reminder may be recycled or sold to cover what is owed. Please bring this receipt, or quote {Number}, when you collect.
- Signed by: Customer, Booked in by
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Quote

The written quote sent after diagnosis: the parts and labour, the VAT inside them, the total and how long the price holds, with how to say yes. It prints for quotes not yet answered; printed from the Quotes form, an answered one says the answer and when. One for each record of Quotes, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Quote {Number}
- Fields: Quote, Date, Valid until, Job number, For, Phone, Make, Model, Serial number
- Fields: Fault reported
- Lines from Quote Lines: Item, Description, Qty or hours, Price, Amount, VAT included
- Totals: Net of VAT, VAT, Total
- Words: {Answer} on {Answered On}.
- Words: This is the price for the repair described above, VAT included, and it holds until {Valid Until}. If we find another fault once the work starts, we will ask you before doing anything more.
- Words: To go ahead, reply to this quote or call us on {Business.Phone}, quoting {Number}. If you would rather not, there is a charge of half an hour at our bench rate for the diagnosis, and you can collect the device as it is.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Invoice

The VAT invoice raised when the work is finished: the parts and labour lines with the VAT in each, the net, VAT and total, and the deposit and balance due when a deposit was paid. A paid invoice says so; an unpaid one says how to pay. One for each record in Invoices, its lines found through its job. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: VAT invoice {Number}
- Fields: Invoice, Date and tax point, Due, Job number, Customer, Account, Address, Postcode, Make, Model, Serial number
- Lines from Job Lines: Item, Description, Qty or hours, Price, Amount, VAT %, VAT included
- Totals: Net of VAT, VAT, Total, Deposit paid, Balance due
- Words: Paid in full on {Paid On}, thank you.
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} By bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Collection receipt

The till receipt handed over with the device: the work done and its price, VAT included, the deposit, what was paid today and a line to sign that the device came back in working order. It prints for jobs collected, with what was paid today or what is still to pay on an account. One for each record of Jobs, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Collection receipt
- Fields: Job, Collected, Customer, Make, Model, Serial, Outcome, Guaranteed until
- Lines from Job Lines: Description, Amount, VAT
- Totals: Total, VAT included, Deposit paid, Paid today, Still to pay
- Words: Nothing to pay: the work was under warranty.
- Words: Handed back with: {Left With It}.
- Signed by: Received in working order
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Warranty certificate

The 90-day warranty given with every repair: the device, the dates, what it covers and what it does not, and how to claim. It prints for warranties still running, the 90 days after the repair. Have the wording checked against the consumer law of your own country. One for each record of Warranties, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Repair warranty {Number}
- Fields: Certificate, Job number, Repaired on, Covered until, Customer, Device, Make, Model, Serial number
- Fields: What it covers
- Words: 1. For 90 days from the repair, until {Job.Warranty Until}, we will put right free of charge, parts and labour included, any fault in the part we fitted or in our work, and the same fault if it comes back.
- Words: 2. It does not cover new damage after the repair (a drop, a crack, liquid or heat), parts of the device we did not work on, or a device that someone else has opened since. It does not cover lost data.
- Words: 3. To claim, bring the device to the shop with this certificate, or quote {Number}, before the warranty ends. We look at warranty work first, usually within two working days.
- Words: 4. This warranty is given on top of your rights as a customer and takes nothing away from them.
- Signed by: For the shop
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Account statement

Sent to each business account at the month end: the invoices still unpaid, oldest first, with the days each is overdue, a running total of what is owed, how much of it is overdue and the day of the statement. One for each record in Accounts. One for each record of Accounts, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Statement of account
- Fields: Account, For the attention of, Address, City, Postcode, Days to pay, Credit limit
- Lines from Invoices: Invoice, Job, Date, Due, Days overdue, Owing, Owed so far, Overdue
- Totals: Statement date, Of which overdue, Balance owing
- Words: Nothing is owing on this account today. Thank you.
- Words: Invoices are due {Payment Days} days from their date. Please pay by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting the invoice numbers. If you have paid in the last few days, thank you, and please ignore what is shown as owing.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name, address, VAT number and payment details, which every document prints. Then Staff, then Suppliers, then Parts (each part pointing at its supplier, with Stocked set to No for parts you only order in), and Accounts for any businesses you invoice. When a customer comes to the counter, add them to Customers, add their device to Devices, then open a Job for that device with its number, the fault, the technician and the promised date. As the job moves on, change its Status, fill in the quote (and a record in Quotes when it is written), and add its parts and labour in Job Lines. When it is finished, raise its Invoice and its Warranty, record each payment in Payments as it is taken, and put Finished and Collected on the job when they happen.

### Making it yours

- For a bike workshop, use Devices for bikes (Kind as Road, Mountain, Hybrid, E-bike; Serial as the frame number) and add a Booked For date for the day the customer wants it back.
- For an engineer who visits homes, add Visit Date and Visit Address to Jobs and a call-out line in Job Lines, and make a query of visits in the next 7 days ordered by postcode.
- Add a Courier Reference to Part Orders, and a query of orders past their Expected date, to chase late suppliers.
- Add a status such as Sent to maker for repairs sent away, and add it to the Stage calculation in the Job board query so it sorts in the right place.
- Add a Disposal Date to Jobs for devices never collected, and a query of devices uncollected for 90 days or more, if your terms say you may then recycle or sell them.
- If you are not registered for VAT, set Tax Rate to 0 in the Business record and on new lines; the documents then show no VAT, and the heading of the Invoice template can be changed from VAT invoice to Invoice.
- Add Passcode Given (Yes/No) and Data Backed Up (Yes/No) to Jobs, so the bench knows what it can test before starting, and add them to the Booking-in receipt.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print an older invoice or quote?**

Open the print template Invoice and choose the invoice by its number; every invoice ever raised is there. The Quote template holds only quotes not yet answered, so print an answered one from the Quotes form with it on screen. To find the number, look the job up on the Jobs form or in the query Job board.

**A customer has lost their receipt. How do I find their device?**

Open the Customers form and find them by name or phone, then look at their devices and jobs. The query Ready for collection lists every finished device still on the shelf with its customer.

**Is this device still under warranty?**

Open the query Under warranty and look for the customer or the serial. If the job is there, its Days Left is how long the cover has to run. Book the return in as a new job with Warranty Of set to the first job and nothing to pay.

**Why does the invoice say less VAT than 20 percent of the total?**

The prices include VAT, so the VAT is one sixth of each line, not a fifth: 20 percent of the price without VAT. On a total of 112.75 the VAT is 18.79.

**How do I change the bench rate or the VAT rate?**

The rate per hour is whatever you type in Unit Price on each labour line, so a new rate applies from the next job. The VAT rate is in the Business record (Tax Rate) and on each line; old lines keep the rate they were charged at.

**How do I see what an account owes?**

Open the query Accounts to chase, or print the Account statement for that business. Both show only invoices without a Paid On date.

**Can I start with my own shop instead of Ironbridge?**

Yes. Make the database empty from the sample, fill in the Business record with your own name, address, VAT number and bank details, and every document prints with them.

## Quarrybank Motors

**Garage and MOT centre.** Customers, vehicles, bookings, job cards, MOT tests, services, reminders, parts and invoices for an independent garage.

Quarrybank Motors is an invented independent garage and MOT test centre in Leeds, with four bays. Three technicians and a workshop manager do the work, two of them as MOT testers, and a service advisor runs the desk: the phone, the diary, the estimates and the customers waiting for their keys. A few local firms run their vans and cars on a trade account and pay by transfer within thirty days.

Each vehicle is one record, known by its registration, with the dates its MOT and its service fall due. Four weeks before either, the garage sends a reminder, and most customers book in. A booking becomes a job card when the vehicle arrives; the labour (hours at the bench rate), the parts and the MOT fee go on it as lines, and when the work is done those lines are the invoice. An MOT test is recorded with its result, its own test number, and its failures and advisories; failures are put right and the car is retested, while most advisories wait for another day, so the garage can ring about them later.

Prices are kept without VAT, as a garage quotes its trade customers, and VAT is added line by line. The MOT fee carries no VAT. The records cover about thirteen months up to the day the file is made, with bookings in the diary for the weeks ahead, reminders ready for next month, cars waiting on parts, a few estimates not yet answered, and trade invoices not yet paid.

Every registration is invented and has a Q among its last three letters, which current British plates never use, and the makes and models are made up.

It suits, with small changes: A tyre and exhaust centre; A van and light commercial workshop; A motorcycle workshop, with bikes as the vehicles; A mobile mechanic, with bookings at the customer's address; A body shop or smart repair business, with estimates for every job; An agricultural or plant repairer servicing machines by the hour.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Prices are kept without VAT and VAT is added on each line and rounded to the penny, then the lines are added up. An invoice's Tax is that sum, so it can differ by a penny from 20 percent of the net worked out once.
- The MOT fee is a line of its own with a Tax Rate of 0: the test carries no VAT. Repairs to put a failure right are ordinary labour and part lines at the full rate.
- An invoice's lines are the job card's own lines, found through the job card it is for. Add all the work to the job card before you invoice it; there is one invoice for each job card.
- The numbers on job cards, invoices, estimates and MOT tests (JC-, INV-, EST-, MT-) are typed, not made by Data Files. Keep each run in date order and start again at 0001 each January. A real test centre records the national MOT test number in Test Number.
- MOT Due and Service Due on a vehicle are kept by hand when a test or service is done here. A test passed up to a month before the due date keeps the same date and adds a year; a later test starts a new year from the test.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: job cards not yet invoiced, estimates not answered or still in date, reminders not yet sent, every invoice and every trade account. A Trade statement lists only unpaid invoices. Printed from a form, the record on screen prints whatever its state.
- Every registration in this sample is invented, with a Q among its last three letters so it cannot be a real car's. Your own records will have real registrations: keep the file safe, as they identify your customers' vehicles.

### Tutorial

#### Take a booking

1. Open the Vehicles form and find the registration. If the vehicle is new to you, first add the owner on the Customers form (choose their trade account in Account if they have one), then press New on Vehicles and fill in Registration, Customer, Make, Model, Fuel, Year and Tyre Size.
2. Open the query Bookings next 7 days to find a day with room.
3. Open the Bookings form and press New. Choose the vehicle, type the Date and Time, say what for in Work (MOT, Service, MOT and service, or the repair), tick Courtesy Car if it is needed, and set Booked On to today.

#### Start the day and open the job cards

1. Open the report Day sheet: today's and tomorrow's bookings in time order.
2. When a vehicle arrives, set its booking's Status to Arrived. Open the Job Cards form, press New, type the next number (JC-2026- and the next in the run), choose the vehicle and the booking, the technician, today in Opened, the mileage in Mileage In and the work in Work Requested.
3. With the job card on screen, open the print template Job card from Print templates and press Print. It goes on the dashboard with the keys; the technician writes on it what was done.
4. During the day, the query Open job cards shows what is in, who has it and what each is waiting for.

#### Record an MOT test

1. Open the MOT Tests form and press New. Type the test number, choose the vehicle, the job card and the tester, and fill in Test Date, Mileage, Result and Fee.
2. In MOT Items below, add each failure (Kind Fail) and each advisory (Kind Advisory) in the tester's words.
3. On a pass, type the new expiry in Expires and the same date in the vehicle's MOT Due. On a fail, ring the customer, put the failures right on the job card, then add a retest with Retest Of set to the failed test and Fee 0, and tick Fixed on each failure.
4. Add the MOT fee to the job card's Job Lines as Kind MOT, with Tax Rate 0.

#### Record a service, then invoice the job

1. On the job card, add a line in Job Lines for each part fitted (Kind Part, the part, its name, how many, its price and cost) and for the labour (Kind Labour, the technician, the hours and the rate). Fill in Done On on each.
2. Open the Services form and press New: choose the vehicle and job card, the kind of service and the mileage, and when the next is due. Put the same date in the vehicle's Service Due.
3. Open the Invoices form and press New. Type the next number (INV-2026-...), choose the job card and the trade account if there is one, and fill in Invoice Date, Due Date, Net, Tax and Total. The invoice lists the job card's lines on its own. Close the job card: Status Invoiced and Closed today.
4. Open the print template Invoice, choose the invoice, and press Print or Save as PDF. When the customer pays, fill in Paid On and Method.

#### Give an estimate

1. Open the Estimates form and press New. Type the next number (EST-2026-...), choose the vehicle, today in Estimate Date, thirty days on in Valid Until, and the work in a few words.
2. In Estimate Lines, add the labour (hours and rate) and each part, without VAT. Put the totals in Net, Tax and Total.
3. Open the print template Estimate, choose it, and press Save as PDF to e-mail it, or Print.
4. The query Estimates awaiting answer lists those not yet answered. When the customer says yes, fill in Answer and Answered On, take a booking, and later choose the job card in Job Card.

#### Send next month's reminders

1. Near the end of each month, open the query MOTs due next month and the query Services due next 30 days.
2. For each vehicle, add a record on the Reminders form: the vehicle, the Kind (MOT, service, or MOT and service), the Due date and the Method from the customer's Remind By.
3. Open the query Reminders to send to check them, then open the print template Reminder letter, which holds the reminders not yet sent, and press Print. Fill in Sent On on each.
4. When a customer books from a reminder, tick Booked on it.

#### Month end: trade statements, hours and VAT

1. Open the report Trade invoices due to see what each trade account owes.
2. Open the print template Trade statement, choose the accounts that owe something, and press Save as PDF to e-mail each one.
3. Open the report Technician hours for the hours each technician sold, and the report VAT by month for the VAT return.
4. Every Monday, open the report Parts to order and place the orders; record them on the Part Orders form.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 31 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The name printed at the top of every document. |
| Address | Short text | The street address. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country. |
| Phone | Short text | The phone number customers call. |
| E-mail | Short text | The address customers write to. |
| Website | Short text | The website, if there is one. |
| Tax Number | Short text | The VAT or sales tax registration number, printed on invoices. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Company Number | Short text | The registered company number, where the business is a company. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Bank Details | Short text | Where customers pay by transfer: the bank, account name and number. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Payment Terms | Short text | The words printed under an invoice's total, such as "Payment within 30 days". |
| Tax Rate | Number | The usual rate of VAT or sales tax as a fraction: 0.2 is twenty percent. Lines may carry a rate of their own. |
| Currency | Short text | The currency the business trades in, as its three-letter code. |
| Document Footer | Long text | A line or two at the foot of every document: thanks, opening hours, returns policy. |

### Queries

#### Bookings today and tomorrow

The diary for today and tomorrow, in time order, with the registration, the customer's number, the work and whether they need the courtesy car. Cancelled bookings are left out. Open it first thing.

From Bookings, Vehicles, Customers. Shows Date, Time, Registration, Vehicle, Customer, Phone, Work, Courtesy Car, Status.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 1` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Bookings next 7 days

How many vehicles are booked in for each of the next seven days, how many are MOTs and how many need the courtesy car, to see where there is room.

From Bookings, Vehicles, Customers. Shows Date, Bookings, MOTs, Courtesy Cars.
Calculated: MOTs is `IIf(Left([Work], 3) = "MOT", 1, 0)`; Courtesy Cars is `IIf([Courtesy Car], 1, 0)`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 7` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### MOTs due next month

Every vehicle whose MOT runs out next month, with the customer's address and how they like reminders: the list to send reminder letters from.

From Vehicles, Customers. Shows MOT Due, Registration, Vehicle, Customer, Address, City, Postcode, Phone, Remind By.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Months Ahead = 1`.

#### Services due next 30 days

Vehicles whose yearly service falls due in the next thirty days, with their last mileage.

From Vehicles, Customers. Shows Service Due, Registration, Vehicle, Mileage, Customer, Phone, Remind By, Days Left.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Service Due])`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 30`.

#### Reminders to send

Reminders made ready and not yet sent, by due date, with how each customer wants them. Print the Reminder letter for the letters, then fill in Sent On.

From Reminders, Vehicles, Customers. Shows Due, Kind, Registration, Customer, Method, E-mail, Phone.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Sent On Is Null`.

#### Advisories not fixed

Advisories from MOT tests in the last year that have not been put right, by registration: worn tyres, thin brake pads, a little corrosion. Ring the customer, or bring it up at the next visit.

From MOT Items, MOT Tests, Vehicles, Customers. Shows Registration, Vehicle, Customer, Phone, Test Date, Advisory.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Kind = Advisory` and `Fixed = No` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Open job cards

Every job card not yet closed, oldest first, with the vehicle, the technician, its status and how many days it has been open.

From Job Cards, Vehicles, Customers, Staff. Shows Job Card, Opened, Registration, Vehicle, Customer, Phone, Work Requested, Technician, Status, Days Open.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`; Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`; Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Days Open is `DateDiff("d", [Opened], Date())`.
Only where `Closed Is Null`.

#### Technician hours last 30 days

Hours of labour each technician has sold in the last thirty days, and what they came to without VAT.

From Job Lines, Staff. Shows Technician, Hours Sold, Labour Sold, Lines.
Calculated: Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Labour Sold is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.
Only where `Kind = Labour` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Technician hours by month

Hours of labour sold by each technician in each month, for the workshop manager's month-end look.

From Job Lines, Staff. Shows Month, Technician, Hours Sold, Labour Sold.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Done On], "yyyy-mm")`; Technician is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Labour Sold is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.
Only where `Kind = Labour` and `Done On Is Not Null`.

#### Parts margin

For each kind of part, what was sold without VAT, what it cost and the margin, the biggest first.

From Job Lines, Parts. Shows Category, Units, Sales, Cost of Parts, Margin.
Calculated: Sales is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`; Cost of Parts is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Cost], 2)`; Margin is `Round([Quantity] * ([Unit Price] - [Unit Cost]), 2)`.
Only where `Done On Is Not Null`.

#### Takings by month

Money received each month from invoices paid, private and trade together.

From Invoices. Shows Month, Invoices Paid, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Paid On], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Paid On Is Not Null`.

#### VAT by month

For each month, the invoices raised, their net value, the VAT and the total: the figures for the VAT return.

From Invoices. Shows Month, Invoices, Net Sales, VAT, Invoiced.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Invoice Date], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### MOT results by month

How many MOT tests were done each month, how many passed and failed, and how many were retests.

From MOT Tests. Shows Month, Tests, Passed, Failed, Retests.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Test Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Passed is `IIf([Result] = "Pass", 1, 0)`; Failed is `IIf([Result] = "Fail", 1, 0)`; Retests is `IIf(Nz([Retest Of], 0) > 0, 1, 0)`.

#### Service history

Every service carried out, vehicle by vehicle, newest first, with the mileage, the job card and when the next is due.

From Services, Job Cards, Vehicles. Shows Registration, Vehicle, Service Date, Kind, Mileage, Job Card, Next Due, Next Due Mileage.
Calculated: Vehicle is `[Make] & " " & [Model]`.

#### Estimates awaiting answer

Estimates the customer has not yet said yes or no to, oldest first, with the phone number to follow up.

From Estimates, Vehicles, Customers. Shows Estimate, Estimate Date, Registration, Customer, Phone, Work, Total, Valid Until.
Calculated: Customer is `[Customers].[First Name] & " " & [Customers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Answer Is Null`.

#### Parts to reorder

Shelf parts at or below their reorder level, by supplier, with what a full reorder would cost.

From Parts, Suppliers. Shows Supplier, Code, Part, In Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity, Cost, Order Value.
Calculated: Order Value is `Round([Reorder Quantity] * [Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Spare <= 0` and `Stocked = Yes`.

#### Trade accounts to chase

Every trade invoice not yet paid, by account and due date, with the registration and how many days overdue it is (nought when it is not due yet).

From Invoices, Accounts, Job Cards, Vehicles. Shows Account, Contact, Phone, Invoice, Registration, Invoice Date, Due Date, Total, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Days Overdue is `IIf(DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date()) > 0, DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date()), 0)`.
Only where `Paid On Is Null`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Accounts, Customers, Staff, Suppliers, Parts, Vehicles, Bookings, Job Cards, Part Orders, Job Lines, MOT Tests, MOT Items, Services, Reminders, Estimates, Estimate Lines, Invoices. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Bookings: today and tomorrow

The diary for today and tomorrow, one section a day in time order: pin it up in the workshop and keep one at the desk.

From the query Bookings today and tomorrow, a group for each Date: Time, Registration, Vehicle, Customer, Phone, Work, Courtesy Car, Status, with the count of Registration.

#### MOTs due next month

Every vehicle with its MOT due next month and the address to write to, for checking the reminder letters before they go.

From the query MOTs due next month: MOT Due, Registration, Vehicle, Customer, Address, City, Postcode, Remind By, with the count of Registration.

#### Advisories to follow up

Unfixed advisories, a section for each vehicle, with the customer's number: the list for a quiet afternoon on the phone.

From the query Advisories not fixed, a group for each Registration: Test Date, Advisory, Customer, Phone, with the count of Advisory.

#### Work in progress

Open job cards, a section for each status, with the technician and how long each has been open.

From the query Open job cards, a group for each Status: Job Card, Opened, Registration, Vehicle, Work Requested, Technician, Days Open, with the count of Job Card.

#### Hours sold by technician, by month

Hours and labour sold by each technician, a section for each month, with the totals.

From the query Technician hours by month, a group for each Month: Technician, Hours Sold, Labour Sold, with the total of Hours Sold, total of Labour Sold.

#### Takings by month

Money received each month with a grand total.

From the query Takings by month: Month, Invoices Paid, Takings, with the total of Invoices Paid, total of Takings.

#### VAT by month, from the invoices

Net sales, VAT and invoiced totals for each month, with the grand totals, for the VAT return or the accountant.

From the query VAT by month: Month, Invoices, Net Sales, VAT, Invoiced, with the total of Net Sales, total of VAT, total of Invoiced.

#### Parts to order

The parts to reorder, a page for each supplier, with the value of each order.

From the query Parts to reorder, a group for each Supplier: Code, Part, In Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity, Cost, Order Value, with the total of Order Value.

#### Trade invoices due

Unpaid trade invoices, a section for each account, with days overdue and the total owed.

From the query Trade accounts to chase, a group for each Account: Invoice, Registration, Invoice Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, Total, with the total of Total.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Estimate

The written estimate for a repair: the vehicle, the work, the labour and parts with VAT, the total and how long it holds. It prints for estimates not yet answered or still in date; an answered one says the answer and when. One for each record of Estimates, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Estimate {Number}
- Fields: Estimate, Date, Valid until, For, Address, Postcode, Registration, Make, Model, Mileage
- Fields: Work to be done
- Lines from Estimate Lines: Item, Description, Qty or hours, Price, Net, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Net, VAT, Estimated total
- Words: {Answer} on {Answered On}.
- Words: This estimate is our price for the work above, and holds until {Valid Until}. If we find anything else once the work starts, we will ring you before we do it: nothing more is done without your say-so.
- Words: To book the work in, call us on {Business.Phone} quoting {Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Job card

Printed when a vehicle arrives and kept with its keys: the vehicle, mileage and work asked for, then the work done and parts fitted with who did them, and two lines to sign. Prices are left off, as the workshop does not need them. It prints for job cards not yet invoiced, the vehicles in the workshop; a closed one prints from the Job Cards form. One for each record of Job Cards, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Job card {Number}
- Fields: Job card, Opened, Technician, Registration, Make, Model, Fuel, Year, Mileage in, Customer, Phone, Tyres, Status, Closed, Courtesy car
- Fields: Work requested, Notes
- Lines from Job Lines: Kind, Work done or part fitted, Part, Qty or hours, By, Date
- Words: Before work starts: check the mileage, note any damage and warning lights, and fit seat and floor covers. Any work beyond what is asked for above is authorised by the customer first, and the call is noted here.
- Signed by: Technician, Road test and quality check

#### Invoice

The VAT invoice for a job card: the labour, parts and MOT fee with the VAT on each line, the net, VAT and total, and how to pay, or when it was paid. The note that the MOT fee carries no VAT prints only when there is one. One for each record in Invoices, its lines found through its job card. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: VAT invoice {Number}
- Fields: Invoice, Date and tax point, Due, Job card, Customer, Trade account, Address, Postcode, Registration, Make, Model, Mileage
- Lines from Job Lines: Item, Description, Qty or hours, Price, Net, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Net, VAT, Total
- Words: The MOT test fee carries no VAT.
- Words: Paid on {Paid On} by {Method}, thank you.
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} By bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Reminder letter

The letter sent four weeks before an MOT or service is due: short and friendly, with the registration, the due date and how to book. It prints for reminders not yet sent, with a paragraph for an MOT or for a service. Have the wording checked for your own country. One for each record of Reminders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Fields: To, Address, Town, Postcode
- Heading: {Vehicle}: {Kind} due on {Due}
- Words: Dear {Vehicle.Customer.First Name} {Vehicle.Customer.Last Name},
- Words: Our records show that your {Vehicle.Make} {Vehicle.Model}, registration {Vehicle}, is due its {Kind} on {Due}. We are writing in good time so that you can book a day that suits you.
- Words: An MOT can be done up to a month before the due date without losing any time on the certificate, and if your service is due too we can do both on the same visit. A courtesy car can be booked if you need one, and we can collect the car from a local address.
- Words: A service on time keeps the warranty and the service history in order, and we will tell you about anything else we find before doing it. A courtesy car can be booked if you need one, and we can collect the car from a local address.
- Words: To book, ring us on {Business.Phone}, write to {Business.E-mail}, or call in. If the car has been sold, or the work done elsewhere, just let us know and we will update our records.
- Words: Yours sincerely,
- Signed by: Service desk
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Trade statement

Sent to each trade account at the month end: the invoices still unpaid, oldest first, with the days each is overdue, a running total of what is owed, how much of it is overdue and the day of the statement. One for each record in Accounts. One for each record of Accounts, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Statement of account
- Fields: Account, For the attention of, Address, City, Postcode, Days to pay, Credit limit
- Lines from Invoices: Invoice, Registration, Date, Due, Days overdue, Owing, Owed so far, Overdue
- Totals: Statement date, Of which overdue, Balance owing
- Words: Nothing is owing on this account today. Thank you.
- Words: Invoices are due {Payment Days} days from their date. Please pay by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting the invoice numbers. If you have paid in the last few days, thank you, and please ignore what is shown as owing.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name, address, VAT number and payment details, which every document prints. Then Staff (tick MOT Tester for your testers), Suppliers and Parts (each part pointing at its supplier, with its cost and price without VAT), and Accounts for any trade customers. Customers and their Vehicles come in as people ring; add each vehicle's MOT Due and Service Due so reminders work from the start. Then the diary: Bookings, Job Cards with their Job Lines, MOT Tests with their items, Services, Invoices, Estimates and Reminders as the work goes on.

### Making it yours

- For a tyre centre, add a Tyre Brand and Load Rating to Parts and a Tread Depth field to Job Lines, and a query of vehicles with tread below 3 mm.
- Add a Courtesy Cars table (registration, insurance, next service) and point Bookings at it instead of the Yes/No, so two cars can be booked separately.
- For a mobile mechanic, add a Visit Address and a Travel line to Job Cards, and sort the day sheet by postcode.
- Add a Labour Rate to Accounts for trade customers on a lower rate, and use it on their labour lines.
- Add a Warranty Until to Job Lines for parts with a maker's warranty, and a query of parts still covered.
- Record what technicians clock on in a Time Sheets table (technician, day, hours attended) and compare it with Technician hours by month to see efficiency.

### Questions people ask

**How do I see everything done to one car?**

Open the Vehicles form and find the registration: its job cards, MOT tests and services are its history. The query Service history lists every service by registration.

**How do I find whose MOT is due so I can send reminders?**

Open the query MOTs due next month, or the report MOT reminder list to print it. Add a Reminders record for each, and print the Reminder letter.

**A car failed its MOT. What do I record?**

The failed test with its failures as MOT Items of Kind Fail. Put the work on the job card, then add a retest with Retest Of pointing at the failed test, and tick Fixed on each failure. Advisories stay unticked until they are done; the query Advisories not fixed lists them.

**Why is there no VAT on the MOT line?**

The MOT test fee carries no VAT, so its line has a Tax Rate of 0. Everything else on the invoice is at the standard rate.

**How do I print an older invoice or job card?**

Open the print template Invoice and choose the invoice by its number; every invoice ever made is there. The Job card template holds only cards still open, so print a closed one from the Job Cards form with it on screen.

**How do I see how busy each technician is?**

Open the query Technician hours last 30 days for hours sold, or the query Open job cards for what each has in the workshop now.

**Can I start with my own garage instead of Quarrybank?**

Yes. Make the database empty from the sample, fill in the Business record with your own name, address, VAT number and bank details, then add your parts and staff. Every document prints with your details.

## Fernhollow Cleaning

**Cleaning company.** Clients, sites, contracts, the rota, visits, one-off jobs, supplies, payslips and invoices for a cleaning company.

For a cleaning business that cleans the same places week after week under contract and takes on one-off jobs as well: an office cleaning company, a domestic cleaning agency, or one that does both. It answers what such a business asks every week: who is going where in the next seven days, which visits were missed or cut short, what each cleaner earned, which contracts pay their way, who has not paid and which contracts come up for renewal.

Fernhollow Cleaning is invented. It works in and around Leeds with a dozen cleaners paid by the hour. It cleans offices, a dental surgery, a nursery, showrooms and shops early in the morning or in the evening, and homes during the day, weekly or every other week. It also quotes for end of tenancy cleans, carpet and upholstery cleaning, oven cleans and cleans after the builders.

The records cover the last fifteen months, counted back from the day the file is made, with the rota booked two weeks ahead. Each visit is done, done short, covered by another cleaner when the regular one is on holiday or ill, or now and then missed. Contracts renew each year at a slightly higher rate and a few end on notice; new clients start through the year. One-off work is busier in the summer, when tenancies end. Every contract is invoiced on the first working day of the month for the month before, with each visit a line, and each cleaner gets a payslip at the end of the month.

It prints the documents such a business uses: the cleaning contract with its schedule of work for the client to sign, the monthly invoice, a quote for a one-off job, each cleaner's payslip showing hours and gross pay, and a visit sheet for the site with the tasks to tick off and a line for the client to sign.

It suits, with small changes: An office or commercial cleaning contractor; A domestic cleaning agency; A window cleaning round; A carpet and upholstery cleaner; A gardening or grounds maintenance business; A pest control or hygiene service; A home care or befriending service that visits on a rota.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Visits come before Contracts in the design, so that a query with both joins each visit to the cleaner who went rather than to the contract's regular cleaner. Keep that order if you add tables.
- Each visit keeps its own Charge Rate and Pay Rate, so a rate change at renewal or a pay rise in April does not alter what past visits were charged or paid.
- Hours Charged, not Hours Worked, is what goes on the invoice: a cleaner who stays longer does not cost the client more, and a short visit is charged only for the time worked.
- Numbers are typed, not made for you: contracts CON-, invoices INV-, jobs JOB- and payslips PAY-, each a new run each year and each used once.
- Payslips show hours and gross pay only. Tax, National Insurance and pension depend on each person's own position, so they are left to payroll.
- In Stock on Supplies is what the Supply Movements add up to. Change stock by adding a movement and then bringing In Stock to match, never by typing over it alone.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: contracts and visit sheets for contracts in force, quotes for jobs waiting for an answer or booked, and every invoice and payslip. Printed from a form, the record on screen prints whatever its state, an ended contract or a declined quote too.

### Tutorial

#### Take on a new contract client

1. Open the Clients form and press New. Type the Name, set Kind to Commercial or Domestic, and fill in the Contact Name, address, Phone, E-mail and Payment Days.
2. Open the Sites form and press New. Choose the Client, type the site's Name, Site Type, address, Site Contact and Access Notes (who holds the key; never the alarm code).
3. Open the Contracts form and press New. Type the next Number (such as CON-2026-0019), choose the Client, Site and regular Cleaner, and type the Start Date, End Date (a year on), Visits per Week, Days, Start Time, Hours per Visit, Rate, Monthly Estimate and Notice Days. Set Status to Pending.
4. In the Contract Tasks below, add each task with its Area, Order and How Often.
5. Open the print template Cleaning contract from Print templates, choose the contract, and press Print or Save as PDF for the client to sign.
6. On the first day of cleaning, set the contract's Status to Active.

#### Plan the week's rota

1. Open the Visits form and press New for each visit of the coming weeks: choose the Contract and the Cleaner, type the Date, Start Time and Planned Hours, and the contract's Rate in Charge Rate and the cleaner's Hourly Pay in Pay Rate. Status is Booked.
2. When a cleaner is on holiday, change the Cleaner on their visits to the one covering, and say so in Notes.
3. Print the report Rota: a page for each cleaner with where they go each day of the next seven days.
4. For a new site, open the print template Site visit sheet, choose the contract, and print a sheet for the cleaner to take.

#### Record the visits as they are done

1. Each day, open the Visits form at each of yesterday's visits. Type the Hours Worked, set Status to Done, and Hours Charged to the Planned Hours.
2. If the visit was cut short, set Status to Short, Hours Charged to the hours worked, and give the reason in Notes. If nobody went, set Status to Missed and Hours Charged to 0.
3. When the client signed the site book or the visit sheet, tick Signed Off and type who in Signed Off By.
4. Run the query Missed or short visits each week to see what needs putting right.

#### Invoice the month's contracts

1. On the first working day of the month, run the query Work to invoice to see the visits done and not yet invoiced.
2. Open the Invoices form and press New for each contract: type the next Number (INV-2026-0144), choose the Client and Contract, type the Period (such as September 2026), the Invoice Date and the Due Date.
3. In the Invoice Lines, add a line for each visit (Date, Kind Visit, Description, Quantity the hours charged, Unit Price the charge rate, Tax Rate 0.2) and a line for each rechargeable supply used.
4. Type the invoice's Net, VAT (each line's VAT added up) and Total. Put the invoice in the Invoice field of each visit it covers.
5. Open the print template Invoice, choose the invoice, and press Print or Save as PDF. When it is paid, type Paid On and set Status to Paid; the query Invoices overdue lists what has not been.

#### Quote for a one-off job, then do it

1. Open the Jobs form and press New. Type the next Number (JOB-2026-0080), choose the Client (add them first in Clients, Kind One-off, with a Site, if they are new), the Site and the Kind, and type Quoted On and Valid Until.
2. In the Job Items below, add each priced part: Description, Quantity, Unit Price. Type the job's Net, VAT and Total and the Estimated Hours.
3. Open the print template Quote, choose the job, and send it. The query Quotes waiting lists those not yet answered.
4. When the client says yes, set Status to Booked, type Booked For and choose the Cleaner. After the job, type the Hours Worked and Signed Off By, set Status to Done, and add an Invoice for it with the job's items as its lines.

#### Run the month's pay

1. At the month's end, run the query Hours by cleaner, last 30 days, to check each cleaner's visits and hours against their own record.
2. Open the Payslips form and press New for each cleaner: the next Number, the Cleaner, the Period, Period Start and End, the Pay Date, and their Contract Hours, Job Hours and Hours.
3. In the Payslip Lines, add the contract hours at their pay rate, the job hours at the job rate, and holiday pay at 12.07 percent of those two. Type the Gross.
4. Open the print template Payslip, choose the payslip, and print it for the cleaner. Send the report Pay summary to payroll, who work out tax and National Insurance.

#### Keep the store stocked and review contracts

1. When supplies go out to a site, open the Supply Movements form and press New: the Supply, the Date, Kind Used, the Quantity below nought, and the Contract. Bring In Stock on the Supplies form down to match.
2. Each Monday run the query Supplies to reorder; when an order arrives, add a Bought movement for it and bring In Stock up.
3. Each month run Contracts up for renewal and Contract profitability: a contract with a thin margin is one to re-price when it renews.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 34 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The name printed at the top of every document. |
| Address | Short text | The street address. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country. |
| Phone | Short text | The phone number customers call. |
| E-mail | Short text | The address customers write to. |
| Website | Short text | The website, if there is one. |
| Tax Number | Short text | The VAT or sales tax registration number, printed on invoices. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Company Number | Short text | The registered company number, where the business is a company. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Bank Details | Short text | Where customers pay by transfer: the bank, account name and number. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Payment Terms | Short text | The words printed under an invoice's total, such as "Payment within 30 days". |
| Tax Rate | Number | The usual rate of VAT or sales tax as a fraction: 0.2 is twenty percent. Lines may carry a rate of their own. |
| Currency | Short text | The currency the business trades in, as its three-letter code. |
| Document Footer | Long text | A line or two at the foot of every document: thanks, opening hours, returns policy. |

Everyone the company cleans for: businesses on contract, households, and people who have had a one-off job. The sample has 107 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |

#### Sites

The places that are cleaned. A client can have more than one: two offices, or a home and a flat they let out. The sample has 120 records.

The cleaners, each paid by the hour. The sample has 12 records.

| Active | Yes/No | No once they have left; their visits and payslips stay in the records. |

#### Visits

Every visit on the rota, booked ahead and then recorded as it went: the heart of the database. The sample has 4,447 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Contract | Points at Contracts, required | The contract the visit is for, which gives the client and the site. |
| Cleaner | Points at Cleaners | Who goes, or went. A cover cleaner when the regular one is away. |
| Date | Date, required | The day of the visit. |
| Start Time | Short text | When the cleaner starts, such as 06:00 or 17:30. |
| Planned Hours | Number | The hours the contract allows for the visit. |
| Hours Worked | Number | The hours the cleaner actually worked; empty until the visit is done. |
| Hours Charged | Number | The hours the client is charged: the planned hours, or only those worked when the visit was cut short; nought when it was missed. |
| Charge Rate | Currency | The contract's rate an hour at the time of the visit. |
| Pay Rate | Currency | The cleaner's pay an hour at the time of the visit. |
| Status | Short text | Booked (still to come), Done, Short (done, but for fewer hours), Missed or Cancelled (by the client). |
| Signed Off | Yes/No | Yes when the client signed the site book or the visit sheet. |
| Signed Off By | Short text | Who signed it off. |
| Notes | Short text | Why a visit was short, missed or covered. |
| Invoice | Points at Invoices | The invoice the visit was charged on. Empty means not invoiced yet. |

#### Contracts

One for each site cleaned under contract: how often, how long, at what rate, from when and on what notice. A contract renews each year until either side gives notice. The sample has 44 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The contract's number, given in the order contracts start, a new run each year: CON-2026-0012. |
| Client | Points at Clients, required | Who the contract is with. |
| Site | Points at Sites, required | The site it covers. |
| Cleaner | Points at Cleaners | The regular cleaner. |
| Start Date | Date | When the contract first started. |
| End Date | Date | When the current year of the contract ends; it then renews for another year unless notice is given. |
| Last Renewed | Date | When it last renewed, at the rate it has now. |
| Visits per Week | Number | How many visits a week: 0.5 for every other week. |
| Days | Short text | The days of the week the visits fall on. |
| Start Time | Short text | When each visit starts. |
| Hours per Visit | Number | The hours each visit is booked and charged for. |
| Rate | Currency | What an hour is charged at, before VAT. Reviewed at each renewal. |
| Monthly Estimate | Currency | What the contract comes to in an average month, before VAT: visits a week, times hours, times the rate, times 52, divided by 12. |
| Notice Days | Whole number | The notice either side must give to end it. |
| Status | Short text | Pending (signed, not started), Active, Notice given or Ended. |
| Notice Given On | Date | The day notice was given. |
| Ended On | Date | The last day of cleaning under it. |
| Notes | Long text | Why it ended, or anything agreed beyond the schedule. |

#### Contract Tasks

The schedule of work for each contract: what is done in each area and how often. It prints on the contract and on the site visit sheet. The sample has 315 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Contract | Points at Contracts, required | The contract the task belongs to. |
| Order | Whole number | Where it comes in the list. |
| Area | Short text | The part of the site, such as Kitchen or Washrooms. |
| Task | Short text, required | What is done there. |
| How Often | Short text | Every visit, Weekly or Monthly. |

One-off work: end of tenancy cleans, carpets, ovens, deep cleans. A job starts as a quote and is booked, done and invoiced, or declined. The sample has 94 records.
