### Relationships

- Sites.Client points at a record in Clients
- Visits.Contract points at a record in Contracts
- Visits.Cleaner points at a record in Cleaners
- Visits.Invoice points at a record in Invoices
- Contracts.Client points at a record in Clients
- Contracts.Site points at a record in Sites
- Contracts.Cleaner points at a record in Cleaners
- Contract Tasks.Contract points at a record in Contracts
- Jobs.Client points at a record in Clients
- Jobs.Site points at a record in Sites
- Jobs.Cleaner points at a record in Cleaners
- Job Items.Job points at a record in Jobs
- Invoices.Client points at a record in Clients
- Invoices.Site points at a record in Sites
- Invoices.Contract points at a record in Contracts
- Invoices.Job points at a record in Jobs
- Invoice Lines.Invoice points at a record in Invoices
- Supply Movements.Supply points at a record in Supplies
- Supply Movements.Contract points at a record in Contracts
- Payslips.Cleaner points at a record in Cleaners
- Payslip Lines.Payslip points at a record in Payslips

### Queries

#### Rota, next 7 days

Every visit booked from today for the next seven days, by cleaner, day and start time, with the client, the site and its address. Print it each week for the cleaners.

From Visits, Cleaners, Contracts, Sites, Clients. Shows Cleaner, Date, Start Time, Hours, Client, Site, Address, Postcode, Notes.
Calculated: Cleaner is `[Cleaners].[First Name] & " " & [Cleaners].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 6`.

#### Missed or short visits

Visits of the last 60 days that were missed or cut short, the newest first, with the reason. For putting things right with the client and spotting a pattern.

From Visits, Cleaners, Contracts, Sites, Clients. Shows Date, Client, Site, Cleaner, Status, Planned Hours, Hours Worked, Reason.
Calculated: Cleaner is `[Cleaners].[First Name] & " " & [Cleaners].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status In ("Missed", "Short")` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 60`.

#### Hours and pay by cleaner, last month

Each cleaner's payslip for last month: contract hours, job hours and gross pay. Send it to payroll.

From Payslips, Cleaners. Shows Cleaner, Payroll Ref, Period, Contract Hours, Job Hours, Hours, Gross, Pay Date.
Calculated: Cleaner is `[Cleaners].[First Name] & " " & [Cleaners].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Months Ago = 1`.

#### Hours by cleaner, last 30 days

Each cleaner's visits of the last 30 days: how many, the hours planned and worked, and how many were short.

From Visits, Cleaners. Shows Cleaner, Visits, Planned, Worked, Short Visits.
Calculated: Cleaner is `[Cleaners].[First Name] & " " & [Cleaners].[Last Name]`; Short Visits is `IIf([Status] = "Short", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Status In ("Done", "Short")` and `Days Ago Between 1 And 30`.

#### Contract profitability

For each site over the last 90 days: what was charged for the visits against the wage cost of the hours worked (with holiday pay), and the margin left to pay for supplies, travel and the office.

From Visits, Contracts, Sites, Clients. Shows Client, Site, Kind, Visits, Hours, Charged, Wage Cost, Margin.
Calculated: Charged is `Round(Nz([Hours Charged]) * [Charge Rate], 2)`; Wage Cost is `Round(Nz([Hours Worked]) * [Pay Rate] * 1.1207, 2)`; Margin is `Round(Nz([Hours Charged]) * [Charge Rate], 2) - Round(Nz([Hours Worked]) * [Pay Rate] * 1.1207, 2)`.
Only where `Status In ("Done", "Short")` and `Days Ago Between 1 And 90`.

#### Supplies used, last 90 days

What each site has used from the store over the last 90 days at cost, and what of it was charged on.

From Supply Movements, Supplies, Contracts, Sites, Clients. Shows Client, Site, Cost, Recharged.
Calculated: Cost is `Round(-[Quantity] * [Supply Movements].[Unit Cost], 2)`; Recharged is `Round(IIf([Rechargeable], -[Quantity] * [Sell Price], 0), 2)`.
Only where `Kind = Used` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Supplies to reorder

Supplies at or below their reorder level, with how many to buy.

From Supplies. Shows Supply, Unit, In Stock, Reorder Level, Reorder Quantity, Unit Cost.
Only where `Above Reorder Level <= 0`.

#### Invoices overdue

Invoices past their due date and not paid, the longest overdue first, with the client's phone number for chasing.

From Invoices, Clients. Shows Invoice, Client, Phone, Period, Invoice Date, Due Date, Total, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Days Overdue > 0` and `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Contracts up for renewal

Active contracts whose year ends in the next 60 days, with their rate, monthly value and notice. Time to review the price and talk to the client.

From Contracts, Sites, Clients. Shows End Date, Days Left, Contract, Client, Site, Visits per Week, Hours per Visit, Rate, Monthly Estimate, Notice Days.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [End Date])`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 60` and `Status = Active`.

#### Work to invoice

Visits done and not yet invoiced, by client and contract, with their hours and value: what next month's invoices will bring in.

From Visits, Contracts, Clients. Shows Client, Contract, From, Visits, Hours, Value.
Calculated: Value is `Round(Nz([Hours Charged]) * [Charge Rate], 2)`.
Only where `Status In ("Done", "Short")` and `Invoice Is Null`.

#### Quotes waiting

Quotes for one-off jobs sent and not yet answered, the oldest first. For a follow-up call.

From Jobs, Sites, Clients. Shows Quoted On, Quote, Client, Kind, Address, Total, Valid Until, Days Waiting.
Calculated: Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Quoted On], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Quoted`.

#### Jobs booked, next 14 days

One-off jobs booked for the next two weeks, with the address and the cleaner.

From Jobs, Sites, Clients, Cleaners. Shows Booked For, Job, Kind, Client, Address, Postcode, Cleaner, Estimated Hours.
Calculated: Cleaner is `[Cleaners].[First Name] & " " & [Cleaners].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 13`.

#### Revenue by month

What was invoiced each month, split between contracts and one-off jobs, with VAT and totals.

From Invoices. Shows Month, Invoices, Contracts, One-off Jobs, Net, VAT, Total.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Invoice Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Contracts is `IIf(Nz([Job]) = 0, [Net], 0)`; One-off Jobs is `IIf(Nz([Job]) = 0, 0, [Net])`.

#### Active contracts

Every contract in force, about to start or under notice, with its days, times, hours, rate and regular cleaner.

From Contracts, Sites, Clients, Cleaners. Shows Kind, Client, Site, Contract, Days, Start Time, Hours per Visit, Rate, Monthly Estimate, Regular Cleaner, Status.
Calculated: Regular Cleaner is `[Cleaners].[First Name] & " " & [Cleaners].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status In ("Active", "Notice given", "Pending")`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Clients, Sites, Cleaners, Visits, Contracts, Contract Tasks, Jobs, Job Items, Invoices, Invoice Lines, Supplies, Supply Movements, Payslips, Payslip Lines. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Rota, next 7 days

The coming week's visits, a section for each cleaner with their hours. Give each cleaner their page.

From the query Rota, next 7 days, a group for each Cleaner: Date, Start Time, Hours, Client, Site, Address, Postcode, Notes, with the total of Hours.

#### Missed and short visits, last 60 days

The last 60 days' missed and short visits by client, with the hours lost.

From the query Missed or short visits, a group for each Client: Date, Site, Cleaner, Status, Planned Hours, Hours Worked, Reason, with the total of Planned Hours, total of Hours Worked.

#### Hours and pay, last month

Last month's hours and gross pay for each cleaner, with the totals, for payroll.

From the query Hours and pay by cleaner, last month: Cleaner, Payroll Ref, Period, Contract Hours, Job Hours, Hours, Gross, with the total of Hours, total of Gross.

#### Contract profitability, last 90 days

Charge, wage cost and margin for each site over the last 90 days, commercial and domestic apart, with totals.

From the query Contract profitability, a group for each Kind: Client, Site, Visits, Hours, Charged, Wage Cost, Margin, with the total of Charged, total of Wage Cost, total of Margin.

#### Overdue invoices

Unpaid invoices past their due date by client, with a total owed.

From the query Invoices overdue, a group for each Client: Invoice, Period, Invoice Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, Total, with the total of Total.

#### Contracts up for renewal, next 60 days

Contracts coming up for renewal in the next 60 days, with their monthly value.

From the query Contracts up for renewal: End Date, Contract, Client, Site, Rate, Monthly Estimate, Notice Days, with the total of Monthly Estimate.

#### Monthly revenue

One line a month with the invoiced contracts, jobs and totals.

From the query Revenue by month: Month, Invoices, Contracts, One-off Jobs, Net, Total, with the total of Net, total of Total.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Cleaning contract

The contract for a record in Contracts, for the client to sign. It prints for contracts in force; an ended one prints from the Contracts form and says when it ended. In it: the parties and the site, the days, times and hours, the rate and an average month, the schedule of tasks, invoicing and payment, supplies, cleaners, keys, complaints, insurance, renewal and notice. It is a plain starting point written for this sample, not legal advice: have it checked for your own country before you use it. One for each record of Contracts, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Cleaning contract {Number}
- Words: This contract ended on {Ended On}.
- Words: Notice to end this contract was given on {Notice Given On}.
- Fields: Client, Site, Contact, Site address, Client address, Site postcode, Starts, Runs to, Visit days, Starting at, Hours a visit, Rate an hour, before VAT, About a month, before VAT, Notice, days
- Words: THIS CONTRACT is between {Business.Name} of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} ("we", "us") and {Client.Name} of {Client.Address}, {Client.City} ("you"), for the cleaning of {Site.Name}, {Site.Address}, {Site.City} {Site.Postcode} ("the site").
- Words: 1. The cleaning. We will clean the site on {Days}, starting at about {Start Time}, for {Hours per Visit} hours each visit ({Visits per Week} visits a week, where 0.5 means every other week), doing the work in the schedule below. If you want something added or changed, tell us and we will agree it with you in writing, with any change to the hours.
- Lines from Contract Tasks: Area, What we do, How often
- Words: 2. What it costs. We charge {Rate} an hour plus VAT for the hours of each visit, which comes to about {Monthly Estimate} plus VAT in an average month. A visit we do not make is not charged. If a visit is cut short at our end, we charge only the time worked. The rate is reviewed once a year, when the contract renews, and we will tell you of any change at least 30 days before.
- Words: 3. Invoices and payment. We invoice on the first working day of each month for the visits made in the month before, listing each visit. Each invoice is due {Client.Payment Days} days after its date, by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}. If an invoice is more than 30 days overdue we may stop the visits until it is paid.
- Words: 4. Equipment and supplies. We bring the cleaning products, cloths, mops and machines. Toilet rolls, hand towels, soap and bin liners can be supplied by us and charged on the monthly invoice at our list price, or you may supply your own.
- Words: 5. Our cleaners. Every cleaner we send has been vetted and is trained for the work. We aim to send the same cleaner each time and will send another if they are on holiday or ill. If we cannot cover a visit we will tell you before the time it was due.
- Words: 6. Keys and access. Keys and alarm codes you give us are held securely, labelled with a reference and never with your address, and given back when the contract ends. Please tell us of any change to the site that affects access or safety.
- Words: 7. If something is not right. Tell us within two working days and we will come back and put it right without charge. A cleaner's visit is signed off in the site book or on the visit sheet; if you sign it off, we take it that the work was done.
- Words: 8. Damage and insurance. We carry public liability insurance. Report any breakage or damage to us in writing within seven days and we will deal with it fairly, putting right damage our cleaners caused.
- Words: 9. How long it runs. This contract starts on {Start Date} and runs to {End Date}. It then renews for a further twelve months each time unless either of us gives notice. Either of us may end it at any time by giving {Notice Days} days' notice in writing. Visits up to the end of the notice are charged as usual.
- Words: 10. Your details. We keep your details only to run this contract and do not pass them to anyone else except as the law requires.
- Signed by: For the cleaning company, For the client

#### Invoice

The VAT invoice for a record in Invoices: for a contract, every visit of the month with its date, hours and rate, and any washroom supplies; for a one-off job, its items. Then the net, VAT and total due, and how to pay, or the day it was paid. Numbered INV-2026-0042. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Invoice {Number}
- Fields: Bill to, Invoice, For the attention of, Date, Address, Payment due, City, For, Postcode, Site, Contract, Job, Site address
- Lines from Invoice Lines: Date, Description, Hours or qty, Rate, Amount, VAT
- Totals: Net, VAT at 20%, Total due
- Words: Please pay by {Due Date}. {Business.Payment Terms} Pay to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}. VAT registration {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: Paid on {Paid On}, thank you. VAT registration {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Quote

The quote for a one-off job, for a record in Jobs: the address, each priced item, the net, VAT and total, how long the price holds and how to book. It prints for jobs quoted and not yet answered, and for jobs booked and still to do, which say the day booked. Numbered JOB-2026-0031. One for each record of Jobs, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Quote {Number}: {Kind}
- Fields: For, Quote, Address of the job, Date, City, Price holds until, Postcode, Time on site, hours, Booked for
- Lines from Job Items: Description, Quantity, Price, Amount, VAT
- Totals: Net, VAT at 20%, Total
- Words: The price covers our cleaners, products and machines. Please make sure there is water and power at the property and that it is empty of furniture where the job says so. To book, call us on {Business.Phone} or reply to this quote with the day you would like. We invoice when the job is done; payment is due within seven days.
- Words: Thank you for booking. The price covers our cleaners, products and machines. Please make sure there is water and power at the property on the day and that it is empty of furniture where the job says so. We invoice when the job is done; payment is due within seven days.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Payslip

A cleaner's monthly payslip from Payslips: contract hours and job hours at their rates, holiday pay, and the gross pay. Deductions are left to payroll, which issues its own payslip with the pay after tax. One for each record of Payslips, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Payslip {Number}
- Fields: Name, Pay period, Payroll reference, Paid on, From, To
- Lines from Payslip Lines: Description, Hours, Rate, Amount
- Totals: Hours worked, Gross pay
- Words: This shows your hours and gross pay for the period. Income tax, National Insurance and any pension are worked out by payroll from the gross pay and shown on the payroll's own payslip, with your pay after deductions.
- Words: Holiday pay is paid as 12.07 percent of the pay for the hours you work, with each month's pay. Questions about your hours: call the office on {Business.Phone}.

#### Site visit sheet

A sheet for each contract's site, printed for the cleaner to take: the address, access notes, the days and hours, every task with a box to tick, room for times and notes, and lines for the cleaner and the client to sign. It prints for contracts in force. One for each record of Contracts, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Visit sheet: {Site.Name}
- Fields: Client, Contract, Address, Visit days, Postcode, Start at, On site, Hours a visit, Regular cleaner, Access
- Lines from Contract Tasks: Area, Task, How often, Done
- Words: Date: ....................   Time in: ..............   Time out: ..............   Hours: ........
- Words: Anything not done, and why, or anything the client should know (a breakage, supplies running low):
- Words: ..........................................................................................................................
- Signed by: Cleaner, Signed off for the client

### Starting empty

Start with Business: your own name, address, VAT number, bank details and the words for the foot of your documents. Then Cleaners and Supplies. Then each client in Clients with their Sites, and a contract in Contracts for each site cleaned regularly, with its Contract Tasks. From then on, book and record Visits, add Jobs as they are quoted, Supply Movements as stock comes and goes, and at each month's end the Payslips and the Invoices.

### Making it yours

- Pay travel time between sites: add a Travel Minutes field to Visits and a payslip line for it at the cleaner's rate.
- Charge a fixed monthly price instead of by the hour: add a Monthly Price field to Contracts and invoice one line for the month, with the visits listed for information only.
- Keep a key register: add a Keys table (site, key reference, held by, signed out, signed in) so you know where every key is.
- Record a quality check: add an Inspections table (site, date, inspector, score, notes) and a query of the lowest scores.
- Clean windows or gardens on a round: rename Contracts to Rounds and set Visits per Week to 0.25 for every four weeks.
- Track the cleaners' training and checks: add a Training table pointing at Cleaners with what was done and when it falls due again.

### Questions people ask

**How do I see who is cleaning where tomorrow?**

Run the query Rota, next 7 days, or print the report Rota. Both list the booked visits of the next seven days by cleaner, day and start time, with the address.

**A cleaner is off sick. How do I cover their visits?**

Open each of their booked visits in the Visits form and choose another cleaner in Cleaner, with a word in Notes. If nobody can go, set Status to Missed once the day has passed, and Hours Charged to 0, so the client is not charged.

**Why is a contract's invoice less than its Monthly Estimate?**

The estimate is an average month. The invoice charges the visits actually made: a month with four Mondays has fewer than one with five, missed visits are not charged, and short ones are charged for the time worked.

**How do I put the price up when a contract renews?**

Open the contract in the Contracts form, type the new Rate and Monthly Estimate, move End Date on a year and type the day in Last Renewed. Visits booked from then on take the new rate in Charge Rate.

**How do I print last month's invoices again?**

Open the print template Invoice and choose the invoices by number, or open an invoice in the Invoices form and print it from there.

**Which contracts make money?**

Run Contract profitability. It sets what each site was charged over the last 90 days against the wage cost of the hours worked, with holiday pay. Supplies used are in Supplies used, last 90 days.

**Can I use the cleaning contract as it is?**

Treat it as a draft. It is written plainly for this sample and is not legal advice; have it checked for your own country, then change the words in the print template Cleaning contract.

## Bramble Studio

**Consultancy or agency.** Clients, projects, time sheets, expenses and invoices for a small studio or consultancy.

For a small firm that sells its time: a design studio, a consultancy, a bookkeeper or anyone who quotes for work, logs hours against it and invoices for it. It answers the questions such a firm asks each week: what time has not been billed yet, which projects are eating their budget, who is owed what and for how long.

Bramble Studio is invented. Six people work there: two partners, a senior designer, a designer, a developer and a project manager. They make brand identities, websites, annual reports, packaging and campaigns for about two dozen small and mid-sized clients, most in the UK and a few in Ireland and the US. Some work is for a fixed fee paid in stages; some is by the hour, invoiced at the start of each month for the month before, including three retainers that renew.

The records cover the last sixteen months, counted back from the day the file is made. Proposals come in every few days and about two in three are won, fewer when the studio is already busy. Every hour is logged to a task, including the studio's own time on admin and new business, so the billable share of each person's week shows. Some projects overrun, a few are paused by the client for a while, some invoices are paid late or in two parts, and the studio is quiet in August and shut over Christmas.

It prints what a studio sends out: the invoice, with time, fee stages and expenses on separate lines and VAT worked out line by line; a proposal listing the parts of the work and the hours allowed for each; a statement of a client's invoices and what is still owed; each person's weekly time sheet to sign; and a letter of engagement setting out the work, the fee, payment and who owns the result.

It suits, with small changes: A freelance designer or developer; A marketing or branding agency; An architect's practice; IT or management consultants; An accountant or bookkeeper who bills by the hour; A small law practice; A translation or copywriting business; A video or photography studio.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- The studio is in Clients too, as Bramble Studio with the Sector Internal, so that its own time (admin, new business, training) can be logged to three internal projects. Leave it out of anything you send: it has no invoices.
- Numbers are typed, not made for you: invoices INV-, proposals QUO- and time sheets TS-, each a new run each year. Each number can be used only once.
- An invoice's Net, VAT and Total are kept on the invoice as it was sent. If you change a line afterwards, change these too, or the totals block on the printed invoice and the figures in the revenue queries will differ.
- VAT comes from the client: 0.2 for clients in the UK, 0 for clients abroad. Each invoice line carries its own Tax Rate so an old invoice keeps the rate it was sent at.
- An hourly project's Fee is the estimate while the work goes on; when it is completed the Fee becomes what its billable time came to, so Project profit compares like with like.
- Some print templates print only the records they are for: the Proposal for projects whose Status is Proposal, the Letter of engagement for Active client projects, and the Statement for every client but the studio itself. A record you choose from its form always prints, so an old proposal or the letter for a finished project can be printed again.
- The Statement lists only invoices with money still owing, so it reads the same as Unpaid invoices for that client; the balance owing is the sum of the Owing column, and the statement date is the day it is printed.

### Tutorial

#### Quote for new work and send the proposal

1. Open the Projects form and press New. Type the Name, choose the Client and the Contact the work is for, and set Kind to Fixed fee or Hourly. Leave Status as Proposal.
2. Type the Work Type, the Budget Hours you have estimated, the Fee, Proposed On (today) and the Start Date and Due Date you could manage. Give it a Quote No in the next number of the year's run, such as QUO-2026-0064.
3. In the Tasks below, add each part of the work with its Role and Estimated Hours. Their hours should add up to the Budget Hours.
4. Open the print template Proposal from Print templates, choose the project, and press Print or Save as PDF to send it.
5. Each week, run the query Proposals waiting to see which proposals have had no answer and how long they have waited.

#### Win the work and send the letter of engagement

1. When the client says yes, open the project in the Projects form and change Status from Proposal to Active. If the client gave you a purchase order, type it in Client PO.
2. Open the print template Letter of engagement, choose the project, and press Print or Save as PDF. Send it with the proposal for the client to sign and return.
3. For a fixed fee, raise the first stage invoice on the day the work starts (see Invoice the month's work).

#### Log time and print the week's time sheet

1. On Monday, open the Time Sheets form and press New for each person: choose the Staff, type Week Commencing (the Monday) and the next Number, such as TS-2026-0252. Status is Open.
2. Each day, open the Time Entries form and press New for each stretch of work: Date, Staff, Project, Task, Hours (in quarters, such as 2.25), Billable, a Note, and the person's Time Sheet for the week.
3. Time on the studio's own work goes to one of the internal projects (INT-1 New business and proposals, INT-2 Studio admin, INT-3 Training and development) with Billable set to No.
4. On Friday, open the print template Weekly time sheet, choose the person's sheet, and print it for them to check and sign. Set Status to Submitted and type Submitted On.
5. Once checked, the project manager sets Status to Approved and types Approved On. The report Time sheet shows the last 14 days for everyone at once.

#### Invoice the month's work

1. In the first days of the month, run the query Unbilled time (or print the report Work in progress) to see the hourly time not yet invoiced, and Unbilled expenses for costs to pass on.
2. Open the Invoices form and press New. Type the next Number of the year (INV-2026-0111), choose the Project and its Client, and type the Invoice Date and the Due Date (the invoice date plus the client's Payment Days).
3. In the Invoice Lines below, add a line for each grade of person (such as "Designer time, September 2026", Quantity in hours, Unit Price their rate), a fee stage for fixed-fee work, and a line for each expense. Set Tax Rate to the client's VAT Rate.
4. Type the invoice's Net (the lines added up), VAT (each line's VAT added up) and Total. Then put the invoice in the Invoice field of each time entry and expense it covers, so they drop out of the unbilled queries.
5. Open the print template Invoice, choose the invoice, and press Print or Save as PDF.

#### Record a payment and chase what is owed

1. When money arrives, open the Payments form and press New: choose the Invoice, type Received On, Amount, Method and the client's Reference.
2. Open the invoice in the Invoices form and bring Paid up to what has been received, and Status to Part paid or Paid.
3. Run the query Overdue invoices: it lists what is past due, the longest first, with the client's phone number.
4. Open the print template Statement, choose the client, and send it: it lists only the invoices with money still owing, with the days each is overdue and the balance.

#### Keep projects on budget

1. Before the weekly meeting, print the report Project budget report: each project in hand with its budget hours, hours used, fee and the cost of the time so far.
2. For a project near its budget, run the query Task hours against estimate to see which part of the work is running over.
3. Run Projects due for anything due in the next 30 days or already late.
4. When a project is finished, set its Status to Completed and type Finished On. The report Project profit then shows its fee against the cost of its time.

### Queries

#### Unbilled time

Billable hours on hourly projects not yet on an invoice, by client, project and person, with what they are worth at charge-out rates. Run it before the monthly invoices go out.

From Time Entries, Projects, Clients, Staff. Shows Client, Project, Person, Earliest, Hours, Value.
Calculated: Person is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Value is `Round([Hours] * [Charge-out Rate], 2)`.
Only where `Kind = Hourly` and `Billable = Yes` and `Invoice Is Null`.

#### Unbilled expenses

Rechargeable costs not yet passed on to the client, oldest first, so nothing is forgotten on the next invoice.

From Expenses, Projects, Clients. Shows Client, Project, Date, Category, Description, Amount.
Only where `Rechargeable = Yes` and `Invoice Is Null`.

#### Project budgets

Each project in hand: its budget hours against the hours used so far, and its fee against the time used at charge-out rates and at cost. A project whose time at rates is near its fee needs a word with the client.

From Time Entries, Projects, Clients, Staff. Shows Client, Code, Project, Kind, Due Date, Budget Hours, Hours Used, Fee, Time at Rates, Cost of Time.
Calculated: Time at Rates is `Round([Hours] * [Charge-out Rate], 2)`; Cost of Time is `Round([Hours] * [Hourly Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Kind <> "Internal"` and `Status In ("Active", "On hold")`.

#### Task hours against estimate

For each project in hand, each task's estimated hours against the hours logged to it, to see which part of the work is running over.

From Time Entries, Tasks, Projects. Shows Code, Project, Task, Role, Estimated Hours, Hours Used.
Only where `Status In ("Active", "On hold")` and `Kind <> "Internal"`.

#### Hours by person, last 30 days

Each person's hours over the last 30 days, how many of them were billable and what those were worth. Use it to see who is stretched and who has room.

From Time Entries, Staff. Shows Person, Role, Hours, Billable Hours, Billable Value.
Calculated: Person is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Billable Hours is `IIf([Billable], [Hours], 0)`; Billable Value is `Round(IIf([Billable], [Hours] * [Charge-out Rate], 0), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Time sheet

Every entry of the last 14 days, by person and day, with the client, project and task. For checking time sheets before invoicing.

From Time Entries, Tasks, Projects, Clients, Staff. Shows Person, Date, Client, Project, Task, Hours, Billable, Note.
Calculated: Person is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 13`.

#### Overdue invoices

Invoices past their due date with money still owed, the longest overdue first, with the client's phone number for chasing.

From Invoices, Projects, Clients. Shows Invoice, Client, Project, Invoice Date, Due Date, Total, Paid, Outstanding, Days Overdue, Client Phone.
Calculated: Outstanding is `Round([Total] - [Paid], 2)`; Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Invoices].[Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Outstanding > 0` and `Days Overdue > 0`.

#### Unpaid invoices

Every invoice with money still owed, by client, with the days it is overdue (below nought when it is not due yet).

From Invoices, Projects, Clients. Shows Client, Invoice, Project, Invoice Date, Due Date, Total, Outstanding, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Outstanding is `Round([Total] - [Paid], 2)`; Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Invoices].[Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Outstanding > 0`.

#### Revenue by client

Each client's invoiced fees before VAT, last year and this year, the biggest this year first. Shows who the studio depends on.

From Invoices, Projects, Clients. Shows Client, Sector, Last Year, This Year, Invoices.
Calculated: Last Year is `Round(IIf(Year([Invoice Date]) = Year(Date()) - 1, [Net], 0), 2)`; This Year is `Round(IIf(Year([Invoice Date]) = Year(Date()), [Net], 0), 2)`.

#### Revenue by month

What was invoiced each month, net, VAT and total, for seeing the busy and quiet months.

From Invoices. Shows Month, Invoices, Net, VAT, Total.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Invoice Date], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Income by kind

Invoiced amounts each year split into fixed-fee stages, hourly time and recharged expenses.

From Invoice Lines, Invoices. Shows Year, Kind, Lines, Amount.
Calculated: Year is `Format([Invoice Date], "yyyy")`; Amount is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.

#### Cash received by month

The money that actually came in each month, which is what pays the wages.

From Payments. Shows Month, Payments, Received.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Received On], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Project profit

Completed projects, newest first: the fee earned against the cost of the time spent, and the time at charge-out rates. Fee less cost of time is what the project made towards the studio's other costs.

From Time Entries, Projects, Clients, Staff. Shows Finished On, Code, Project, Client, Kind, Fee, Hours, Time at Rates, Cost of Time.
Calculated: Time at Rates is `Round([Hours] * [Charge-out Rate], 2)`; Cost of Time is `Round([Hours] * [Hourly Cost], 2)`.
Only where `Kind <> "Internal"` and `Status = Completed`.

#### Projects due

Projects in hand due within the next 30 days, and any already late (Days Left below nought), soonest first.

From Projects, Clients. Shows Due Date, Days Left, Code, Project, Client, Kind, Start Date, Status.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Due Date])`.
Only where `Days Left <= 30` and `Status In ("Active", "On hold")`.

#### Proposals waiting

Proposals sent and not yet answered, the oldest first, with how long each has waited. For a follow-up call.

From Projects, Clients. Shows Proposed On, Days Waiting, Code, Project, Client, Kind, Budget Hours, Fee, Could Start.
Calculated: Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Proposed On], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Proposal`.

#### Recent invoice lines

The lines of every invoice sent in the last 45 days, for checking what went out.

From Invoice Lines, Invoices, Projects, Clients. Shows Invoice, Invoice Date, Client, Project, Description, Quantity, Unit Price, Amount.
Calculated: Amount is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 45`.

#### Client contacts

The people at each client, the main contact first, with their e-mail and phone.

From Contacts, Clients. Shows Client, Main Contact, First Name, Last Name, Job Title, E-mail, Phone.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Clients, Contacts, Staff, Projects, Tasks, Time Sheets, Time Entries, Expenses, Invoices, Invoice Lines, Payments. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Time sheet, last 14 days

The last 14 days of time, one section per person with their total hours. For each person to check, and for the project manager before invoicing.

From the query Time sheet, a group for each Person: Date, Client, Project, Task, Hours, Note, with the total of Hours.

#### Work in progress to invoice

Unbilled hourly time by client, with hours and value, and a total for the studio: what the next round of invoices will bring in.

From the query Unbilled time, a group for each Client: Project, Person, Earliest, Hours, Value, with the total of Hours, total of Value.

#### Invoices due

Money owed by each client, invoice by invoice, with the days overdue and the total outstanding. For the partner who chases payment.

From the query Unpaid invoices, a group for each Client: Invoice, Project, Invoice Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, Total, Outstanding, with the total of Outstanding.

#### Project budget report

Projects in hand by client, with budget hours, hours used, fee, time at rates and cost of time. For the weekly project meeting.

From the query Project budgets, a group for each Client: Code, Project, Kind, Due Date, Budget Hours, Hours Used, Fee, Time at Rates, Cost of Time, with the total of Hours Used, total of Fee, total of Time at Rates, total of Cost of Time.

#### Revenue by client

One line per client with last year's and this year's invoiced fees, and the totals.

From the query Revenue by client: Client, Sector, Invoices, Last Year, This Year, with the total of Last Year, total of This Year.

#### Completed projects: fee against cost of time

Completed projects with their fee and the cost of the time they took, and the totals for the period.

From the query Project profit: Finished On, Code, Project, Client, Kind, Hours, Fee, Cost of Time, with the total of Fee, total of Cost of Time.

#### Invoices issued, last 45 days

Each invoice of the last 45 days with its lines and its total before VAT.

From the query Recent invoice lines, a group for each Invoice: Invoice Date, Client, Description, Quantity, Unit Price, Amount, with the total of Amount.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Invoice

The VAT invoice for a record in Invoices: the client and the person it is for, the project, the client's order number where they have one, each line (hours by grade, a fee stage or an expense) with its VAT rate and VAT, then the total. Once something has been paid it shows what has come in and the balance due; a paid invoice says so in place of how to pay, and one to a client abroad says why no VAT is charged. Numbered INV-2026-0042. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Invoice {Number}
- Fields: Bill to, Invoice, For the attention of, Date, Address, Payment due, City, Our reference, Postcode, Project, Country, Your order number
- Lines from Invoice Lines: Description, Hours or qty, Rate, Amount, VAT %, VAT
- Totals: Fees and expenses, VAT, Total, Paid so far, Balance due
- Words: No VAT is charged on this invoice: the client is outside the UK.
- Words: Please pay by the payment due date above. {Business.Payment Terms} Pay to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}. VAT registration {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: Paid in full. Thank you. VAT registration {Business.Tax Number}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Proposal

The quote for a project whose Status is Proposal: the parts of the work with the hours allowed for each, the total hours, the fee before VAT (a fixed fee, or an estimate for hourly work, each with its own wording), and when it could start and finish. A project already won or lost prints when you choose it from the Projects form. One for each record of Projects, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Proposal {Quote No}: {Name}
- Fields: For, Proposal, Address, Date, City, Our reference, Postcode, The work, Country, Charged as, Could start, Could finish by, For the attention of
- Words: Thank you for asking us to quote. Below is the work as we would plan it, in its parts, with the hours we allow for each. We could start and finish on the dates above, given your comments at each stage within a week of asking.
- Lines from Tasks: Part of the work, Who does it, Hours
- Totals: Hours planned, Fixed fee, before VAT, Estimated fee, before VAT
- Words: The fixed fee covers the work above with two rounds of changes at each stage, and is invoiced in stages as the work goes: the first part when it starts and the last on completion.
- Words: This work is charged by the hour for the time we spend, and invoiced at the start of each month for the month before. The fee above is our estimate, and we will tell you before the time used goes past it.
- Words: VAT is added for clients in the UK. Printing, licences, hosting and travel are passed on at cost. This proposal holds for 60 days from its date.
- Words: To go ahead, reply to this proposal and we will send a letter of engagement to sign. {Business.Document Footer}

#### Statement

A statement for each client (not the studio itself), dated the day it is printed: only the invoices with money still owing, with what was invoiced, what has been paid and what is owing on each, the days overdue, how many are unpaid and the balance owing. A client who owes nothing gets a short note saying so. One for each record of Clients, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Statement of account
- Totals: Statement date
- Fields: Client, Address, City, Postcode, Country, Payment terms, days
- Lines from Invoices: Invoice, Date, Due, Project, Invoiced, Paid, Owing, Days overdue
- Totals: Invoices unpaid, Balance owing
- Words: Please pay the balance owing to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting the invoice numbers. If you think anything here is wrong, call us on {Business.Phone}.
- Words: Nothing is owing on your account. Thank you.

#### Weekly time sheet

One person's week from Time Sheets, day by day: each day's entries with client, project, task and hours, and the day's hours under it, then the hours worked, the billable hours and the billable share, the days it was submitted and approved once it has been, and lines for the person to sign and for the approver. One for each record of Time Sheets, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Time sheet {Number}
- Fields: Name, Role, Week commencing, Contracted hours, Status, Submitted on, Approved on
- Lines from Time Entries: Day, Client, Code, Project, Task, Note, Hours, Billable
- Totals: Hours worked, Billable hours, Billable share, %
- Words: I confirm these are the hours I worked this week.
- Signed by: Signed, Approved by

#### Letter of engagement

The letter that goes to the client with a won proposal, for each project whose Status is Active (not the studio's internal ones): the work and its dates, the fee and how it is charged and invoiced (worded for a fixed fee or for hourly work), costs passed on, who owns the work once paid for, confidentiality and how either side can end it, with two signature lines. A finished project prints when you choose it from the Projects form. It is a plain starting point written for this sample, not legal advice: have it checked for your own country and trade before you use it. One for each record of Projects, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Letter of engagement: {Name}
- Fields: Client, Our reference, Address, Proposal, City, Starting, Postcode, Finishing by, The work, Charged as, Hours planned, Fixed fee, before VAT, Estimated fee, before VAT, For the attention of
- Words: Dear {Contact.First Name},
- Words: Dear colleagues at {Client},
- Words: Thank you for asking us to do this work. This letter sets out what we will do, what it costs, how we invoice it, who owns the result and how either of us can bring it to an end, so that we both know where we stand. Please sign a copy and send it back to us before the work starts.
- Words: 1. The work. We will carry out the {Work Type} work set out in our proposal {Quote No}, which goes with this letter, starting and finishing on the dates above. Those dates depend on your comments reaching us when the plan says; if they are late, or you ask us to pause, the finish date moves on by the same time.
- Words: 2. The fee. This work is for the fixed fee above, plus VAT where it applies, worked out from the hours planned. It covers the work in the proposal with two rounds of changes at each stage; changes beyond those, or work you add, we quote for before we do them.
- Words: 2. The fee. This work is charged by the hour, in quarters of an hour, for the time we spend, at the rates in the proposal, plus VAT where it applies. The fee above is our estimate from the hours planned, and we will tell you before the time used goes past it.
- Words: 3. Costs we pay for you. Printing, licences for photographs and fonts, hosting, couriers and travel to see you are passed on at what they cost us and shown on the invoice. We will ask you before taking on any single large cost.
- Words: 4. How we invoice. The fixed fee is invoiced in stages: the first part when the work starts, the next as the proposal sets out, and the last on completion. Each invoice is due {Client.Payment Days} days after its date, paid by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting the invoice number. If an invoice is more than 30 days overdue we may pause the work until it is paid.
- Words: 4. How we invoice. The time is invoiced at the start of each month for the month before, with the hours by person. Each invoice is due {Client.Payment Days} days after its date, paid by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting the invoice number. If an invoice is more than 30 days overdue we may pause the work until it is paid.
- Words: 5. Who owns the work. Once every invoice for this work has been paid in full, the rights in the final work we deliver pass to you. Until then the work stays ours and you may use it only to review it. Ideas and drafts you did not choose stay ours. Photographs, fonts and software made by others are licensed to you on their makers' terms, which we will hand over with the files. We may show the finished work in our portfolio unless you ask us not to.
- Words: 6. Keeping things private. We keep to ourselves anything you tell us about your business that is not public, and ask the same of you for what we tell you about our methods and prices.
- Words: 7. Ending the work. Either of us may end this engagement by writing to the other with 14 days' notice. You then pay for the work done up to the day it ends, at our hourly rates and never more than the fixed fee, and for any costs already taken on for you. The rights pass to you in the work that has been paid for.
- Words: 7. Ending the work. Either of us may end this engagement by writing to the other with 14 days' notice. You then pay for the time spent up to the day it ends, and for any costs already taken on for you. The rights pass to you in the work that has been paid for.
- Words: 8. Keeping in touch. We will name one person to look after the work day to day, and ask you to do the same. Approvals are best given by e-mail, so that there is a record of them.
- Words: If this is as you understand it, please sign and return a copy. We look forward to working with you.
- Words: Yours sincerely, for {Business.Name}
- Signed by: For the studio, For the client

### Starting empty

Start with Business: your own name, address, VAT number, bank details and the words for the foot of your documents, which every print template uses. Then Staff: each person with their hourly cost and charge-out rate. Then Clients and their Contacts, adding your own firm as a client if you want to record internal time. Add a project for each piece of work, with its kind, budget hours and fee, and break it into Tasks. From then on, log Time Entries and Expenses as the work goes. When you invoice, add the Invoice and its Invoice Lines, and put the invoice in the Invoice field of the time entries and expenses it covers, so they drop out of the unbilled queries. Record each Payment when the money arrives and bring the invoice's Paid and Status up to date.

### Making it yours

- If rates differ by client, add a Rate field to Projects and use it instead of the person's charge-out rate in the Unbilled time query.
- A law or accounting practice can rename Projects to Matters and Tasks to Stages, and add a Matter Type and a Fee Earner field.
- Add a Payment Link field to Invoices for clients who pay by card online, and a line in the Invoice template that prints it under the bank details.
- Add a Leave table, or an internal Holiday project, so time off shows on the time sheet and the hours per week add up.
- Add a Status of Invoiced to fixed-fee projects whose last stage has gone out but whose work is not signed off yet.
- Add a Mileage expense category with a Miles field, and a calculated column at your mileage rate in the Unbilled expenses query.
- Make a query of Time Entries by Work Type to see which kinds of job overrun most, before quoting for the next one.

### Questions people ask

**How do I see what has not been invoiced yet?**

Run the query Unbilled time for hourly work, or print the report Work in progress. Unbilled expenses lists costs to pass on. Fixed-fee work is invoiced in stages instead, so its hours never show there.

**How do I print an old invoice again?**

Open the print template Invoice and choose the invoice by its number, or open the invoice in the Invoices form and print from there. The template prints whatever is in the record, paid or not.

**Why does a time entry need a Time Sheet?**

So the week's hours can be printed, signed and approved together. Each entry points at its person's sheet for that week; open a new sheet each Monday for each person.

**A client pays in two parts. What do I do?**

Add a Payments record for each part. Bring the invoice's Paid up to the total received and set Status to Part paid until the rest arrives, then Paid.

**How do I see who is busy and who has room?**

Run Hours by person, last 30 days. It shows each person's hours, how many were billable and what those were worth, against their Hours per Week in Staff.

**A client needs their order number on our invoices. Where does it go?**

Type it in Client PO on the project. The Invoice prints it as Your order number on every invoice for that project.

**Can I use the letter of engagement as it is?**

Treat it as a draft. It is written plainly for this sample and is not legal advice; have it checked for your own country and kind of work, then change the words in the print template Letter of engagement.

## Tannery Yard Fitness

**Gym and fitness studio.** Members on monthly plans, direct debits, classes and bookings, personal training packs and visits for an independent gym.

For an independent gym, a fitness studio or a club with a timetable: one database for the members and what they pay, the classes and who books them, personal training, and who has stopped coming.

Tannery Yard Fitness is an invented gym and studio in Leeds with a gym floor, a main studio and a cycle studio. Members join on one of four monthly plans, pay a joining fee, and then pay by direct debit on the day of the month they joined. A weekly timetable of about twenty-five classes is taught by self-employed instructors paid by the class, and three trainers sell personal training in packs of five, ten or twenty sessions.

The records cover about twelve months up to today, and the fortnight ahead: next week's classes with places already booked, personal training sessions on the diary, and the next month's fees invoiced. A few direct debits fail each month and are tried again; most are then paid at the desk and a few are written off. Members freeze, give notice and leave, and some keep paying long after their last visit, which the gym wants to know about before they cancel.

It suits, with small changes: A boxing or martial arts club with monthly members; A yoga or pilates studio with a class timetable; A climbing wall or swimming club; A dance school with termly or monthly fees; A personal training studio selling session packs; A leisure centre run by a community trust.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Prices are shown with VAT in them, as the price list on the wall shows them. Each invoice line's VAT is worked out from its price to the penny and the lines added up, so an invoice's Net and Tax agree with what the Monthly invoice prints.
- Places Booked on Class Sessions and Sessions Used on PT Packs are kept up to date by hand as bookings are made, cancelled and used, the way a stock figure is. The free places and packs running low come from them.
- Invoice, membership and receipt numbers are typed, one on from the last, with a new run each year. The sample gave them in date order; Data Files does not fill them in for you.
- A member who has given notice stays Active until their Ends day has passed, so they still show in Plan mix and still pay. Cancel Requested and Ends tell them apart.
- A member whose payment failed twice cannot get in until they pay at the desk. If they never do, their invoice is set to Written off and their Status to Lapsed about a month later.
- Every visit comes from the door reader, including members coming for a class, so a member who only comes to classes is not missed by Not seen for 30 days.
- Print templates print only the records they are for: the Membership agreement for memberships still running, the Membership card for Active and Frozen members, the Welcome letter for members who joined in the last 30 days, and the Monthly invoice for every invoice not written off. A record you choose from its form always prints, whatever its status.
- The gym is closed on Christmas Day and New Year's Day, so those days have no visits, classes or training sessions. Fees are still collected on them.

### Tutorial

#### Join a new member

1. Open the Members form and press New. Type the next membership number in Number (MEM-2026-0042 after MEM-2026-0041), their name, date of birth, address, phone, e-mail and emergency contact.
2. Choose their plan in Plan and type its fee in Monthly Fee. Type today in Joined, the day of the month in Payment Day (28 if today is later than the 28th), and the day their minimum term ends in Minimum Term Ends. Tick Health Declaration once they have answered the health questions.
3. Open the Invoices form and press New for their first invoice: the next number in Number, the member, today as Invoice Date and Due Date, and the dates the first month covers. Add a line for the joining fee and one for the first month, each with Kind and Tax Rate.
4. Take the payment by card, type today in Paid On, set Status to Paid and Method to Card on joining, and add a Collected line in the Payments form.
5. Open the print templates Membership agreement, Welcome letter and Membership card from Print templates, choose the new member, and print each one. The member signs the agreement.

#### Raise and collect the monthly fees

1. Each day, open the Members form and find the members whose payment day is ten days away. For each, open the Invoices form, press New, and enter the invoice with one line for the month (or for the freeze fee, if they are frozen then).
2. Open the print template Monthly invoice, choose the new invoices, and press Save as PDF to e-mail them.
3. On the payment day, when the bank reports the collections, add a line in the Payments form for each: Collected, or Failed with the reason. Set each invoice's Status to Paid with Paid On, or to Retry due.
4. Five days later, add the second try in Payments. If it fails again, set the invoice to Failed.
5. Run the query Payments to chase, or print the report Payments to chase, and call each member. When they pay at the desk, add the payment and set the invoice to Paid with Method Card at the desk.

#### Put the timetable in and take class bookings

1. Each week, open the Class Sessions form and press New for each class on the timetable a week or two ahead: the Class, the Instructor, Starts, Studio and Capacity, the instructor's rate in Instructor Fee, and Status Scheduled.
2. When a member books, open the Bookings form and press New: choose the Session and the Member, type the time in Booked At, and Status Booked. Add one to Places Booked on the session; take one off if they cancel.
3. Run the query Classes in the next 7 days, or print the report Classes with places, for the desk and the noticeboard.
4. Before each class, print the report Class registers. Afterwards set each booking to Attended or No-show, and the session's Status to Held.

#### Sell a pack of personal training

1. Open the PT Packs form and press New. Type the next receipt number in Number (PT-2026-0042), choose the Member and the Trainer, type today in Bought On, the Sessions, Price and Paid By, and the use-by date in Expires. Status is Open.
2. Open the print template PT pack receipt, choose the pack, and print the receipt for the member.
3. Book each session in the PT Sessions form: the Pack, the Trainer, Session At, Status Booked and the trainer's rate in Trainer Fee. Afterwards set it to Done, No-show or Cancelled, and add one to Sessions Used on the pack for Done or No-show.
4. Each week run the query PT packs running low, or print the report PT packs to renew, so each trainer can offer a new pack before the last session.

#### Freeze a membership or take a cancellation

1. For a freeze, open the Freezes form and press New: the Member, Starts on their next payment day, Ends one to three months later, the Reason and the plan's freeze fee in Monthly Fee. The query Freezes now and coming lists them.
2. For a cancellation, open the member in the Members form, type today in Cancel Requested, and in Ends the day before the first payment day a month or more ahead (or the end of their minimum term, if that is later).
3. Run the query Members in notice each week and ask those leaving why. When their Ends day has passed, set their Status to Cancelled.

#### Win back members who have stopped coming

1. Each Monday, run the query Not seen for 30 days, or print the report Members to win back.
2. Call or e-mail each member on it, longest gone first; offer a free session with a trainer, or a freeze if they are away.
3. Note what they said in Notes on the Members form.

#### Pay instructors and trainers, and see the month's income

1. At the month end, print the report Instructor pay by month for the classes each instructor taught, and the report Trainer pay by month for the personal training sessions.
2. Print the report Monthly income for the fees taken, with the VAT for the accountant, and run the query PT packs sold for personal training takings.
3. Print the report Plan mix to see how many members are on each plan and what they bring in each month.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 31 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |

| Joined | Date | The day they joined and paid the joining fee. |
| Payment Day | Whole number | The day of the month their fee is collected, the day they joined (the 28th for anyone who joined on the 29th, 30th or 31st). |
| Minimum Term Ends | Date | The last day of their minimum term. |
| Status | Short text | Active (including members working out their notice), Frozen, Cancelled once their notice has run out, or Lapsed when they stopped paying. |
| Cancel Requested | Date | The day they gave notice; empty for a member who has not. |
| Ends | Date | The last day of the membership, once they have given notice or lapsed. |
| Health Declaration | Yes/No | Ticked when they have answered the health questions on joining. |
| Emergency Contact | Short text | Who to call if they are taken ill. |
| Emergency Phone | Short text | That person's phone number. |
| Notes | Long text | Anything staff should know, such as an injury to work around or the others on a family plan. |

### Relationships

- Members.Plan points at a record in Plans
- Freezes.Member points at a record in Members
- Invoices.Member points at a record in Members
- Invoice Lines.Invoice points at a record in Invoices
- Payments.Invoice points at a record in Invoices
- Class Sessions.Class points at a record in Classes
- Class Sessions.Instructor points at a record in Staff
- Bookings.Session points at a record in Class Sessions
- Bookings.Member points at a record in Members
- Visits.Member points at a record in Members
- PT Packs.Member points at a record in Members
- PT Packs.Trainer points at a record in Staff
- PT Sessions.Pack points at a record in PT Packs
- PT Sessions.Trainer points at a record in Staff

### Queries

#### Classes in the next 7 days

Classes on the timetable for the next week that still have places, with how many are booked and free. For the desk, the website and the weekly e-mail.

From Class Sessions, Classes, Staff. Shows Starts, Day, Time, Class, Instructor, Studio, Capacity, Booked, Free Places.
Calculated: Day is `Format([Starts], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Time is `Mid([Starts], 12, 5)`; Instructor is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Free Places is `[Class Sessions].[Capacity] - [Places Booked]`.
Only where `Free Places > 0` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 7` and `Status = Scheduled`.

#### Class register

Everyone booked into each class in the next 7 days, with their membership number and phone, for the instructor's register.

From Bookings, Class Sessions, Classes, Members. Shows Class, Member, Member No, Phone, Booked At.
Calculated: Class is `[Classes].[Name] & ", " & Format([Starts], "yyyy-mm-dd") & " " & Mid([Starts], 12, 5)`; Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 7`.

#### Payments to chase

Invoices whose direct debit failed, either waiting for the second try or failed twice, with the member's phone and e-mail and how long ago the payment was due.

From Invoices, Members. Shows Invoice, Member, Phone, E-mail, Due Date, Total, Status, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Status In ("Retry due", "Failed")`.

#### Not seen for 30 days

Active members whose last visit was 30 days ago or more, the longest gone first. These are the members most likely to cancel; a call or a free session often brings them back.

From Members, Plans, Visits. Shows Member, Member No, Plan, Phone, E-mail, Last Visit, Days Since.
Calculated: Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Since is `DateDiff("d", [Visited At], Date())`.
Only where `Days Since >= 30` and `Status = Active`.

#### Attendance by class

For each class over the last year: places booked, how many came, no-shows and late cancellations. Shows which classes to add to and which to change.

From Bookings, Class Sessions, Classes. Shows Class, Booked, Came, No-shows, Cancelled.
Calculated: Came is `IIf([Bookings].[Status] = "Attended", 1, 0)`; No-shows is `IIf([Bookings].[Status] = "No-show", 1, 0)`; Cancelled is `IIf([Bookings].[Status] = "Cancelled", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Status = Held` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Instructor pay

The classes each instructor taught each month and what they are owed for them. Cancelled classes are not paid.

From Class Sessions, Staff. Shows Month, Instructor, Classes, Pay.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Starts], "yyyy-mm")`; Instructor is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Held`.

#### Trainer pay

The personal training sessions each trainer gave each month, missed ones included, and what they are owed.

From PT Sessions, Staff. Shows Month, Trainer, Sessions, Pay.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Session At], "yyyy-mm")`; Trainer is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Status In ("Done", "No-show")`.

#### Plan mix

How many members are on each plan now and what they bring in each month, frozen members at the freeze fee.

From Members, Plans. Shows Plan, Members, Fee, Monthly Income.
Calculated: Monthly Income is `IIf([Status] = "Frozen", [Freeze Fee], [Members].[Monthly Fee])`.
Only where `Status In ("Active", "Frozen")`.

#### Income by month

The fees taken each month, before VAT, the VAT, and in all, by the day they were paid.

From Invoices. Shows Month, Invoices, Before VAT, VAT, Taken.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Paid On], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Status = Paid`.

#### Income by kind

What the last year's paid invoices brought in from monthly fees, joining fees and freeze fees.

From Invoice Lines, Invoices. Shows Kind, Lines, Taken.
Calculated: Taken is `Round([Quantity] * [Unit Price], 2)`.
Only where `Status = Paid` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### PT packs sold

Personal training packs sold each month, the sessions in them and the takings.

From PT Packs. Shows Month, Packs, Sessions, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Bought On], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### PT packs running low

Open personal training packs with three sessions or fewer left, soonest to expire first. The trainer offers the member a new pack.

From PT Packs, Members, Staff. Shows Pack, Member, Phone, Trainer, Sessions, Used, Left, Expires.
Calculated: Member is `[Members].[First Name] & " " & [Members].[Last Name]`; Trainer is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Left is `[Sessions] - [Sessions Used]`.
Only where `Left Between 1 And 3` and `Status = Open`.

#### Freezes now and coming

Freezes running now or booked to start, with who, why and to when.

From Freezes, Members. Shows Starts, Ends, Member, Member No, Reason, Freeze Fee.
Calculated: Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Left >= 0`.

#### Members in notice

Members who have given notice and are working it out, with the day their membership ends. A last chance to ask why and keep them.

From Members, Plans. Shows Ends, Member, Member No, Plan, Joined, Cancel Requested, Days Left, Phone.
Calculated: Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Ends])`.
Only where `Days Left >= 0` and `Cancel Requested Is Not Null`.

#### New members by month

How many joined each month on each plan.

From Members, Plans. Shows Month, Plan, Joined.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Joined], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 400`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Plans, Staff, Members, Freezes, Invoices, Invoice Lines, Payments, Classes, Class Sessions, Bookings, Visits, PT Packs, PT Sessions. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

#### Class attendance over the last year

Bookings, attendance, no-shows and late cancellations for each class over the last year.

From the query Attendance by class: Class, Booked, Came, No-shows, Cancelled, with the total of Booked, total of Came.

#### Personal training packs running low

Packs with three sessions or fewer left, a page for each trainer.

From the query PT packs running low, a group for each Trainer: Pack, Member, Phone, Sessions, Left, Expires, with the total of Left.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Membership agreement

The agreement a member signs, for every membership still running (Active, Frozen, or in notice; not Cancelled or Lapsed): their plan, fees, payment day, minimum term and freeze fee, then numbered clauses on fees, freezing, cancelling with notice, health and the gym's rules, and two signatures. A member who has not answered the health questions gets a line saying they cannot train until they do. Written for this sample; have it checked for your own country before you use it. One for each record of Members, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Membership agreement
- Fields: Membership no, Start date, First Name, Last Name, Date of Birth, Phone, Address, Town, Postcode, Plan, Monthly fee, Joining fee, Payment day each month, Minimum term ends, Freeze fee a month, Health questions done, Emergency Contact, Emergency Phone
- Words: 1. The parties. This agreement is between {Business.Name} of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} ("the gym") and {First Name} {Last Name} of {Address}, {City} {Postcode} ("the member"). It starts on the start date above.
- Words: 2. The plan. The member joins on the {Plan.Name} plan: {Plan.Description}. The member may use the gym {Plan.Access Hours}. A family plan covers the people named on it at one address, and the member who signs pays the fees for all of them.
- Words: 3. Fees. The joining fee and the first month's fee, both shown above, are paid on joining. After that the monthly fee is collected by direct debit on day {Payment Day} of each month. Prices include VAT. If a payment fails, the gym tries again five days later; if that fails too, the member's card stops opening the door until the amount is paid at the desk. The gym gives at least a month's notice in writing of any change to the fee.
- Words: 4. Minimum term. The plan has a minimum term of {Plan.Minimum Months} months, ending on the day shown above, and the monthly fee is paid for the whole of it. The gym will let a member leave early for a serious illness or injury, or a move of more than 20 miles away, if they show evidence of it.
- Words: 5. Freezing. The member may freeze the membership for one to three months in any twelve, from a payment day, by asking at the desk at least ten days before it. While it is frozen the member pays the freeze fee shown above instead of the monthly fee, and cannot use the gym or book classes.
- Words: 6. Cancelling. The member may cancel at any time, in person at the desk or in writing, giving {Plan.Notice Months} month's notice. The membership then ends the day before the first payment day that is at least that far ahead, or at the end of the minimum term if that is later; fees up to that day are still due. The gym may end a membership at once if the member seriously or repeatedly breaks the rules below.
- Words: 7. Health. The member confirms that their answers to the health questions are true, that they will tell staff of any change, and that they will stop and ask for help if they feel unwell while exercising. Anyone with a health condition should ask their doctor before starting a new kind of exercise.
- Words: The health questions are not answered yet. The member may not use the gym floor or join a class until they have answered them at the desk.
- Words: 8. The rules. Show your card at the door and do not let anyone in on it. Wipe equipment down after use and put weights back. Wear clean indoor shoes on the gym floor. Classes are booked up to seven days ahead; a place not cancelled at least two hours before counts as a no-show, and three no-shows in a month stop booking for a fortnight. Children aged 14 to 17 on a family plan use the gym floor only with an adult on the same plan. Lockers are emptied each night.
- Words: 9. Personal details. The gym keeps the member's details to run the membership, collect the fees and contact them about it. It passes them to no one but its bank, for the direct debit. The member may ask to see what is kept about them.
- Words: 10. Belongings and injury. The gym is not responsible for belongings left in the building unless it has been careless with them. Nothing here limits the gym's responsibility for injury caused by its own negligence.
- Signed by: Member, For the gym
- Words: {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}.

Once your minimum term ends on the date above, you can cancel with a month's notice; you can also freeze for up to three months if you are injured or away.

#### Monthly invoice

Each month's invoice, sent ten days before the payment day: the period it covers, each line with the VAT in its price, and the total collected. The first one has the joining fee on it. Its last words follow the Status: when it will be collected, paid with thanks, a failed payment to be tried again (Retry due), or one to pay at the desk (Failed). Written-off invoices are not printed unless you choose one. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Fields: Member, Invoice no, Address, Invoice date, Town, Collected on, Postcode, Member no, Period from, Period to, Status, Paid on

- Totals: Price before VAT, VAT included, Total
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms}
- Words: Paid, with thanks.
- Words: The direct debit on the collection day did not go through. We will try again five days later: please make sure the money is in your account.
- Words: Both tries at the direct debit failed. Please pay this invoice at the desk or call {Business.Phone}; until it is paid your card will not open the door.
- Words: Prices include VAT. VAT number {Business.Tax Number}. {Business.Document Footer}

The till receipt for a pack of personal training: the trainer, the sessions in it, the use-by date, the price per session and the VAT within the price. One for each record of PT Packs, on receipt-80 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Date, Member, Member no, Trainer, Personal training sessions, Use by, Paid by
- Totals: Price per session, VAT rate, %, VAT included, Total paid
