### Starting empty

Start with Business: the gym's name, address and VAT number, which every document prints. Then Plans (your prices and terms), Staff, and Classes. Enter Members as they join, each with a plan, fee and payment day, and raise their first invoice. Then each week put the timetable into Class Sessions and take Bookings, and each month raise the invoices and record each collection in Payments. Visits come from your door reader, or can be typed at the desk.

### Making it yours

- Add a Junior plan with a Minimum Months of nought and a field on Members for the parent who pays.
- Keep a waiting list for full classes: a Waiting status on Bookings, and a query of waiting bookings for classes where a place has come free.
- Charge for classes on their own, for people who are not members: a Price field on Classes and a Class Payments table.
- Record inductions: an Induction Date on Members and a query of members who joined over a week ago and have none.
- Track goals for personal training: a Goal field on PT Packs and a Notes field on PT Sessions for what was done.
- Raise fees once a year: change Monthly Fee on Plans, and on each member after their written notice, so invoices take the new price.
- Pay instructors by attendance as well as by the class: a bonus column in the Instructor pay query worked out from the bookings that came.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print this month's invoices only?**

Open the print template Monthly invoice and choose the invoices in the list (sort it by Invoice Date), then press Print or Save as PDF. Or open one in the Invoices form and print it from there.

**Why does a member show in Not seen for 30 days when they came to a class last week?**

They came in without their card, so the door reader has no visit for them. Add a visit in the Visits form with Entry Class, or ask them to use their card.

**How do I change a plan's price?**

Change Monthly Fee in Plans for new members. Existing members keep the fee in their own Monthly Fee until you change it there, after giving them the month's notice the agreement promises.

**A class shows no free places but someone cancelled. Why?**

Places Booked on the session was not taken down when the booking was cancelled. Open the session in the Class Sessions form and correct it.

**How do I see how much each instructor is owed?**

Print the report Instructor pay by month: the classes held and their fees for each instructor. Cancelled classes are left out.

**Can a family plan hold more than one person?**

The family plan is one member record for the person who pays; write the others on it in Notes. To give each their own card and visits, add a Members record for each with a fee of nought and a note of who pays.

**How do I change the gym's address or VAT number on every document?**

Open the Business form and change it there. Every print template takes its letterhead and footer from that one record.

## Cedar Lane Clinic

**Clinic.** Patients, appointments, visit notes, invoices and recalls for a small private clinic.

For a small clinic that books appointments, writes a short note at each visit and bills patients or their insurers. Cedar Lane Clinic is invented: two doctors, a practice nurse and two physiotherapists, with a reception desk that takes bookings by phone and online.

The records cover the year up to the day the file is made, and the weeks after it. Patients book a few days ahead. Some cancel and a few do not turn up, and the clinic charges a fee for some of those. A physiotherapy assessment leads to a course of weekly sessions, a health check sets a recall for a year later, and the doctors are busier in winter while the nurse is busiest in the autumn when flu vaccinations are given.

Each visit has an invoice, made out to the patient or, when the policy covers the service, to the insurer. Most patients pay at the desk; insurers pay within their terms, one of them slowly, so there is always something to chase. The saved queries answer what a practice manager asks each day and each month: who is booked this week, how full each diary is, who missed an appointment, who owes what, what came in, and which patients are due to be recalled.

It prints what the desk sends out: invoices numbered INV-2026-0042 (to an insurer with the patient's policy reference, or to the patient), receipts for payments, a letter confirming each appointment, a recall letter, and a statement of claims for each insurer. Medical care is exempt from VAT, so no VAT is charged and the invoices say so.

Every patient and every note in it is made up. The notes are short and ordinary on purpose; a real clinic keeps its own wording and its own rules on who may read them.

It suits, with small changes: A family doctor or GP practice that sees private patients; A physiotherapy or sports injury practice; A chiropractic or osteopathy clinic; A dental surgery, with treatments in place of services; A podiatry or foot care clinic; A veterinary practice, with pets as patients and owners for contact details; A counselling or talking therapy practice.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- An invoice's Amount Paid and Paid On are not worked out by themselves: when you add a payment, add its amount to the invoice's Amount Paid, and type Paid On when the invoice is paid in full. The unpaid invoice queries read those two fields.
- The Bill To fields are copied on to each invoice when it is made, so a patient who moves house, or an insurer that changes its address, does not change invoices already sent.
- Medical care is exempt from VAT, so Business has a Tax Rate of nought and the invoice's VAT row comes to nothing. A clinic that also sells things VAT is charged on would put its rate in Business and keep those sales on invoices of their own.
- Visit Notes holds short notes in everyday words. A real clinic decides who may open that table, and keeps clinical records under the rules where it works.
- Some print templates print only the records they are for: the Appointment letter for booked appointments still to come, the Recall letter for open recalls due within 30 days with no letter sent, and the Insurer statement for insurers, not Self-pay. A record you choose from its form always prints, so a past appointment's letter can be printed again.
- The Self-pay record in Insurers stands for patients who pay for themselves. Do not delete it: every patient must point at an insurer or at Self-pay.

### Tutorial

#### Book an appointment and send the letter

1. Open the Patients form and find the patient with the search box, or press New and fill in their name, date of birth, address, phone, Insurer and Policy Reference.
2. Open the Diary next 14 days query to see whose diary has room.
3. Open the Appointments form and press New. Choose the Patient, the Practitioner and the Service, type the Start date and time, and set Booked On to today and Booked Via to Phone, Online or At the desk. Status stays Booked.
4. Open the print template Appointment letter from Print templates, choose the appointment you just made, and press Print, or Save as PDF to e-mail it.

#### Run the day

1. Print the Day sheet report in the morning: a page for each practitioner and day of the week ahead.
2. As each patient arrives and is seen, open their appointment in the Appointments form and set Status to Attended. If they do not come, set it to No-show.
3. After the visit the practitioner opens the Visit Notes form, presses New, chooses the appointment and writes the Reason, the Note and the Plan.
4. If the patient cancels, set Status to Cancelled and type the Cancelled On date. The No-shows and late cancellations query lists those with a day or less of notice.

#### Invoice a visit and take payment

1. Open the Invoices form and press New. Type the next Number (INV, the year, and the next number in the run), choose the Appointment, and type the Invoice Date.
2. For an insured patient on a service insurers pay for, set Bill To to Insurer, choose the Insurer, and copy the insurer's name and address and the patient's Policy Reference into the Bill To fields. Otherwise set Bill To to Patient and copy the patient's name and address. Set Due Date 14 days on for a patient, or the insurer's Payment Days on.
3. Type the Amount from the service's Price, or half of it for a missed appointment or a late cancellation, and set For to match.
4. When the patient pays, open the Payments form, press New, give it the next RCP number, choose the Invoice, and type Paid On, Amount and Method. Then add the amount to the invoice's Amount Paid, and type Paid On on the invoice once it is paid in full.
5. Print the Payment receipt template for that payment, and the Invoice template for the invoice when it is sent.

#### Chase what is owed

1. Open the Money owed query: the unpaid balance for each insurer and each patient, the largest first.
2. Print the Invoices due report for the list with days overdue.
3. Once a month, print the Insurer statement template for each insurer and send it with a covering note.
4. When an insurer pays, record one payment for each invoice on its remittance list, Method Insurer, with the remittance reference in Reference.

#### Send the recall letters

1. Each Monday, open the Recall letters to send query: open recalls due in the next 30 days for patients who agree to letters.
2. Open the print template Recall letter: it holds a letter for each open recall due in the next 30 days. Print those for the patients the query lists (it leaves out patients who want no reminders).
3. Type today's date in Sent On on each recall you sent a letter for.
4. When the patient books, type the date in Booked On. The Recalls due query lists the ones still open, including patients who do not want letters, for a phone call instead.

#### Look at the month

1. Print the Takings by month report for money received from patients and from insurers.
2. Open the Fees by service query to see which services earn the most, and Takings by practitioner if practitioners are paid a share.
3. Open the Busy days and Busy hours queries to plan staff hours, and New patients by month to see how the list is growing.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 28 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The name printed at the top of every document. |
| Address | Short text | The street address. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country. |
| Phone | Short text | The phone number customers call. |
| E-mail | Short text | The address customers write to. |
| Website | Short text | The website, if there is one. |
| Tax Number | Short text | The VAT or sales tax registration number, printed on invoices. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Company Number | Short text | The registered company number, where the business is a company. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Bank Details | Short text | Where customers pay by transfer: the bank, account name and number. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Payment Terms | Short text | The words printed under an invoice's total, such as "Payment within 30 days". |
| Tax Rate | Number | The usual rate of VAT or sales tax as a fraction: 0.2 is twenty percent. Lines may carry a rate of their own. |
| Currency | Short text | The currency the business trades in, as its three-letter code. |
| Document Footer | Long text | A line or two at the foot of every document: thanks, opening hours, returns policy. |

#### Insurers

The health insurers whose policies the clinic accepts, and one record called Self-pay for patients who pay for themselves. Every patient points at one of these, so a patient list can always say who pays. The sample has 5 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required, unique | The insurer as it appears on claims and on the patient list. The Self-pay record stands for no insurer. |
| Kind | Short text | Insurer for a real insurer, Self-pay for the record that stands for paying yourself. Queries use it to tell the two apart. |
| Address | Short text | The street address claims and statements are posted to. |
| City | Short text | The town or city of the claims address. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode of the claims address. |
| Phone | Short text | The claims line the reception desk rings about a claim. |
| E-mail | Short text | Where claims and questions about them are sent. |
| Payment Days | Whole number | How many days the insurer takes to pay a claim under its agreement with the clinic. An invoice to the insurer falls due this many days after the visit. |
| Notes | Long text | Anything reception should know: what a policy usually covers, or that an insurer wants a referral letter first. |

#### Patients

One record per patient registered with the clinic, with contact details, who pays for their care and whether they agree to reminders. The sample has 825 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Patient No | Short text, unique | The clinic's own number for the patient, printed on day sheets and letters. It is not a national health number. |
| First Name | Short text | The patient's first name. |
| Last Name | Short text, required | The patient's family name. Lists are sorted by it. |
| Date of Birth | Date | Used to tell two patients with the same name apart and to see who is due a check for their age. |
| Address | Short text | The street address, for recall letters and invoices. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode, for letters. |
| Phone | Short text | The number reception rings to confirm or move an appointment. |
| E-mail | Short text | Where appointment reminders and invoices are sent, if the patient has given one. |
| Insurer | Points at Insurers, required | Who pays: the patient's insurer, or Self-pay. |
| Policy Reference | Short text | The patient's policy or membership reference with the insurer, quoted on every claim. Empty for self-pay patients. |
| Registered | Date | The day the patient first registered. The new patients query counts these by month. |
| Reminders | Yes/No | Ticked when the patient agrees to reminders and recall letters. Patients without it are rung instead, or not contacted. |
| Notes | Long text | Practical things reception should know before a visit, such as needing step-free access. Not clinical notes, which go in Visit Notes. |

#### Practitioners

The people who see patients: the doctors, the nurse and the physiotherapists. Reception staff are not here because they do not hold a diary. The sample has 5 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |

| First Name | Short text | The practitioner's first name. |
| Last Name | Short text, required | The practitioner's family name. |
| Known As | Short text, required | The name used on day sheets and letters, such as Dr and the name, or the name and Physio. |
| Role | Short text | Doctor, Nurse or Physiotherapist. Services say which role gives them. |

| Phone | Short text | The practitioner's extension or direct line. |

#### Services

What the clinic offers, how long each takes in the diary and what it costs. The sample has 14 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required, unique | The service as it appears in the diary and on invoices. |
| Kind | Short text | A group of services: Consultation, Follow-up, Health check, Nursing, Vaccination or Physiotherapy. |
| Given By | Short text | The role that gives it: Doctor, Nurse or Physiotherapist. |
| Minutes | Whole number | How long the appointment lasts. The diary is kept in quarter hours, so these are multiples of 15. |

#### Appointments

Every booking in the diary, past and future, with what came of it. The sample has 5,265 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Patient | Points at Patients, required | Who the appointment is for. |

#### Visit Notes

A short note written by the practitioner after each attended appointment. In this sample they are invented and kept to everyday words. The sample has 4,573 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Appointment | Points at Appointments, required | The visit the note is about, which gives the patient, the practitioner and the date. |

#### Invoices

What the clinic charges, one invoice per visit, and for a missed appointment or a late cancellation when a fee is charged. Each invoice keeps the name and address it was made out to, so a reprint reads as the one that was sent. The sample has 4,786 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The invoice's number, given in date order and once only, a new run each year: INV-2026-0042. Quote it on claims and payments. |
| Appointment | Points at Appointments, required | The appointment the invoice is for. |
| Invoice Date | Date | The day the invoice was raised: the day of the visit, or of the missed or cancelled appointment. |
| Due Date | Date | When payment is due: 14 days for patients, the insurer's payment days for claims. |
| Bill To | Short text | Patient or Insurer. An insurer is billed when the patient is insured and the service is one insurers pay for. |
| Insurer | Points at Insurers | The insurer the claim is made to. Empty when the patient is billed. The insurer's statement lists the invoices that point at it. |
| Bill To Name | Short text | Who the invoice is made out to: the insurer's name, or the patient's. |
| Bill To Address | Short text | The street address the invoice went to. |
| Bill To City | Short text | The town or city the invoice went to. |
| Bill To Postcode | Short text | The postcode the invoice went to. |
| Policy Reference | Short text | The patient's policy reference, copied on to a claim so the insurer can match it. Empty on an invoice to the patient. |
| For | Short text | Visit, Missed appointment or Late cancellation. |
| Amount | Currency | The amount charged. |
| Amount Paid | Currency | How much has been paid so far, the sum of the payments against it. |
| Paid On | Date | The day the invoice was paid in full. Empty while anything is still owed. |

Money received against invoices. An invoice can have more than one payment when a patient pays in parts. Each payment has a receipt. The sample has 4,557 records.

| Paid On | Date | The day the money came in. |
| Amount | Currency | How much was paid. |

Patients the clinic should ask back: for a yearly health check, a blood pressure review, the autumn flu vaccination or a review after physiotherapy. The sample has 752 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|

| Patient | Points at Patients, required | Who to recall. |
| Service | Points at Services, required | The service they are being asked back for. |
| Due Date | Date | When the recall falls due. |

### Relationships

- Patients.Insurer points at a record in Insurers
- Appointments.Patient points at a record in Patients
- Appointments.Practitioner points at a record in Practitioners
- Appointments.Service points at a record in Services
- Visit Notes.Appointment points at a record in Appointments
- Invoices.Appointment points at a record in Appointments
- Invoices.Insurer points at a record in Insurers
- Payments.Invoice points at a record in Invoices
- Recalls.Patient points at a record in Patients
- Recalls.Service points at a record in Services

### Queries

#### Next 7 days

For each day of the coming week and each practitioner, how many appointments are booked and the hours they fill, with the first and last start times. Reception uses it to see the shape of the week at a glance.

From Appointments, Practitioners, Services. Shows Day, Practitioner, Appointments, Booked Hours, First Start, Last Start.
Calculated: Day is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Booked Hours is `[Minutes] / 60`; First Start is `Mid([Start], 12, 5)`; Last Start is `Mid([Start], 12, 5)`.
Only where `Status = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 6`.

#### Day sheet

Every booked appointment for the next seven days, by day and practitioner, with the patient's number, phone, who pays and any practical notes. It is what each practitioner and the desk work from each morning.

From Appointments, Patients, Practitioners, Services, Insurers. Shows Sheet, Time, Patient, Patient No, Phone, Service, Minutes, Paid By, Patient Notes.
Calculated: Sheet is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd") & " " & [Known As]`; Time is `Mid([Start], 12, 5)`; Patient is `[Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 6`.

#### Diary next 14 days

How full each practitioner's diary is for the next two weeks: appointments, hours booked, hours open and the percentage full. Use it to see who can take more patients or where to offer a cancellation slot.

From Appointments, Practitioners, Services. Shows Practitioner, Role, Appointments, Booked Hours, Open Hours, Percent Full.
Calculated: Booked Hours is `[Minutes] / 60`; Open Hours is `[Hours per Week] * 2`; Percent Full is `Round([Minutes] * 100 / ([Hours per Week] * 120), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Booked` and `Days Ahead Between 0 And 13`.

#### No-shows and late cancellations

Appointments in the last 90 days the patient did not attend, or cancelled the day before or on the day, with the phone number. Use it to decide on fees and to talk to patients who miss often.

From Appointments, Patients, Practitioners, Services. Shows Start, Patient, Phone, Practitioner, Service, Status, Cancelled On, Days Notice.
Calculated: Patient is `[Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name]`; Days Notice is `DateDiff("d", [Cancelled On], Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd"))`.
Only where `Status = No-show` and `Status = Cancelled` and `Days Notice <= 1` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 90` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Unpaid invoices

Every invoice not yet paid in full, with who owes it, what has been paid and how many days overdue it is. A minus figure means it is not due yet.

From Invoices, Appointments, Patients, Insurers. Shows Invoice, Owed By, Bill To, Patient, For, Invoice Date, Due Date, Amount, Paid So Far, Balance, Days Overdue.
Calculated: Owed By is `IIf([Bill To] = "Insurer", [Insurers].[Name], [Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name])`; Patient is `[Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name]`; Balance is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Amount Paid]), 2)`; Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Money owed

The unpaid balance added up for each insurer and each patient, with the number of invoices and the oldest due date. Start here when chasing payments.

From Invoices, Appointments, Patients, Insurers. Shows Owed By, Bill To, Invoices, Balance, Oldest Due.
Calculated: Owed By is `IIf([Bill To] = "Insurer", [Insurers].[Name], [Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name])`; Balance is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Amount Paid]), 2)`.
Only where `Paid On Is Null`.

#### Takings by month

Money received each month, split into what came from patients and what came from insurers.

From Payments. Shows Month, From Patients, From Insurers, Takings.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Paid On], "yyyy-mm")`; From Patients is `Round(IIf([Method] = "Insurer", 0, [Amount]), 2)`; From Insurers is `Round(IIf([Method] = "Insurer", [Amount], 0), 2)`.

#### Takings by practitioner

Money received in the last twelve months for each practitioner's appointments, and how many payments it came in.

From Payments, Invoices, Appointments, Practitioners. Shows Practitioner, Role, Payments, Takings.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Fees by service

For each service, how many visits were invoiced in the last twelve months and the total charged. It shows which services earn the most.

From Invoices, Appointments, Services. Shows Service, Kind, Visits, Invoiced.
Only where `For = Visit` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Busy days

Appointments attended or missed in the last year by day of the week, with the hours they took. Use it to plan staff hours.

From Appointments, Services. Shows Day No, Day, Appointments, Hours Booked.
Calculated: Day No is `DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")) Mod 7 + 1`; Day is `Mid("MonTueWedThuFriSatSun", (DateDiff("d", #2024-01-01#, Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")) Mod 7) * 3 + 1, 3)`; Hours Booked is `[Minutes] / 60`.
Only where `Status In ("Attended", "No-show")` and `Days Ago Between 1 And 365`.

#### Busy hours

The same appointments by the hour they started, which shows the busy mornings and late afternoons.

From Appointments, Services. Shows Hour, Appointments, Hours Booked.
Calculated: Hour is `Mid([Start], 12, 2) & ":00"`; Hours Booked is `[Minutes] / 60`.
Only where `Status In ("Attended", "No-show")` and `Days Ago Between 1 And 365`.

#### Recalls due

Open recalls falling due in the next 30 days, with contact details and whether a letter has gone out or the patient has agreed to letters at all.

From Recalls, Patients, Services. Shows Due Date, Days Left, Patient, Phone, E-mail, Recall For, Reason, Letters Allowed, Sent On.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Due Date])`; Patient is `[Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 30` and `Booked On Is Null`.

#### Recall letters to send

Recalls due in the next 30 days for patients who agree to letters and have not been sent one yet, with their address. It feeds the recall letters report.

From Recalls, Patients, Services. Shows Recall For, Patient, Address, City, Postcode, Due Date, Days Left.
Calculated: Patient is `[Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name]`; Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Due Date])`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 30` and `Reminders = Yes` and `Sent On Is Null` and `Booked On Is Null`.

#### New patients by month

How many patients registered each month over the last year, and how many of them are insured.

From Patients, Insurers. Shows Month, New Patients, Insured.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Registered], "yyyy-mm")`; Insured is `IIf([Kind] = "Insurer", 1, 0)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Not seen for six months

Patients whose last attended appointment was more than six months ago, with the date of that visit. Use it for a "we have not seen you for a while" letter or to tidy the list.

From Patients, Appointments. Shows Patient, Patient No, Phone, Last Visit, Days Since.
Calculated: Patient is `[Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name]`; Last Visit is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Days Since is `DateDiff("d", Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd"), Date())`.
Only where `Days Since > 180` and `Status = Attended`.

#### Patient list

All patients by family name with their date of birth, contact details, insurer and policy reference.

From Patients, Insurers. Shows Last Name, First Name, Patient No, Date of Birth, Phone, E-mail, Insurer, Policy Reference, Reminders, Registered.

#### Visit history

Every visit note by patient, newest first, with the practitioner, the service, the reason and the plan.

From Visit Notes, Appointments, Patients, Practitioners, Services. Shows Patient, Patient No, Seen, Practitioner, Service, Reason, Plan.
Calculated: Patient is `[Patients].[First Name] & " " & [Patients].[Last Name]`; Seen is `Format([Start], "yyyy-mm-dd")`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Insurers, Patients, Practitioners, Services, Appointments, Visit Notes, Invoices, Payments, Recalls. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Day sheets for the week ahead

A page for each practitioner and day of the week ahead, listing each appointment's time, patient, phone, service and who pays, with the number of patients and minutes booked. Printed each morning for the practitioner and the desk.

From the query Day sheet, a group for each Sheet: Time, Patient, Patient No, Phone, Service, Minutes, Paid By, with the count of Patient, total of Minutes.

#### Invoices due

Unpaid invoices grouped by who owes them, each insurer and each patient, with the balance and days overdue and a total for each. For whoever chases payments.

From the query Unpaid invoices, a group for each Owed By: Invoice, Patient, For, Invoice Date, Due Date, Days Overdue, Balance, with the total of Balance.

#### Takings by month

A month by month list of money received from patients and from insurers, with totals. For the owners and the accountant.

From the query Takings by month: Month, From Patients, From Insurers, Takings, with the total of From Patients, total of From Insurers, total of Takings.

#### Takings by practitioner, last 12 months

Money received in the last twelve months for each practitioner, with a total. Useful when practitioners are paid a share of their takings.

From the query Takings by practitioner: Practitioner, Role, Payments, Takings, with the total of Takings.

#### Recall letters to send

The names and addresses of patients to send a recall letter to, grouped by what they are recalled for. Print it, or use it for a mail merge.

From the query Recall letters to send, a group for each Recall For: Patient, Address, City, Postcode, Due Date, with the count of Patient.

#### Patient list

Patients grouped by insurer, with patient number, date of birth, phone and policy reference, and a count for each insurer.

From the query Patient list, a group for each Insurer: Last Name, First Name, Patient No, Date of Birth, Phone, Policy Reference, with the count of Patient No.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Invoice

The invoice for a visit, a missed appointment or a late cancellation, made out to the insurer with the patient's policy reference, or to the patient. It shows the visit and, once something has been paid, the payments received and the balance due; the policy reference only on a claim to an insurer; and how to pay, or that it is paid in full. With no VAT rate in Business it says that medical care is exempt from VAT; with one, it adds a VAT row. Numbered INV-2026-0042. One for each record of Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Invoice {Number}
- Fields: Invoice to, Invoice number, Address, Date, Town, Payment due, Postcode, Charge for
- Fields: Patient, Service, Patient number, Appointment, Date of birth, Seen by, Minutes, Policy reference
- Words: Payments received against this invoice:
- Lines from Payments: Receipt, Paid on, Method, Reference, Received
- Totals: Fee, VAT, Total, Paid, Balance due
- Words: Medical care given at the clinic is exempt from VAT, so no VAT is charged.
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Please pay by card at the desk, or by transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}.
- Words: Paid in full. Thank you.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Payment receipt

Given to a patient who pays at the desk, or sent when a transfer arrives: who paid, how much, for which invoice and visit, the payment's reference when it has one, and the invoice total and what has been paid to date. Numbered RCP-2026-0042. One for each record of Payments, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Received from, Date, For invoice, Paid by, Patient, Service, Appointment, Reference
- Totals: Amount received
- Fields: Invoice total, Paid to date
- Words: Thank you. Medical care is exempt from VAT, so this receipt shows none.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Appointment letter

Sent when an appointment is booked: the day, date and time, who it is with, where to come, who pays and the fee, and how to cancel or move it. It prints for appointments still Booked and still to come; a past one prints when you choose it from the Appointments form. One for each record of Appointments, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Your appointment
- Fields: To, Patient number, Address, Booked on, Town, Postcode
- Words: Dear {Patient.First Name},
- Words: Thank you for booking with us. This letter confirms your appointment.
- Fields: Date and time, Appointment for, With, Length in minutes, Paid by, Fee, Policy reference
- Words: Where: {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}. Please come to reception five minutes before your time. The front door has step-free access and every treatment room is on the ground floor.
- Words: If your insurer is paying, please check that your policy covers this appointment and bring your policy reference with you. If you pay for yourself, the fee above is paid at the desk on the day, by card or cash.
- Words: If you need to cancel or move the appointment, please ring us on {Business.Phone} or write to {Business.E-mail} at least 24 hours before. We may charge half the fee for an appointment that is missed, or cancelled with less notice, because we cannot offer the time to someone else.
- Words: We look forward to seeing you.
- Words: Yours sincerely,
- Words: Reception, {Business.Name}

#### Recall letter

A short, friendly letter asking a patient back for a check that is due, with the month it is due and how to book. It prints for open recalls (not booked, no letter sent yet) due in the next 30 days, the same recalls as the Recall letters to send query, except that it cannot see a patient's Reminders: leave out anyone the query does not list. Have the wording checked against the rules where you work. One for each record of Recalls, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: A reminder from {Business.Name}
- Fields: To, Patient number, Address, Town, Postcode, Due
- Words: Dear {Patient.First Name},
- Words: This is a friendly reminder that you are due to come back and see us for your {Service.Name}, in the month shown above. It takes about {Service.Minutes} minutes.
- Words: To book a time that suits you, ring us on {Business.Phone}, write to {Business.E-mail}, or book online at {Business.Website}.
- Words: If you have already booked, or have had this done elsewhere, please ignore this letter, or tell us and we will update our records. If you would rather not have reminders from us, just let us know.
- Words: With best wishes,
- Words: The team at {Business.Name}

#### Insurer statement

Sent to each insurer, dated the day it is printed: only the claims it has not paid, with what was claimed, any part paid and what is owing on each, how many there are, and the balance owing. The Self-pay record has no statement. One for each record of Insurers, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Statement of claims
- Totals: Statement date
- Fields: Insurer, Terms (days), Address, Claims e-mail, Town, Postcode
- Lines from Invoices: Invoice, Date, Patient, Policy, Service, Due, Claimed, Paid, Owing
- Totals: Claims unpaid, Claimed, Paid, Balance owing
- Words: Please pay the balance owing to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting each invoice number, and send the remittance list to {Business.E-mail}. If you have paid since this statement was made, thank you.
- Words: Every claim we have made to you is paid. Thank you.

### Starting empty

Start with Business: the clinic's name, address, phone and bank details, which every invoice, receipt and letter prints. Then Insurers: add a Self-pay record first (Kind Self-pay), then each insurer you accept with its payment days. Then add your Practitioners with their hours, then your Services with their minutes and prices. Once those are in, register Patients, pointing each at an insurer or at Self-pay, and book Appointments. Write a Visit Note after each attended appointment, raise an Invoice for it, and record Payments as they arrive, updating the invoice's Amount Paid and Paid On. Add Recalls as visits call for them.

### Making it yours

- For a dental surgery, rename Services to Treatments and add check-ups, scale and polish, fillings and crowns with their minutes and fees, then add a Tooth field to Visit Notes.
- For a vet, add a Pets table pointing at the owner in Patients, with species and breed, and point Appointments at the pet instead of the owner.
- Add a Room field to Appointments, or a Rooms table, if the treatment rooms are shared and you need to see which is free.
- Add a Referred By field to Patients and a query that counts new patients by where they heard of you.
- If you take deposits for a course of treatment, add a Deposit For field to Payments and a status of Deposit paid to Invoices.
- Add an Excess field to Patients for insurers that leave the patient to pay the first part of a claim, and raise a second invoice to the patient for it.
- Add a Consent Signed date to Patients if your practice asks for written consent before treatment, and a query listing patients booked this week who have none.

### Questions people ask

**Why does the invoice show no VAT?**

Medical care is exempt from VAT in the UK, so the clinic charges none and is not registered. The invoice says so in its small print. If your services are taxed, put the rate in Business, Tax Rate, and the invoice adds it.

**How do I bill an insurer instead of the patient?**

On the invoice, set Bill To to Insurer, choose the Insurer, copy the insurer's claims address into the Bill To fields and the patient's Policy Reference into Policy Reference. The claim then appears on that insurer's statement.

**A patient paid half now and half later. How do I record it?**

Add two records in Payments, each pointing at the same invoice, each with its own receipt number. Add both to the invoice's Amount Paid; type Paid On on the invoice only when the second arrives.

**How do I print last month's invoices?**

Open the Invoices form, choose the invoices dated last month (sort by Invoice Date), and print the Invoice template for those chosen.

**Can I change what the appointment letter says?**

Yes. Open the Appointment letter template from Print templates and edit its text blocks. Words in curly brackets, such as {Start} or {Business.Phone}, are filled from the appointment and from the Business record.

**How do I stop sending recall letters to someone?**

Untick Reminders on their record in Patients. The Recall letters to send query leaves them out, and Recalls due still lists them so reception can ring instead.

**What is the cancellation fee?**

The sample charges half the fee for some missed appointments and cancellations with a day or less of notice, as an invoice with For set to Missed appointment or Late cancellation. Set your own rule and put it in the Business record's Document Footer, which every document prints.

## Lantern Learning Centre

**School or training centre.** Students, families, classes, registers, test results and termly fees for a tuition or training centre.

For a centre that teaches groups in terms and bills by the term: a tuition business, a language or music school, a dance studio, a sports academy. It keeps who comes, who pays, which class each student is in, who was there at each lesson, how they did in their tests and what is still owed.

Lantern Learning Centre is an invented tuition centre in Leeds with about a hundred and twenty students. After school and on Saturday mornings it teaches children from Year 3 to Year 11 (ages seven to sixteen) in groups of eight to ten: maths, English and science for each stage up to the GCSE exams, and coding. On weekday evenings adults come for Spanish, French and Mandarin, and for bookkeeping in the computer room. In the school holidays it runs daytime workshops: a maths booster, GCSE revision days, a coding club, a reading and writing club and science lab days. Ten teachers are paid by the hour.

The records go back to the start of a term fourteen to eighteen months before the day the file is made: three terms a year with the holidays between, run to the end of the current one, with the next term or holiday planned when it starts within six weeks. Each class has its lessons on one weekday at one time, a register for every lesson that has happened, and tests twice a term for the children. Families get one invoice a term, three weeks before it starts, with ten percent off for a second or third child; most pay before the first lesson, some pay in three instalments, some pay late and a few still owe from earlier terms.

It prints what such a centre sends out: a fee invoice to each family each term, with a line for each child's class, the discounts and what has been paid; a receipt for every payment; a letter confirming each place, with the day, time, room, first lesson and what to bring; a progress report for each student at the end of each term, with attendance and marks for each class; a certificate for each adult course and holiday workshop finished; and a pay statement for each teacher each month. Tuition is exempt from VAT here, so no VAT is charged.

Children's records hold only what a centre needs: a name, the date of birth, the school year, a short note such as an allergy or an inhaler, and whether photographs may be taken. Addresses and phone numbers belong to the family, not the child. All of it is invented.

It suits, with small changes: A tutoring business with group or one-to-one lessons; A language school with evening classes; A music or dance school that teaches in terms; A driving school, with a class for each instructor's block of lessons; A sports academy or swimming club with weekly sessions; A small private or weekend school; An adult education or evening class programme.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- An invoice's lines are the enrolments that point at it, so an enrolment with no Invoice is not on any invoice yet. Set it when you send the invoice; a place booked after the invoice was sent goes on a new invoice of its own.
- Paid So Far on an invoice and Balance After on a payment are typed, not worked out. Keep Paid So Far equal to the invoice's payments added up, or the balance printed on the invoice will be wrong.
- The Enrolment letter prints only for places whose Status is Enrolled. The other print templates print every record of their table (every invoice, receipt, report, certificate and pay statement there is), so choose the ones you want, such as this term's invoices, before pressing Print. A record you choose from its form always prints.
- Term reports and certificates are records of their own, written once at the end of a term. Changing the register later does not change a report already written: update its line by hand if a mark was wrong.
- A pay statement's lines are the lessons that point at it. A lesson covered by another teacher has that teacher in its Teacher field, so it is paid on their statement, not the class teacher's.
- Tuition here is exempt from VAT, so the Business record's Tax Rate is 0 and no document shows VAT. If yours is not, see the last of the ways to adapt the sample.
- School Year on a student is this year's and moves up each September; the term report keeps the year the student was in at the time.

### Tutorial

#### Book a new family and their child into a class

1. Open the query Classes with free places to find a class of the right course with room in it.
2. Open the Families form and press New. Type the family's Name (such as Okafor family), the Contact, Phone, E-mail and address.
3. Open the Students form and press New. Choose the family in Family, type the child's names, Date of Birth and School Year, any Medical Note, and tick Photo Consent if the family agrees.
4. Open the Enrolments form and press New. Choose the student and the Class, type today in Enrolled On, Status Enrolled, the Lessons Billed (all of the class's lessons, or those left), the Discount if any, and the First Lesson they will come to.
5. Open the print template Enrolment letter from Print templates, choose the new enrolment, and press Print or Save as PDF.

#### Send the term's fee invoices

1. About three weeks before a term, open the Fee Invoices form and press New for each family with places booked. The Number is the next in the year's run (INV-2026-0043 after INV-2026-0042). Choose the Family and Term, and type the Invoice Date and the Due Date (the first day of term).
2. Type the Amount: the sum of the family's places, each the course's Fee per Lesson times the Lessons Billed, less its Discount.
3. Open the Enrolments form, find each of the family's places for the term and choose the new invoice in Invoice. These are the invoice's lines.
4. Open the print template Fee invoice, choose the invoices just made, and press Print or Save as PDF. Check that the Total for the term matches the Amount you typed.

#### Record a payment and give a receipt

1. Open the Payments form and press New. Type the next receipt Number (RCP-2026-0042), choose the Invoice, and type Paid On, the Amount and the Method.
2. Type in Balance After what is still owed on the invoice once this payment is in.
3. Open the Fee Invoices form, find the invoice and add the payment to Paid So Far.
4. Open the print template Payment receipt, choose the payment and press Print. It fits on A5.

#### Take the register and mark a test

1. Print the report Class register before the lessons: a page for each class with medical notes and the family's phone number.
2. After the lesson, open the Lessons form, find the lesson by its date and class, and set Status to Taught. Set Teacher to whoever took it if someone covered.
3. Open the Attendance form and press New for each student: choose the Lesson and Student and set Mark to Present, Late or Absent, with a Reason if the family gave one.
4. On a test day, open the Assessments form and press New: choose the Class, type the Assessment Date, Title and Out Of. Then add a Results record for each student who sat it, with their Score.

#### Write and print the term reports

1. In the week after a term ends, open the query Progress by student to see each student's marks, and the report Attendance concerns for anyone who has missed a lot.
2. Open the Term Reports form and press New for each student: choose the Student and Term, type the School Year they were in, the Written On date and a short Comment on the term.
3. In the Report Lines below, add a line for each class they took: the Class, the Lessons, Present, Late and Absent from the register, the Half-term % and End of Term % from their results, and the teacher's comment.
4. Open the print template Term report, choose the term's reports, and press Print or Save as PDF to send home.
5. For adult courses and holiday workshops finished, open the Certificates form and press New for each learner who came to three lessons in four: choose the Enrolment, type the Number, Issued On, Lessons Attended and Hours. Print them with the print template Certificate of completion.

#### Pay the teachers for the month

1. On the first working day of the month, run the query Teacher hours last month, or print the report Teacher pay: the lessons, hours and pay for each teacher for the month just ended.
2. Open the Pay Statements form and press New for each teacher: the Number (PAY-2026-0042), Teacher, Month (2026-09), Period Start and Period End, the Hourly Rate, and the Lessons, Hours and Gross from the query.
3. Open the Lessons form and set Pay Statement on each lesson they taught that month, so the statement lists them.
4. Open the print template Pay statement, choose the month's statements, and press Print. Type Paid On when the pay has gone out.

#### Chase fees that are overdue

1. Run the query Fees outstanding by family to see who owes what, largest first.
2. Print the report Fees due letters: each overdue invoice, family by family, with the address and what is left to pay.
3. Print the family's Fee invoice again from Print templates: it shows the payments made so far and the balance due.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 33 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The name printed at the top of every document. |
| Address | Short text | The street address. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country. |
| Phone | Short text | The phone number customers call. |
| E-mail | Short text | The address customers write to. |
| Website | Short text | The website, if there is one. |
| Tax Number | Short text | The VAT or sales tax registration number, printed on invoices. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Company Number | Short text | The registered company number, where the business is a company. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Bank Details | Short text | Where customers pay by transfer: the bank, account name and number. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Payment Terms | Short text | The words printed under an invoice's total, such as "Payment within 30 days". |
| Tax Rate | Number | The usual rate of VAT or sales tax as a fraction: 0.2 is twenty percent. Lines may carry a rate of their own. |
| Currency | Short text | The currency the business trades in, as its three-letter code. |
| Document Footer | Long text | A line or two at the foot of every document: thanks, opening hours, returns policy. |

#### Terms

The blocks of weeks the centre teaches in: three terms a year and the school holidays between them, when holiday workshops run. Every class belongs to one, and fees are invoiced by it. Enter these first. The sample has 7 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required, unique | The name families know the block by, such as Autumn 2026 or Easter holiday 2026. |
| Kind | Short text | Term for a teaching term, Holiday for the holiday workshops between terms. |
| Starts | Date, required | The first day of the block. Invoices go out three weeks before it. |
| Ends | Date, required | The last day of the block. A class whose term has not ended is current or coming, and the class lists and free places look only at those. |

| Pay Statement | Points at Pay Statements | The month's pay statement the lesson was paid on, set when the month's statements are made. Empty for planned and cancelled lessons and for this month's. |

One invoice for each family for each term or holiday they book, covering every class their students take in it. Its lines are the Enrolments that point at it. The sample has 464 records.

### Queries

#### Class lists

Every student in every class that is running now or about to start, with the class's day, time, room and teacher, any medical note, photo consent and the family's phone number. Print it as the register before a lesson.

From Enrolments, Students, Classes, Courses, Terms, Teachers, Families. Shows Class, Course, Weekday, Start Time, Room, Teacher, Student, School Year, Medical Note, Photo Consent, Contact, Phone.
Calculated: Class is `[Classes].[Code] & ", " & [Terms].[Name]`; Teacher is `[Teachers].[First Name] & " " & [Teachers].[Last Name]`; Student is `[Students].[First Name] & " " & [Students].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status = Enrolled` and `Days to End >= 0`.

#### Timetable, next 7 days

Every lesson from today to a week ahead, in date and time order, with the room, the teacher and the planned topic. Use it to plan rooms and cover.

From Lessons, Classes, Courses, Teachers. Shows Lesson Date, Weekday, Start Time, Course, Class, Room, Teacher, Minutes, Topic.
Calculated: Teacher is `[Teachers].[First Name] & " " & [Teachers].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 7` and `Status <> "Cancelled"`.

#### Attendance below 85 percent

Students who have missed more than fifteen in a hundred of their lessons in the last 90 days, with at least four lessons in that time, and the family to call.

From Attendance, Students, Lessons, Families. Shows Student, School Year, Contact, Phone, Lessons, Absences, Attendance %.
Calculated: Student is `[Students].[First Name] & " " & [Students].[Last Name]`; Absences is `IIf([Mark] = "Absent", 1, 0)`; Attendance % is `IIf([Mark] = "Absent", 0, 100)`.
Only where `ID >= 4` and `Attendance % < 85` and `Days Ago Between 1 And 90`.

#### Fees outstanding by family

Each family that still owes something, with how many invoices are open, the oldest due date and the total left to pay, largest first.

From Fee Invoices, Families. Shows Family, Contact, Phone, Invoices, Oldest Due, Outstanding.
Calculated: Outstanding is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Paid So Far]), 2)`.
Only where `Balance > 0`.

#### Overdue fees

Each invoice past its due date that is not fully paid, with its number, the family's address, the term, how many days late it is and what is left to pay. The fees letters are written from it.

From Fee Invoices, Families, Terms. Shows Family, Contact, Address, City, Postcode, Invoice, Term, Due Date, Amount, Days Overdue, Outstanding.
Calculated: Days Overdue is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`; Outstanding is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Paid So Far]), 2)`.
Only where `Days Overdue > 0` and `Outstanding > 0`.

#### Classes with free places

Classes running now or next with room for more students: places, how many are enrolled and how full the class is. Use it when a family asks for a place.

From Classes, Courses, Terms, Teachers, Enrolments. Shows Class, Term, Course, Weekday, Start Time, Teacher, Places, Enrolled, Percent Full.
Calculated: Teacher is `[Teachers].[First Name] & " " & [Teachers].[Last Name]`; Percent Full is `100 / [Classes].[Capacity]`.
Only where `Percent Full < 100` and `Status = Enrolled` and `Days to End >= 0`.

#### Results by course

For each course, how many test results there were in the last twelve months and the average, highest and lowest marks as percentages.

From Results, Assessments, Classes, Courses. Shows Course, Subject, Results, Average %, Highest %, Lowest %.
Calculated: Average % is `Round([Score] * 100 / [Out Of], 0)`; Highest % is `Round([Score] * 100 / [Out Of], 0)`; Lowest % is `Round([Score] * 100 / [Out Of], 0)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Progress by student

Every test result of the last twelve months, student by student, with the mark, the percentage and the teacher's comment. The progress report prints it.

From Results, Students, Assessments, Classes, Courses. Shows Student, Course, Assessment, Assessment Date, Score, Out Of, Percent, Comment.
Calculated: Student is `[Students].[First Name] & " " & [Students].[Last Name] & " (" & [School Year] & ")"`; Percent is `Round([Score] * 100 / [Out Of], 0)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Enrolments by course and term

How many places were booked on each course in each term and holiday, and the fees charged for them.

From Enrolments, Classes, Courses, Terms. Shows Starts, Term, Course, Enrolments, Fees.
Calculated: Fees is `Round([Fee per Lesson] * [Lessons Billed] * (1 - Nz([Discount])), 2)`.

#### Teacher hours last month

For each teacher, the lessons they taught last month, the hours and what they are owed at their hourly rate. Run it at the start of each month for the pay run.

From Lessons, Teachers. Shows Month, Teacher, Hourly Rate, Lessons, Hours, Pay.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Lesson Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Teacher is `[Teachers].[First Name] & " " & [Teachers].[Last Name]`; Hours is `[Minutes] / 60`; Pay is `Round([Minutes] / 60 * [Hourly Rate], 2)`.
Only where `Status = Taught` and `Months Ago = 1`.

#### Fees received by month

Money received each month from fees, and how many payments made it up.

From Payments. Shows Month, Payments, Received.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Paid On], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Birthdays coming up

Active students with a birthday in about the next month, with the age they turn. Adults have no date of birth here, so only children appear.

From Students. Shows Student, School Year, Birthday, Turns.
Calculated: Student is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Birthday is `Format([Date of Birth], "dd") & "/" & Format([Date of Birth], "mm")`; Turns is `Year(Date()) - Year([Date of Birth]) + IIf(Month([Date of Birth]) * 31 + Day([Date of Birth]) < Month(Date()) * 31 + Day(Date()), 1, 0)`.
Only where `Days Away Between 0 And 30` and `Active = Yes`.

#### Background checks due

Teachers whose background check is 33 months old or more, so it can be renewed before three years are up.

From Teachers. Shows Teacher, Subjects, Background Check, Months Old.
Calculated: Teacher is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Months Old is `DateDiff("m", [Background Check], Date())`.
Only where `Months Old >= 33` and `Active = Yes`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Terms, Families, Students, Teachers, Courses, Classes, Enrolments, Lessons, Attendance, Assessments, Results, Fee Invoices, Payments, Term Reports, Report Lines, Certificates, Pay Statements. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Class register

A page for each class running now or next: the students with their school year, medical note, photo consent and the family's contact and phone. Teachers take it into the lesson.

From the query Class lists, a group for each Class: Student, School Year, Medical Note, Photo Consent, Contact, Phone, with the count of Student.

#### Timetable for the next 7 days

The lessons of the coming week, day by day and in time order, with course, class, room and teacher. Pin it up in the office.

From the query Timetable, next 7 days, a group for each Lesson Date: Start Time, Course, Class, Room, Teacher, Minutes, with the count of Class.

#### Fees overdue

Overdue invoices family by family, with the address to write to and the total owed. Use it to send reminder letters.

From the query Overdue fees, a group for each Family: Contact, Address, City, Postcode, Invoice, Term, Due Date, Days Overdue, Outstanding, with the total of Outstanding.

#### Progress report

Each student's test results over the last year with the teacher's comments and their average percentage, to send home at the end of term.

From the query Progress by student, a group for each Student: Course, Assessment, Assessment Date, Score, Out Of, Percent, Comment, with the average of Percent.

#### Teacher pay

Hours and pay for each teacher for last month, with the totals, for the pay run.

From the query Teacher hours last month: Month, Teacher, Hourly Rate, Lessons, Hours, Pay, with the total of Hours, total of Pay.

#### Attendance concerns

The students whose attendance has fallen below 85 percent, with the family to call.

From the query Attendance below 85 percent: Student, School Year, Contact, Phone, Lessons, Absences, Attendance %.

#### Enrolments by course

For each course, the places booked and the fees charged term by term, with totals.

From the query Enrolments by course and term, a group for each Course: Term, Starts, Enrolments, Fees, with the total of Enrolments, total of Fees.

#### Fees received

Fee income month by month, with the total.

From the query Fees received by month: Month, Payments, Received, with the total of Payments, total of Received.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Fee invoice

Sent to each family about three weeks before a term or holiday starts: a line for each child's class with the lessons, the price per lesson and any discount, then the total. The discounts row and the line about discounts show only when there is one; once something has been paid it shows what has come in and the balance due, and a paid invoice says so in place of how to pay. Numbered INV-2026-0042. Print it again later and it shows the payments since. One for each record of Fee Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Fee invoice {Number}
- Fields: To, Invoice, Address, Invoice Date, City, Please pay by, Postcode, For, Account
- Lines from Enrolments: Student, Course, Day, Time, Lessons, Per Lesson, Fees, Discount, To Pay
- Totals: Fees, Less discounts, Total for the term, Paid so far, Balance due
- Words: Brothers and sisters after the first child booked in a term have ten percent off; a bursary place is half fees.
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Pay by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}, or by card or cash at the office.
- Words: Paid in full. Thank you.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Payment receipt

Given or sent for each payment, on A5: the receipt number, who paid, how, which invoice it was for, what was owing before it, and what is left to pay, or that the invoice is now paid in full. One for each record of Payments, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Receipt {Number}
- Fields: Receipt, Received on, Received from, Paid by, For invoice, Term
- Totals: Owing before this payment, Received with thanks, Left to pay on the invoice
- Words: The invoice is now paid in full.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}
- Signed by: Received for the centre

#### Enrolment letter

Sent when a place is booked: the class, its day, time and room, the teacher, the first lesson, the term's dates, what to bring, any discount or bursary, and what happens if the student cannot come. It prints for places whose Status is Enrolled; a finished or withdrawn place prints when you choose it from the Enrolments form. Have the wording checked for your own centre and country. One for each record of Enrolments, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Fields: To, Date, Address, City, Postcode, Our reference
- Heading: Your place is confirmed: {Student.First Name} on {Class.Course.Name}
- Words: Dear {Student.Family.Contact},
- Words: Thank you for booking with us. This letter confirms the place for {Student} and tells you what to expect before the first lesson.
- Fields: First lesson, Term starts, Term ends
- Words: 1. The class. {Class.Course.Name} meets every {Class.Weekday} at {Class.Start Time} in {Class.Room}, and each lesson lasts {Class.Course.Minutes} minutes. The teacher is {Class.Teacher}.
- Words: 2. When it starts. The first lesson for {Student.First Name} is on the day above. {Class.Term} runs between the dates above, and the class has {Class.Lessons Planned} lessons in that time.
- Words: 3. What to bring. {Class.Course.What to Bring}
- Words: 4. Fees. The place is charged for {Lessons Billed} lessons, on the invoice for the term. Fees are not refunded part way through a term, but if a lesson is cancelled by us it is made up or taken off the next invoice.
- Words: Another place in the family was booked first this term, so this place for {Student.First Name} has ten percent off.
- Words: This is a bursary place, at half fees.
- Words: 5. Arriving and going home. Please arrive five minutes before the start. Children are signed in at the front desk and wait inside until they are collected, so please tell the office if someone new is coming for them. Adult learners go straight to the room.
- Words: 6. If you cannot come. Ring {Business.Phone} or write to {Business.E-mail} before the lesson, so the register can be marked and work kept back.
- Words: We look forward to seeing {Student.First Name}.
- Words: Yours sincerely,
- Words: The office, {Business.Name}

#### Term report

The progress report sent home after each term: for each class, the lessons, late marks and absences, the attendance percentage, the half-term and end of term marks and the teacher's comment, then the attendance for the term and the centre's comment. One for each record of Term Reports, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Progress report, {Term}
- Fields: Student, School Year, Term, Date, Sent to
- Lines from Report Lines: Course, Teacher, Lessons, Late, Absent, Attended %, Half-term %, End of Term %, Teacher's comment
- Totals: Classes, Lessons this term, Missed, Attendance, %
- Words: {Comment}
- Words: Marks are percentages of the test. A blank mark means the test was missed or the course has none.
- Signed by: Centre director

#### Certificate of completion

Given to each adult learner who finishes a course and each child who finishes a holiday workshop with three lessons in four attended: the course, its level, the term, the teacher, the lessons and hours, signed by the teacher and the director. One for each record of Certificates, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Certificate of completion
- Words: This is to certify that
- Heading: {Enrolment.Student}
- Words: has completed {Enrolment.Class.Course.Name} ({Enrolment.Class.Course.Level}) at {Business.Name}, {Enrolment.Class.Term}, taught by {Enrolment.Class.Teacher}, attending {Lessons Attended} lessons and {Hours} hours of teaching.
- Fields: Certificate, Issued On
