#### Pay statement

Given to each teacher each month: every lesson they taught with its day, class, minutes and pay at their hourly rate, then the lessons counted, the hours and the gross pay, and the day it was paid once it has been. Tax and National Insurance are worked out by the payroll, not here. One for each record of Pay Statements, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Pay statement {Number}
- Fields: Teacher, Statement, Month, Hourly Rate, From, To, Paid On
- Lines from Lessons: Date, Class, Course, Minutes, Hours, Rate, Pay
- Totals: Lessons taught, Hours, Gross pay
- Words: Pay is for lessons taught, at your hourly rate; cancelled lessons are not paid. Tax and National Insurance are taken by the payroll and shown on the payslip it sends.

### Starting empty

Start with Business, the centre's own name, address and bank details, which every document prints. Then Terms (this year's terms and holidays), then Teachers and Courses (what you teach, how long and at what price). Then set up the Classes for the first term, each with its course, teacher, day, time and room. Enter Families and then their Students as they book, and an Enrolment for each place. Add the Lessons of each class (one for each week of the term), take the register in Attendance as the lessons happen, and record Assessments and Results when tests are marked. Raise a Fee Invoice for each family each term and set each of their enrolments' Invoice to it, then enter Payments as they come in, adding each to the invoice's Paid So Far. At the end of a term write a Term Report for each student, with a Report Line for each class; at the end of a month make each teacher's Pay Statement and set it on the lessons they taught.

### Making it yours

- For one-to-one tutoring, set each course's Capacity to 1 and make a class for each student's regular slot; the timetable and teacher pay work as they are.
- For a music or dance school, use the subjects for instruments or dance styles and the levels for grades; add a Grade field to Results for exam grades.
- If you charge by the month instead of by the term, make each month a Term record and raise the invoices monthly.
- Add a Waiting status to Enrolments for full classes, and a query listing waiting students by class, oldest first.
- For a driving school, make each learner's block of lessons a class with Capacity 1 and the instructor as the teacher; add a Test Date field to Students.
- To keep a fuller register, add a Minutes Late field to Attendance, or a Homework Done yes/no field.
- If teachers are paid a fixed amount a lesson instead of by the hour, add a Rate per Lesson field to Teachers and change the Pay column of Teacher hours last month to use it.
- Add a Rooms table with each room's size if you have many rooms, and point Classes at it instead of typing the room.
- If your centre is registered for VAT and its courses are not exempt, add a Tax Rate field to Courses and a VAT column to the Fee invoice print template, as the trading sample's invoice has.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print one family's invoice?**

Open the print template Fee invoice, choose that family's invoice from the list (or open it in the Fee Invoices form and print from there), and press Print or Save as PDF.

**How is the discount for brothers and sisters worked out?**

The first child booked in a term pays the full fee; each brother or sister booked after them has 0.1 in Discount on their enrolments, ten percent off. A bursary place has 0.5. The invoice shows the fee, the discount taken off and what is left to pay on each line.

**A child joins half way through the term. What do I charge?**

Set Lessons Billed on the enrolment to the lessons left, and First Lesson to the first one they will come to. The invoice charges for those lessons only.

**Why does the invoice say nothing about VAT?**

Private tuition and education are exempt from VAT in many countries, and the sample is set up that way. If you must charge it, add a tax rate as the ways to adapt the sample describe, and ask your accountant first.

**How do I print last month's pay statements?**

Open the print template Pay statement and choose the statements whose Month is last month, then press Print. Each lists the lessons the teacher taught, the hours and the gross pay.

**Who gets a certificate?**

In the sample, adult learners who finish a course and children who finish a holiday workshop, when they came to at least three lessons in four. Children on term courses get their term report instead. Change the rule to suit your centre: a certificate is simply a record in Certificates.

**Can I change the wording of the enrolment letter?**

Yes. Open Print templates, choose Enrolment letter and edit its text blocks. The words in curly brackets, such as {Class.Weekday}, are filled from the enrolment and its class; keep them as they are or the letter will print them as blanks.

## Rowanmere Community Trust

**Charity or club.** Members, supporters, gifts, tax claims, events, volunteers and grants for a small community charity or club.

For a small charity or club run by a committee and a part-time treasurer: one database for the people who belong, give, come to events and help out, and for the money that comes in.

Rowanmere Community Trust is an invented community charity in Glasgow. It has about two hundred members who pay a yearly fee, regular supporters who give by standing order, appeals for things like a minibus or a new garden path, a hall where it holds a quiz, a ceilidh or a coffee morning most fortnights, a few dozen volunteers, and grants from a handful of invented trusts and the local council.

The records cover the last eighteen months and run into the coming weeks: memberships due for renewal, events with bookings already taken, the volunteer rota and grant reports still to write. Gifts from people who have made a tax declaration are gathered into a claim each quarter, as a UK charity claims Gift Aid; the current quarter's gifts are waiting for the next claim. Every payment in is also written once in the Income table, so the treasurer can see income by source and by month.

It suits, with small changes: A sports or social club with yearly subscriptions; A local history, gardening or arts society; A parent teacher association; A place of worship with regular givers and volunteers; A community centre or village hall committee; A small animal rescue or food bank run by volunteers.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Every payment in is written twice: once where it belongs (a gift in Donations, a fee in Memberships, a booking in Event Bookings) and once in Income, the cash book. The income queries and reports read only Income, so a payment left out of it is missing from the treasurer's figures.
- Receipt, membership, ticket and certificate numbers are typed, one on from the last, with a new run each year. The sample gave them in date order; Data Files does not fill them in for you.
- A renewal is a new Memberships record, not a change to the old one. Tick Renewed on the old one, or the member stays in Renewals due and later in Lapsed members.
- Claimable is set from the declaration in place on the day of the gift. Where your scheme lets a new declaration cover earlier gifts, as the UK's does for four years, tick Claimable on those gifts too.
- The claim of a quarter of each gift is written in three places: the Gifts to claim query, the Donation receipt and the Tax claim schedule. Change all three if your scheme pays a different share.
- Some print templates print only the records they are for: the Donation receipt for gifts that are not standing orders, the Renewal reminder for memberships ending in the next 30 days and not renewed, the Membership card for memberships still good, and the Event ticket for bookings not cancelled. A record you choose from its form always prints. The rest print every record, so choose the ones you mean before pressing Print.
- The trust is not registered for VAT, so Tax Rate in Business is nought and no document shows VAT. Company Number holds the charity number, printed at the foot of each letter.
- The volunteer shifts go back further than the other records, so the whole of the last volunteer year (to 31 March) is there to count for the certificates.

### Tutorial

#### Record a gift and send the thank-you letter

1. Open the People form and find the giver by name. For someone new, press New and type their name, address and phone, tick what they have agreed to be contacted by, and tick Tax Declaration with its Declaration Date if they have signed one.
2. Open the Donations form and press New. Type the next receipt number in Number, one on from the last (RCP-2026-0042 after RCP-2026-0041). Choose the giver in Person and the appeal in Campaign (General Fund when they named none), then type the Gift Date, Amount and Method.
3. Tick Claimable if the giver had a tax declaration on the day of the gift. Tick Regular only for a monthly standing order.
4. Open the Income form, press New and write the same money in the cash book: Received On, Source Donations, the appeal in Description, the Amount, the Method, and the receipt number in Reference.
5. Open the print template Donation receipt from Print templates, choose the gift, and press Print or Save as PDF.

#### Send renewal reminders and renew a membership

1. Each week, run the query Renewals due: memberships ending in the next 30 days that have not been renewed. The report Renewal reminders prints the same list.
2. Open the print template Renewal reminder from Print templates: it holds a letter for each membership on that list. Press Print.
3. When the fee comes in, open the Memberships form, find the old membership and tick Renewed.
4. Press New for the new year: choose the Person and Membership Type, set Starts to the day after the old Ends and Ends a year on, type the Amount, Paid On and Method, and the next membership number in Number (MEM-2026-0042).
5. Write the fee in the Income form with Source Membership and the membership number in Reference.
6. Open the print template Membership card, choose the new membership, and print the card to post or hand over.

#### Take a booking for an event and print the ticket

1. Open the Events form and find the event, or press New and type its Name, Event Date, Start Time, Venue, Capacity and Ticket Price. Status stays Planned until it is held.
2. Open the Event Bookings form and press New. Type the next ticket number in Number (TKT-2026-0042), choose the Event and the Person, and type Booked On, Tickets and Amount Paid.
3. Write the money in the Income form with Source Events and the ticket number in Reference.
4. Open the print template Event ticket, choose the booking, and press Print or Save as PDF to e-mail it.
5. On the night, print the report Event guest list for the door and tick Attended on each booking that came. Afterwards set the event's Status to Held and type its Costs.

#### Make the quarterly tax claim

1. Run the query Gifts to claim: claimable gifts not yet in a claim, with each giver's house and postcode. Print the report Claim schedule to check them.
2. Open the Tax Claims form and press New. Type the Reference (TC-007), the last gift date covered in Gifts Up To, today in Submitted On, and the report's total Claim Value in Amount Claimed.
3. Open the Donations form as a datasheet, and set Tax Claim to the new claim on each gift in the schedule, so they leave Gifts to claim.
4. Open the print template Tax claim schedule, choose the new claim, and print it or save it as a PDF to keep with the claim.
5. When the money arrives, type Received On and Amount Received on the claim, and write it in the Income form with Source Tax claims.

#### Keep the volunteer rota and thank volunteers at the year end

1. Open the Volunteer Shifts form and press New for each turn on the rota: the Person, the Role, the Shift Date, Start Time and Hours.
2. Run the query Volunteer rota for the next fortnight and pin it on the noticeboard.
3. After 31 March, run the query Volunteers to see each person's hours. Open the Volunteer Certificates form and press New for each one who gave their time: the Number, Person, Main Role, the year's dates, Shifts, Hours and Roles.
4. Open the print template Volunteer certificate, choose the certificates, and print them for the annual general meeting. Type Presented On when they are handed over.

#### Report to the trustees each month

1. Print the report Income by month for the treasurer's report: income by source with each month's total.
2. Print the report Donations by campaign to show each appeal against its target.
3. Print the report Membership list for the number of members of each type, and the report Grant reports for reports owed to funders.
4. Run the query Lapsed members and share it with whoever makes the friendly calls.

#### Apply for a grant and report on it

1. Open the Funders form and press New for a funder you have not applied to before.
2. Open the Grants form and press New: choose the Funder, type the Purpose, Applied On and Amount Asked. Status stays Applied.
3. When the funder decides, type Decided On and set Status to Awarded or Declined; for an award, type Amount Awarded, Paid On when it arrives, Period Ends and Report Due, and write the money in Income with Source Grants.
4. Run the query Grant reports due each month. When a report is sent, type Report Sent and set Status to Completed.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 37 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Order | Whole number | The order the steps are read in. |
| Task | Short text, required | The everyday task the step belongs to. |
| Step | Whole number | The step's number within its task. |
| What To Do | Long text | What to open and what to do there. |

#### Business

The business's own details, in one record. Every document it prints, an invoice, a receipt, a statement or a letter, takes its name, address and payment details from here, so they are changed in one place. The sample has 1 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The name printed at the top of every document. |
| Address | Short text | The street address. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country. |
| Phone | Short text | The phone number customers call. |
| E-mail | Short text | The address customers write to. |
| Website | Short text | The website, if there is one. |
| Tax Number | Short text | The reference the tax office gives the trust for its tax claims on gifts, printed on nothing but kept here with the rest. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Company Number | Short text | The charity's registered number, printed at the foot of every letter, as a charity must. The sample has a placeholder of zeros. |
| Bank Details | Short text | Where customers pay by transfer: the bank, account name and number. The sample has a placeholder. |
| Payment Terms | Short text | The words printed under an invoice's total, such as "Payment within 30 days". |
| Tax Rate | Number | The rate of VAT the trust charges: nought, as a small charity that is not registered for VAT. Change it if yours is. |
| Currency | Short text | The currency the business trades in, as its three-letter code. |
| Document Footer | Long text | A line or two at the foot of every document: thanks, opening hours, returns policy. |

#### People

One record per person the trust knows: members, donors, event guests and volunteers are all here, once each. What someone is to the trust comes from their other records (a membership, a gift, a shift). The sample has 871 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| First Name | Short text | The given name, used on letters and lists. |
| Last Name | Short text, required | The family name; lists are sorted by it. |
| Address | Short text | House number and street, for letters and for a tax claim, which needs the house and postcode of each giver. |
| City | Short text | The town or city. |
| Postcode | Short text | The postcode or ZIP code. |
| Country | Short text | The country, United Kingdom unless you enter another. |
| Phone | Short text | A phone number, used for the volunteer rota and event changes. |
| E-mail | Short text | An e-mail address, left empty for people who have none. |
| Joined | Date | The day the person first came onto the records, by joining, giving or booking. |
| Contact by Post | Yes/No | Yes when the person has agreed to letters and the newsletter by post. The mailing list uses it. |
| Contact by E-mail | Yes/No | Yes when the person has agreed to e-mail from the trust. |
| Contact by Phone | Yes/No | Yes when the person has agreed to be phoned. |
| Tax Declaration | Yes/No | Yes when the person has declared that they pay enough tax for the trust to claim tax back on their gifts (in the UK, a Gift Aid declaration). Many countries have a scheme like it; where yours has none, ignore it. |
| Declaration Date | Date | The day the declaration was made. Gifts from that day on are claimable. |
| Notes | Long text | Anything worth remembering, such as a gift made in memory of someone or a request for large print. |

#### Membership Types

The kinds of membership on offer and what each costs. Enter these first. The sample has 5 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required, unique | The name of the membership, such as Adult or Family. |
| Fee | Currency | What the membership costs now. A renewal is charged at this fee. |
| Months | Whole number | How long it lasts, usually 12. Nought means it never ends, as for a life membership. |
| Description | Short text | Who the membership is for. |

#### Memberships

One record for each year of membership paid. A renewal is a new record starting the day after the last one ends, so a member's history stays. The sample has 501 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The membership number, printed on the card and quoted when paying: MEM-2026-0042. Given in the order fees are paid, a new run each year, and used once. |
| Person | Points at People, required | The member. |
| Membership Type | Points at Membership Types, required | The kind of membership. |
| Starts | Date | The first day of the membership. |
| Ends | Date | The last day of the membership; empty for a life membership. |
| Amount | Currency | What was paid for it. |
| Paid On | Date | The day the fee was paid. |
| Method | Short text | How it was paid: standing order, card, cash or bank transfer. |
| Renewed | Yes/No | Yes once a later membership has been taken out, so this one no longer shows as due or lapsed. |

Appeals for a stated purpose, each with a target, and the General Fund for gifts given to no appeal in particular. Every gift belongs to one. The sample has 6 records.

| Closes | Date | The day it ended or ends; empty for a fund that stays open. |

Each claim made to the tax office for tax back on gifts, made each quarter. The gifts in a claim point at it. The sample has 6 records.

### Relationships

- Memberships.Person points at a record in People
- Memberships.Membership Type points at a record in Membership Types
- Donations.Person points at a record in People
- Donations.Campaign points at a record in Campaigns
- Donations.Tax Claim points at a record in Tax Claims
- Event Bookings.Event points at a record in Events
- Event Bookings.Person points at a record in People
- Volunteer Shifts.Person points at a record in People
- Volunteer Shifts.Role points at a record in Volunteer Roles
- Volunteer Certificates.Person points at a record in People
- Volunteer Certificates.Main Role points at a record in Volunteer Roles
- Grants.Funder points at a record in Funders

### Queries

#### Current members

Everyone whose membership has started and not yet ended, and life members, by type. Use it to check who may vote at the AGM or use members' rates.

From Memberships, People, Membership Types. Shows Type, Member, Starts, Ends, E-mail, Phone.
Calculated: Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days In >= 0` and `Days In >= 0` and `Days Left >= 0` and `Ends Is Null`.

#### Members by type

How many current members there are of each type and what they paid. A quick count for the committee.

From Memberships, Membership Types. Shows Type, Members, Fees Paid.
Only where `Days In >= 0` and `Days In >= 0` and `Days Left >= 0` and `Ends Is Null`.

#### Renewals due

Memberships ending in the next 30 days that have not been renewed, with addresses and the fee to ask for. Run it each week and send the reminders.

From Memberships, People, Membership Types. Shows Ends, Days Left, Member, Type, Renewal Fee, Address, City, Postcode, E-mail, Contact by E-mail.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Ends])`; Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 30` and `Renewed = No`.

#### Lapsed members

Members whose membership ended in the last year and who have not renewed. Worth a friendly call or e-mail; some simply forgot.

From Memberships, People, Membership Types. Shows Member, Type, Ended, Days Lapsed, E-mail, Phone, Contact by E-mail.
Calculated: Member is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Lapsed is `DateDiff("d", [Ends], Date())`.
Only where `Days Lapsed Between 1 And 365` and `Renewed = No`.

#### Appeals against target

Each appeal and fund with its target, what has been given to it and how many gifts. Shows which appeals reached their target.

From Campaigns, Donations. Shows Campaign, Opens, Closes, Target, Given, Gifts.

#### Gifts to claim

Claimable gifts not yet put into a tax claim, with the giver's name, house and postcode and what the claim on each brings back. This is the next claim.

From Donations, People. Shows Gift Date, First Name, Last Name, Address, Postcode, Amount, Claim Value.
Calculated: Claim Value is `Round([Amount] * 0.25, 2)`.
Only where `Claimable = Yes` and `Tax Claim Is Null`.

#### Tax claims made

Each tax claim with the gifts in it, what was claimed and when the money came; a claim still awaited has no date received.

From Tax Claims, Donations. Shows Reference, Gifts Up To, Submitted On, Gifts, Gifts Total, Claimed, Received On, Received.

#### Top supporters

The people who gave most in the last 12 months, with the number of gifts. Use it for thank-you letters.

From People, Donations. Shows Supporter, City, Given, Gifts, Tax Declaration.
Calculated: Supporter is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Regular givers

Supporters with a monthly gift that arrived in the last 45 days, and the amount. A giver missing from it may have stopped their standing order.

From People, Donations. Shows Supporter, Monthly Gift, Last Gift, Tax Declaration.
Calculated: Supporter is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Regular = Yes` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 45`.

#### Volunteer hours by month

Hours given each month in each role, and their value at the role's hourly rate. Funders and annual reports often ask for this.

From Volunteer Shifts, Volunteer Roles. Shows Month, Role, Hours, Value.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Shift Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Value is `Round([Hours] * [Hour Value], 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago >= 0`.

#### Volunteers

Each volunteer's shifts and hours in the last 12 months and their last shift, most hours first.

From Volunteer Shifts, People. Shows Volunteer, Phone, Shifts, Hours, Last Shift.
Calculated: Volunteer is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Volunteer rota

Who is on which shift in the next 14 days, with a phone number, for the rota sheet on the noticeboard.

From Volunteer Shifts, Volunteer Roles, People. Shows Shift Date, Start Time, Role, Volunteer, Phone, Hours.
Calculated: Volunteer is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 14`.

#### Upcoming events

Events in the next 60 days with tickets booked so far against the capacity and the money taken.

From Events, Event Bookings. Shows Event Date, Event, Start Time, Venue, Capacity, Booked, Taken.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 60` and `Cancelled = No`.

#### Event attendance

Each event held, with tickets booked, how many came and the ticket income against the costs.

From Events, Event Bookings. Shows Event Date, Event, Capacity, Booked, Came, Ticket Income, Costs.
Calculated: Came is `IIf([Attended] = 1, [Tickets], 0)`.
Only where `Status = Held` and `Cancelled = No`.

#### Guests booked

Every booking for events in the next 60 days, by event, for the door list.

From Event Bookings, Events, People. Shows Event, Event Date, Guest, Tickets, Amount Paid, Phone.
Calculated: Event is `[Events].[Name] & ", " & Format([Event Date], "yyyy-mm-dd")`; Guest is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Ahead Between 0 And 60` and `Cancelled = No`.

#### Grant reports due

Grants awarded whose report to the funder is not yet sent, soonest first; a negative Days Left means the report is late.

From Grants, Funders. Shows Funder, Purpose, Amount Awarded, Period Ends, Report Due, Days Left, Contact Name.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Report Due])`.
Only where `Status = Awarded` and `Report Sent Is Null`.

#### Grants by funder

For each funder, how many applications were made, how much was asked and how much awarded.

From Grants, Funders. Shows Funder, Kind, Applications, Asked, Awarded.
Calculated: Awarded is `Nz([Amount Awarded])`.

#### Income by source by month

All income each month by source: membership, donations, events, collections, grants and tax claims.

From Income. Shows Month, Source, Received, Payments.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Received On], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Income by source

Income in the last 12 months by source, largest first, for the treasurer's report.

From Income. Shows Source, Received, Payments.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Mailing list

Everyone who agreed to post, with their address, sorted by name, for the newsletter labels.

From People. Shows Last Name, First Name, Address, City, Postcode.
Only where `Contact by Post = Yes`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, People, Membership Types, Memberships, Campaigns, Tax Claims, Donations, Events, Event Bookings, Volunteer Roles, Volunteer Shifts, Volunteer Certificates, Funders, Grants, Income. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Membership list

The current members by type, with dates and contact details, and a count of each type. For the membership secretary.

From the query Current members, a group for each Type: Member, Starts, Ends, E-mail, Phone, with the count of Member.

#### Renewal reminders

Members due to renew in the next 30 days with their address and fee, to write or print the reminders from.

From the query Renewals due: Member, Address, City, Postcode, Type, Ends, Renewal Fee, with the total of Renewal Fee.

#### Donations by campaign

Each appeal and fund with its target, the number of gifts and the total given. For the trustees' meeting.

From the query Appeals against target: Campaign, Opens, Closes, Target, Gifts, Given, with the total of Given, total of Gifts.

#### Gifts for the next tax claim

The gifts for the next tax claim with each giver's name, house and postcode, date and amount, and the total to claim. Keep it with the claim.

From the query Gifts to claim: First Name, Last Name, Address, Postcode, Gift Date, Amount, Claim Value, with the total of Amount, total of Claim Value.

#### Volunteer hours

Volunteer hours and their value by month and role, with totals. For the annual report and grant reports.

From the query Volunteer hours by month, a group for each Month: Role, Hours, Value, with the total of Hours, total of Value.

#### Event guest list

The guests booked for each event in the next 60 days with their tickets, for the door.

From the query Guests booked, a group for each Event: Guest, Tickets, Amount Paid, Phone, with the total of Tickets, total of Amount Paid.

Income by source for each month with the month's total. For the treasurer.

From the query Income by source by month, a group for each Month: Source, Payments, Received, with the total of Received.

Grant reports still to write, with the amount and the date each is due.

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Donation receipt

The thank-you letter for a gift, which is also its receipt: the amount, the day it came, the appeal it goes to, whether the giver has a tax declaration and, when they have, what the tax claim adds to it; without one, a line asking them for the form. It prints for every gift but standing orders, which are thanked once a year (choose one from the Donations form to print it anyway); print those of the last week or two by choosing them. One for each record of Donations, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Thank you for your gift
- Fields: To, Receipt, Address, Received on, Town, Given to, Postcode, Tax declaration
- Words: Dear {Person.First Name},
- Words: Thank you for your gift, which reached us on the day above. It goes to the {Campaign}: {Campaign.Description}.
- Totals: Your gift, Tax we can claim back on it, What your gift is worth to us
- Words: You have told us that you pay enough UK income tax for us to claim tax back on your gifts. We will put this one in our next claim, which adds a quarter to it at no cost to you; please tell us if your tax changes.
- Words: We cannot claim tax back on this gift. If you do pay UK income tax, a short declaration lets us claim on this gift and on your future ones, adding a quarter at no cost to you: ask us for the form.
- Words: Please keep this letter as your receipt. Our newsletter tells you how the money is spent; let us know whether you would like it by post or by e-mail.
- Words: With warm thanks,
- Signed by: Treasurer
- Words: Registered charity number {Business.Company Number}. {Business.Document Footer}

#### Renewal reminder

A short letter to a member whose membership ends in the next 30 days and has not been renewed, the same memberships as the Renewals due query: the day it ends, the fee for next year, how to pay (worded for a standing order, which renews itself, or for paying at the office or by transfer), and what membership gives. A life membership has no end and gets no reminder. One for each record of Memberships, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Your membership is due for renewal
- Fields: To, Membership no, Address, Membership, Town, Ends on, Postcode, Fee for next year
- Words: Dear {Person.First Name},
- Words: Your {Membership Type} membership of {Business.Name} comes to an end on the day above. We hope you will stay with us for another year, for the fee shown above.
- Words: You pay by standing order, so your membership renews itself on the day and there is nothing you need to do, unless your bank details have changed.
- Words: You can pay by card or cash at the hall office, or by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting your membership number, {Number}. A standing order renews it each year without a letter: ask us for the form.
- Words: Members pay members' rates for events and the junior sessions, and have a vote at the annual general meeting. Your fee also helps to keep the hall warm and open for everyone who uses it.
- Words: If you have renewed since this letter was printed, thank you, and please ignore it. If you would rather not renew, you need do nothing, though we would be glad to know why: write to {Business.E-mail} or call {Business.Phone}.
- Words: With best wishes,
- Signed by: Membership Secretary
- Words: Registered charity number {Business.Company Number}. {Business.Document Footer}

#### Membership card

A small card for each membership, to show for members' rates: the member, the membership number, the kind of membership and the dates it is good for, or Life for a life membership. It prints for memberships still good today and those starting soon; print it for a new or renewed membership. One for each record of Memberships, on receipt-58 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Membership card
- Fields: Member, Membership no, Membership, Valid from, Valid until, Valid until
- Words: Show this card for members' rates at events.
- Words: If found, please return to {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}.

#### Event ticket

Sent or handed to each guest when they book: the event, when and where, how many it admits, what was paid (or that entry is free), and a ticket number to check at the door. It prints for bookings not cancelled; a cancelled one chosen from its form says the ticket is no longer valid. One for each record of Event Bookings, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: {Event}
- Fields: Ticket, Date, Name, Starts, Admits, Venue, Booked on, Paid
- Words: Entry is free.
- Words: This booking has been cancelled, and the ticket is no longer valid.
- Words: Please bring this ticket, printed or on your phone, and give the number at the door. Tickets are refunded only if the event is cancelled.
- Words: {Business.Name}, {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode}. Registered charity number {Business.Company Number}.

#### Volunteer certificate

A certificate of thanks for each volunteer, with the hours and shifts they gave in the volunteer year, its dates, and the roles they did. Handed out at the annual general meeting, and useful to a volunteer for a job or college application. One for each record of Volunteer Certificates, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Certificate of thanks
- Words: This certificate is presented to
- Heading: {Person}
- Words: in thanks for the {Hours} hours given as a volunteer with {Business.Name}, over {Shifts} shifts, in the volunteer year below.
- Fields: From, To, Roles, Most hours in, Certificate, Presented on
- Words: Our work depends on people who give their time freely. Thank you for yours.
- Signed by: Chair of trustees, Volunteer coordinator

#### Tax claim schedule

The list of gifts that goes with each claim to the tax office: each giver's name, house and postcode, the date and amount of each gift and the tax back on it, with the number of gifts, the totals, and what was received once the claim is paid. The form your tax office wants may differ: check what it asks for in your own country. One for each record of Tax Claims, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Tax claim schedule {Reference}
- Fields: Claim, Charity number, Gifts up to, Tax office reference, Submitted on, Paid on
- Lines from Donations: Date, Receipt, First name, Last name, House and street, Postcode, Amount, Tax back
- Totals: Gifts listed, Gifts, Tax back on them, Amount claimed, Amount received
- Words: Every gift listed was made by a person who had a tax declaration in place on the day of the gift. Keep this schedule, with the declarations, as long as the tax office asks.

### Starting empty

Start with Business: the trust's own name, address and charity number, which every letter, card and ticket prints. Then the lookup tables: Membership Types (your fees), Campaigns (at least a General Fund for gifts given to nothing in particular), Volunteer Roles and Funders. Then enter People as you meet them, with what they have agreed to be contacted by. After that, record Memberships, Donations, Events and their Bookings, Volunteer Shifts and Grants as they happen, and write each payment received in Income too. Make a Tax Claim when you send one and set each gift's Tax Claim to it. Volunteer Certificates come once a year, after the volunteer year ends on 31 March.

### Making it yours

- If your country has no scheme for claiming tax on gifts, leave Tax Declaration empty and delete the Tax Claims table, the Gifts to claim query and the Claim schedule report.
- If your scheme pays a different share than a quarter, change the 0.25 in the Claim Value column of the Gifts to claim query.
- For a club with monthly subscriptions, add a Monthly membership type with Months set to 1, and the renewal queries work as before.
- Add a Spending table (date, kind, description, amount) to see income against costs each month.
- Add an Event field to Volunteer Shifts, pointing at Events, to see who stewarded each event.
- For a parent teacher association, rename Memberships to Families and add a field for the children's classes.
- Add a Gift in Memory Of field to Donations if people often give in memory of someone.
- Add a Safeguarding Check date to People, and a query of volunteers whose check is over three years old.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print thank-you letters for last week's gifts only?**

Open the print template Donation receipt, choose the gifts in the list (sort it by Gift Date), and press Print. Or open the gift in the Donations form and print the letter from there.

**A member has paid but still shows in Renewals due. Why?**

The old membership has not been ticked Renewed. Open it in the Memberships form, tick Renewed, and check the new year's membership has been entered.

**Our country has no scheme for claiming tax on gifts. Can we still use this?**

Yes. Leave Tax Declaration and Claimable unticked, and do not use the Tax Claims table, the Gifts to claim query or the Tax claim schedule. The Donation receipt will show nought for the tax line; take that row out of the template if you like.

**How do I see how much an appeal has raised?**

Run the query Appeals against target, or print the report Donations by campaign: each appeal with its target, the number of gifts and the total given.

**Where do the standing orders come from?**

Each monthly gift is a Donations record with Regular ticked, entered from the bank statement. The query Regular givers shows who has given in the last 45 days, so someone missing from it may have stopped.

**How do we change the trust's address or charity number on every letter?**

Open the Business form and change it there. Every print template takes its letterhead and footer from that one record.

**How do I count volunteer hours for a funder?**

Print the report Volunteer hours: the hours and their value at each role's hourly rate, by month and role. Change a role's Hour Value in Volunteer Roles if the funder uses another rate.

## Hollybrook Lettings

**Property rentals.** Buildings, units, tenants, leases, rent invoices, deposits, repairs, safety checks and the accounts for a landlord.

Hollybrook Lettings is an invented letting business in Leeds that owns and manages twelve buildings: six houses, two blocks of flats, two houses split into flats, a parade of three shops with two flats above, and a yard of two workshops bought about a year ago and refitted. Between them they hold thirty-eight units let to tenants on residential and commercial leases.

The sample holds eighteen months of letting. Each unit has its run of leases: tenants who renewed, tenants who left, and the weeks a unit stood empty between them. A rent invoice goes out two weeks before each rent day, numbered RENT-2026-0042. Most tenants pay on the day by standing order, some pay late, and a few have fallen behind and pay part of what is due; a reminder letter goes to anyone a week behind, and every fortnight after while the rent is still unpaid. Things break and are reported, more of them in winter, and a contractor is booked to mend each one. Homes are inspected twice a year and shops and workshops once a year, gas appliances are checked every year and the wiring every five years, and the tenant gets a written notice before each visit. Insurance, loan interest, cleaning of shared areas, letting costs and the bills for empty units are paid out of each building's account.

Rent on a home carries no VAT. The workshop yard is a building the landlord has opted to tax, so its rent invoices add VAT at twenty percent, and the VAT collected is paid over to the tax office each quarter.

Money for each building goes through one Transactions table, rent in and costs out, so income and expenditure, net income and the month-by-month accounts come from one place. A rent payment also points at the rent invoice it pays, and the invoice keeps the total paid against it, which is how arrears are found. Seven print templates make the papers a landlord sends: the rent invoice, the rent statement with a running balance, the tenancy agreement for a home, the summary of a commercial lease, the deposit receipt, the arrears letter listing the months unpaid, and the notice of an inspection. Each prints only for the records it is for, and leaves out what does not apply: no VAT lines on a home's rent, no payments table before anything is paid.

It suits, with small changes: A private landlord with a few houses or flats; A small letting agent managing homes for owners; Holiday lets, with weekly lets in place of leases; Student houses let by the room; Storage units or lock-up garages; Allotments or moorings let by the year; A small commercial landlord with shops and workshops.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- A rent payment is recorded twice on purpose: once in Transactions, where the money is, and once in the invoice's Amount Paid, which is how arrears are found. When you enter one, change the other.
- Monthly Rent on a lease is the rent before VAT. A rent invoice's Amount is the rent and VAT together, and that is what Amount Paid is measured against.
- Only the workshop yard is opted to tax, so only its two workshops have a Tax Rate of 0.2. The shops in Market Parade are commercial lets without VAT, which is how a building is until its landlord opts to tax it.
- The Status of units and leases (Let, Vacant, Upcoming, Active, Ended) is as it stood on the day the sample was made. Change it by hand when a tenancy starts or ends; the queries for current tenants and the rent roll read it.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: the rent invoices of the last 31 days, the leases running or about to start (homes for the Tenancy agreement, shops and workshops for the Commercial lease summary), the deposits still held, the arrears letters still waiting, and the visits of the next three weeks. A record printed from its own form always prints, whatever the template would choose.
- An arrears letter keeps the amount owed on the day it was written. It is a record of what the tenant was told, so it does not change when they pay.
- A renewal is a new lease for the same tenant and unit. It keeps the deposit and its protection reference from the lease before, so it has no Deposits record of its own.
- Tenants keep a correspondence address. For a tenant living in one of your units it is that unit; when they leave, change it to their forwarding address so the final statement and the deposit letter reach them.

### Tutorial

#### Let a unit to a new tenant

1. Open the query Vacant units to see what is empty and what it would let for.
2. Open the Tenants form and press New. Give the next rent account in Account (TEN- and the next number), then the name, Address (the unit's address, where letters will go), City, Postcode, phone, e-mail and emergency contact. Tick References Checked and ID Checked when they are done.
3. Open the Leases form and press New. Choose the Unit and the Tenant, set Type to Residential or Commercial, and type Signed On, Start, End, Monthly Rent, Rent Day, Pays By and Deposit. For a home type the Pets agreed, or None; for a shop or workshop type the Permitted Use, the Rent Review date and a Tax Rate of 0.2 if the building is opted to tax. Set Status to Upcoming or Active.
4. Open the print template Tenancy agreement (or Commercial lease summary for a shop or workshop) from Print templates, choose the new lease and press Print. Both sides sign two copies.
5. Open the Units form, find the unit, set Status to Let and clear Vacant Since.

#### Take and protect a deposit

1. When the deposit comes in, open the Deposits form and press New. Give the next receipt number in Number (DRC-, the year and the next number), choose the Lease, and type Received On, Amount, Paid By and Held By.
2. Open the print template Deposit receipt, choose the new deposit and press Print or Save as PDF, and give it to the tenant.
3. For a home, protect the deposit with your scheme within 30 days. Open the query Deposits to protect to see which are still waiting and how many days are left.
4. When the scheme gives you its reference, open the Leases form, find the lease and type it into Deposit Ref.

#### Raise the rent invoices

1. Each working day, open the query Rent due in the next 14 days, or the Leases form, to see whose rent day is two weeks away.
2. Open the Rent Charges form and press New for each one. Give the next number in Number (RENT-, the year and the next number), choose the Lease and the Tenant, and type Period (as 2026-11), Invoice Date (today), Due Date (the rent day) and Period End (the day before the next rent day).
3. Type Net (the lease's Monthly Rent) and Tax Rate (the lease's Tax Rate), then Tax (the rent times the rate, to the penny) and Amount (Net and Tax together). Leave Amount Paid at nought.
4. Open the print template Rent invoice from Print templates: it holds the invoices raised in the last 31 days. Choose the new ones and press Print or Save as PDF to send them.
5. At the end of the month, open the report Rent invoices this month to check the month's invoicing.

#### Record a rent payment

1. When rent reaches the bank, open the Transactions form and press New. Choose the Property, type the Date, set Kind to Rent, choose the rent invoice in Charge, type the tenant in Payee or Payer, the Method, and the sum in Money In.
2. Open the Rent Charges form, find the same invoice, add the payment to Amount Paid and type the day in Last Paid On.
3. Open the query Unpaid rent: the invoice drops off it once Amount Paid reaches Amount.

#### Chase rent that is late

1. Open the query Rent arrears by tenant, or the report Arrears letters for every unpaid month by tenant.
2. For each tenant a week or more behind, open the Rent Reminders form and press New. Give the next reference in Number (ARR-, the year and the next number), choose the Lease, and type Sent On, Stage, Amount Owed, Months Owing, Since and Pay By (fourteen days on). Copy the Next Step wording from an earlier letter of the same stage.
3. Open the print template Rent arrears letter, choose the new letter and press Print. Print the tenant's Rent statement from Print templates too, choosing the tenant, and send it with the letter.
4. When the pay-by date comes, set Outcome to Paid in full, Part paid or Not paid. Open the query Arrears letters sent to see the last three months of letters and what came of them.

#### Arrange an inspection or safety check

1. Open the query Inspections due, or the report Checks due, to see what falls due in the next 30 days. For gas and electrical checks, open the query Safety certificates due, which looks 60 days ahead.
2. Agree a day with the inspector or the engineer. Open the Inspections form, find the visit, set Due to the day, type the Visit Time, choose the running Lease, and type today in Notice Sent.
3. Open the print template Notice of inspection, choose the visit and press Print, and send it to the tenant at least a week ahead.
4. After the visit, type Done, Inspector, Outcome and, for a safety check, the Certificate Number. Then press New and enter the next one with its due date. If something needs mending, add it to Maintenance Requests with Reported By set to Inspection.

#### Deal with a repair

1. When a tenant reports a problem, open the Maintenance Requests form and press New. Choose the Unit, type Reported, Reported By, the Problem and the Priority.
2. Book a contractor: choose them in Contractor, type Booked For and set Status to Booked. Open the report Repairs for contractors to print each firm's list of jobs.
3. When the work is done, type Completed and Cost and set Status to Done. Open the Transactions form and enter the bill as money out with Kind set to Repairs and the building in Property.
4. Open the query Open repairs each morning to see what is still waiting, the most urgent first.

#### Close the month

1. Open the report Monthly accounts for money in and out each month, and the report Income and expenditure for each building over the last year.
2. Open the query Costs by kind to see where the money went.
3. At the end of each VAT quarter, add up the Tax on the quarter's paid invoices for the opted building and pay it over; enter it in Transactions with Kind set to VAT.
4. Open the report Rent roll for the units, tenants and rents as they stand, and the report Leases ending to plan renewals.

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 37 records.
