| Pays By | Short text | Standing order, Bank transfer, Card or Cash. |
| Deposit | Currency | The deposit agreed: five weeks' rent for a home, three months' for a shop or workshop. The money itself is recorded in Deposits. |
| Deposit Ref | Short text | The reference the deposit protection scheme gave for a home's deposit (invented here). Empty until it is protected. A renewal keeps the same one. |
| Renewal | Yes/No | Yes when the lease follows an earlier one for the same tenant. |
| Pets | Short text | The pets agreed for a home, in words the agreement prints, or None. |
| Permitted Use | Short text | For a shop or workshop, what the tenant may use it for, as the lease says. |
| Rent Review | Date | For a commercial lease, the day the rent is next reviewed; empty when the lease has no review. |
| Status | Short text | Upcoming, Active or Ended, as it stands today. |
| Notes | Long text | Anything agreed that is not in the fields: a break clause, who repairs what. The commercial lease summary prints it. |

#### Rent Charges

The rent invoices: one record for each lease and month, raised two weeks before the rent day (on the day of signing for a lease's first month). The Rent invoice is printed from here and the Rent statement lists them. The sample has 650 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The invoice's number, given in the order invoices go out and once only: RENT-2026-0042, a new run each year. |
| Lease | Points at Leases, required | The lease the rent is due on. |
| Tenant | Points at Tenants | The tenant charged, the same as the lease's; kept here so a tenant's statement can list their invoices. |
| Period | Short text | The month it is for, as 2026-10. |
| Invoice Date | Date | The day the invoice was raised. |
| Due Date | Date | The day the rent is due, the first day the month's rent covers. |
| Period End | Date | The last day the month's rent covers. |
| Net | Currency | The rent before VAT. |
| Tax Rate | Number | The VAT rate, taken from the lease when the invoice is raised. |
| Tax | Currency | The VAT: the rent times the rate, rounded to the penny. |
| Amount | Currency | What the invoice comes to: rent and VAT together. |
| Amount Paid | Currency | How much has been paid against it so far. Add each payment here as you enter it in Transactions; what is left is owed. |
| Last Paid On | Date | The day the last payment against it came in; empty while nothing has been paid. |

#### Deposits

Each deposit taken, one record for each new tenancy: a renewal keeps the deposit already held. The Deposit receipt is printed from here. The sample has 63 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The receipt's number, given in the order deposits come in: DRC-2026-0042. |
| Lease | Points at Leases, required | The lease the deposit is for. |
| Received On | Date | The day it was paid, usually the day the agreement was signed. |
| Amount | Currency | How much was paid. |
| Paid By | Short text | How it was paid. |
| Held By | Short text | Deposit protection scheme for a home, Landlord for a shop or workshop. |
| Returned On | Date | The day it was paid back after the tenancy ended; empty while it is held. |
| Amount Returned | Currency | How much was paid back. Anything kept back is explained in Notes. |
| Notes | Long text | What was kept back and why, or anything agreed about it. |

#### Rent Reminders

Each letter sent about rent that is late: the first a week after the rent day, then one a fortnight while it is still unpaid. The Rent arrears letter is printed from here. The sample has 156 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The letter's reference: ARR-2026-0042. |
| Lease | Points at Leases, required | The lease the rent is owed on. |
| Sent On | Date | The day the letter went out. |
| Stage | Short text | First reminder, Second reminder or Final notice. |
| Amount Owed | Currency | The rent unpaid on the day the letter was written. |
| Months Owing | Whole number | How many months of rent that covers. |
| Since | Date | The due date of the oldest unpaid month. |
| Pay By | Date | The date the letter asks the tenant to pay by, fourteen days after it is sent. |
| Next Step | Long text | The paragraph saying what happens if the rent is not paid, which the letter prints. It is firmer at each stage; change it for one letter if you need to. |
| Outcome | Short text | Waiting until the pay-by date, then Paid in full, Part paid or Not paid. |

#### Contractors

The trades you call on for repairs and safety checks. The sample has 10 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The firm's name. |
| Trade | Short text | What they do, such as Plumbing and heating or Electrical. |
| Contact | Short text | The person you deal with. |
| Phone | Short text | Their phone number. |
| E-mail | Short text | Where to send job details. |
| Notes | Long text | Rates, insurance, call-out hours. |

#### Maintenance Requests

Each repair asked for or found, from the day it is reported to the day it is done. The sample has 148 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Unit | Points at Units, required | The unit where the problem is. |
| Reported | Date | The day you heard of it. |
| Reported By | Short text | Tenant, Inspection or Landlord. |
| Problem | Short text, required | What is wrong, in a few words. |
| Priority | Short text | Urgent (same or next day), High (within three days), Normal or Low. |
| Status | Short text | Reported, Booked, Done or Cancelled. |
| Contractor | Points at Contractors | Who is doing the work; empty until someone is booked. |
| Booked For | Date | The day the contractor is due. |
| Completed | Date | The day the work was finished. |
| Cost | Currency | What the work cost. The same sum goes into Transactions as money out. |
| Notes | Long text | Access arrangements, parts on order, what was found. |

#### Inspections

Routine inspections of each unit and the safety checks the law asks for, each one due on a date. When one is done, the next one is entered with its due date. The Notice of inspection is printed from here. The sample has 247 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Unit | Points at Units, required | The unit inspected. |
| Lease | Points at Leases | The lease running on the day of the visit, whose tenant gets the notice; empty when the unit is empty. |
| Kind | Short text | Routine inspection, Gas safety or Electrical safety. |
| Due | Date | When it must be done by, and the day the visit is booked for. |
| Visit Time | Short text | The part of the day the visit is booked for, in words the notice prints: between 10am and 1pm. |
| Notice Sent | Date | The day the notice went to the tenant; empty until it has. |
| Done | Date | The day it was done; empty until then. |
| Inspector | Short text | Who did it: one of your staff, or the contractor who did the check. |
| Outcome | Short text | What was found, such as Good, Action needed, Pass or Unsatisfactory. |
| Certificate Number | Short text | The number on the safety certificate (invented here). |
| Notes | Long text | Anything to know before going, or what happened. |

#### Transactions

Every sum of money in or out for a building: rent received, and every cost paid. Each building's accounts are made from these. The sample has 1,122 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Property | Points at Properties, required | The building the money is for. |
| Date | Date | The day it was paid or received. |
| Kind | Short text | Rent, Repairs, Insurance, Loan interest, Shared areas, Safety checks, Letting costs, Agent fees, Empty unit costs or VAT. |
| Description | Short text | What it was for. |
| Charge | Points at Rent Charges | For rent, the rent invoice it pays; empty for a cost. |
| Payee or Payer | Short text | Who paid you, or who you paid. |
| Method | Short text | How it was paid. |
| Money In | Currency | What came in; nought for a cost. |
| Money Out | Currency | What went out; nought for rent. |

### Relationships

- Units.Property points at a record in Properties
- Leases.Unit points at a record in Units
- Leases.Tenant points at a record in Tenants
- Rent Charges.Lease points at a record in Leases
- Rent Charges.Tenant points at a record in Tenants
- Deposits.Lease points at a record in Leases
- Rent Reminders.Lease points at a record in Leases
- Maintenance Requests.Unit points at a record in Units
- Maintenance Requests.Contractor points at a record in Contractors
- Inspections.Unit points at a record in Units
- Inspections.Lease points at a record in Leases
- Transactions.Property points at a record in Properties
- Transactions.Charge points at a record in Rent Charges

### Queries

#### Rent roll

Every lease running today, by building and unit, with the tenant, the term, the rent and the deposit.

From Leases, Units, Properties, Tenants. Shows Property, Unit, Tenant, Type, Start, End, Monthly Rent, Deposit.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`.
Only where `Status = Active`.

#### Rent arrears by tenant

Each tenant who owes rent that is past due, with how many months are unpaid, how much they owe and how many days late the oldest month is. Former tenants who still owe are on it too.

From Rent Charges, Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Tenant, Unit, Phone, Months Owing, Owed, Days Late.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`; Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`; Owed is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Amount Paid]), 2)`; Days Late is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Unpaid > 0` and `Overdue > 0`.

#### Unpaid rent

Every month's rent past its due day and not paid in full, by tenant, with its invoice number and the address to write to.

From Rent Charges, Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Tenant, Address, Invoice, Period, Due Date, Amount, Amount Paid, Owed, Days Late.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`; Address is `[Units].[Postal Address] & ", " & [Properties].[Postcode]`; Owed is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Amount Paid]), 2)`; Days Late is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Owed > 0` and `Days Late > 0`.

#### Rent due in the next 14 days

Rent falling due in the next two weeks and not yet paid, with how each tenant pays, so you know what to expect in the bank.

From Rent Charges, Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Due Date, Days Until, Invoice, Tenant, Unit, Pays By, Amount.
Calculated: Days Until is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Due Date])`; Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`; Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`.
Only where `Days Until Between 0 And 14` and `Owed > 0`.

#### Rent invoices raised

The rent invoices raised in the last 31 days, in number order, with the rent, the VAT and what has been paid.

From Rent Charges, Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Invoice, Invoice Date, Due Date, Tenant, Unit, Net, VAT, Amount, Amount Paid.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`; Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 31`.

#### Leases ending in the next 60 days

Leases whose term ends within two months, with the rent now and what the unit would let for, so you can offer a renewal or plan to relet.

From Leases, Units, Properties, Tenants. Shows Property, Unit, Tenant, Phone, End, Days Left, Monthly Rent, Market Rent.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`; Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [End])`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 60` and `Status = Active`.

#### Vacant units

Units standing empty, how long for, and the rent lost at the market rent since they emptied.

From Units, Properties. Shows Property, Unit, Kind, Bedrooms, Market Rent, Vacant Since, Days Empty, Rent Lost.
Calculated: Days Empty is `DateDiff("d", [Vacant Since], Date())`; Rent Lost is `Round([Market Rent] * 12 / 365 * DateDiff("d", [Vacant Since], Date()), 2)`.
Only where `Status = Vacant`.

#### Open repairs

Repairs not yet done or cancelled, the most urgent first and then the oldest, with how many days each has been open.

From Maintenance Requests, Units, Properties. Shows Job, Priority, Unit, Problem, Reported, Days Open, Status.
Calculated: Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`; Days Open is `DateDiff("d", [Reported], Date())`.
Only where `Status Not In ("Done", "Cancelled")`.

#### Repairs booked

Jobs booked with a contractor and not yet done, by contractor and day, with the address and the problem.

From Maintenance Requests, Units, Properties, Contractors. Shows Contractor, Phone, Job, Booked For, Priority, Address, Problem.
Calculated: Address is `[Units].[Postal Address] & ", " & [Properties].[Postcode]`.
Only where `Status = Booked`.

#### Repair costs by contractor

What each contractor has been paid for finished jobs in the last twelve months, and how many jobs.

From Maintenance Requests, Contractors. Shows Contractor, Trade, Jobs, Spent.
Only where `Status = Done` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Inspections due

Inspections and safety checks due in the next 30 days or already overdue (a Days Left below nought is overdue), with the day the notice went out.

From Inspections, Units, Properties. Shows Due, Days Left, Kind, Unit, Notice Sent, Notes.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Due])`; Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`.
Only where `Days Left <= 30` and `Done Is Null`.

#### Safety certificates due

Gas and electrical safety checks due in the next 60 days or overdue, so the engineer can be booked in time.

From Inspections, Units, Properties. Shows Due, Days Left, Kind, Unit.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Due])`; Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`.
Only where `Days Left <= 60` and `Kind In ("Gas safety", "Electrical safety")` and `Done Is Null`.

#### Deposits held

The deposit taken on every lease running today, with its protection reference.

From Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Property, Unit, Tenant, Type, Deposit, Deposit Ref.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`.
Only where `Status = Active` and `Deposit > 0`.

#### Deposits to protect

Home deposits not yet protected, with how many days are left of the 30 allowed from the start of the lease.

From Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Tenant, Unit, Start, Status, Deposit, Days to Protect.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`; Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`; Days to Protect is `30 - DateDiff("d", [Start], Date())`.
Only where `Type = Residential` and `Deposit Ref Is Null` and `Status In ("Active", "Upcoming")`.

#### Arrears letters sent

The reminder letters sent in the last 90 days, the newest first, with the stage, the amount, the pay-by date and what happened.

From Rent Reminders, Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Letter, Sent On, Tenant, Unit, Stage, Amount Owed, Pay By, Outcome.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`; Unit is `[Units].[Name] & ", " & [Properties].[Name]`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 90`.

#### Current tenants

Everyone living or trading in your units today, with their rent account, phone, e-mail and emergency contact.

From Leases, Tenants, Units, Properties. Shows Property, Unit, Tenant, Account, Phone, E-mail, Emergency Contact, Emergency Phone.
Calculated: Tenant is `Nz([Business Name], [First Name] & " " & [Last Name])`.
Only where `Status = Active`.

#### Income and expenditure by property

For each building over the last twelve months: rent received, costs paid and the net income.

From Transactions, Properties. Shows Property, Money In, Money Out, Net.
Calculated: Net is `Round(Nz([Money In]) - Nz([Money Out]), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Costs by kind

What was spent in the last twelve months on each kind of cost, the biggest first. VAT paid over is left out, as it is not a cost.

From Transactions. Shows Kind, Payments, Spent.
Only where `Kind <> "VAT"` and `Money Out > 0` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Money in and out by month

Money in, money out and the net for each month of the last year.

From Transactions. Shows Month, Money In, Money Out, Net.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Net is `Round(Nz([Money In]) - Nz([Money Out]), 2)`.
Only where `Months Ago Between 0 And 12`.

#### Gross yield by property

Each building's rent for a year at market rents as a percentage of its current value, the highest first.

From Properties, Units. Shows Property, Kind, Units, Value, Annual Rent, Gross Yield %.
Calculated: Annual Rent is `Round([Market Rent] * 12, 2)`; Gross Yield % is `Round([Market Rent] * 1200 / [Current Value], 2)`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Properties, Units, Tenants, Leases, Rent Charges, Deposits, Rent Reminders, Contractors, Maintenance Requests, Inspections, Transactions. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Rent roll

The rent roll: each building's units, tenants, terms, rents and deposits, with totals for each building and for all of them. The page a lender or buyer asks for.

From the query Rent roll, a group for each Property: Unit, Tenant, Start, End, Monthly Rent, Deposit, with the total of Monthly Rent, total of Deposit.

#### Rent arrears

Each tenant in arrears on their own section, with every unpaid month and the total owed: the list to write the reminder letters from.

From the query Unpaid rent, a group for each Tenant: Address, Invoice, Period, Due Date, Days Late, Amount, Amount Paid, Owed, with the total of Owed.

#### Jobs booked

A page for each contractor listing the jobs booked with them, the day, the address and the problem, to send or hand over.

From the query Repairs booked, a group for each Contractor: Job, Booked For, Priority, Address, Problem.

#### Income and expenditure, last 12 months

Money in, money out and the net for each building over the last twelve months, with the totals: the figures for your accounts.

From the query Income and expenditure by property: Property, Money In, Money Out, Net, with the total of Money In, total of Money Out, total of Net.

#### Leases ending in the next 60 days

Leases ending in the next 60 days with the tenant's phone, the rent now and the market rent.

From the query Leases ending in the next 60 days: Property, Unit, Tenant, Phone, End, Days Left, Monthly Rent, Market Rent, with the total of Monthly Rent.

#### Vacant units and rent lost

The units standing empty, how long for and the rent lost on each.

From the query Vacant units: Property, Unit, Kind, Market Rent, Vacant Since, Days Empty, Rent Lost, with the total of Rent Lost, total of Market Rent.

#### Inspections and safety checks due

Inspections and safety checks due in the next 30 days or overdue, grouped by kind, to plan the visits.

From the query Inspections due, a group for each Kind: Due, Days Left, Unit, Notice Sent, Notes.

#### Monthly accounts

One line a month for the last year with money in, money out and the net, and the totals.

From the query Money in and out by month: Month, Money In, Money Out, Net, with the total of Money In, total of Money Out, total of Net.

#### Rent invoices raised in the last 31 days

The rent invoices raised in the last 31 days with the rent, VAT and totals: the month's invoicing at a glance.

From the query Rent invoices raised: Invoice, Invoice Date, Due Date, Tenant, Unit, Net, VAT, Amount, with the total of Net, total of VAT, total of Amount.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Rent invoice

The invoice each tenant gets two weeks before the rent day: who it is addressed to (a business by its name), the month it covers, the rent, and for a workshop in the opted building the VAT rate, the VAT and the total. Once something is paid, it lists the payments received and what is left to pay; paid in full, it says so. Numbered RENT-2026-0042. It prints the invoices raised in the last 31 days; print an older one from the Rent Charges form. One for each record of Rent Charges, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Rent invoice {Number}
- Fields: Invoice number, Date, Rent account, Rent due, You pay by, Rent paid up to
- Lines from Tenants: Invoice to, Address
- Words: Rent for {Lease.Unit.Postal Address}, {Lease.Unit.Property.City} {Lease.Unit.Property.Postcode}, for the month from {Due Date} to {Period End}, due in advance.
- Words: Payments received against this invoice:
- Lines from Transactions: Received, Method, Amount
- Totals: Rent, VAT rate %, VAT, Total for the month, Already paid, Balance to pay
- Words: {Business.Payment Terms} Bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting {Number}. If you pay by standing order, it pays this on the due date by itself and there is nothing more to do.
- Words: Paid in full: thank you. There is nothing more to pay for this month.
- Words: VAT registration {Business.Tax Number}. The landlord has opted to tax this building, so VAT is added to the rent of its shops and workshops.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Rent statement

A tenant's account on the day it is printed: every rent invoice with what was charged, what was paid and when, what is unpaid on each month, and the running balance after each, ending with the balance owing. Sent when a tenant asks, with an arrears letter, or when a tenancy ends. It prints for every tenant, past and present; choose the one you want, or print from the Tenants form. One for each record of Tenants, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Rent statement: {First Name} {Last Name}
- Totals: Statement date
- Fields: Rent account, Phone, Address, E-mail, City, Postcode, Trading as
- Lines from Rent Charges: Invoice, Month, Due, Charged, Paid, Paid on, Unpaid, Balance
- Totals: Rent charged, Rent paid, Balance owing
- Words: Please pay the balance owing to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting your rent account {Account}. If you have paid since this statement was made, thank you. If anything here looks wrong, call us on {Business.Phone} and we will look into it.
- Words: Your rent account is clear: nothing is owed. Thank you. If anything here looks wrong, call us on {Business.Phone} and we will look into it.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Tenancy agreement

The agreement for a home, filled from the lease, the tenant, the unit and the building: the parties, the property, the term, the rent and rent day, the deposit and its protection, what the rent includes, each side's duties, repairs and access, pets and smoking, ending the tenancy, and places to sign. A renewal says so, and keeps the deposit already held; the pets clause reads one way when pets are agreed and another when none are. It prints for residential leases running or about to start. It is a plainly worded starting point of our own: have it checked against the law where your homes are before you use it. One for each record of Leases, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Tenancy agreement for a home
- Fields: Tenant, Date of this agreement, The property, Tenancy begins, City, Fixed term ends, Postcode, Rent day each month, Bedrooms, Rent paid by, Rent account, Deposit protection reference
- Totals: Rent each month, Deposit
- Words: This agreement is made on {Signed On} between {Business.Name} of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} ("the Landlord") and {Tenant} ("the Tenant"). The Landlord lets the property named above ("the Property") to the Tenant as a home, on the terms below.
- Words: It renews the Tenant's earlier tenancy of the Property, which ends the day before this one begins.
- Words: 1. The property. The Property is let together with the use of any shared entrance, halls, stairs, paths, garden and bin store that serve it, and with the contents listed in the inventory. It is to be lived in by the Tenant and the members of the Tenant's household named on the application, and no one else without the Landlord's written consent.
- Words: 2. The term. The tenancy begins on {Start} and its fixed term ends on {End}. If neither side has ended it by then, it carries on from month to month on the same terms until it is ended as clause 11 says.
- Words: 3. The rent. The rent is {Monthly Rent} a month, paid in advance on day {Rent Day} of each month, the first payment on {Start}. The Tenant pays it by the method shown above into the Landlord's account, {Business.Bank Details}, quoting the rent account {Tenant.Account}. The Landlord sends a rent invoice before each rent day. The rent does not go up during the fixed term. After it, the Landlord may raise it no more than once a year, by giving at least two months' notice in writing.
- Words: 4. What the rent includes. The rent includes: {Unit.Rent Includes}. The Tenant pays for everything else used at the Property, among them council tax, gas, electricity, water and sewerage, telephone and broadband.
- Words: 5. The deposit. The Tenant pays a deposit of {Deposit} before the tenancy begins. Within 30 days of receiving it, the Landlord protects it in a government-approved tenancy deposit scheme and gives the Tenant the scheme's details; its reference is shown above once it has been given. At the end of the tenancy the deposit is returned within ten days of both sides agreeing what, if anything, is kept back for unpaid rent, damage beyond fair wear and tear, or cleaning needed to bring the Property back to its condition at the start. If they cannot agree, either of them may ask the scheme to decide.
- Words: 5. The deposit. The deposit of {Deposit} paid for the earlier tenancy is kept, and carries on as the deposit for this one, protected in the same scheme under the reference shown above. At the end of the tenancy it is returned within ten days of both sides agreeing what, if anything, is kept back for unpaid rent, damage beyond fair wear and tear, or cleaning needed to bring the Property back to its condition at the start of the first tenancy. If they cannot agree, either of them may ask the scheme to decide.
- Words: 6. The Tenant agrees: to pay the rent on time; to keep the Property clean and in good order, and to heat and air it so that damp and mould do not build up; to tell the Landlord promptly of any repair needed or damage done; to test the smoke alarms once a month; not to make alterations, redecorate or change the locks without the Landlord's written consent; not to cause a nuisance or annoyance to the neighbours; not to sublet the Property or take in a lodger without the Landlord's written consent; and to give back all the keys at the end.
- Words: 7. The Landlord agrees: to let the Tenant live in the Property in peace, without needless interruption; to keep the structure and outside in repair, including the roof, walls, windows, gutters and drains; to keep the supplies of water, gas and electricity, and the heating and hot water, in repair and working order; to have any gas appliances checked by a registered engineer every year and the wiring every five years, and to give the Tenant a copy of each certificate; to fit smoke alarms, and carbon monoxide alarms where they are needed; and to insure the building.
- Words: 8. Repairs and access. The Tenant reports repairs to the Landlord on {Business.Phone} or at {Business.E-mail}, and the Landlord arranges them in a reasonable time, the most urgent first. The Landlord, or a contractor sent by the Landlord, may come in at a reasonable time of day to inspect the Property or carry out repairs after giving the Tenant at least 24 hours' notice in writing. In an emergency, such as a gas leak, a flood or a fire, they may come in at once.
- Words: 9. Pets and smoking. No pets are agreed for this tenancy. A pet needs the Landlord's written consent first, which will not be refused without good reason. No one may smoke or vape inside the Property.
- Words: 9. Pets and smoking. Pets agreed for this tenancy: {Pets}. Any other pet needs the Landlord's written consent first, which will not be refused without good reason. No one may smoke or vape inside the Property.
- Words: 10. The inventory. An inventory and record of condition, with photographs, is made at the start of the tenancy and signed by both sides. At the end, the Property is compared with it, allowing for fair wear and tear.
- Words: 11. Ending the tenancy. The Tenant may end the tenancy at the end of the fixed term, or at any time after it, by giving at least one month's notice in writing, ending the day before a rent day. The Landlord may end it only on the grounds, and with the notice, that the law allows, and always in writing. Before the fixed term ends, the Landlord will ask the Tenant whether they would like to renew.
- Words: 12. Notices. Notices to the Landlord go to {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} or {Business.E-mail}. Notices to the Tenant go to the Property, or to {Tenant.E-mail}.
- Words: Each side keeps a signed copy of this agreement and of the inventory.
- Signed by: Signed for the Landlord, Date, Signed by the Tenant, Date

#### Commercial lease summary

A summary of the main terms of a lease of a shop or workshop: the premises, the use allowed, the term, the rent with its VAT where the building is opted to tax, the rent review where there is one, the deposit, outgoings, repairs, access and the end of the lease. It prints for commercial leases running or about to start. It goes with the full lease, which a solicitor draws up; have both checked for your own country. One for each record of Leases, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Commercial lease: summary of terms
- Fields: Tenant, Date of the lease, Signed for the tenant by, Term begins, The premises, Term ends, City, Rent day each month, Postcode, Rent account, Permitted use, Rent review
- Totals: Rent each month, VAT rate %, VAT on the rent, Each month with VAT, Rent for a year, Deposit held
- Words: This summary sets out the main terms agreed between {Business.Name} ("the Landlord") and {Tenant.Business Name} ("the Tenant") for the lease of the premises named above. It goes with the lease and does not replace it: where the two differ, the lease is what counts.
- Words: 1. The premises. The unit named above, with the right to use the shared paths, service yard and bin store in common with the other occupiers.
- Words: 2. Use. The premises may be used for the permitted use shown above and for nothing else without the Landlord's written consent, which will not be refused without good reason.
- Words: 3. Term. The lease runs from {Start} to {End}. The Tenant has no right to end it early except as the lease says.
- Words: 4. Rent. The rent is {Monthly Rent} a month, paid in advance by bank transfer on day {Rent Day} of each month, quoting the rent account. The Landlord has opted to tax the building, so VAT is added to the rent at the rate shown above.
- Words: 4. Rent. The rent is {Monthly Rent} a month, paid in advance by bank transfer on day {Rent Day} of each month, quoting the rent account. No VAT is added: the Landlord has not opted to tax the building, and will give the Tenant notice in writing before ever doing so.
- Words: The rent is reviewed on {Rent Review} to the rent the premises would then let for on the open market. It does not go down at review.
- Words: 5. Deposit. The Tenant pays the deposit shown above, three months' rent, before the term begins. The Landlord holds it until the lease ends and returns it within 28 days, less any rent or other sums then owed and the cost of any repairs the Tenant should have done.
- Words: 6. Outgoings. The Tenant pays the business rates, water, power and telephone for the premises. The Landlord insures the building; the premium is included in the rent.
- Words: 7. Repairs. The Tenant keeps the inside of the premises in good repair and decoration, together with the shop front or roller door, the doors and the glass, and the Tenant's own fittings. The Landlord keeps the roof, the structure, the outside walls and the shared parts in repair.
- Words: 7. Repairs. The Tenant keeps the inside of the premises in good repair and decoration, together with the shop front or roller door, the doors and the glass, and the Tenant's own fittings. The Landlord keeps the roof, the structure, the outside walls and the shared parts in repair. Agreed for this lease: {Notes}
- Words: 8. Access. The Landlord may come in to inspect or repair after giving at least 48 hours' notice, and at once in an emergency. The premises are inspected once a year.
- Words: 9. Alterations, signs and assignment. Alterations other than minor ones inside, and any sign outside, need the Landlord's written consent. The Tenant may not assign the lease or sublet without the Landlord's written consent, which will not be refused without good reason.
- Words: 10. The end of the lease. At the end the Tenant gives the premises back clean, in the repair the lease asks for, with the Tenant's own fittings and signs taken away if the Landlord asks. The Landlord will talk to the Tenant about a new lease at least six months before the term ends.
- Signed by: For the Landlord, Date, For the Tenant, Date

#### Deposit receipt

Given when a new tenant pays the deposit: how much, on what day, for which tenancy, and who holds it, with the words for a home's protected deposit or a shop's deposit held by the landlord. Numbered DRC-2026-0042. It prints for the deposits still held. One for each record of Deposits, on a5 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Deposit receipt {Number}
- Fields: Received from, Receipt number, For the tenancy of, Received on, Rent account, Paid by, Tenancy begins, Held by, Trading as, Returned on, Amount returned
- Totals: Deposit received
- Words: This deposit is held as security for the tenant's side of the agreement. It is not rent and is not used to pay rent while the tenancy runs. It is protected in a government-approved tenancy deposit scheme within 30 days of being received, and the scheme's details and reference are sent to the tenant. At the end it is returned, less anything owed, as the agreement says.
- Words: This deposit is held as security for the tenant's side of the lease. It is not rent and is not used to pay rent while the lease runs. The landlord holds it until the lease ends and returns it within 28 days, less any rent or other sums then owed, as the lease says.
- Words: Returned on {Returned On}. {Notes}
- Signed by: Received for the Landlord

#### Rent arrears letter

The reminder sent when rent is a week late, and each fortnight after while it is unpaid: polite, clear about the amount, the months unpaid when it was written (and anything already paid towards them) and the date to pay by, and firmer at each stage, ending with the final notice. It prints the letters still waiting for their pay-by date; print an older one from the Rent Reminders form. Have the final notice's wording checked for your own country before you rely on it. One for each record of Rent Reminders, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Fields: To, Date, Address, Our reference, City, Rent account, Postcode, Please pay by
- Heading: Rent arrears: {Stage}
- Words: Dear {Lease.Tenant},
- Words: Our records show that rent of {Amount Owed} is unpaid on your tenancy of {Lease.Unit.Postal Address}. The months unpaid are listed below; the oldest fell due on {Since}.
- Lines from Rent Charges: Invoice, Month, Due, Rent
- Totals: Rent for these months, Paid towards them, Rent unpaid
- Words: Please pay the full amount by {Pay By}, by bank transfer to {Business.Bank Details}, quoting your rent account {Lease.Tenant.Account}, or by card by calling us on {Business.Phone}.
- Words: {Next Step}
- Words: If you have paid in the last few days, thank you, and please ignore this letter. If you cannot pay it all by that date, please call us before then: we would much rather agree a plan with you to clear it in steps than take things further. Free and confidential advice on money and debt is available from advice services near you.
- Words: Yours sincerely,
- Words: Rent accounts, {Business.Name}

#### Notice of inspection

The letter that tells a tenant, at least a week ahead, the day and time of a routine inspection or safety check, what happens at that kind of visit and how to change the day. It prints for the visits of the next three weeks to a unit with a tenant, dated the day the notice went, or today for one not sent yet. One for each record of Inspections, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Totals: Date
- Fields: To, Visit for, Address, Day of the visit, City, Time, Postcode
- Heading: Notice of a visit to {Unit.Postal Address}
- Words: Dear {Lease.Tenant},
- Words: We are writing to let you know that we will visit {Unit.Postal Address} on {Due}, {Visit Time}. The visit is for: {Kind}.
- Words: A routine inspection takes about half an hour. We look at the general condition of the property, test the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, look for any damp, leaks or damage, and note anything that needs mending so that we can arrange it.
- Words: The gas safety check is made by a registered gas engineer from our contractor and takes about an hour. The engineer checks the boiler, the cooker, any gas fire and the flues, so please make sure they and the gas meter are easy to reach. You will be given a copy of the certificate.
- Words: The electrical safety check is made by a qualified electrician from our contractor and takes two to three hours. The electrician tests the wiring, the sockets and the fuse board, and the power is off for short spells, so please save any work on a computer, and expect to reset clocks afterwards. You will be given a copy of the report.
- Words: You do not need to be in, though you are welcome to be, and it is a good time to tell us about anything that needs attention. If you are out, we will let ourselves in with our key, lock up when we leave, and leave a card to say that we have been.
- Words: If the day or time does not suit you, please call us on {Business.Phone} or write to {Business.E-mail}, and we will find another time in the next two weeks. This letter gives you at least 24 hours' notice in writing, as your agreement asks.
- Words: Yours sincerely,
- Words: Property management, {Business.Name}

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name, address, VAT number and bank details, which every invoice, statement and letter prints. Then enter Properties, then the Units in each one (with the Postal Address and what the rent includes), then Contractors. Enter each Tenant with their rent account, their Lease, and the Deposit taken, and for every unit the next inspection and safety checks due. Two weeks before each rent day, add a Rent Charge for each running lease; when rent comes in, enter it in Transactions pointing at the charge, and add it to the charge's Amount Paid. Enter repairs in Maintenance Requests as they are reported, reminder letters in Rent Reminders as you send them, and every bill you pay in Transactions with its building.

### Making it yours

- Manage for owners: add an Owners table with their management fee, point Properties at it, and add a query that takes your fee off each owner's rent to show what you pay them.
- Let holiday homes: use a weekly Rent Charge in place of a monthly one, rename Leases to Bookings with arrival and departure dates, and add a cleaning cost to each booking.
- Let rooms in shared houses: make each room a unit, and add a field to Units for the shared bathroom and kitchen it uses.
- Let storage units or garages: drop Bedrooms and Has Gas from Units, add a Size field, and keep the rest as it is.
- Keep the energy rating: add an Energy Rating and an Energy Certificate Expires field to Units, and a query for certificates running out.
- List rent reviews coming up: add a query on Leases with a calculated Days to Review column, DateDiff("d", Date(), [Rent Review]), and the criteria Between 0 And 90.
- Recharge damage to tenants: add a Recharge field to Maintenance Requests, and take it from the deposit when the lease ends.
- Charge a service charge on the shops: add a Service Charge line to Rent Charges as a second amount, and print it on the Rent invoice as its own total row.

### Questions people ask

**How do I print one tenant's rent invoice?**

Open the Rent Charges form, find the invoice by its Number, and print the template Rent invoice from there. Or open Print templates, choose Rent invoice, pick the invoice from the list and press Print.

**How do I see who owes rent?**

Open the query Rent arrears by tenant for a line a tenant with what they owe and how late the oldest month is, or the report Arrears letters for every unpaid month. The query Unpaid rent lists each unpaid invoice.

**Why do the workshop invoices have VAT and the others not?**

Rent on a home never carries VAT. A commercial landlord adds VAT only after opting to tax the building, and here only Riverside Yard is opted (its VAT on Rent is ticked), so its leases have a Tax Rate of 0.2 and its invoices add VAT. The VAT collected is paid over each quarter and shows in Transactions as VAT.

**How do I renew a tenancy?**

Open the Leases form, press New, and enter the same Unit and Tenant with the new Start, End and rent, tick Renewal and copy the Deposit and Deposit Ref from the old lease. Set the old lease's Status to Ended on its last day. Print a new Tenancy agreement for the new lease.

**What happens to the deposit at the end?**

Agree any deductions with the tenant against the inventory, then return the rest. Open the Deposits form, find the deposit and type Returned On, Amount Returned and, in Notes, what was kept back and why.

**How do I print older documents?**

Open the record's own form and print from there: a record asked for by its form prints whether or not the template would list it. An old rent invoice prints from the Rent Charges form, an old arrears letter from the Rent Reminders form, an ended lease's agreement from the Leases form.

**Can I use this for flats I manage for other owners?**

Yes, with an Owners table: see the first idea under adapting it. The Properties, Units, Leases and rent invoices stay as they are.

## Fernleigh Estates

**Estate and letting agent.** Sellers and landlords, properties, applicants, viewings, offers, sales to completion, managed lets, rent and landlord statements for an estate agent.

Fernleigh Estates is an invented estate and letting agency in Bristol with seven staff: a director who values homes, two sales negotiators, a sales progressor, a lettings negotiator, a property manager and an administrator. It sells homes for their owners across eight parts of the city, and lets homes for about sixteen landlords, managing most of them: it collects the rent and arranges repairs, and each month pays the landlord what is left after its fees.

The sample holds eighteen months of trading. Homes come on the market at a price the owner chooses, some sensibly and some too high; applicants register to buy or rent with an area, a number of bedrooms and a budget, and view the homes that suit them. Offers come in, most a little under the asking price; the owner accepts or turns each down, and an accepted sale moves through solicitors, searches and survey, the buyer's mortgage and exchange of contracts to completion, when the agency invoices its commission. About one sale in ten falls through and the home goes back on the market, and a few homes that will not sell are reduced or taken off.

On the lettings side each home has its run of tenancies: renewals, tenants who leave, and the weeks a home is marketed and viewed before the next tenant moves in. For a managed home the rent comes to the agency, most of it on the day and some late, and on the third working day of each month every landlord gets a statement of the rent collected, the management fee and VAT taken, any letting fee and repairs, and the sum paid to them. The agency's own invoices, for commission on sales, letting fees and monthly management fees, all carry VAT at twenty percent.

It suits, with small changes: An estate agent that only sells homes; A letting agent that only lets and manages; A commercial property agent, with units in place of homes; A holiday let agency, with bookings in place of tenancies; An auction house selling property lots; A relocation or property finding service.

### Things you should know

- Everything in a sample's records is invented: the business, the people, their addresses, e-mail addresses on example domains that reach nobody, and phone numbers from the ranges kept for drama and fiction. Tax, company and bank numbers are placeholders of zeros.
- The dates count back from the day the file was made, and some run on into the weeks after it, as real bookings and due dates do. Made from the Data Files start screen, a sample is dated from that day. Queries that compare with today (overdue, due this week) show more as a downloaded file gets older.
- To start empty, choose the same business on the start screen and then Empty: the same tables, queries, forms, reports and print templates, with nothing in them but the Start Here guide.
- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Clients and applicants are kept apart: clients are the sellers and landlords the agency acts for, applicants are the buyers and tenants it finds for them. A tenant is an applicant whose Status is Rented, and a buyer one whose Status is Bought.
- A property's Price means two things: the asking price when its Purpose is Sale, and the monthly rent asked when it is Let. The queries that compare it with an applicant's Budget compare like with like, because a buyer's budget is a price and a tenant's is a monthly rent.
- Applicants are matched to homes through their Area: the query Applicants matching a property joins the two by it. An applicant happy to look in two areas needs a second record, or a second area field and a second query.
- Rent the agency collects is the landlord's money, not the agency's. It shows on the landlord statements, while the agency's own income is only its invoices, which is what Commission earned by month adds up.
- A landlord statement's Paid Out is the rent collected less everything deducted. When the repairs of a month cost more than the rent left after fees, they are carried to the next month's statement, so a statement never asks a landlord for money.
- Statuses on properties, applicants, sales and tenancies are as they stood on the day the sample was made. Change them by hand as things move on; the queries read them.
- Each print template prints only the records it is for: this month's landlord statements, the tenancies running or about to start, the viewings still to come, the sales going through and the invoices of the last 31 days. A record printed from its own form always prints, whatever the template would choose.
- Commission on sales is taken from the sale money by the seller's solicitor on completion, so most sale invoices are paid within a few days. Letting and management fees for managed homes are taken from the rent, so they are paid the day the statement is made.

### Tutorial

#### Take on a home to sell

1. Open the Clients form and press New. Give the next account in Account (CL- and the next number), the owner's name, address, phone and e-mail, set Kind to Seller and type today in Client Since.
2. Open the Properties form and press New. Give the next reference (FE- and the next number), choose the Client and the Area, type the Address and Postcode, set Purpose to Sale, and type Kind, Bedrooms, Bathrooms, Price (the asking price), Energy Rating and the agreed commission in Fee Rate (0.012 for 1.2 percent). Set Listed On to today and Status to For sale.
3. Open the query Applicants matching a property to see who is looking for a home like it, and call them.

#### Register an applicant and book a viewing

1. Open the Applicants form and press New. Type their name, phone, e-mail and address, set Looking To to Buy or Rent, choose the Area, and type Min Bedrooms, Budget and Position. Type today in Registered On and leave Status as Active.
2. Open the Viewings form and press New. Choose the Property and the Applicant, choose who will show them round in Accompanied By, and type Booked On (today), Viewing Date and Viewing Time. Leave Status as Booked.
3. Open the print template Viewing confirmation from Print templates, choose the viewing and press Print or Save as PDF, and send it. Type today in Confirmation Sent.
4. Each morning, open the report Viewing diary for the week ahead. After each viewing, set Status to Done, Cancelled or No-show and type the applicant's Feedback for the owner.

#### Put an offer to the owner and agree a sale

1. When an applicant offers, open the Offers form and press New. Choose the Property and the Applicant, type Made On, Amount and Conditions, and leave Status as Awaiting decision.
2. Open the report Offers to decide, call each owner, and when they answer set Status to Accepted or Rejected and type Decided On. Turn down any other offers waiting on a home whose owner has accepted one.
3. For an accepted offer, open the Sales form and press New. Give the next number (SALE-, the year and the next number), choose the Property, the Offer and the Buyer, the Negotiator and both solicitors, and type Price, Accepted On, Target Completion, what is Included and the Fee Rate from the property. Set the property's Status to Under offer and the buyer's Status to Bought.
4. Open the print template Memorandum of sale, choose the sale and press Print, and send it to the seller, the buyer and both solicitors. Type today in Memorandum Sent.

#### Move a sale on to completion

1. Each week, open the report Sales progress. Call both solicitors about each sale and type the date each step was reached: Solicitors Instructed, Searches Back, Mortgage Offered, Exchanged On.
2. Change Stage as each step is reached, so the queries Sales in progress and Sales by stage show where things are.
3. On completion, type Completed On, set Stage to Completed and type the Fee (the price times the fee rate). Set the property's Status to Sold.
4. Open the Agency Invoices form and press New: give the next number, choose the seller in Client and the Sale, type Invoice Date and Due Date, and add an Invoice Lines record with Kind Sale commission, the Property and the Net fee. Type Net, Tax and Amount on the invoice, then print the Commission invoice and send it to the seller's solicitor.
5. If a sale falls through, set Stage to Fell through, say why in Notes, and set the property back to For sale.

#### Let a home and start the tenancy

1. Enter the landlord in Clients with Kind set to Landlord, and the home in Properties with Purpose set to Let, the monthly rent in Price and Status set to To let.
2. Book viewings for rent applicants as for a sale. When the landlord chooses a tenant, set the property's Status to Let agreed and the applicant's Status to Rented.
3. Open the Tenancies form and press New. Give the next reference, choose the Property and the Tenant, and type Signed On, Start, End, Monthly Rent, Rent Day, Deposit, the Service, the Management Fee and the Letting Fee. Type in Rent Paid To and Repairs To who the tenant pays and calls, as the agreement should say them.
4. Open the print template Tenancy agreement, choose the tenancy, print two copies and have them signed. When the deposit is protected, type the scheme's reference in Deposit Ref.
5. Raise the letting fee as an Agency Invoice with one line of Kind Letting fee. For a managed let it is taken from the first month's rent on the landlord's statement.

#### Collect the rent and arrange repairs

1. At the start of each month, open the Rent Charges form and press New for each tenancy whose rent you collect: choose the Tenancy and type Period, Due Date and Amount.
2. When rent reaches the client account, find the month's charge and type Received and Received On. Open the report Rent arrears each week to chase anything late.
3. When a tenant reports a problem at a managed home, open the Repairs form and press New: choose the Property and Tenancy, type Reported, Problem and Priority, choose a Contractor and type the Quote. For work over 250, set Status to Awaiting approval and ask the landlord first; then type Approved On and set Status to Booked with the Booked For day.
4. When it is done, type Done On and Cost and set Status to Done. Open the query Open repairs each morning to see what is still waiting.

#### Pay the landlords at the month end

1. On the third working day of the month, open the query Rent collected and owed to landlords, or the report Rent for landlords, to see each landlord's rent, fees and what they are owed.
2. For each landlord, open the Landlord Statements form and press New: give the next number (STM-, the year and the next number), choose the Client, type Period and Statement Date. Add Statement Lines: a Rent received line for each rent that came in, a Management fee line for each home, a VAT on fees line, and a Repair line for each finished repair.
3. Type Rent Collected, Deductions and Paid Out (the first less the second) on the statement, pay the landlord, and type Paid On. Type the statement in the Statement field of each rent charge and repair it covers.
4. Raise the month's management fees as an Agency Invoice for each landlord, with a line for each home. Print the Landlord statement and the Commission invoice together and send them.
5. Open the report Commission by month to see what the agency earned, and the query Paid to landlords by month for the year so far.

### Tables

#### Start Here

The guide to this database: the everyday tasks a step at a time, each step saying which table, form, query, report or print template to open. Open its report, Start Here, to read or print it. Delete the table when you no longer need it; nothing else uses it. The sample has 34 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |

### Queries

#### Viewings in the next 7 days

Every viewing booked for the coming week, by day and time, with the applicant's phone and who is going.

From Viewings, Properties, Applicants, Staff. Shows Viewing Date, Viewing Time, Reference, Property, Purpose, Applicant, Phone, Accompanied By, Confirmation Sent.
Calculated: Applicant is `[Applicants].[First Name] & " " & [Applicants].[Last Name]`; Accompanied By is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Until Between 0 And 7` and `Status = Booked`.

#### Offers awaiting a decision

Offers the owner has not yet answered, oldest first, with the asking price, the offer as a percentage of it, how the buyer is buying, and the seller's phone.

From Offers, Properties, Applicants, Clients. Shows Made On, Property, Asking Price, Offer, % of Asking, Buyer, Position, Conditions, Seller, Seller Phone, Days Waiting.
Calculated: % of Asking is `Round([Amount] * 100 / [Properties].[Price], 1)`; Buyer is `[Applicants].[First Name] & " " & [Applicants].[Last Name]`; Seller is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Made On], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Awaiting decision`.

#### Sales in progress

Every agreed sale not yet completed, in the order of its stage, with how long since the offer was accepted, the completion hoped for and the fee to come.

From Sales, Properties, Applicants, Clients, Staff. Shows Stage, Sale, Property, Price, Accepted On, Days Since Offer, Target Completion, Buyer, Seller, Negotiator, Fee Due.
Calculated: Days Since Offer is `DateDiff("d", [Accepted On], Date())`; Buyer is `[Applicants].[First Name] & " " & [Applicants].[Last Name]`; Seller is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Negotiator is `[Staff].[First Name] & " " & [Staff].[Last Name]`; Fee Due is `Round([Sales].[Price] * [Sales].[Fee Rate], 2)`.
Only where `Stage Not In ("Completed", "Fell through")`.

#### Sales by stage

How many sales are at each stage, their value and the fees they will bring.

From Sales, Properties. Shows Stage, Sales, Value, Fees to Come.
Calculated: Fees to Come is `Round([Sales].[Price] * [Sales].[Fee Rate], 2)`.
Only where `Stage Not In ("Completed", "Fell through")`.

#### On the market over 60 days

Homes for sale or to let that have been on the market more than 60 days, the longest first, to talk to the owner about the price.

From Properties, Areas, Clients. Shows Reference, Address, Area, Purpose, Price, Listed On, Days on Market, Client, Phone.
Calculated: Days on Market is `DateDiff("d", [Listed On], Date())`; Client is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days on Market > 60` and `Status In ("For sale", "To let")`.

#### Rent collected and owed to landlords

For each landlord, the rent due in the last 30 days, what was collected and what is outstanding, the fees and VAT on it, and what is owed to the landlord before any repairs.

From Rent Charges, Tenancies, Properties, Clients. Shows Landlord, Account, Rents Due, Rent Due, Collected, Outstanding, Fees and VAT, Owed to Landlord.
Calculated: Landlord is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Collected is `Nz([Received])`; Outstanding is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Received]), 2)`; Fees and VAT is `Round(Nz([Received]) * [Management Fee], 2) + Round(Round(Nz([Received]) * [Management Fee], 2) * 0.2, 2)`; Owed to Landlord is `Round(Nz([Received]) - (Round(Nz([Received]) * [Management Fee], 2) + Round(Round(Nz([Received]) * [Management Fee], 2) * 0.2, 2)), 2)`.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 30`.

#### Commission earned by month

The agency's fees before VAT each month: sales commission, letting fees and management fees.

From Invoice Lines, Agency Invoices. Shows Month, Sales, Letting Fees, Management Fees, Total.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Invoice Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Sales is `IIf([Kind] = "Sale commission", [Invoice Lines].[Net], 0)`; Letting Fees is `IIf([Kind] = "Letting fee", [Invoice Lines].[Net], 0)`; Management Fees is `IIf([Kind] = "Management fee", [Invoice Lines].[Net], 0)`.

#### Applicants matching a property

For each home on the market, the active applicants in its area who want to buy or rent (whichever it is for), can afford it and want no more bedrooms than it has. Call them first.

From Properties, Areas, Applicants. Shows Reference, Property, Area, Purpose, Bedrooms, Price, Applicant, Phone, Budget, Min Bedrooms, Position.
Calculated: Applicant is `[Applicants].[First Name] & " " & [Applicants].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Status In ("For sale", "To let")` and `Status = Active` and `Same Purpose = Yes` and `Within Budget = Yes` and `Enough Bedrooms = Yes`.

#### Rent arrears

Rent on managed tenancies more than three days late and not fully paid, by tenant, with the landlord.

From Rent Charges, Tenancies, Properties, Applicants, Clients. Shows Tenant, Property, Landlord, Period, Due Date, Amount, Received, Owed, Days Late.
Calculated: Tenant is `[Applicants].[First Name] & " " & [Applicants].[Last Name]`; Landlord is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`; Owed is `Round([Amount] - Nz([Received]), 2)`; Days Late is `DateDiff("d", [Due Date], Date())`.
Only where `Owed > 0` and `Days Late > 3`.

#### Tenancies ending in the next 60 days

Tenancies whose fixed term ends within two months, to ask the landlord and tenant about renewing.

From Tenancies, Properties, Applicants, Clients. Shows End, Days Left, Property, Tenant, Landlord, Monthly Rent, Service.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [End])`; Tenant is `[Applicants].[First Name] & " " & [Applicants].[Last Name]`; Landlord is `[Clients].[First Name] & " " & [Clients].[Last Name]`.
Only where `Days Left Between 0 And 60` and `Status = Active`.

#### Open repairs

Repairs at managed homes not yet done or cancelled, oldest first, with the quote and the day the contractor is booked for.

From Repairs, Properties. Shows Reported, Property, Problem, Priority, Status, Quote, Booked For, Days Open.
Calculated: Days Open is `DateDiff("d", [Reported], Date())`.
Only where `Status Not In ("Done", "Cancelled")`.

#### Paid to landlords by month

Rent collected, deducted and paid to landlords each month over the last year, from the statements.

From Landlord Statements. Shows Month, Statements, Rent Collected, Deducted, Paid to Landlords.
Only where `Days Ago Between 0 And 366`.

#### Asking prices by area

For each area, the homes on the market for sale and to let, with the lowest, average and highest price asked.

From Properties, Areas. Shows Area, Purpose, On the Market, Lowest, Average, Highest.
Calculated: Average is `Round([Price], 0)`.
Only where `Status In ("For sale", "To let", "Under offer", "Let agreed")`.

### Print templates

#### Landlord statement

Sent to each landlord on the third working day of the month: every rent received for them, the management fee and VAT, any letting fee and repairs, each sum on its own side as received or deducted, and the sum paid into their account (or, in a month when repairs took it all, why nothing was paid). Numbered STM-2026-0042. It prints this month's statements, and in the first week of a month last month's too; print an older one from the Landlord Statements form. One for each record of Landlord Statements, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Landlord statement {Number}
- Totals: For the month
- Fields: Landlord, Statement, Address, Date, City, Your account, Postcode
- Lines from Statement Lines: Date, Property, Description, Received, Deducted
- Totals: Rent collected, Fees, VAT and repairs, Paid to you
- Words: We paid {Paid Out} into your account by bank transfer on {Paid On}.
- Words: Nothing was paid to you this month: the repairs came to more than the rent left after our fees, and what was left of them is carried to next month's statement. A statement never asks you for money.
- Words: Our fees are shown with VAT; our VAT invoices for them come with this statement. Repairs are charged at what the contractor billed, with nothing added.
- Words: Rent we collect for you is held in our client account, kept apart from our own money, until it is paid to you. Questions about this statement: call {Business.Phone} or write to {Business.E-mail}.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Tenancy agreement

The agreement for a home the agency lets, filled from the tenancy, the tenant, the home and its landlord. The agency signs it for the landlord and says that it acts for the landlord. A renewal says so and keeps the deposit already held; the pets clause reads one way when pets are agreed and another when none are. It prints for tenancies running or about to start. It is a plainly worded starting point of our own: have it checked against the law where your homes are before you use it. One for each record of Tenancies, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Tenancy agreement {Reference}
- Fields: Landlord, Date of this agreement, Tenant, Tenancy begins, The property, Fixed term ends, City, Rent day each month, Postcode, Bedrooms, Our service to the landlord, Deposit protection reference
- Totals: Rent each month, Deposit
- Words: This agreement is made on {Signed On} between {Property.Client} of {Property.Client.Address}, {Property.Client.City} {Property.Client.Postcode} ("the Landlord") and {Tenant} ("the Tenant"). {Business.Name} of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} ("the Agent") signs it for the Landlord and acts for the Landlord, not for the Tenant. The Landlord lets the property named above ("the Property") to the Tenant as a home, on the terms below.
- Words: It renews the Tenant's earlier tenancy of the Property, which ends the day before this one begins.
- Words: 1. The property. The Property is let together with the use of any shared entrance, paths, garden and bin store that serve it, and with the contents listed in the inventory. It is to be lived in by the Tenant and the members of the Tenant's household named on the application.
- Words: 2. The term. The tenancy begins on {Start} and its fixed term ends on {End}. If neither side has ended it by then, it carries on from month to month on the same terms until it is ended as clause 11 says.
- Words: 3. The rent. The rent is {Monthly Rent} a month, paid in advance on day {Rent Day} of each month, the first payment before the tenancy begins. It is paid to {Rent Paid To}, by standing order, quoting the reference {Reference}. The rent does not go up during the fixed term; after it, it may be raised no more than once a year, by at least two months' notice in writing.
- Words: 4. Bills. The Tenant pays council tax, gas, electricity, water and sewerage, telephone and broadband for the Property from the start of the tenancy, and tells the suppliers of the meter readings on the day of moving in.
- Words: 5. The deposit. The Tenant pays a deposit of {Deposit} before the tenancy begins. Within 30 days of receiving it, the Agent protects it for the Landlord in a government-approved tenancy deposit scheme and gives the Tenant the scheme's details; its reference is shown above once given. At the end, the deposit is returned within ten days of both sides agreeing what, if anything, is kept back for unpaid rent, damage beyond fair wear and tear, or cleaning; if they cannot agree, either may ask the scheme to decide.
- Words: 5. The deposit. The deposit of {Deposit} paid for the earlier tenancy is kept, and carries on as the deposit for this one, protected in the same scheme under the reference shown above. At the end, it is returned within ten days of both sides agreeing what, if anything, is kept back for unpaid rent, damage beyond fair wear and tear, or cleaning; if they cannot agree, either may ask the scheme to decide.
- Words: 6. The Tenant agrees: to pay the rent on time; to keep the Property clean and in good order, and to heat and air it so that damp and mould do not build up; to report any repair needed promptly; to test the smoke alarms once a month; not to make alterations, redecorate or change the locks without consent in writing; not to cause a nuisance to the neighbours; not to sublet or take in a lodger without consent in writing; and to give back all the keys at the end.
- Words: 7. The Landlord agrees: to let the Tenant live in the Property in peace; to keep the structure and outside in repair, and the supplies of water, gas and electricity, the heating and the hot water in repair and working order; to have any gas appliances checked every year and the wiring every five years, and give the Tenant copies of the certificates; to fit smoke alarms, and carbon monoxide alarms where needed; and to insure the building.
- Words: 8. Repairs and access. The Tenant reports repairs to {Repairs To}. The Landlord or the Agent, or a contractor sent by either, may come in at a reasonable time of day to inspect the Property or carry out repairs after giving at least 24 hours' notice in writing, and at once in an emergency such as a gas leak, a flood or a fire.
- Words: 9. Pets and smoking. No pets are agreed for this tenancy. A pet needs consent in writing first, which will not be refused without good reason. No one may smoke or vape inside the Property.
- Words: 9. Pets and smoking. Pets agreed for this tenancy: {Pets}. Any other pet needs consent in writing first, which will not be refused without good reason. No one may smoke or vape inside the Property.
- Words: 10. The inventory. An inventory and record of condition, with photographs, is made at the start and signed by both sides. At the end, the Property is compared with it, allowing for fair wear and tear.
- Words: 11. Ending the tenancy. The Tenant may end the tenancy at the end of the fixed term, or at any time after it, by giving at least one month's notice in writing ending the day before a rent day. The Landlord may end it only on the grounds, and with the notice, that the law allows, and always in writing.
- Words: 12. Notices. Notices to the Landlord may be sent to the Agent at {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} or {Business.E-mail}, and count as given to the Landlord. Notices to the Tenant go to the Property, or to {Tenant.E-mail}.

The agency's VAT invoice to a client: commission on a completed sale, the letting fee for a new tenancy, or a month's management fees, each line with its VAT. One for each record of Agency Invoices, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.
