| Number | Short text, unique | The absence's number, given in date order and once only: LV-2026-0042, a new run each year. |
| Employee | Points at Employees, required | Who is away. |
| Kind | Short text | Holiday, Sickness, Appointment, Compassionate leave or Unpaid leave. |
| Allowance | Points at Holiday Allowances | For holiday, the person's Holiday Allowances record for the year it comes out of. Empty for other kinds. |
| Starts | Date | The first day away. |
| Ends | Date | The last day away (for sickness still going on, the day they expect to be back at work, less one). |
| Days | Number | The working days it covers, on the person's own working days. A half day is 0.5. |
| Reason | Short text | A few plain words, kept general: "Cold or flu", "Family matter". Medical details do not belong here. |
| Status | Short text | Requested (waiting for a decision), Approved, Declined, or Recorded for sickness and compassionate leave. |
| Requested On | Date | The day it was asked for, or the day sickness was reported. |
| Decided By | Points at Employees | The manager who approved or declined it, or recorded it. |
| Decided On | Date | The day it was decided or recorded. |
| Paid | Yes/No | Ticked when the days are paid: holiday, sickness, appointments and compassionate leave in the sample. Unpaid leave is not. |
| Notes | Short text | Anything else, such as a handover arranged. |

#### Pay Years

The years pay is added up in, for the year-to-date figures and the annual pay summary. A payslip belongs to the pay year its pay date falls in. The sample uses the calendar year; set your own dates where your tax year differs. The sample has 2 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required, unique | The year's name: 2026. |
| Starts | Date | The first day of the pay year. |
| Ends | Date | The last day of the pay year. |
| Notes | Short text | Anything worth knowing about the year. |

#### Pay Runs

Each time pay is worked out and paid: once a month in the sample, with a payslip for each person. A salary is paid for the run's own month; hours are paid a month behind, for the weeks that ended in the month before. The sample has 22 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The run's number: PAY-2026-M10 for October 2026. A weekly run would be PAY-2026-W14. |
| Pay Year | Points at Pay Years, required | The pay year its pay date falls in. |
| Frequency | Short text | Monthly, or Weekly for a weekly run. |
| Period | Short text | The period in words: October 2026. |
| Period Starts | Date | The first day of the month the salaries cover. |
| Period Ends | Date | The last day of that month. |
| Pay Date | Date | The day the money reaches people's accounts: the last working day of the month. |
| Status | Short text | Open while it is being prepared, Paid once the money has gone. |
| Notes | Short text | Anything worth knowing about the run. |

#### Timesheets

One for each person paid by the hour, for each week they worked, with a line for each day. The person hands it in when their week is done and their manager approves it, in time for the month's pay run. The sample has 1,527 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The timesheet's number, given in date order: TS-2026-0042, a new run each year. |
| Employee | Points at Employees, required | Whose hours they are. |
| Week Commencing | Date | The Monday the week starts on. |
| Contract Hours | Number | Their contract hours for that week, kept here so a later change of hours does not alter it. |
| Total Hours | Number | All the hours worked in the week: the lines added up. |
| Overtime Hours | Number | The hours worked above the contract hours for the week. |
| Status | Short text | Submitted (waiting for the manager) or Approved. |
| Submitted On | Date | The day the person handed it in. |
| Approved By | Points at Employees | The manager who approved it. |
| Approved On | Date | The day it was approved. |
| Pay Run | Points at Pay Runs | The pay run it was paid in: the run at the end of the month after the week ended. Empty until then. |
| Notes | Short text | Anything said about the week. |

#### Timesheet Lines

One line for each day worked in a week. The sample has 5,588 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Timesheet | Points at Timesheets, required | The timesheet the day belongs to. |
| Date | Date | The day worked. |
| Day | Short text | The day of the week, as it reads on the printed timesheet. |
| Start | Short text | The time they started, on the 24-hour clock: 08:30. |
| End | Short text | The time they finished: 17:00. |
| Break Minutes | Whole number | The unpaid break taken, in minutes. |
| Hours | Number | The hours worked that day: finish less start less the break. |
| Overtime | Number | The part of the day's hours that took the week above the contract hours. |
| Note | Short text | Why a day was different: stayed late, an extra shift, a half day off. |

#### Deduction Rates

The rates the business uses to work out what is taken from pay, and what it pays on top as the employer. You fill these in yourself. The tax, social insurance and pension rates in this sample are invented examples, named "(example rate)". They are not the rules of any country. Before paying anyone, replace them in Deduction Rates with your own country's current rules or your payroll provider's figures. The sample has 7 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The deduction as it is printed on the payslip. |
| Paid By | Short text | Employee (taken from pay and shown on the payslip) or Employer (paid by the business on top of pay). |
| Percent | Number | The rate as a percentage of pay above the threshold: 18 is eighteen percent. Empty for a fixed amount. |
| Fixed Amount | Currency | A set amount a year, shared equally across the pay periods: 52 a year is 1.00 a week or 4.33 a month. Empty for a percentage. |
| Threshold | Currency | The yearly pay below which nothing is taken, shared across the pay periods the same way. Empty or 0 for none. |
| Applies From | Date | The first pay date the rate is used for. |
| Applies To | Date | The last pay date it is used for; empty while it is still in force. When a rate changes, end the old record and add a new one. |
| Print Order | Whole number | Where the deduction comes on the payslip, lowest first. |
| Notes | Short text | Where the figure comes from; in the sample, that it is an invented example. |

#### Payslips

One for each person in each pay run, with its lines. The money figures are stored as they were paid, so a later change of rate never alters an old payslip. The sample has 511 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Number | Short text, unique | The payslip's number, given in pay date order: PS-2026-0042, a new run each pay year. |
| Pay Run | Points at Pay Runs, required | The pay run it belongs to. |
| Employee | Points at Employees, required | Who is paid. |
| Pay Date | Date | The day the pay goes into their bank, the same as the pay run's: the payslip prints it, and the Payslip template finds the latest run's payslips by it. |
| Tax Code | Short text | The tax code used for this payslip, from the person's record. Left empty in the sample. |
| Hours From | Date | For someone paid by the hour, the Monday of the first week paid. |
| Hours To | Date | For someone paid by the hour, the Sunday of the last week paid. |
| Hours Paid | Number | The hours paid, for someone paid by the hour: worked, overtime and paid absence. |
| Gross | Currency | All the pay before deductions: the payment lines added up. |
| Deductions | Currency | Everything taken from pay: the deduction lines added up. |
| Net | Currency | What reaches the person's bank account: gross less deductions. |
| Employer Costs | Currency | What the business pays on top of gross pay, from the employer rates. |
| Gross to Date | Currency | Gross pay in the pay year so far, this payslip included. |
| Deductions to Date | Currency | Deductions in the pay year so far. |
| Net to Date | Currency | Net pay in the pay year so far. |

#### Payslip Lines

The lines of each payslip: the payments first (basic pay, overtime, holiday pay, sick pay), then each deduction. The sample has 2,540 records.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|

| Kind | Short text | Payment or Deduction. |
| Item | Short text | What the line is, as printed: Basic pay, Overtime, Holiday pay, or for a deduction the name of the Deduction Rates record it was worked out from. |
| Hours | Number | For hourly pay, the hours paid on the line. |
| Rate | Currency | For hourly pay, the rate per hour on the line; overtime is at one and a half times. |

| Year to Date | Currency | The same item added up over the pay year so far, this payslip included. |

### Queries

#### Who is off, next 7 days

Everyone away today or in the next seven days, for holiday, sickness or other leave, with Off Today marked Yes for those away now. Requests not yet approved are left out. Use it each morning to plan cover.

From Absences, Employees, Departments. Shows Employee, Department, Kind, Starts, Ends, Days, Off Today.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Off Today is `IIf(DateDiff("d", [Starts], Date()) >= 0 And DateDiff("d", Date(), [Ends]) >= 0, "Yes", "No")`.
Only where `Starts In <= 7` and `Ends In >= 0` and `Status In ("Approved", "Recorded")`.

#### Leave requests to decide

Holiday and other leave asked for but not yet approved or declined, by the first day off, with how many days each has waited.

From Absences, Employees, Departments. Shows Number, Employee, Department, Kind, Starts, Ends, Days, Requested On, Days Waiting.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Requested On], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Requested`.

#### Holidays left

This holiday year's allowance for each person still working for you: the allowance, days carried over, days booked and the days left, by department.

From Holiday Allowances, Employees, Departments. Shows Department, Employee, Holiday Year, Allowance, Carried Over, Days Booked, Days Left.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Left is `[Allowance] + Nz([Carried Over]) - Nz([Days Booked])`.
Only where `Days Into Year >= 0` and `Days Left in Year >= 0` and `Leave Date Is Null`.

#### Holiday taken and to come

Approved holiday this year from the absences themselves: the days already taken and the days still to come for each person, beside Days Booked on their allowance, which they should add up to. Someone with no holiday approved this year is not listed.

From Absences, Holiday Allowances, Employees. Shows Employee, Holiday Year, Days Booked, Days Taken, Days To Come.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Taken is `IIf(DateDiff("d", [Starts], Date()) > 0, [Days], 0)`; Days To Come is `IIf(DateDiff("d", [Starts], Date()) > 0, 0, [Days])`.
Only where `Status = Approved` and `Days Into Year >= 0` and `Days Left in Year >= 0`.

#### Timesheets to approve

Timesheets submitted and not yet approved, the oldest week first, with the days each has waited. Clear it each week, and before the month's pay run.

From Timesheets, Employees, Departments. Shows Number, Employee, Department, Week Commencing, Total Hours, Overtime Hours, Submitted On, Days Waiting.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Days Waiting is `DateDiff("d", [Submitted On], Date())`.
Only where `Status = Submitted`.

#### Overtime by department, last month

The shifts, hours and overtime hours worked in each department last calendar month, from the timesheet lines.

From Timesheet Lines, Timesheets, Employees, Departments. Shows Month, Department, Shifts, Hours Worked, Overtime Hours.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`.
Only where `Months Ago = 1`.

#### Hours and overtime by month

Hours and overtime worked by hourly staff each month, which shows the busy seasons.

From Timesheet Lines. Shows Month, Shifts, Hours Worked, Overtime Hours.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Date], "yyyy-mm")`.

#### Payroll cost by department

For each month and department: how many payslips, gross pay, the employer costs on top, the total cost to the business and the net paid. The department is the one each person is in now.

From Payslips, Pay Runs, Employees, Departments. Shows Month, Department, Payslips, Gross, Employer Costs, Total Cost, Net.
Calculated: Month is `Format([Pay Runs].[Pay Date], "yyyy-mm")`; Total Cost is `Round([Gross] + [Employer Costs], 2)`.

#### Pay run totals

Each pay run, the newest first, with its payslips and its gross, deductions, net and employer costs.

From Pay Runs, Payslips. Shows Number, Frequency, Period, Pay Date, Payslips, Gross, Deductions, Net, Employer Costs.

#### Pay to date

For each pay year and person: the payslips, gross pay, deductions, net pay and employer costs so far. The current year's figures are the year to date.

From Payslips, Pay Runs, Pay Years, Employees. Shows Pay Year, Employee No, Employee, Payslips, Gross, Deductions, Net, Employer Costs.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.

#### Pay to date by item

The same, item by item: basic pay, overtime and holiday pay, and each deduction, for each person in each pay year.

From Payslip Lines, Payslips, Pay Runs, Pay Years, Employees. Shows Pay Year, Employee No, Employee, Kind, Item, Amount to Date.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.

#### Starters and leavers

People who joined or left in the last 12 months, and anyone due to start in the next three months, the newest first.

From Employees, Departments. Shows Employee No, Employee, Department, Job Title, Start Date, Leave Date, Leaving Reason, Change.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Change is `IIf(Nz([Leave Date], "") = "", IIf(DateDiff("d", Date(), [Start Date]) > 0, "Starting soon", "Joined"), IIf(DateDiff("d", [Start Date], Date()) <= 365, "Joined and left", "Left"))`.
Only where `Days Since Start Between -90 And 365` and `Days Since Leaving Between 0 And 365`.

#### Absence by person

Absence other than holiday in the last 12 months for each person: sickness spells and days, other days, and the days absent in all, the most first. Days in 12 months is the person's absence rate in days a year.

From Absences, Employees, Departments. Shows Employee, Department, Sickness Spells, Sickness Days, Other Days, Days Absent.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Sickness Spells is `IIf([Kind] = "Sickness", 1, 0)`; Sickness Days is `IIf([Kind] = "Sickness", [Days], 0)`; Other Days is `IIf([Kind] = "Sickness", 0, [Days])`.
Only where `Kind <> "Holiday"` and `Status In ("Approved", "Recorded")` and `Days Ago Between 0 And 365`.

#### Birthdays and anniversaries

Staff with a birthday or a work anniversary this month or next, with the date and the years served.

From Employees, Departments. Shows Employee, Department, Birthday, Work Anniversary, Years.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; Birthday is `IIf((Month([Date of Birth]) - Month(Date()) + 12) Mod 12 <= 1, Format([Date of Birth], "dd") & "/" & Format([Date of Birth], "mm"), "")`; Work Anniversary is `IIf((Month([Start Date]) - Month(Date()) + 12) Mod 12 <= 1 And Year(Date()) - Year([Start Date]) + IIf(Month([Start Date]) < Month(Date()), 1, 0) >= 1, Format([Start Date], "dd") & "/" & Format([Start Date], "mm"), "")`; Years is `IIf((Month([Start Date]) - Month(Date()) + 12) Mod 12 <= 1 And Year(Date()) - Year([Start Date]) + IIf(Month([Start Date]) < Month(Date()), 1, 0) >= 1, Year(Date()) - Year([Start Date]) + IIf(Month([Start Date]) < Month(Date()), 1, 0), Null)`.
Only where `Birthday In <= 1` and `Anniversary In <= 1` and `Years Served >= 1` and `Days Served >= 0` and `Days Served >= 0` and `Leave Date Is Null` and `Leave Date Is Null`.

#### Documents to chase

Contracts not yet signed back, right to work checks and other papers not yet done, and checks that must be done again within 60 days, for people still working for you.

From Documents Held, Employees. Shows Employee, Document, Issued On, Completed On, Expires On, To Do.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`; To Do is `IIf(Nz([Completed On], "") = "", "Not done yet", "Check again before it expires")`.
Only where `Completed On Is Null` and `Days to Expiry <= 60` and `Leave Date Is Null` and `Leave Date Is Null`.

#### Staff list

Everyone working for you now, by department, with their job, start date, pay type, hours and rate.

From Employees, Departments. Shows Department, Employee No, Employee, Job Title, Start Date, Pay Type, Pay Frequency, Hours per Week, Hourly Rate, Annual Salary, Phone.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Leave Date Is Null` and `Days Served >= 0`.

#### Emergency contacts

Who to call for each person working for you now, by department.

From Employees, Departments. Shows Department, Employee, Phone, Emergency Contact, Emergency Relationship, Emergency Phone.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.
Only where `Leave Date Is Null`.

#### Pay history

Every change of job, pay or hours, by person, the newest first.

From Pay Changes, Employees. Shows Employee, Effective From, Reason, Job Title, Pay Type, Hourly Rate, Annual Salary, Hours per Week.
Calculated: Employee is `[First Name] & " " & [Last Name]`.

#### Deduction rates in use

The deduction and employer rates that apply today, in payslip order.

From Deduction Rates. Shows Name, Paid By, Percent, Fixed Amount, Threshold, Applies From, Applies To.
Only where `Days in Force >= 0` and `Days Still to Run >= 0`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Start Here, Business, Departments, Employees, Pay Changes, Documents Held, Holiday Allowances, Absences, Pay Years, Pay Runs, Timesheets, Timesheet Lines, Deduction Rates, Payslips, Payslip Lines, Annual Summaries, Annual Summary Lines. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

The staff list on a page for each department, with a head count and the hours.

Each person's emergency contact, by department: print it for the office wall or the first-aid box.

This year's holiday allowance, days booked and days left for each person, by department.

Sickness and other absence in the last 12 months for each person, by department, with totals.

#### Monthly payroll cost

Gross pay, employer costs and total cost for each department, month by month.

#### Pay run register

Every pay run with its totals: the record of what was paid and when.

From the query Pay run totals: Number, Frequency, Period, Pay Date, Payslips, Gross, Deductions, Net, Employer Costs, with the total of Gross, total of Net, total of Employer Costs.

Hours and overtime for each department last month.

Timesheets waiting for a manager, by department.

Each person's gross, deductions and net for each pay year, with totals for the year.

#### Start here: the everyday tasks, step by step

The guide to this database printed: each everyday task and its steps, from the Start Here table.

From the table Start Here, a group for each Task: Step, What to do.

### Print templates

#### Payslip

The payslip for one person and one pay run: their details, the month, the pay date and, for someone paid by the hour, the weeks their hours are from and the hours paid, each payment and each deduction on its own side with its year-to-date figure, then gross, deductions and net pay, and the year to date. The tax code prints once you type it on the payslip. It prints the latest pay run's payslips: this month's once the pay date has come, last month's until then; print an older one from the Payslips form. The tax, social insurance and pension rates in this sample are invented examples, named "(example rate)". They are not the rules of any country. Before paying anyone, replace them in Deduction Rates with your own country's current rules or your payroll provider's figures. One for each record of Payslips, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Payslip: {Pay Run.Period}
- Fields: Name, Employee number, Payslip, Job, Department, Pay date, Period from, Period to, Paid, Pay type, Pay year, Tax code, Hours worked from, Hours worked to, Hours paid
- Lines from Payslip Lines: Pay and deductions, Hours, Rate, Payments, Deductions, Year to date
- Totals: Gross pay, Total deductions, Net pay
- Fields: Gross pay, year to date, Deductions, year to date, Net pay, year to date
- Words: Net pay is paid by bank transfer on {Pay Date} to bank code {Employee.Bank Code}, account {Employee.Account Number}.
- Words: On top of your pay, {Business.Name} pays {Employer Costs} in employer contributions for this period.
- Words: Please check your payslip and tell us within 14 days if anything looks wrong. Keep your payslips: you may need them to show what you earn.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

#### Timesheet

A week's timesheet for one person: each day's start, finish, break and hours, the overtime above their contract hours when there is any, and lines for the employee and the manager to sign. It prints the timesheets waiting for approval. One for each record of Timesheets, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Timesheet {Number}
- Fields: Name, Employee number, Department, Week commencing, Contract hours, Status, Submitted, Approved by, Approved
- Lines from Timesheet Lines: Day, Date, Start, Finish, Break, minutes, Hours, Overtime, Note
- Totals: Hours worked, Within contract hours, Overtime
- Words: Overtime is the time worked above the contract hours for the week, and is paid at one and a half times the hourly rate. Days of holiday or sickness are not shown here: they are paid from the absence record.
- Words: I confirm that these are the hours I worked in the week shown.
- Signed by: Employee, Approved by

#### Employment contract summary

A summary of a person's main terms, to give with the offer letter and sign: the job, start date, pay, hours, holiday, sickness, pension and notice, filled in from their Employees record, with the hours and pay clauses worded for someone paid by the hour or for a salary. The words are a plain example of our own, not legal advice: have them checked for your own country before you use them. It prints for everyone working here now and those about to start; print a leaver's from the Employees form. One for each record of Employees, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Summary of terms of employment
- Fields: First name, Family name, Address, Employee number, City, Postcode, Job, Department, Starts on, Reports to, Pay type, Paid, Hourly rate, Annual salary, Hours a week, Days a week, Holiday a year, days, Notice, weeks
- Words: This summary sets out the main terms on which {Business.Name}, of {Business.Address}, {Business.City} {Business.Postcode} ("the employer"), employs {First Name} {Last Name} ("you"). It goes with your offer letter and the staff handbook. Please read it, sign both copies and give one back to us.
- Words: 1. Your job. You are employed as {Job Title} in the {Department} department, reporting to {Manager}. Your manager may ask you to do other reasonable work that suits your skills, such as helping another department at a busy time.
- Words: 1. Your job. You are employed as {Job Title} in the {Department} department, reporting to the owners. You may be asked to do other reasonable work that suits your skills, such as helping another department at a busy time.
- Words: 2. Where you work. You work at {Business.Address}, {Business.City}. We will not ask you to work anywhere else for more than a day without agreeing it with you first.
- Words: 3. Start and trial period. Your employment starts on {Start Date}. The first three months are a trial period, during which either of us may end the employment with one week's notice. Your manager will meet you before it ends to talk about how it has gone.
- Words: 4. Hours. Your normal hours are {Hours per Week} hours a week over {Days per Week} days, on a rota your manager gives you at least two weeks ahead. Any shift longer than six hours has an unpaid break of 30 minutes. Time worked above your weekly hours is overtime: it is agreed with your manager beforehand and paid at one and a half times your hourly rate.
- Words: 4. Hours. Your normal hours are {Hours per Week} hours a week over {Days per Week} days. Any working day longer than six hours has an unpaid break of 30 minutes. Your salary covers reasonable extra hours at busy times.
- Words: 5. Pay. You are paid {Hourly Rate} for each hour worked, {Pay Frequency}, by bank transfer on the last working day of the month. Pay by the hour is paid a month behind, from your approved timesheets: each month's pay covers the weeks that ended in the month before. Each payslip shows your pay and everything deducted from it: the deductions the law requires, your pension contributions, and anything else you have agreed to in writing.
- Words: 5. Pay. Your salary is {Annual Salary} a year, paid {Pay Frequency} in twelve equal parts, by bank transfer on the last working day of the month, for that month. Each payslip shows your pay and everything deducted from it: the deductions the law requires, your pension contributions, and anything else you have agreed to in writing.
- Words: 6. Holiday. Your holiday is {Holiday Days} days a year, worked out for the days you work each week. The holiday year runs from 1 January to 31 December; if you join or leave during the year you have a share for the part of the year you work. Ask for holiday on a leave request at least two weeks ahead. At the busiest times of year we may ask you to choose other dates. Up to five unused days may be carried into the next year, and holiday you have earned but not taken when you leave is paid with your last pay.
- Words: 7. Sickness. If you are ill and cannot work, call your manager before your shift starts, or as soon as you can, and say how long you expect to be off. Sick pay is set out in the staff handbook and is never less than the law requires.
- Words: 8. Pension. We will offer you a place in the workplace pension scheme where the law requires it, and you may ask to join at any time. What you and we pay in is shown on each payslip.
- Words: 9. Notice. After the trial period, either of us may end your employment by giving {Notice Weeks} weeks' notice in writing, or more where the law requires it. We may pay you for the notice period instead of asking you to work it.
- Words: 10. Rules and concerns. The staff handbook sets out how we deal with discipline and with any concern you raise. Speak first to your manager; if your concern is about your manager, speak to the office.
- Words: 11. Changes. We will tell you in writing at least one month ahead of any change to these terms, unless you agree to it sooner.
- Words: Signed for {Business.Name}, and by you to show that you have received these terms and agree to them.
- Signed by: For the employer, Employee, Date

#### Leave request

The form for asking for leave and recording the manager's decision, with the holiday allowance for the year when it is holiday. It prints the requests still to decide and the leave still to come; sickness and compassionate leave are recorded, not asked for, and print only from the Absences form. One for each record of Absences, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Leave request {Number}
- Fields: Name, Employee number, Department, Manager, Kind of leave, Asked for on, First day off, Last day off, Working days, Reason, Paid leave
- Words: Holiday allowance for the year:
- Fields: Holiday year, Allowance, days, Carried over, days, Booked so far, days
- Words: Request. I would like to take the leave shown above. I have checked the rota with my team, and my work will be covered or handed over before I go.
- Fields: Decision, Decided by, Decided on
- Words: {Notes}
- Words: Decision: approved / declined (the manager crosses out one).
- Words: Once approved, holiday is taken from the allowance for the year and paid as holiday pay. If a request is declined, your manager will tell you why and help you find other dates.
- Signed by: Employee, Manager

#### Annual pay summary

The end-of-year summary for one person and one pay year: each kind of pay and each deduction added up for the year, and the net pay, with a note for someone who has left. Give it to each person after the last pay run of the year. One for each record of Annual Summaries, on a4 paper, with the Business record at the head.

- Heading: Annual pay summary {Pay Year.Name}
- Fields: Name, Summary, Employee number, Issued, Address, Pay year from, City, Pay year to, Postcode, Payslips in the year, Tax code
- Lines from Annual Summary Lines: Pay and deductions for the year, Pay, Deducted
- Totals: Total pay, Total deductions, Net pay
- Words: This summary shows the pay {Business.Name} paid you in the pay year from {Pay Year.Starts} to {Pay Year.Ends}, and everything deducted from it. In the same year we paid {Employer Costs} in employer contributions on top of your pay.
- Words: {Notes}
- Words: Please keep it safe: you may be asked for it to show your income, for example for a tax return, a loan or a tenancy. Ask the office if you need another copy.
- Words: {Business.Document Footer}

### Starting empty

Start with Business, your own name and address, which every document prints, then Departments and Pay Years. Fill in Deduction Rates with your own country's current rates or your payroll provider's. Then add each person in Employees with a Pay Changes record for the terms they are on, their Documents Held and this year's Holiday Allowances. Absences and timesheets come in as people book holiday and work their weeks, and Pay Runs, Payslips and Annual Summaries as you pay them.

### Making it yours

- Pay hourly staff weekly: set their Pay Frequency to Weekly and add a weekly pay run, with one timesheet on each payslip.
- Add more kinds of pay, such as a bonus, tips or a night allowance: they are Payment lines on the payslip with an Item of their own, and the Pay to date by item query adds them up.
- Keep timesheets for salaried staff too: add a timesheet for them each week without paying overtime, to see the hours they really work.
- Pay overtime at more than one rate, such as double time on public holidays: add a Rate Multiplier field to Timesheet Lines and an Overtime line for each rate.
- Track training and certificates, such as first aid or food hygiene: add them to Documents Held with an Expires On, and the Documents to chase query will show those running out.
- Keep a rota: add a Shifts table (person, date, start, end) for the weeks ahead and a query of who is working each day.
- Run more than one site: add a Sites table and point Employees at it, then group the payroll cost and overtime queries by site.

### Questions people ask

**Are the tax and pension rates real?**

No. The tax, social insurance and pension rates in this sample are invented examples, named "(example rate)". They are not the rules of any country. Before paying anyone, replace them in Deduction Rates with your own country's current rules or your payroll provider's figures.

**How do I print one person's payslip, or a whole month's?**

The print template Payslip holds the latest pay run's payslips, so print it from Print templates for the whole month. For one, or an older one, open the Payslips form, find the payslip by its Number or the person, and print it from there.

**Can I pay some staff weekly?**

Yes. Set their Pay Frequency to Weekly and add a weekly pay run each week (Frequency Weekly, the Monday to Sunday in Period Starts and Period Ends), with a payslip for each of them from that week's timesheet. Share the yearly thresholds and fixed amounts by 52 instead of 12.

**Why is someone missing from Holidays left?**

Holidays left lists the people who have a Holiday Allowances record for the year that takes in today and have no Leave Date. Add this year's record for anyone new. Leavers are left out on purpose.

**How is a part-timer's holiday worked out?**

Their days a week times the full-time days, divided by five: three days a week with 28 full-time days is 16.8, rounded up to 17. Someone who joins during the year has a share for the months left.

**How is overtime worked out?**

For the whole week: the hours on the timesheet above the person's contract hours. On the lines, it is the part of the day when the week went over. It is paid at one and a half times their hourly rate.

**Where do the year-to-date figures come from?**

From the payslips: each payslip keeps Gross to Date, Deductions to Date and Net to Date, and each line its Year to Date. The queries Pay to date and Pay to date by item add up the payslips themselves for each pay year.

**Can I use the contract summary as it is?**

It is a plain example written for this sample, not legal advice. Have it checked for your own country, change the words in the print template Employment contract summary, and keep your full contract and staff handbook alongside it.

## Contacts

**Address book.** People you know or deal with, how to reach them, and a phone list to print.

Contacts is an address book for anyone who keeps a list of people: a small office, a club secretary, a tradesman with regular customers, or a household. It starts empty and holds one record for each person.

Each record has the person's name, the company they work for and their job, their e-mail, phone and mobile numbers, a postal address, a birthday and room for notes. Only the last name has to be filled in, so a record can start with very little and grow.

There is a single table, so nothing points anywhere else. The company is typed on each person rather than chosen from a list, which keeps it simple; the Customers and sales template keeps companies in a table of their own when you need that.

It suits, with small changes: A small office keeping its business contacts; A club or society secretary; A self-employed tradesman or cleaner with regular customers; A family address book with birthdays; A school or nursery keeping parents' details; An event organiser keeping suppliers and helpers.

### Things you should know

- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Only Last Name must be filled in. For a company with no named person, type the company's name in Last Name and leave First Name empty.
- A change in a form or in the table is kept when you leave the box: there is no Save button to press for each record.
- There are no pointing fields in this template, so Company is plain text. Type a company the same way each time ("Hill Street Dental", not "Hill St Dental") so a query can find all its people.
- The whole address book is one file on this computer. Keep a copy elsewhere with File, Save As, on a memory stick or a cloud folder, and do it again from time to time.

### Tutorial

#### Add a contact

1. Open the Contacts form from the Forms list and press New Record.
2. Type at least the Last Name, then whatever else you know: First Name, Company, Phone, Mobile and E-mail.
3. Press Add Record. The new contact is kept and the form shows it.

#### Change someone's details

1. Open the Contacts form and move to the person with the Next record and Previous record arrows.
2. Click in the box to change, such as Phone, type the new number and press Enter or click in another box. The change is kept as soon as you leave the box.
3. For many changes at once, open the Contacts table from the Tables list instead: every contact is a row, and a cell you type in is kept the same way.

#### Look someone up

1. Run the query Contact list from the Queries list. It shows everyone by last name.
2. To see only the people at one company, open the query's design and type the company's name in the criteria under Company, in quotes: "Hill Street Dental".
3. Run it again to see the shorter list. Clear the criteria to go back to everyone.

#### Print the phone list

1. Open the report Phone list from the Reports list.
2. Check the order in Sort by: Last Name keeps it alphabetical.
3. Press Print, or Save as PDF to e-mail it or keep a copy.

#### Remove a contact

1. Open the Contacts form, move to the person and press Delete.
2. Before you delete, check it is the right person: there is no undo for a deleted record other than a copy made with File, Save As.
3. To remove several, open the Contacts table from the Tables list, tick the box at the start of each row and press Delete.

### Tables

#### Contacts

One record for each person you keep in touch with.

| Company | Short text | The company or organisation they work for, typed as you would write it. |

### Relationships


### Queries

#### Contact list

Every contact with their company, e-mail and phone, sorted by last name and then first name. There are no criteria, so it shows everyone; use it to look someone up or copy the list elsewhere.

From Contacts. Shows Last Name, First Name, Company, E-mail, Phone.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Contacts. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Phone list

A printed list of every contact by last name, with their phone, mobile and e-mail, to pin up by the phone or keep in a folder.

From the table Contacts: Last name, First name, Phone, Mobile, E mail.

### Starting empty

There is only one table, so start straight away: open the Contacts form and add the people you call most, then fill in the rest as you come to them. If your contacts are already in a spreadsheet, you can save it as a CSV file and bring it in with Import as a table of its own.

### Making it yours

- Group your contacts: add a Group field (Family, Work, Club, Supplier) and a query that chooses one group in its criteria.
- Keep companies once: add a Companies table and change Company into a field that points at it, so the form gives a list of names to choose from.
- Send cards: add a Christmas Card field (Yes/No) and a query of everyone ticked, with their address, to print labels from.
- Record when you last spoke: add a Last Contacted date and sort the Contact list query by it to see who you have not called for a while.
- Add the social side: a Website field, or one for a messaging name, for people you reach that way.

### Questions people ask

**How do I sort the list by company instead of name?**

In the report Phone list, choose Company in Sort by. In the query Contact list, open its design and move the sort from Last Name to Company.

**Can I keep more than one e-mail address for a person?**

Not as it comes. Add a second field to the Contacts table in its design, such as Work E-mail, and it appears on the form.

**Why does the form refuse to add a contact?**

Last Name is empty. Type something in it, even a company's name, and press Add Record again.

**Can I bring in contacts I already have in a spreadsheet?**

Save the spreadsheet as a CSV file and bring it in with Import. It comes in as a table of its own, which you can keep beside Contacts or use in its place.

**How do I see whose birthday is coming up?**

Make a new query on Contacts with First Name, Last Name and Birthday, sorted by Birthday. The template has no birthday query of its own.

**Is my address book sent anywhere?**

No. It is a file on this computer and stays there unless you copy or send it yourself.

## Inventory

**Stock control.** Products, the suppliers you buy them from, every stock movement and what is running low.

Inventory is for anyone who holds goods and needs to know what is on the shelf and when to buy more: a small shop, a workshop with spare parts, a stores cupboard or an online seller working from a spare room.

It keeps your suppliers, the products you stock with their price, the units in stock and the level at which you reorder, and a record of each time stock comes in or goes out. A query lists what is getting low with the supplier's phone number beside it, and a report lists every product under its supplier.

Each product points at the supplier you buy it from, and each stock movement points at a product. One supplier has many products, and one product has many movements.

It suits, with small changes: A small shop or market stall; A workshop or garage keeping spare parts; An office or school stores cupboard; An online seller packing orders at home; A cafe or bar keeping dry goods and drinks; A charity shop or food bank.

### Things you should know

- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Units in Stock is a number you keep up to date yourself: adding a stock movement does not change it. Change both together, and count the stock now and then to check them.
- Supplier on a product, and Product on a stock movement, are lists of names on the form: you choose from what is already in the other table. Add the supplier before its products, and the product before its movements. In the table's rows the same field shows the record's number instead.
- The Low stock query compares each product with its own Reorder Level, so set a reorder level on every product you keep: one left at nought never shows until it runs out.
- A supplier with products cannot be deleted while those products point at it, and a product with movements cannot be deleted while they point at it. Tick Discontinued on a product you no longer keep instead.
- Keep a copy of the file with File, Save As before a big change such as a year-end stock count.

### Tutorial

#### Add a supplier and a product

1. Open the Suppliers form, press New Record, type the Name, Contact, E-mail and Phone, and press Add Record.
2. Open the Products form and press New Record. Type the Name, an SKU and a Category, and choose the supplier in the Supplier list.
3. Type the Unit Price, the Units in Stock you have now and a Reorder Level that suits how quickly it sells, then press Add Record.

#### Book in a delivery

1. Open the Stock Movements form and press New Record.
2. Choose the product in Product, type the day in When and the number received in Quantity (24 for twenty-four). Type Delivery in Note and press Add Record.
3. Open the Products form, move to the same product and add the same number to Units in Stock.

#### Record goods going out

1. Open the Stock Movements form, press New Record and choose the Product.
2. Type the day in When and the number with a minus in Quantity (-2 for two sold). Type Sold or Damaged in Note and press Add Record.
3. On the Products form, take the same number off Units in Stock.

#### See what to reorder

1. Run the query Low stock from the Queries list.
2. Each line shows the product, how many are left, its reorder level, the supplier and the supplier's Phone, ready to call.
3. To order sooner or later, open the query's design and change the 10 in the criteria under Units in Stock.

#### Print a stock sheet

1. Open the report Products by supplier from the Reports list.
2. It lists each supplier's products with the units in stock and a total for each supplier.
3. Press Print to take round the shelves for a stock count, or Save as PDF.

#### Put the stock right after a count

1. Count the shelf. If it differs from Units in Stock, open the Stock Movements form and add a movement for the difference, above or below nought, with Stock count in Note.
2. Then type the counted number in Units in Stock on the Products form.
3. Run the query Low stock afterwards: the count may show something lower than you thought.

### Tables

#### Suppliers

The businesses you buy from, one record each.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The supplier's name. It must be filled in, and it is what the Supplier list on a product shows. |
| Contact | Short text | The person you deal with there. |
| E-mail | Short text | Where to send an order. |
| Phone | Short text | The number to call when you need to reorder. |
| Address | Short text | Their address, for returns or collecting goods. |

#### Products

What you keep in stock, one record for each line.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The product as you know it. It must be filled in, and it is what the Product list on a stock movement shows. |
| SKU | Short text, unique | Your own code for the product, or the barcode number. Each SKU can be used once only. |
| Category | Short text | The group it belongs to, such as Drinks, Stationery or Brake Parts, typed the same way each time. |
| Supplier | Points at Suppliers | Who you buy it from, chosen from your Suppliers. |
| Unit Price | Currency | What one unit sells for, or what it costs you if you only track stock. |
| Units in Stock | Whole number | How many are on the shelf now. A new product starts at nought. |
| Reorder Level | Whole number | The number at which you mean to order more. It starts at 5. |
| Discontinued | Yes/No | Ticked for a product you no longer stock. It drops out of the Low stock query but keeps its history. |

#### Stock Movements

Each time stock comes in or goes out: a delivery, a sale, a breakage or a stock count.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Product | Points at Products, required | The product that moved, chosen from your Products. It must be filled in. |
| When | Date | The day it moved. |
| Quantity | Whole number | How many: above nought for goods coming in, below nought for goods going out (-3 for three sold). |
| Note | Short text | Why it moved: Delivery, Sold, Damaged, Stock count, or a reference such as an order number. |

### Relationships

- Products.Supplier points at a record in Suppliers
- Stock Movements.Product points at a record in Products

### Queries

#### Low stock

Products at or below their own Reorder Level, by name, with the units in stock, the reorder level, the supplier and the supplier's phone. Discontinued products are left out. Run it before you place an order.

From Products, Suppliers. Shows Product, Units in Stock, Reorder Level, Supplier, Phone.
Only where `Spare <= 0` and `Discontinued = No`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Suppliers, Products, Stock Movements. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Products by supplier

Every product under the supplier you buy it from, by name, with its SKU, category, price and units in stock, and the units in stock added up for each supplier and for the whole. Use it as a stock sheet or to check what you buy from whom.

From the table Products, a group for each Supplier: Name, SKU, Category, Unit price, Units in stock, with the total of Units in Stock.

### Starting empty

Enter your Suppliers first, then your Products, choosing each one's supplier from the list and typing what is on the shelf now in Units in Stock. From then on add a stock movement each time goods come in or go out. If you want the history to match, add one movement per product for the stock you start with, with Opening stock in Note.

### Making it yours

- Keep a buying price as well as a selling price: add a Cost Price field to Products and a query with a calculated column for the stock's value at cost.
- Hold stock in more than one place: add a Locations table, a Location field on Stock Movements that points at it, and a query of movements by location.
- Say what kind of movement it is: add a Kind field to Stock Movements (Received, Sold, Damaged, Counted) instead of writing it in Note.
- Record purchase orders: add an Orders table that points at Suppliers and an Order Lines table that points at Orders and Products.
- Keep a little more of what sells fast: raise its Reorder Level, and Low stock warns you sooner for that product alone.

### Questions people ask

**Why did Units in Stock not change when I added a movement?**

The template keeps the two apart: Stock Movements is the history, Units in Stock is today's number. Change Units in Stock on the Products form as well.

**Can a product come from more than one supplier?**

Not as it comes: each product points at one supplier. Choose the one you use most, or add a Second Supplier field that points at Suppliers too.

**What should I put in Unit Price?**

Whatever you need to know most often. A shop usually keeps the selling price; a stores cupboard the cost. To keep both, add a Cost Price field.

**Why can I not use the same SKU twice?**

SKU is unique, so each code points at one product. If two products share a barcode, add a letter to one of them.

**How do I see every movement for one product?**

Open the Products form at that product: the stock movements that point at it are listed below its fields.

**A discontinued product still shows on the stock sheet. Is that right?**

Yes. The report Products by supplier lists every product. Only the Low stock query leaves discontinued lines out.

## Membership

**Clubs and societies.** Members, what they have paid and the renewals coming due.

Membership is for a club, society or association that has members who join, pay and renew: a sports club, a choir, an allotment society, a residents' association or a small professional body.

It keeps each member's name and how to reach them, the type of membership they hold, when they joined, when their renewal is due and whether they are still active. Every payment a member makes is kept as its own record, so you can see what each person has paid over the years.

Each payment points at the member who made it. One member has many payments. A query lists the active members by their renewal date, and a report adds up what each member has paid.

It suits, with small changes: A sports or social club; A choir, band or drama group; An allotment or gardening society; A residents' or parents' association; A small trade or professional body; A gym or dance class with members who pay by the year.

### Things you should know

- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Member on a payment is a list of names on the Payments form, taken from the Members table by first and last name. Add the member before their first payment. In the Payments table's rows the same field shows the member's number instead.
- Renewal Due is not moved on by itself when a payment comes in. Move it on a year on the member's record each time they renew.
- A member who has payments cannot be deleted while those payments point at them. Untick Active instead, which also keeps your records of who paid what complete.
- Membership Type is typed text. Type each type the same way every time (Junior, not Juniors) so you can choose by it in a query.
- Members' details are personal data. Keep the file somewhere only the committee can open it, and keep a copy with File, Save As.

### Tutorial

#### Add a new member

1. Open the Members form and press New Record.
2. Type First Name, Last Name, E-mail, Phone and Address. Change Membership Type if they are not Standard.
3. Type today in Joined and the day their first renewal falls in Renewal Due, usually a year on. Leave Active ticked and press Add Record.

#### Record a payment

1. Open the Payments form and press New Record.
2. Choose the member by name in Member, type the day in Paid On, the sum in Amount and what it was for in For.
3. Press Add Record. The payment also appears under the member on the Members form.

#### Chase this month's renewals

1. Run the query Renewals due from the Queries list. The members whose renewal is soonest, or already past, are at the top.
2. Use the E-mail column to send each one a reminder.
3. When someone pays, record the payment, then open the Members form at that member and move Renewal Due on a year.

#### Mark someone who has left

1. Open the Members form and move to the member with the Next record arrow.
2. Untick Active. They drop out of Renewals due but their payments stay on record.
3. If they come back, tick Active again and type a new date in Renewal Due.

#### Print the treasurer's report

1. Open the report Payments by member from the Reports list.
2. Each member's payments are listed under their name with a total, and the grand total is at the foot.
3. Press Print for the meeting, or Save as PDF to send to the committee.

|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Member | Points at Members, required | Who paid, chosen from the list of members by name. It must be filled in. |
| Paid On | Date | The day the money came in. |
| Amount | Currency | How much they paid. |
| For | Short text | What it was for, such as 2026 subscription, Joining fee or Annual dinner. |

### Relationships

- Payments.Member points at a record in Members

### Queries

#### Renewals due

Active members who have a renewal date, the soonest first, with their name, e-mail and membership type. Only renewals due in the next 30 days, or already past, with the days left (below nought when overdue). Members who have left (Active unticked) and members with no date are left out. Those at the top whose date has passed are overdue.

From Members. Shows Renewal Due, Days Left, First Name, Last Name, E-mail, Membership Type.
Calculated: Days Left is `DateDiff("d", Date(), [Renewal Due])`.
Only where `Renewal Due Is Not Null` and `Days Left <= 30` and `Active = Yes`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Members, Payments. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Payments by member

Each member's payments by the day they were paid, with what each was for and its amount, and the total for each member and for everyone. Use it for the treasurer's report or to answer a member who asks what they have paid.

From the table Payments, a group for each Member: Paid on, For, Amount, with the total of Amount.

### Starting empty

Enter your Members first, with the type each holds, the day they joined and when their renewal is due. Then add their Payments, choosing each member from the list. If you are moving from a paper list, start with the current members and add past payments only if you need them.

### Making it yours

- Keep the fee for each type: add a Membership Types table with a name and an annual fee, and change Membership Type on Members into a field that points at it.
- Record how they paid: add a Method field to Payments (Cash, Card, Bank transfer, Cheque) and a query that totals each method.
- Note consent for mailings: add a Mailing Consent field (Yes/No) and the day it was given, and choose by it before you send news.
- Track attendance: add an Events table and an Attendance table that points at both Members and Events.
- Keep an emergency contact for a sports club: add Emergency Name and Emergency Phone fields to Members.
- Add a Left On date to Members alongside Active, to see how long people stay.

### Questions people ask

**How do I see who has not renewed?**

Run Renewals due. Anyone whose Renewal Due date is before today has not renewed yet, and they are at the top of the list.

**Can I record a family on one membership?**

Enter one member for the person who pays, with Membership Type Family, and put the other names in a field you add, or enter each person and record the payment against one of them.

**What if a member pays in instalments?**

Record each instalment as its own payment with the same words in For. The report adds them up under the member.

**How do I give everyone the same renewal date?**

Type the club's renewal day in Renewal Due for each member, such as 1 April. The query lists them all together on that day.

**Why is a member missing from Renewals due?**

Their renewal is more than 30 days away, or Active is unticked, or Renewal Due is empty. Change the 30 in the query's Days Left criteria to look further ahead.

**How do I see one member's payments quickly?**

Open the Members form at that member: their payments are listed below their details.

## Customers and sales

**Sales tracking.** Companies you sell to, the people there, the deals in hand and each call or meeting.

Customers and sales is a simple customer list and sales tracker for a business that sells to other businesses: a consultant, a small agency, a supplier to the trade or a sales team of a few people.

It keeps the companies you deal with and the people at each one, the opportunities you are working on with their stage, value and the day you expect them to close, and a log of every call, e-mail or meeting with a person. A query lists the deals still open by close date, and a report shows the pipeline under each company.

People point at the company they work for, and opportunities point at a company too. Activities point at a person, so a call is kept against whoever you spoke to, and through them against their company.

It suits, with small changes: A consultant or freelancer winning work from businesses; A small marketing or design agency; A supplier to shops, offices or the trade; A sales team of two to ten people; A training company selling courses to employers; A charity seeking corporate sponsors.

### Things you should know

- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Company on a person and on an opportunity, and Person on an activity, are lists of names on the form, taken from the other table. Add the company before its people and deals, and the person before their calls. In the table's rows these fields show the record's number instead.
- Stage is typed text. Open opportunities leaves out any stage with won or lost in it, in capitals or not, so Closed won drops out too; a stage such as Lost interest would drop out as well. Keep to the same few words each time.
- Activities are kept against a person, not a company or a deal. To see every call with a company, open the People form at each of its people: their activities are listed below.
- A company that has people or opportunities cannot be deleted while they point at it, and nor can a person with activities.
- Keep a copy of the file with File, Save As before you share it with a colleague, so you each know which is the latest.

### Tutorial

#### Add a company and the person you deal with

1. Open the Companies form, press New Record, type the Name, Industry, Website, Phone, City and Country, and press Add Record.
2. Open the People form and press New Record. Choose the company in Company, type First Name, Last Name, Job Title, E-mail and Phone, and press Add Record.
3. Open the Companies form again at the company: the person you added is listed below its fields.

#### Record a new opportunity

1. Open the Opportunities form and press New Record.
2. Choose the company in Company and type a short Title. Stage starts as Lead.
3. Type what it is worth in Value, the day you expect an answer in Expected Close and your name in Owner, then press Add Record.

#### Log a call or meeting

1. Open the Activities form and press New Record.
2. Choose who you spoke to in Person and type the day and time in When.
3. Change Kind if it was not a call, type what was said and agreed in Notes, and press Add Record.

#### Move a deal on and close it

1. Open the Opportunities form and move to the deal with the Next record arrow.
2. Change Stage as it progresses, such as from Lead to Proposal, and change Expected Close or Value if they have moved.
3. When you hear, type Won or Lost in Stage exactly so. It then drops out of Open opportunities.

#### Review the week's pipeline

1. Run the query Open opportunities from the Queries list. The deals due to close soonest are at the top.
2. Open the report Pipeline by company for each company's deals with their total value.
3. Press Print or Save as PDF to take it to a sales meeting.

### Tables

#### Companies

The businesses you sell to or hope to, one record each.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Name | Short text, required | The company's name. It must be filled in, and it is what the Company list on a person or opportunity shows. |
| Industry | Short text | What line of business they are in, such as Retail, Construction or Education. |
| Website | Short text | Their web address. |
| Phone | Short text | Their main switchboard number. |
| City | Short text | The town or city they are based in. |
| Country | Short text | The country they are based in. |

#### People

The people you deal with, each at a company.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Company | Points at Companies | The company they work for, chosen from your Companies. It can be left empty for someone between jobs. |
| First Name | Short text | Their first or given name. |
| Last Name | Short text, required | Their family name. It must be filled in. |
| Job Title | Short text | Their job, such as Buyer, Office Manager or Director. |
| E-mail | Short text | Their e-mail address. |
| Phone | Short text | Their direct line or mobile. |

#### Opportunities

Each piece of business you are trying to win, from the first enquiry to won or lost.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Company | Points at Companies, required | The company the deal is with, chosen from your Companies. It must be filled in. |
| Title | Short text, required | A short name for the deal, such as New website or 200 chairs for the hall. It must be filled in. |
| Stage | Short text | Where it has got to: it starts as Lead, then perhaps Qualified, Proposal or Negotiation, and ends as Won or Lost. |
| Value | Currency | What the deal is worth if you win it. |
| Expected Close | Date | The day you expect to hear yes or no. |
| Owner | Short text | Who in your business is looking after it, typed by name. |

#### Activities

Every call, e-mail or meeting, kept against the person it was with.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Person | Points at People | Who you spoke to or met, chosen from People by name. |
| When | Date and time | The day and time it happened, or is booked for. |
| Kind | Short text | What it was: Call (the start), E-mail, Meeting or Visit. |
| Notes | Long text | What was said, what was agreed and what to do next. |

### Relationships

- People.Company points at a record in Companies
- Opportunities.Company points at a record in Companies
- Activities.Person points at a record in People

### Queries

#### Open opportunities

Deals whose Stage says neither won nor lost (however it is typed: Won, won, Closed won), the soonest expected close first, with the company, the title, the stage, the value and who owns it. Use it each week to see what needs a push.

From Opportunities, Companies. Shows Expected Close, Company, Title, Stage, Value, Owner.
Only where `Stage Not Like "*won*"` and `Still Open Not Like "*lost*"`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Companies, People, Opportunities, Activities. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Pipeline by company

Every opportunity under its company, by expected close, with its title, stage and value, and the value added up for each company and for the whole. It includes won and lost deals as well as open ones, so it shows all the business you have had with each company.

From the table Opportunities, a group for each Company: Title, Stage, Expected close, Value, with the total of Value.

### Starting empty

Enter your Companies first, then the People at each, choosing the company from the list. Then add your Opportunities, choosing the company again, and log Activities as you make calls and hold meetings. Start with the deals open now and add closed ones later if you want the history.

### Making it yours

- Keep stages to a list: add a Stages table and change Stage into a field that points at it, so it cannot be mistyped.
- Weight the pipeline: add a Probability field to Opportunities and a query with a calculated column for Value times Probability.
- Link calls to deals: add an Opportunity field to Activities that points at Opportunities.
- Plan the next step: add a Follow Up date to Activities and a query of follow-ups in the next 7 days.
- Record why deals are lost: add a Lost Reason field to Opportunities and a query that counts each reason.

### Questions people ask

**What stages should I use?**

Any that suit how you sell. A common set is Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Negotiation, Won and Lost. Only Won and Lost matter to the query, which leaves them out.

**How do I see the total value of open deals?**

Make a new report from the query Open opportunities with a total on Value. The report Pipeline by company adds up won and lost deals too, so its totals are larger.

**Can I link an activity to a deal?**

Not as it comes. Add an Opportunity field to Activities that points at Opportunities, and choose the deal as you log the call.

**Can more than one person use it?**

It is one file on one computer. To share it, keep it in a shared folder and agree who changes it when, or send a copy with File, Save As.

**How do I see everyone at one company?**

Open the Companies form at that company: the people and opportunities that point at it are listed below.

**Why is Owner not a list of names?**

Owner is typed text so the template works for one person as well as a team. Add a Staff table and point Owner at it if you want a list to choose from.

## Lending library

**Lending.** Books, the people who borrow them, each loan and what is out and when it is due back.

Lending library is for anyone who lends books and wants them back: a school or classroom library, a church or community book box, a club's shared collection, an office reading shelf or a family that lends to friends.

It keeps your books with their author, publisher, year, shelf and number of copies, the people who borrow them, and a record of each loan with the day it went out, the day it is due back and the day it came back. A query lists what is still out by due date, and a report shows each borrower's loans.

Each loan points at one book and one borrower. A book can be lent many times, and a borrower can have many loans, so the Loans table is where the two meet.

It suits, with small changes: A school or classroom library; A church, village hall or community book box; A book club sharing its copies; An office or staff room reading shelf; A toy or tool library, with the fields renamed; A family keeping track of books lent to friends.

### Things you should know

- Your records live in one file on your computer. Keep copies: File, Save As makes one, and a copy on another drive or in your own cloud storage keeps it safe if this computer is lost. Close the database before copying the file by hand.
- Every change to the design (a new field, a renamed table) is a numbered step that Data Files keeps, so you can see what was changed and when.
- Book and Borrower on a loan are lists of names on the Loans form, taken from Books by title and from Borrowers by first and last name. Add the book and the borrower before the loan. In the Loans table's rows these fields show the record's number instead.
- A loan is never deleted when the book comes back: typing Returned On is what closes it. That keeps the history the report prints.
- Copies is a count you keep for your own reference. The template does not stop you lending more copies than you hold, so check On loan before lending the last one.
- A book or borrower that has loans cannot be deleted while those loans point at it.
- Keep a copy of the file with File, Save As, at the end of each term or season.

### Tutorial

#### Add a book

1. Open the Books form from the Forms list and press New Record.
2. Type the Title, Author and ISBN, and the Publisher and Year if you have them.
3. Type where it lives in Shelf, change Copies if you hold more than one, and press Add Record.

#### Add a borrower and lend them a book

1. Open the Borrowers form, press New Record, type First Name, Last Name, E-mail and Phone, and press Add Record.
2. Open the Loans form and press New Record. Choose the book in Book and the person in Borrower.
3. Type today in Lent On and the return day in Due Back, such as two weeks on. Leave Returned On empty and press Add Record.

#### See what is overdue

1. Run the query On loan from the Queries list.
2. The books due back soonest are at the top; any whose Due Back is before today are overdue.
3. Use the Phone column to ring the borrower, or look up their e-mail on the Borrowers form.

#### Record a return

1. Open the Loans form and move to the loan with the Next record and Previous record arrows. The Books form at that book also lists its loans below.
2. Type today in Returned On and press Enter. The book drops out of the On loan query.
3. Put the book back on the shelf named in its Shelf field on the Books form.

#### Print the loans report

1. Open the report Loans by borrower from the Reports list.
2. Each borrower's loans are listed under their name with a count of books.
3. Press Print, or Save as PDF to keep a copy for the end of term.

### Tables

#### Books

One record for each title you lend.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Title | Short text, required | The book's title. It must be filled in, and it is what the Book list on a loan shows. |
| Author | Short text | Who wrote it, family name first if you want them to sort that way. |
| ISBN | Short text | The number on the back cover above the barcode, useful when two books share a title. |
| Publisher | Short text | Who published it. |
| Year | Whole number | The year it was published. |
| Shelf | Short text | Where it is kept, such as Fiction A-F or Box 3. |
| Copies | Whole number | How many copies you hold. It starts at 1. |

#### Borrowers

The people who borrow from you, one record each.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| First Name | Short text | Their first or given name. |
| Last Name | Short text, required | Their family name. It must be filled in. |
| E-mail | Short text | Where to send a reminder. |
| Phone | Short text | The number to ring when a book is overdue. |

#### Loans

Each time a book goes out, one record per book lent.

| Field | Type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| ID | AutoNumber | The number Data Files gives each record. Other tables point at a record by it. |
| Book | Points at Books, required | The book lent, chosen from your Books by title. It must be filled in. |
| Borrower | Points at Borrowers, required | Who borrowed it, chosen from your Borrowers by name. It must be filled in. |
| Lent On | Date | The day it went out. |
| Due Back | Date | The day it should come back. |
| Returned On | Date | The day it came back. Empty while the book is still out. |

### Relationships

- Loans.Book points at a record in Books
- Loans.Borrower points at a record in Borrowers

### Queries

#### On loan

Every book still out, which is every loan with no Returned On date, the soonest due back first, with the title and the borrower's name and phone. Those at the top whose date has passed are overdue.

From Loans, Books, Borrowers. Shows Due Back, Title, First Name, Last Name, Phone.
Only where `Returned On Is Null`.

### Forms

Every table has a form of the same name, made by the form wizard: Books, Borrowers, Loans. A form shows one record at a time; a field that points at another table is a list of that table's records, and the records that point at this one are listed below it.

### Reports

#### Loans by borrower

Every loan under its borrower, by the day it was lent, with the book, when it was due and when it came back, and a count of books for each borrower and for the whole. Returned loans are included, so it is each person's full borrowing history.

From the table Loans, a group for each Borrower: Book, Lent on, Due back, Returned on, with the count of Book.

### Starting empty

Enter your Books first, then your Borrowers, then add a Loan each time a book goes out, choosing the book and the borrower from the lists. If books are out already, add a loan for each with the day it went out and the day it is due.

### Making it yours

- Set a loan length for each book: add a Loan Days field to Books (14 for most, 7 for books in demand) and use it when you type Due Back.
- Charge late fees: add a Fine field to Loans and a query of returned loans whose Returned On is later than Due Back.
- Group the borrowers: add a Class or Group field to Borrowers so a school can print each class's loans.
- Sort by subject: add a Subject or Genre field to Books and a query that lists the books in one subject.
- Take reservations: add a Reservations table that points at Books and Borrowers, with the day it was asked for.

### Questions people ask

**How do I see who has a particular book?**

Open the Books form at that book: its loans are listed below, and the one with no Returned On is out now.

**How do I lend two books at once?**

Add a loan for each book, both with the same borrower and dates.

**Can I renew a loan?**

Yes. Open the loan on the Loans form and type the new date in Due Back.

**Two books have the same title. How do I tell them apart in the list?**

The Book list shows titles only. Add the author or year to the Title, such as Collected Poems (Hardy), or keep each by its ISBN.

**Can I lend things other than books?**

Yes. Rename the fields in the Books table's design, such as Author to Make, and use it for toys, tools or games.

**Why is a book still showing as on loan?**

Its loan has no Returned On date. Open the loan and type the day it came back.
